“Man-*Fred*, I tell you!” here bawled out Miss Bas-Bleu, as I led Mrs. Pirouette to a seat. “Did ever anybody hear the like? It’s Man-*Fred*, I say, and not at all by any means Man-*Friday*.” Here Miss Bas-Bleu beckoned to me in a very peremptory manner; and I was obliged, will I nill I, to leave Mrs. P. for the purpose of deciding a dispute touching the title of a certain poetical drama of Lord Byron’s. Although I pronounced, with great promptness, that the true title was Man-*Friday*, and not by any means Man-*Fred*, yet when I returned to seek Mrs. Pirouette she was not to be discovered, and I made my retreat from the house in a very bitter spirit of animosity against the whole race of the Bas-Bleus.

Matters had now assumed a really serious aspect, and I resolved to call at once upon my particular friend, Mr. Theodore Sinivate; for I knew that here at least I should get something like definite information.

“Smith!” said he, in his well-known peculiar way of drawling out his syllables; “Smith!﻿—why, not General John A. B. C.? Savage affair that with the Kickapo-o-o-os, wasn’t it? Say! don’t you think so?﻿—perfect despera-a-ado﻿—great pity, ’pon my honor!﻿—wonderfully inventive age!﻿—pro-o-odigies of valor! By the by, did you ever hear about Captain Ma-a-a-a-n?”

“Captain Mann be d﻿—﻿—﻿d!” said I; “please to go on with your story.”

“Hem!﻿—oh well!﻿—quite *la même cho-o-ose*, as we say in France. Smith, eh? Brigadier-General John A﻿—B﻿—C.? I say”﻿—[here Mr. S. thought proper to put his finger to the side of his nose]﻿—“I say, you don’t mean to insinuate now, really and truly, and conscientiously, that you don’t know all about that affair of Smith’s, as well as I do, eh? Smith? John A﻿—B﻿—C.? Why, bless me, he’s the ma-a-an﻿—”

“*Mr.* Sinivate,” said I, imploringly, “*is* he the man in the mask?”

===Chinese===

「史密斯！」皮鲁埃特夫人说，我们正双双旋着*微风舞步*；「史密斯！——怎么，总不会是约翰·A·B·C·将军吧？布加布人那桩可怕的事，是不是？——可怕的生灵，那些印第安人！——*请*把脚尖转出去！我真替你害臊——勇气过人的汉子，可怜的人！——可这是个了不得的发明时代——哦天哪，我喘不上气了——十足的亡命徒——英勇的奇迹——*从没听说过*！——不能信——我得坐下好好开导开导你——史密斯！怎么，他就是那个人——」

「*曼*弗雷德，我跟你说！」我扶皮鲁埃特夫人落座时，巴斯布吕（Bas-Bleu）小姐在这里嚷起来。「有谁听说过这样的话？是*曼*弗雷德，我说，绝绝对对不是什么*人*星期五（Man-Friday）。」巴斯布吕小姐在这里以十分专断的样子朝我招手；我不得不，愿意也罢不愿意也罢，丢下皮鲁埃特夫人，去裁决一场关于拜伦勋爵某部诗剧题目的争执。虽然我以极大的敏捷断定，真正的题目是《*人*星期五》，绝绝对对不是《*曼*弗雷德》，等我回身再找皮鲁埃特夫人，她已无从寻见，我便怀着对巴斯布吕全族深仇大恨的苦涩心绪，退出了那座宅子。

事态如今已呈出一种真正严重的样子，我决意立刻去拜见我的挚友西奥多·西尼维特（Theodore Sinivate）先生；因为我知道，至少在他这里，我能得到近乎确切的情报。

「史密斯！」他以他那出了名的、把音节拖得老长的特别腔调说；「史密斯！——怎么，总不会是约翰·A·B·C·将军吧？同基卡——普——普人的那桩野蛮事，是不是？你说！你不这样想吗？——十足的亡命——命——命徒——可惜呀，我以名誉担保！——了不得的发明时代！——英——英——英勇的奇迹！对了，你可听说过曼恩上尉的事？」

「曼恩上尉见鬼去吧！」我说；「请把你的故事讲下去。」

「咳！——哦好吧！——正如我们在法国说的，*完完全全一码事*（la même cho-o-ose）。史密斯，嗯？准将约翰·A——B——C·？我说」[这里西尼维特先生认为得体的做法是把手指抵在鼻侧]「我说，你不是当真——真心实意、凭良心地暗示，你并不像我一样全知道史密斯的那桩事吧，嗯？史密斯？约翰·A——B——C·？怎么，老天，他就是那个——人——」

「西尼维特*先生*，」我恳求说，「他*是不是*那个戴面具的人？」

===Original===

“No-o-o!” said he, looking wise, “nor the man in the mo-o-on.”

This reply I considered a pointed and positive insult, and so left the house at once in high dudgeon, with a firm resolve to call my friend, Mr. Sinivate, to a speedy account for his ungentlemanly conduct and ill-breeding.

In the meantime, however, I had no notion of being thwarted touching the information I desired. There was one resource left me yet. I would go to the fountainhead. I would call forthwith upon the General himself, and demand, in explicit terms, a solution of this abominable piece of mystery. Here, at least, there should be no chance for equivocation. I would be plain, positive, peremptory﻿—as short as pie-crust﻿—as concise as Tacitus or Montesquieu.

It was early when I called, and the General was dressing; but I pleaded urgent business, and was shown at once into his bedroom by an old negro valet, who remained in attendance during my visit. As I entered the chamber, I looked about, of course, for the occupant, but did not immediately perceive him. There was a large and exceedingly odd-looking bundle of something which lay close by my feet on the floor, and, as I was not in the best humor in the world, I gave it a kick out of the way.

“Hem! ahem! rather civil that, I should say!” said the bundle, in one of the smallest, and altogether the funniest little voices, between a squeak and a whistle, that I ever heard in all the days of my existence.

“Ahem! rather civil that, I should observe.”

I fairly shouted with terror, and made off, at a tangent, into the farthest extremity of the room.

“God bless me! my dear fellow,” here again whistled the bundle, “what﻿—what﻿—what﻿—why, what *is* the matter? I really believe you don’t know me at all.”

What *could* I say to all this﻿—what *could* I? I staggered into an armchair, and, with staring eyes and open mouth, awaited the solution of the wonder.

“Strange you shouldn’t know me though, isn’t it?” presently re-squeaked the nondescript, which I now perceived was performing, upon the floor, some inexplicable evolution, very analogous to the drawing on of a stocking. There was only a single leg, however, apparent.

“Strange you shouldn’t know me, though, isn’t it? Pompey, bring me that leg!” Here Pompey handed the bundle, a very capital cork leg, already dressed, which it screwed on in a trice; and then it stood up before my eyes.

===Chinese===

「不——是！」他说，做出聪明相，「也不是月——亮上的人。」

我认为这一回答是尖刻而彻底的侮辱，于是立刻怀着极大的恼怒离开那座宅子，下定决心要我的朋友西尼维特先生就他这不成体统的行径和欠修的教养，从速给我一个交代。

然而与此同时，我并不甘心在我想要的情报上受挫。我还有一样手段。我要到源头去。我要立刻去拜见将军本人，用明确的语言，讨这个可憎之谜的解。至少在这里，不该有搪塞的余地。我要直截、肯定、不容分说——短得像馅饼皮——简得像塔西佗或孟德斯鸠。

我拜访得早，将军正在更衣；但我推说有急务，立刻被一个年老的黑人贴身男仆带进他的卧室——那仆人在我拜访期间一直在旁伺候。进屋时我自然四下找那位住户，却没有立刻看见他。有一大捆样子古怪得出奇的东西，紧紧靠着我脚边的地板躺着；我当时心境不大好，一脚把它从路上踢开。

「哼！啊哼！这可相当无礼，我看！」那捆东西说，用一种极细小的、又是我一生所听过的顶顶滑稽的小嗓音，介于吱叫和哨音之间。

「啊哼！这可相当无礼，我必须指出。」

我吓得放声大叫，一头斜刺里冲到屋子最远的角落。

「老天保佑我！我亲爱的朋友，」那捆东西又哨了起来，「什么——什么——什么——哎呀，*到底*出了什么事？我真相信您压根儿不认得我了。」

对这一切我*能*说什么——我*能*说什么呢？我跌跌撞撞扑进一张扶手椅，瞪着眼睛，张着嘴，等这奇观的下文。

「怪就怪您不认得我，是不是？」那说不清道不明的东西过一会儿又吱叫起来；我此刻看出，它正在地板上作某种无法解释的演进，极像套一只长袜的动作。不过露在外面的只有单独一条腿。

「怪就怪您不认得我，是不是？庞培，把那条腿递给我！」庞培把一条十分出色的软木腿递给那捆东西，腿已经穿好衣裳，它一转眼便旋上去；然后它在我眼前站起来了。

===Original===

“And a bloody action it *was*,” continued the thing, as if in a soliloquy; “but then one mustn’t fight with the Bugaboos and Kickapoos, and think of coming off with a mere scratch. Pompey, I’ll thank you now for that arm. Thomas” [turning to me] “is decidedly the best hand at a cork leg; but if you should ever want an arm, my dear fellow, you must really let me recommend you to Bishop.” Here Pompey screwed on an arm.

“We had rather hot work of it, that you may say. Now, you dog, slip on my shoulders and bosom! Pettitt makes the best shoulders, but for a bosom you will have to go to Ducrow.”

“Bosom!” said I.

“Pompey, will you *never* be ready with that wig? Scalping is a rough process after all; but then you can procure such a capital scratch at De L’Orme’s.”

“Scratch!”

“Now, you nigger, my teeth! For a *good* set of these you had better go to Parmly’s at once; high prices, but excellent work. I swallowed some very capital articles, though, when the big Bugaboo rammed me down with the butt end of his rifle.”

“Butt end! ram down!! my eye!!”

“O yes, by the by, my eye﻿—here, Pompey, you scamp, screw it in! Those Kickapoos are not so very slow at a gouge; but he’s a belied man, that Dr. Williams, after all; you can’t imagine how well I see with the eyes of his make.”

I now began very clearly to perceive that the object before me was nothing more nor less than my new acquaintance, Brevet Brigadier-General John A. B. C. Smith. The manipulations of Pompey had made, I must confess, a very striking difference in the appearance of the personal man. The voice, however, still puzzled me no little; but even this apparent mystery was speedily cleared up.

“Pompey, you black rascal,” squeaked the General, “I really do believe you would let me go out without my palate.”

Hereupon, the negro, grumbling out an apology, went up to his master, opened his mouth with the knowing air of a horse-jockey, and adjusted therein a somewhat singular-looking machine, in a very dexterous manner, that I could not altogether comprehend. The alteration, however, in the entire expression of the General’s countenance was instantaneous and surprising. When he again spoke, his voice had resumed all that rich melody and strength which I had noticed upon our original introduction.

===Chinese===

「那*确凿*是一场血战，」那东西接着说，像在自言自语；「不过跟布加布人和基卡普人打仗，谁也不能指望只带一道划伤就脱身。庞培，现在劳驾把那条胳膊给我。托马斯」[转向我]「装软木腿实在是最拿手的；可亲爱的朋友，您要是哪天缺一条胳膊，一定得让我举荐毕晓普给您。」庞培在这里旋上一条胳膊。

「那一仗打得火热，您可以这么说。来，狗东西，把我的肩膀和胸脯套上！佩蒂特做的肩膀最好，胸脯您可就得去找杜克罗了。」

「胸脯！」我说。

「庞培，你*到底*什么时候才把那顶假发弄好？剥头皮终究是个粗活；不过在德洛姆的铺子里，您能配上等极佳的假发。」

「假发！」

「来，黑小子，我的牙！要配*一副好*牙，您最好马上去帕姆利那里；价钱高，活儿出色。不过布加布大个子用枪托把我捣倒的时候，我咽下去过几件很不错的物件。」

「枪托！捣倒！！我的天！！」

「哦对了，对了，我的眼睛——庞培，你这小子，旋进去！那些基卡普人剜起眼珠来手脚并不算慢；不过那位威廉斯医生，毕竟是个被人冤枉的人；您想象不到他做的眼睛我看得多么清楚。」

我此刻开始十分清楚地看出，眼前的物件不多不少，正是我的新交，名誉准将约翰·A·B·C·史密斯将军。我必须承认，庞培的摆弄已在那人的外观上造成了十分显著的变化。可是那嗓音仍旧叫我困惑不小；但连这表观的神秘也很快澄清了。

「庞培，你这黑无赖，」将军吱叫说，「我真相信你会叫我连上颚也不戴就出门。」

于是那仆人嘟嘟囔囔赔了个不是，走到主人跟前，以一种相马师般的内行神气掰开他的嘴，以我全然无从领会的十分灵巧的手法，在嘴里安置了一件样子颇为奇特的机器。然而将军整个面部表情的改变是顷刻的、惊人的。他再开口时，声音已恢复了我们最初引见时我注意到的那全部丰润、悦耳和洪亮。

===Original===

“D﻿—﻿—﻿n the vagabonds!” said he, in so clear a tone that I positively started at the change, “D﻿—﻿—﻿n the vagabonds! they not only knocked in the roof of my mouth, but took the trouble to cut off at least seven-eighths of my tongue. There isn’t Bonfanti’s equal, however, in America, for really good articles of this description. I can recommend you to him with confidence,” [here the General bowed,] “and assure you that I have the greatest pleasure in so doing.”

I acknowledged his kindness in my best manner, and took leave of him at once, with a perfect understanding of the true state of affairs﻿—with a full comprehension of the mystery which had troubled me so long. It was evident. It was a clear case. Brevet Brigadier-General John A. B. C. Smith was the man﻿—was *the man that was used up*.

===Chinese===

「咒死那些恶棍！」他说，声音清亮，我当真被这变化吓了一跳，「咒死那些恶棍！他们不但打塌了我上颚的顶，还好心地把我舌头割掉了至少八分之七。不过论这类物件的真正好货，全美国没有比得上邦凡蒂的。我可以放心举荐您去找他，」[将军在这里一躬身]「并且向您保证，我这样举荐，心里有最大的快乐。」

我以最得体的方式谢了他的好意，立刻向他告辞——对事情的真相有了透彻的了解——对搅扰我如此长久的谜，有了全然的领会。事情是明摆着的。案情清楚。名誉准将约翰·A·B·C·史密斯就是那个人——正是*那个被用尽的人*。

## The Fall of the House of Usher / 厄舍府的倒塌
===Original===

Son cœur est un luth suspendu;

Sitôt qu’on le touche il résonne.

> De Béranger

===Chinese===

他的心是一张悬挂着的鲁特琴；

刚一触碰，它便铮然作响。

> 德·贝朗瑞

===Original===

During the whole of a dull, dark, and soundless day in the autumn of the year, when the clouds hung oppressively low in the heavens, I had been passing alone, on horseback, through a singularly dreary tract of country; and at length found myself, as the shades of the evening drew on, within view of the melancholy House of Usher. I know not how it was﻿—but, with the first glimpse of the building, a sense of insufferable gloom pervaded my spirit. I say insufferable; for the feeling was unrelieved by any of that half-pleasurable, because poetic, sentiment, with which the mind usually receives even the sternest natural images of the desolate or terrible. I looked upon the scene before me﻿—upon the mere house, and the simple landscape features of the domain﻿—upon the bleak walls﻿—upon the vacant eye-like windows﻿—upon a few rank sedges﻿—and upon a few white trunks of decayed trees﻿—with an utter depression of soul which I can compare to no earthly sensation more properly than to the after-dream of the reveller upon opium﻿—the bitter lapse into everyday life﻿—the hideous dropping off of the veil. There was an iciness, a sinking, a sickening of the heart﻿—an unredeemed dreariness of thought which no goading of the imagination could torture into aught of the sublime. What was it﻿—I paused to think﻿—what was it that so unnerved me in the contemplation of the House of Usher? It was a mystery all insoluble; nor could I grapple with the shadowy fancies that crowded upon me as I pondered. I was forced to fall back upon the unsatisfactory conclusion, that while, beyond doubt, there *are* combinations of very simple natural objects which have the power of thus affecting us, still the analysis of this power lies among considerations beyond our depth. It was possible, I reflected, that a mere different arrangement of the particulars of the scene, of the details of the picture, would be sufficient to modify, or perhaps to annihilate its capacity for sorrowful impression; and, acting upon this idea, I reined my horse to the precipitous brink of a black and lurid tarn that lay in unruffled lustre by the dwelling, and gazed down﻿—but with a shudder even more thrilling than before﻿—upon the remodelled and inverted images of the gray sedge, and the ghastly tree-stems, and the vacant and eye-like windows.

===Chinese===

这一年秋天，有一整天都沉闷、昏暗、无声，云层低低压在天际；这一整天，我都独自骑着马，穿过一片格外凄凉的原野；到暮色四合时分，我终于发现自己已望见了那郁郁的厄舍府（House of Usher）。我说不清是怎么回事——只是乍见那座建筑，一种难以忍受的阴郁便弥漫了我的心灵。我说难以忍受；因为这感觉里没有得到半点纾解，不曾掺入那种因诗意而半含愉悦的情愫——心智领受荒凉或可怖的自然景象时，哪怕最严酷的，通常也总带着几分这种情愫。我望着眼前的景象——望着那孤零零的宅子，望着这片领地上平淡无奇的几处景致——望着萧索的墙——望着空洞的、眼睛似的窗——望着几丛蔓生的莎草——望着几株枯树惨白的树干——心头弥漫着一种彻底的沮丧，这感觉若要比拟，尘世间再没有什么比得上吸食鸦片者梦醒后的余绪——跌回日常生活的苦涩——面纱骇人地滑落。心头一阵冰凉，一阵下沉，一阵作呕——思绪陷于一种无从救赎的凄凉，任凭想象力怎样鞭策，也挤榨不出半点崇高。那是什么——我驻足思索——究竟是什么，在凝望厄舍府时令我如此丧魂失魄？这是个全然无解的谜；我苦苦思量，也敌不过纷纷涌上心头的幽晦幻想。我只得退回那个不能令人满意的结论：毋庸置疑，确有一些极简单的自然物的组合，具有这般左右我们的力量；但对这力量的分析，却属于我们力所不及的考量。我暗自思忖：这景象的诸般细节、这幅画的笔笔细部，若只是换一种安排，或许便足以改变、甚或完全抹去它令人悲愁的力量；本着这个念头，我勒转马头，来到一泓黑色阴惨的小湖陡峭的边缘——那湖卧在宅旁，泛着纹丝不动的幽光——朝下望去；可是望着那灰色莎草、狰狞树干、空洞而眼睛似的窗的倒影——变形倒置的模样——我这一颤，竟比先前更彻骨。

===Original===

Nevertheless, in this mansion of gloom I now proposed to myself a sojourn of some weeks. Its proprietor, Roderick Usher, had been one of my boon companions in boyhood; but many years had elapsed since our last meeting. A letter, however, had lately reached me in a distant part of the country﻿—a letter from him﻿—which, in its wildly importunate nature, had admitted of no other than a personal reply. The MS. gave evidence of nervous agitation. The writer spoke of acute bodily illness﻿—of a mental disorder which oppressed him﻿—and of an earnest desire to see me, as his best, and indeed his only personal friend, with a view of attempting, by the cheerfulness of my society, some alleviation of his malady. It was the manner in which all this, and much more, was said﻿—it was the apparent *heart* that went with his request﻿—which allowed me no room for hesitation; and I accordingly obeyed forthwith what I still considered a very singular summons.

===Chinese===

尽管如此，在这座阴郁的宅子里，我如今却打算小住几星期。宅子的主人罗德里克·厄舍（Roderick Usher），是我少年时代要好的游伴；可我们上次见面，已是许多年前的事了。然而不久前，一封信寄到了我客居的偏远之地——是他写来的——那信写得狂乱急切，除了亲自前往，不容我作别的答复。手稿的字里行间透着神经质的激动。写信人说到自己身罹急症——说到一种压在心头的精神病症——还说到切望见我一面：我是他的至交，也实在是他唯一的朋友，他想借我相伴的欢愉，稍解他的沉疴。打动我的，是这一切、连同许多别的话的说法——是伴随他请求而来的那份显然的*诚心*——这使我无从犹豫；于是我立刻听从了这召唤，尽管我始终觉得它蹊跷得很。

===Original===

Although, as boys, we had been even intimate associates, yet I really knew little of my friend. His reserve had been always excessive and habitual. I was aware, however, that his very ancient family had been noted, time out of mind, for a peculiar sensibility of temperament, displaying itself, through long ages, in many works of exalted art, and manifested, of late, in repeated deeds of munificent yet unobtrusive charity, as well as in a passionate devotion to the intricacies, perhaps even more than to the orthodox and easily recognisable beauties, of musical science. I had learned, too, the very remarkable fact, that the stem of the Usher race, all time-honored as it was, had put forth, at no period, any enduring branch; in other words, that the entire family lay in the direct line of descent, and had always, with very trifling and very temporary variation, so lain. It was this deficiency, I considered, while running over in thought the perfect keeping of the character of the premises with the accredited character of the people, and while speculating upon the possible influence which the one, in the long lapse of centuries, might have exercised upon the other﻿—it was this deficiency, perhaps, of collateral issue, and the consequent undeviating transmission, from sire to son, of the patrimony with the name, which had, at length, so identified the two as to merge the original title of the estate in the quaint and equivocal appellation of the “House of Usher”﻿—an appellation which seemed to include, in the minds of the peasantry who used it, both the family and the family mansion.

===Chinese===

尽管少年时我们甚至过从甚密，可我对这位朋友实在知之甚少。他的缄默一向过甚，且已成积习。然而我也知道，他那极古老的世家，久已以一种独特的气质敏感著称：许多世纪以来，它在诸多高华的艺术作品里显露自己；晚近以来，又显诸一桩桩慷慨而不张扬的善举，显诸一种对音乐之学精微曲折处的热忱钻研——这热忱，或许比对音乐中正统而一目了然的美的爱好，还要深挚。我还得知一件极可注意的事实：厄舍家族的血脉，虽古老尊荣，却从未在任何时期抽出过一条绵延的旁枝；换句话说，整个家族一脉单传，历来如此，仅有极细小而转瞬即逝的变通。我在心里把宅邸为人称道的品格与这家人的品格两两细较，又揣想前者千百年来可能施于后者的影响，觉得正是这一缺憾——正是这旁支的阙如，以及产业连同姓氏由此而父传子、子传孙、从无旁落的传承——到头来使两者浑然合一，把这份产业的原有名号，并入了「厄舍府」这个古怪而语义两可的称呼里——在使用这称呼的乡民心里，它似乎既指这一族，又指这一族的宅邸。

===Original===

I have said that the sole effect of my somewhat childish experiment﻿—that of looking down within the tarn﻿—had been to deepen the first singular impression. There can be no doubt that the consciousness of the rapid increase of my superstition﻿—for why should I not so term it?﻿—served mainly to accelerate the increase itself. Such, I have long known, is the paradoxical law of all sentiments having terror as a basis. And it might have been for this reason only, that, when I again uplifted my eyes to the house itself, from its image in the pool, there grew in my mind a strange fancy﻿—a fancy so ridiculous, indeed, that I but mention it to show the vivid force of the sensations which oppressed me. I had so worked upon my imagination as really to believe that about the whole mansion and domain there hung an atmosphere peculiar to themselves and their immediate vicinity﻿—an atmosphere which had no affinity with the air of heaven, but which had reeked up from the decayed trees, and the gray wall, and the silent tarn﻿—a pestilent and mystic vapor, dull, sluggish, faintly discernible, and leaden-hued.

Shaking off from my spirit what *must* have been a dream, I scanned more narrowly the real aspect of the building. Its principal feature seemed to be that of an excessive antiquity. The discoloration of ages had been great. Minute fungi overspread the whole exterior, hanging in a fine tangled web-work from the eaves. Yet all this was apart from any extraordinary dilapidation. No portion of the masonry had fallen; and there appeared to be a wild inconsistency between its still perfect adaptation of parts, and the crumbling condition of the individual stones. In this there was much that reminded me of the specious totality of old woodwork which has rotted for long years in some neglected vault, with no disturbance from the breath of the external air. Beyond this indication of extensive decay, however, the fabric gave little token of instability. Perhaps the eye of a scrutinizing observer might have discovered a barely perceptible fissure, which, extending from the roof of the building in front, made its way down the wall in a zigzag direction, until it became lost in the sullen waters of the tarn.

===Chinese===

我已说过，我那多少带点孩子气的试验——俯望那泓湖水——唯一的效用，便是加深了起初那奇异的印象。无可怀疑，我意识到自己的迷信——为何不这样称呼它呢？——正急速滋长，而这意识本身，恰恰主要加速了这滋长。我早就明白，凡以恐怖为根基的情绪，都遵循这条悖谬的法则。或许单单为着这个缘故，当我把目光从池中倒影重新抬向宅子本身时，我心里生出了一个怪诞的幻想——这幻想实在荒唐，我提它，只为表明压迫着我的那些感觉何等鲜活有力。我在想象中这样反复运思，竟至当真相信：整座宅邸与领地的四周，悬着一层为它们及其紧邻之地所独有的大气——这大气与天上的空气毫无亲缘，而是从朽树、灰墙和死寂的湖里蒸发升腾的一股瘴毒而神秘的雾汽，滞重、迟钝、依稀可辨，铅灰之色。我从心头抖落那*必定*是一场梦的东西，更仔细地端详这座建筑的真实面目。它的主要特征，似乎是一种过分的古老。经年累月的侵蚀变色已经很深。细小的真菌爬满整个外墙，从檐口垂下，织成一片精细而纠结的网。然而这一切，谈不上什么非同寻常的倾颓。砖石的任何部分都没有坍落；各部分之间的拼合依旧完好无缺，与个别石块的碎裂剥蚀之间，显出一种狂悖的矛盾。这情形大可让我想起蛀朽多年的旧木器——它们在一些无人过问的地窖里烂了多年，丝毫不受外界气息的扰动，看上去整体完好，其实内里已朽。不过，除了这大片朽坏的迹象，屋宇本身几乎没有露出不稳固的征兆。也许，唯有细察之人的眼睛，才能发现一道几乎无法察觉的裂缝：它从前面楼房的屋顶蜿蜒而下，曲曲折折顺着墙身延伸，直到没入小湖阴沉的水中。

===Original===

Noticing these things, I rode over a short causeway to the house. A servant in waiting took my horse, and I entered the Gothic archway of the hall. A valet, of stealthy step, thence conducted me, in silence, through many dark and intricate passages in my progress to the *studio* of his master. Much that I encountered on the way contributed, I know not how, to heighten the vague sentiments of which I have already spoken. While the objects around me﻿—while the carvings of the ceilings, the sombre tapestries of the walls, the ebon blackness of the floors, and the phantasmagoric armorial trophies which rattled as I strode, were but matters to which, or to such as which, I had been accustomed from my infancy﻿—while I hesitated not to acknowledge how familiar was all this﻿—I still wondered to find how unfamiliar were the fancies which ordinary images were stirring up. On one of the staircases, I met the physician of the family. His countenance, I thought, wore a mingled expression of low cunning and perplexity. He accosted me with trepidation and passed on. The valet now threw open a door and ushered me into the presence of his master.

The room in which I found myself was very large and lofty. The windows were long, narrow, and pointed, and at so vast a distance from the black oaken floor as to be altogether inaccessible from within. Feeble gleams of encrimsoned light made their way through the trellissed panes, and served to render sufficiently distinct the more prominent objects around; the eye, however, struggled in vain to reach the remoter angles of the chamber, or the recesses of the vaulted and fretted ceiling. Dark draperies hung upon the walls. The general furniture was profuse, comfortless, antique, and tattered. Many books and musical instruments lay scattered about, but failed to give any vitality to the scene. I felt that I breathed an atmosphere of sorrow. An air of stern, deep, and irredeemable gloom hung over and pervaded all.

===Chinese===

留意到这些，我便策马走过一道短短的堤道，来到宅前。一名侍立的仆人牵过我的马，我走进了大厅那哥特式的拱门。一名男仆迈着悄没声儿的步子，从那里领着我，一路无言，穿过许多幽暗曲折的过道，往他主人的*书房*去。一路上我所见的许多东西，也不知怎的，都助长了我先已说到的那些隐隐的情绪。我周围的物件——顶棚的雕饰、墙上幽暗的织锦挂毯、乌黑发亮的地板，还有我大步走过时嘎嘎作响的、幻影般的纹章甲胄——都不过是我自幼惯见、或与之同类的东西；我毫不犹豫地承认这一切何其熟悉；可寻常的物象此刻搅起的幻想，竟何其陌生，这令我暗暗称奇。在一段楼梯上，我遇见了这家的医生。我觉得他脸上带着卑琐的狡黠与困惑杂糅的神情。他战战兢兢地招呼了我一声，便径自过去了。这时男仆推开一扇门，把我领到他主人面前。我置身其中的这间屋子，十分宽大高敞。窗子狭长，顶端尖拱，距黑橡木地板高不可及，从屋里根本够不着。微弱的血红色光线透过格棂窗渗进来，勉强照得清四围较显眼的物件；然而眼睛怎么也望不进屋子深处的角落，也望不进那带穹顶花格的天顶的凹处。墙上挂着深色的帷幔。满屋的家具繁多，却毫不舒适，古旧，破烂。许多书籍和乐器散乱地搁着，却给这场景添不进半点生气。我觉得自己呼吸在一种悲哀的气氛里。一种冷峻、深沉、无可救药的阴郁，笼罩一切，浸透一切。

===Original===

Upon my entrance, Usher arose from a sofa on which he had been lying at full length, and greeted me with a vivacious warmth which had much in it, I at first thought, of an overdone cordiality﻿—of the constrained effort of the *ennuye* man of the world. A glance, however, at his countenance, convinced me of his perfect sincerity. We sat down; and for some moments, while he spoke not, I gazed upon him with a feeling half of pity, half of awe. Surely, man had never before so terribly altered, in so brief a period, as had Roderick Usher! It was with difficulty that I could bring myself to admit the identity of the wan being before me with the companion of my early boyhood. Yet the character of his face had been at all times remarkable. A cadaverousness of complexion; an eye large, liquid, and luminous beyond comparison; lips somewhat thin and very pallid, but of a surpassingly beautiful curve; a nose of a delicate Hebrew model, but with a breadth of nostril unusual in similar formations; a finely moulded chin, speaking, in its want of prominence, of a want of moral energy; hair of a more than web-like softness and tenuity; these features, with an inordinate expansion above the regions of the temple, made up altogether a countenance not easily to be forgotten. And now in the mere exaggeration of the prevailing character of these features, and of the expression they were wont to convey, lay so much of change that I doubted to whom I spoke. The now ghastly pallor of the skin, and the now miraculous lustre of the eye, above all things startled and even awed me. The silken hair, too, had been suffered to grow all unheeded, and as, in its wild gossamer texture, it floated rather than fell about the face, I could not, even with effort, connect its Arabesque expression with any idea of simple humanity.

===Chinese===

我进屋时，厄舍从他直挺挺躺着的长沙发上起身，热络活泼地迎接我；起初我觉得那热络有几分过甚其辞的殷勤——像社交场上厌倦一切的人勉强做出的亲热。然而望一眼他的脸，我便确信他是全然出于真心。我们坐下来；有片刻他一言不发，我望着他，半是怜悯，半是敬畏。真的，从来没有人像罗德里克·厄舍这样，在这样短的时日里，变得这样骇人！我好不容易才肯承认，眼前这个面容惨白的人，就是我少年时代的伙伴。不过他的相貌，一向是出众的。面色的死灰；一只大眼睛，水汪汪，亮得无可比拟；嘴唇略薄，极苍白，却弯出一条美得惊人的弧线；鼻梁是秀气的希伯来式样，鼻孔之宽却在同类鼻型中罕见；下巴的轮廓精致，只是不够前凸，透出意志力的匮乏；头发细软稀薄得赛过蛛丝——这些容貌，加上太阳穴上方异样开阔的额角，合起来构成一张不易忘怀的脸。而如今，仅仅由于这些容貌的主导气质、连同它们惯常流露的表情被过分放大，其中就起了这么多的变化，以致我疑心自己在同谁说话。皮肤此刻的死灰之白，眼睛此刻神异的光泽，尤其叫我心惊，甚至叫我不寒而栗。那丝缎般的头发也任其长得不再经管；它以狂乱的蛛丝质地，与其说披在脸上，不如说飘拂在脸周，我纵然竭力去想，也无法把那阿拉伯花纹般的怪异意态，与凡人的任何意念联到一起。

===Original===

In the manner of my friend I was at once struck with an incoherence﻿—an inconsistency; and I soon found this to arise from a series of feeble and futile struggles to overcome an habitual trepidancy﻿—an excessive nervous agitation. For something of this nature I had indeed been prepared, no less by his letter, than by reminiscences of certain boyish traits, and by conclusions deduced from his peculiar physical conformation and temperament. His action was alternately vivacious and sullen. His voice varied rapidly from a tremulous indecision (when the animal spirits seemed utterly in abeyance) to that species of energetic concision﻿—that abrupt, weighty, unhurried, and hollow-sounding enunciation﻿—that leaden, self-balanced and perfectly modulated guttural utterance, which may be observed in the lost drunkard, or the irreclaimable eater of opium, during the periods of his most intense excitement.

It was thus that he spoke of the object of my visit, of his earnest desire to see me, and of the solace he expected me to afford him. He entered, at some length, into what he conceived to be the nature of his malady. It was, he said, a constitutional and a family evil, and one for which he despaired to find a remedy﻿—a mere nervous affection, he immediately added, which would undoubtedly soon pass off. It displayed itself in a host of unnatural sensations. Some of these, as he detailed them, interested and bewildered me; although, perhaps, the terms, and the general manner of the narration had their weight. He suffered much from a morbid acuteness of the senses; the most insipid food was alone endurable; he could wear only garments of certain texture; the odors of all flowers were oppressive; his eyes were tortured by even a faint light; and there were but peculiar sounds, and these from stringed instruments, which did not inspire him with horror.

===Chinese===

我朋友举止间那种语无伦次——那种前后失据，立刻攫住了我；我很快便发现，这源自他想克服一种惯常的战栗——一种过度的神经质激动——而作的一连串软弱而徒劳的挣扎。这一类情形，我原本就有几分料到：他的信、我对某些少年心性的追忆、以及从他独特的体格与气质推得的结论，都早给了我预备。他的举止忽而活泼，忽而阴郁。他的嗓音变化极快：从一种颤抖的迟疑（那是血气全然沉寂的时候），一变而为那种有力的简截——那种突兀、沉实、不慌不忙而空谷似的吐字——那种铅一般沉着、自我平衡、节制得完美无缺的喉音；这等嗓音，只有不可救药的酒鬼，或无可挽回的鸦片瘾君子，在最亢奋的当口才有。他便这样谈起我此行的目的，谈起他见我的恳切愿望，谈起他期待我给他的慰藉。他相当详细地阐述了他对自己病症性质的见解。这病，他说，是一种体质性的、家族性的痼疾，他已不指望寻得疗法——但他随即又补上一句，这不过是个神经性的小恙，无疑很快就会过去。它表现在一大堆反常的感觉上。他一一细数，其中几条听得我又关切又迷惑；虽说其中或许也有他用的字眼、以及叙述的总体方式在起作用。他为感官病态的敏锐所苦：只有最无味的饭食才吃得下；衣裳也只能穿某几种质地的；一切花香都叫他窒息；哪怕微光也刺得他眼睛生疼；唯独某几类声音不使他恐怖——而且那还必须是弦乐器的声音。

===Original===

To an anomalous species of terror I found him a bounden slave. “I shall perish,” said he, “I *must* perish in this deplorable folly. Thus, thus, and not otherwise, shall I be lost. I dread the events of the future, not in themselves, but in their results. I shudder at the thought of any, even the most trivial, incident, which may operate upon this intolerable agitation of soul. I have, indeed, no abhorrence of danger, except in its absolute effect﻿—in terror. In this unnerved﻿—in this pitiable condition﻿—I feel that the period will sooner or later arrive when I must abandon life and reason together, in some struggle with the grim phantasm, **Fear**.”

I learned, moreover, at intervals, and through broken and equivocal hints, another singular feature of his mental condition. He was enchained by certain superstitious impressions in regard to the dwelling which he tenanted, and whence, for many years, he had never ventured forth﻿—in regard to an influence whose supposititious force was conveyed in terms too shadowy here to be restated﻿—an influence which some peculiarities in the mere form and substance of his family mansion, had, by dint of long sufferance, he said, obtained over his spirit﻿—an effect which the physique of the gray walls and turrets, and of the dim tarn into which they all looked down, had, at length, brought about upon the morale of his existence.

===Chinese===

我发现，他已被一种反常的恐怖死死奴役着。「我必死无疑，」他说，「我*注定*要葬身于这可悲的痴愚。就是这样，就是这样，而不是别的什么，我会走向毁灭。我惧怕未来的种种变故，不是惧怕它们本身，而是惧怕它们的结果。哪怕最不足道的小事，只要可能触动我这灵魂难堪的激动，我一想到就发抖。诚然，对于危险，我并不厌恶，我只怕它绝对的后果——恐怖。在这样心神俱疲——这样可悯的境地中——我感到，那个时刻迟早要来：我得在与那狰狞幻影——**恐惧**——的某场搏斗里，把性命和理智一并交出去。」此外，我还不时地、透过断续而含糊的暗示，得知他精神状况的另一奇异之处。他被某些迷信的印象锁住了，那印象关乎他所居住的这座宅子——多年来他从不敢迈出它一步——也关乎一种影响力，其假想的力量，此处难以用不昏昧的话复述；他说，单是他家宅子在形制与质料上的某些特质，就凭着长年的隐忍，使这影响力攫住了他的精神；那灰墙与塔楼的形骸，连同它们俯临的一泓幽暗湖水，到头来，就这样作用于他存在的元气。

===Original===

He admitted, however, although with hesitation, that much of the peculiar gloom which thus afflicted him could be traced to a more natural and far more palpable origin﻿—to the severe and long-continued illness﻿—indeed to the evidently approaching dissolution﻿—of a tenderly beloved sister﻿—his sole companion for long years﻿—his last and only relative on earth. “Her decease,” he said, with a bitterness which I can never forget, “would leave him (him the hopeless and the frail) the last of the ancient race of the Ushers.” While he spoke, the lady Madeline (for so was she called) passed slowly through a remote portion of the apartment, and, without having noticed my presence, disappeared. I regarded her with an utter astonishment not unmingled with dread﻿—and yet I found it impossible to account for such feelings. A sensation of stupor oppressed me as my eyes followed her retreating steps. When a door, at length, closed upon her, my glance sought instinctively and eagerly the countenance of the brother; but he had buried his face in his hands, and I could only perceive that a far more than ordinary wanness had overspread the emaciated fingers through which trickled many passionate tears.

The disease of the lady Madeline had long baffled the skill of her physicians. A settled apathy, a gradual wasting away of the person, and frequent although transient affections of a partially cataleptical character, were the unusual diagnosis. Hitherto she had steadily borne up against the pressure of her malady, and had not betaken herself finally to bed; but, on the closing in of the evening of my arrival at the house, she succumbed (as her brother told me at night with inexpressible agitation) to the prostrating power of the destroyer; and I learned that the glimpse I had obtained of her person would thus probably be the last I should obtain﻿—that the lady, at least while living, would be seen by me no more.

===Chinese===

不过他也承认，虽说承认得有些迟疑：如此折磨他的那许多特别的阴郁，其实可以追溯到一个更自然、也明显得多的源头——追溯到他挚爱的妹妹那缠绵的重症——事实上，追溯到她显然临近的死期——她是她多年间唯一的伴侣，是他在这个世上最后、也是仅存的亲人。「她的死，」他说道，那口吻中的辛酸我永远忘不了，「将把他——把孤弱无望的他——撇作古老的厄舍一族的最后一人。」他说话间，那位玛德琳小姐（她叫这个名字）从房间远端缓缓走过，没有察觉我在场，转眼消失了。我望着她，满心惊讶，且掺着恐惧——可我又说不清这样的感觉从何而来。我的目光追随着她远去的脚步，一种怔忡之感压住了我。待一扇门终于把她关在门后，我的目光不由自主地、急切地投向哥哥的脸；可他已把脸埋进双手，我只看见一种远超寻常的惨白漫上他那枯瘦的手指，指缝间淌下许多滚烫的热泪。玛德琳小姐的病，早已使医生们的医术束手无策。症状殊为怪异：一种成习的漠然，形体的日渐枯耗，还有频频发作却转瞬即逝的、略带僵直症性质的病征。直到此时，她一直顽强地顶住病魔的重压，不曾最终卧床；可是，在我抵达宅邸那天的暮色四合之际，她终于（她哥哥夜里激动难名地告诉我）向那摧折者的力量屈服了；我于是明白，我方才惊鸿一瞥的那个身影，多半是我见她的最后一眼——这位小姐，至少在生前，我再无缘得见了。

===Original===

For several days ensuing, her name was unmentioned by either Usher or myself; and during this period I was busied in earnest endeavors to alleviate the melancholy of my friend. We painted and read together, or I listened, as if in a dream, to the wild improvisations of his speaking guitar. And thus, as a closer and still closer intimacy admitted me more unreservedly into the recesses of his spirit, the more bitterly did I perceive the futility of all attempt at cheering a mind from which darkness, as if an inherent positive quality, poured forth upon all objects of the moral and physical universe, in one unceasing radiation of gloom.

I shall ever bear about me a memory of the many solemn hours I thus spent alone with the master of the House of Usher. Yet I should fail in any attempt to convey an idea of the exact character of the studies, or of the occupations, in which he involved me, or led me the way. An excited and highly distempered ideality threw a sulphureous lustre over all. His long improvised dirges will ring forever in my ears. Among other things, I hold painfully in mind a certain singular perversion and amplification of the wild air of the last waltz of Von Weber. From the paintings over which his elaborate fancy brooded, and which grew, touch by touch, into vaguenesses at which I shuddered the more thrillingly, because I shuddered knowing not why﻿—from these paintings (vivid as their images now are before me) I would in vain endeavor to educe more than a small portion which should lie within the compass of merely written words. By the utter simplicity, by the nakedness of his designs, he arrested and overawed attention. If ever mortal painted an idea, that mortal was Roderick Usher. For me at least, in the circumstances then surrounding me, there arose out of the pure abstractions which the hypochondriac contrived to throw upon his canvas, an intensity of intolerable awe, no shadow of which felt I ever yet in the contemplation of the certainly glowing yet too concrete reveries of Fuseli.

===Chinese===

此后好几天，厄舍和我都未曾提起她的名字；这段日子里，我一心一意，想方设法排解我朋友的忧郁。我们一起作画、读书；或者，我恍如梦中一般，听他那把会说话的吉他奏出狂放的即兴曲。就这样，随着亲密一日深似一日，我得以更无遮拦地走进他心灵的幽深处，也就越发痛切地体会到：想宽慰这样一颗心，是何等地徒劳——从这颗心里，黑暗仿佛一种内在的、积极的存在，以一道绵绵不绝的幽暗辐射，倾泻在道德世界与物质宇宙的一切对象之上。我这样独自陪着厄舍府主人度过的那许多庄肃的时辰，将永远随我而行。然而，要说出他领我做的那些钻研与消遣究竟是什么性质，任何尝试都注定失败。一种亢奋而极度失序的理想气质，给一切都镀上了硫磺般的光泽。他即兴奏出的那些长长的挽歌，将永远在我耳中回响。其中有一桩，我记得清楚且为之痛心：他把冯·韦伯最后一支圆舞曲的狂放曲调，作了一番奇特的变乱与铺衍。至于他的画——他繁复的幻想在上面盘桓不去，那些画一笔一笔地变得愈益缥缈，我望之而栗，又因不知为何而栗，愈发栗得深切——（它们的影像如今还历历在我眼前）要我从这些纯粹的抽象里提炼出些许能纳入文字范围的东西，也是徒劳，能写下的不过一小部分。若说曾有凡人把「观念」画出来过，那这凡人便是罗德里克·厄舍。至少对于我，在我当时所处的境况里，从这位忧郁症患者投诸画布的纯粹抽象之中，升起了一股难忍的敬畏；这敬畏的强度，是我在观赏富塞利那些确乎炽烈、却嫌过于具象的幻梦时，连一星半点也未曾感受过的。

===Original===

One of the phantasmagoric conceptions of my friend, partaking not so rigidly of the spirit of abstraction, may be shadowed forth, although feebly, in words. A small picture presented the interior of an immensely long and rectangular vault or tunnel, with low walls, smooth, white, and without interruption or device. Certain accessory points of the design served well to convey the idea that this excavation lay at an exceeding depth below the surface of the earth. No outlet was observed in any portion of its vast extent, and no torch, or other artificial source of light was discernible; yet a flood of intense rays rolled throughout, and bathed the whole in a ghastly and inappropriate splendor.

I have just spoken of that morbid condition of the auditory nerve which rendered all music intolerable to the sufferer, with the exception of certain effects of stringed instruments. It was, perhaps, the narrow limits to which he thus confined himself upon the guitar, which gave birth, in great measure, to the fantastic character of his performances. But the fervid *facility* of his *impromptus* could not be so accounted for. They must have been, and were, in the notes, as well as in the words of his wild fantasias (for he not unfrequently accompanied himself with rhymed verbal improvisations), the result of that intense mental collectedness and concentration to which I have previously alluded as observable only in particular moments of the highest artificial excitement. The words of one of these rhapsodies I have easily remembered. I was, perhaps, the more forcibly impressed with it, as he gave it, because, in the under or mystic current of its meaning, I fancied that I perceived, and for the first time, a full consciousness on the part of Usher of the tottering of his lofty reason upon her throne. The verses, which were entitled “The Haunted Palace,” ran very nearly, if not accurately, thus:

I

In the greenest of our valleys,

By good angels tenanted,

Once a fair and stately palace﻿—

Radiant palace﻿—reared its head.

In the monarch Thought’s dominion﻿—

It stood there!

Never seraph spread a pinion

Over fabric half so fair.

II

Banners yellow, glorious, golden,

On its roof did float and flow

(This﻿—all this﻿—was in the olden

Time long ago);

And every gentle air that dallied,

In that sweet day,

Along the ramparts plumed and pallid,

A winged odor went away.

===Chinese===

我朋友那些幻影般的构想之中，有一幅抽象的气质不那么浓烈，或许还能用文字——虽然乏力地——描出个影子。一幅小画，画的是一条极长的矩形地窖或隧道的内部：墙很低，平滑，白色，没有任何间断与纹饰。画中若干辅助的细节，很好地传达出这样一个意思：这处坑穴深藏在地下极深极深之处。它的整个广袤里看不到任何出口，也辨不出火把或任何人工光源；然而一道强烈的光奔涌其间，把整个空间浸浴在一种惨厉而不相称的辉煌里。我方才说过，他听觉神经的病态使一切音乐都令他不堪忍受，唯弦乐器的某些效果除外。也许正是他因此在吉他上自我设限的狭小范围，在很大程度上催生了他演奏的奇幻品格。但他那些即兴曲火热的*娴熟*，却不能这样解释。它们——无论音符，还是他那些狂想曲的唱词（他并不少用押韵的即兴唱词自伴）——必定是、也确实是那种高度的心神凝敛与专注的结果；我前面已提到过，这种凝敛，只有在人工亢奋达到顶点的特定时刻才能观察到。这些狂想曲中有一首的歌词，我轻易便记住了。他唱它的时候，我或许正因下述缘故而印象格外深刻：在它意义的潜流、或者说秘流之中，我仿佛第一次察觉，厄舍对自己高踞王座的堂皇理智正在倾颓，有了全然的自觉。那首题为「闹鬼的宫殿」的诗，大致——即使不逐字——是这样的：

一

在我们最青翠的山谷里，
住着善良的天使，
曾有一座美丽庄严的宫殿——
光华灿灿的宫殿——昂起头颅。
在君王「思想」的治下——
它矗立在那里！
何曾有过炽天使
把羽翼展临一座及它一半美好的建筑。

黄澄澄、辉煌煌、金灿灿的旌旗，
在宫殿顶上飘扬、流淌
（这——这一切——都属于久远
久远的旧时光）；
每一缕流连的柔风，
在那甜美的日子里，
拂过羽饰苍白的城垛，
便有一翼香气远扬。

Wanderers in that happy valley

Through two luminous windows saw

Spirits moving musically

To a lute’s well-tunèd law,

Round about a throne, where sitting

(Porphyrogene!)

In state his glory well befitting,

The ruler of the realm was seen.

IV

And all with pearl and ruby glowing

Was the fair palace door,

Through which came flowing, flowing, flowing

And sparkling evermore,

A troop of Echoes whose sweet duty

Was but to sing,

In voices of surpassing beauty,

The wit and wisdom of their king.

But evil things, in robes of sorrow,

Assailed the monarch’s high estate;

(Ah, let us mourn, for never morrow

Shall dawn upon him, desolate!)

That blushed and bloomed

Is but a dim-remembered story

Of the old time entombed.

And travellers now within that valley,

Through the red-litten windows, see

Vast forms that move fantastically

To a discordant melody;

While, like a rapid ghastly river,

Through the pale door,

A hideous throng rush out forever,

And laugh﻿—but smile no more.

I well remember that suggestions arising from this ballad, led us into a train of thought wherein there became manifest an opinion of Usher’s which I mention not so much on account of its novelty (for other men15 have thought thus), as on account of the pertinacity with which he maintained it. This opinion, in its general form, was that of the sentience of all vegetable things. But, in his disordered fancy, the idea had assumed a more daring character, and trespassed, under certain conditions, upon the kingdom of inorganization. I lack words to express the full extent, or the earnest *abandon* of his persuasion. The belief, however, was connected (as I have previously hinted) with the gray stones of the home of his forefathers. The conditions of the sentience had been here, he imagined, fulfilled in the method of collocation of these stones﻿—in the order of their arrangement, as well as in that of the many fungi which overspread them, and of the decayed trees which stood around﻿—above all, in the long undisturbed endurance of this arrangement, and in its reduplication in the still waters of the tarn. Its evidence﻿—the evidence of the sentience﻿—was to be seen, he said, (and I here started as he spoke,) in the gradual yet certain condensation of an atmosphere of their own about the waters and the walls. The result was discoverable, he added, in that silent, yet importunate and terrible influence which for centuries had moulded the destinies of his family, and which made *him* what I now saw him﻿—what he was. Such opinions need no comment, and I will make none.

===Chinese===

我清楚地记得，由这首叙事歌引出的话头，把我们带进了一连串的沉思；在其中，厄舍的一层见解显露出来。我提它，倒不在于它新异（别人15也有这么想的），而在于他坚持它的那股执拗劲儿。这见解，就其大概而言，是说一切草木皆有知觉。但在他错乱的幻想里，这观念变得更大胆了，在某些条件下，竟越界闯进了无机物的王国。我找不到言语，来表达他这信念推到多远，也表达不出他倾注其中的那份恳切的*忘我*。然而这信念（如我先前暗示的）是与先人宅邸的那些灰色石块联系在一起的。他设想，知觉存在的诸般条件，在这里已经具备：在于这些石块排列之法——在于它们布列的次序，也在于覆满其上的诸种菌类、立于四围的朽树的次序——尤其在于这格局长年累月不受扰动的延续，在于它在那泓死水中的重重倒影。它的明证——知觉的明证——他说（他说这话时我吓了一跳），可以看见：在水与墙的四周，一种它们自有的大气正渐渐然而确凿地凝集。结果，他补充道，就显在那无声却纠缠不休、可怖的影响力里——几个世纪以来，这力量塑造着他家族的命运，也把*他*塑成了我此刻所见的样子——塑成了他现在的样子。这样的见解无须评论，我也不作评论。

===Original===

Our books﻿—the books which, for years, had formed no small portion of the mental existence of the invalid﻿—were, as might be supposed, in strict keeping with this character of phantasm. We pored together over such works as the *Ververt et Chartreuse* of Gresset; the *Belphegor* of Machiavelli; the *Heaven and Hell* of Swedenborg; the *Subterranean Voyage of Nicholas Klimm* by Holberg; the *Chiromancy* of Robert Flud, of Jean D’Indaginé, and of De la Chambre; the *Journey Into the Blue Distance* of Tieck; and the *City of the Sun* of Campanella. One favorite volume was a small octavo edition of the *Directorium Inquisitorium*, by the Dominican Eymeric de Gironne; and there were passages in Pomponius Mela, about the old African Satyrs and Oegipans, over which Usher would sit dreaming for hours. His chief delight, however, was found in the perusal of an exceedingly rare and curious book in quarto Gothic﻿—the manual of a forgotten church﻿—the *Vigiliae Mortuorum secundum Chorum Ecclesiae Maguntinae*.

I could not help thinking of the wild ritual of this work, and of its probable influence upon the hypochondriac, when, one evening, having informed me abruptly that the lady Madeline was no more, he stated his intention of preserving her corpse for a fortnight (previously to its final interment), in one of the numerous vaults within the main walls of the building. The worldly reason, however, assigned for this singular proceeding, was one which I did not feel at liberty to dispute. The brother had been led to his resolution (so he told me) by consideration of the unusual character of the malady of the deceased, of certain obtrusive and eager inquiries on the part of her medical men, and of the remote and exposed situation of the burial-ground of the family. I will not deny that when I called to mind the sinister countenance of the person whom I met upon the staircase, on the day of my arrival at the house, I had no desire to oppose what I regarded as at best but a harmless, and by no means an unnatural, precaution.

===Chinese===

我们的书——那些多年来构成病人精神生活不小一部分的书——可想而知，也同这幻影的气质严丝合缝。我们一起埋头苦读的书，诸如格雷塞的《维尔维与夏尔特勒》、马基雅维利的《贝尔弗戈》、斯威登堡的《天堂与地狱》、霍尔堡的《尼古拉斯·克里姆地下游记》、罗伯特·弗拉德、让·丹达热与德·拉·尚勃尔的《手相术》、蒂克的《驶向蔚蓝远方之旅》、康帕内拉的《太阳城》。他心爱的一部，是多明我会士埃伊梅里克·德·吉罗讷那部《异端裁判官指南》的小八开本；还有蓬波尼乌斯·梅拉书里写古非洲萨提尔与奥伊基潘的段落，厄舍一坐就是几个钟头，对着出神。不过他最大的乐趣，是捧读一部哥特体四开本的奇书——一部被遗忘教会的礼文——《美因茨教会圣咏之亡者夜祷》。一天傍晚，他突兀地告诉我玛德琳小姐已经不在了，并说定意要把她的遗体（在最终下葬之前）暂放在宅子主墙内的诸多地窖之一里，为期两周；这时，我不禁想到这部书里那些狂乱的仪轨，想到它们对这位忧郁症患者可能有的影响。不过，对这一奇特举动，他给出的一个世俗理由，也让我觉得不便争辩。做哥哥的（他这样告诉我）之所以下了这个决心，是考虑到死者病症的特殊性质，考虑到她的医生们那些咄咄逼人的急切查问，也考虑到家族墓地的位置偏远而暴露。我不否认，当我记起抵宅那天在楼梯上遇见的那张阴沉的脸，我实在无意反对这个我至多视为无害的、决非悖乎常情的预防措施。

===Original===

At the request of Usher, I personally aided him in the arrangements for the temporary entombment. The body having been encoffined, we two alone bore it to its rest. The vault in which we placed it (and which had been so long unopened that our torches, half smothered in its oppressive atmosphere, gave us little opportunity for investigation) was small, damp, and entirely without means of admission for light; lying, at great depth, immediately beneath that portion of the building in which was my own sleeping apartment. It had been used, apparently, in remote feudal times, for the worst purposes of a donjon-keep, and, in later days, as a place of deposit for powder, or some other highly combustible substance, as a portion of its floor, and the whole interior of a long archway through which we reached it, were carefully sheathed with copper. The door, of massive iron, had been, also, similarly protected. Its immense weight caused an unusually sharp grating sound, as it moved upon its hinges.

Having deposited our mournful burden upon tressels within this region of horror, we partially turned aside the yet unscrewed lid of the coffin, and looked upon the face of the tenant. A striking similitude between the brother and sister now first arrested my attention; and Usher, divining, perhaps, my thoughts, murmured out some few words from which I learned that the deceased and himself had been twins, and that sympathies of a scarcely intelligible nature had always existed between them. Our glances, however, rested not long upon the dead﻿—for we could not regard her unawed. The disease which had thus entombed the lady in the maturity of youth, had left, as usual in all maladies of a strictly cataleptical character, the mockery of a faint blush upon the bosom and the face, and that suspiciously lingering smile upon the lip which is so terrible in death. We replaced and screwed down the lid, and, having secured the door of iron, made our way, with toil, into the scarcely less gloomy apartments of the upper portion of the house.

===Chinese===

应厄舍之请，我亲自帮他操办了这暂时安放遗体的事宜。遗体入殓之后，只我们两人，把它抬去了安息之所。安放它的那座地窖（它久未开启，我们举的火把在那窒闷的空气里半灭不灭，使我们无从细察）又小又潮，且完全没有透光之处；它深藏在极深处，正在我寝室所在的那部分建筑的正下方。显然，在遥远的封建时代，它曾被用作主堡里最不祥的用途；近代则当作囤放火药或其他极易燃烧之物的库房——因为它的一部分地面，以及我们一路走进来的那条长拱道的整个内壁，都细细地包着铜皮。厚重的铁门也同样这般防护着。它在铰链上转动时，那庞大的重量磨出一声异常尖利的轧轧声。在这恐怖之域里，我们把悲哀的重负搁上木架，将那尚未旋紧的棺盖微微掀开，看了看躺着的人的脸。兄妹之间那惊人的相似，此刻第一次攫住了我的注意；厄舍或许猜到了我的心事，低声吐出几句话，我由此得知死者与他是孪生，而且他们之间一直存在一种近乎不可解的心灵感应。不过我们的目光没敢在死者身上久留——因为我们望着她，不能不生敬畏。这场把她盛年活埋的疾病，一如所有严格僵直症性的病症惯常所为，在她胸上与脸上留下一抹佯作浅红的嘲弄，唇上挂着一丝萦绕不去的可疑微笑——死亡之中它何其可怖。我们放回棺盖，旋紧螺钉，闩好铁门，然后费劲地摸索着，回到宅子上层那几乎同样阴郁的房间里去。

===Original===

And now, some days of bitter grief having elapsed, an observable change came over the features of the mental disorder of my friend. His ordinary manner had vanished. His ordinary occupations were neglected or forgotten. He roamed from chamber to chamber with hurried, unequal, and objectless step. The pallor of his countenance had assumed, if possible, a more ghastly hue﻿—but the luminousness of his eye had utterly gone out. The once occasional huskiness of his tone was heard no more; and a tremulous quaver, as if of extreme terror, habitually characterized his utterance. There were times, indeed, when I thought his unceasingly agitated mind was laboring with some oppressive secret, to divulge which he struggled for the necessary courage. At times, again, I was obliged to resolve all into the mere inexplicable vagaries of madness, for I beheld him gazing upon vacancy for long hours, in an attitude of the profoundest attention, as if listening to some imaginary sound. It was no wonder that his condition terrified﻿—that it infected me. I felt creeping upon me, by slow yet certain degrees, the wild influences of his own fantastic yet impressive superstitions.

===Chinese===

如今，惨痛的哀伤过去了几日，我朋友精神疾患的面貌上，起了一种显而易见的变化。他惯常的举止消失了。日常的事务也被抛置或遗忘。他脚步匆促、忽快忽慢、漫无目的，一间屋一间屋地游荡。他脸上的惨白，如果还能更甚的话，又添了几分死灰——可他眼中的光焰，却彻底熄灭了。从前偶或可闻的嘶哑嗓音，如今再听不见；一种发颤的、仿佛出于极怖的震颤，成了他说话的常态。确实，有些时候，我觉得他那无时不在激荡的心，正被某个沉重的秘密折磨着，他挣扎着想鼓起吐露它所必需的勇气。另一些时候，我又只得把这一切归为疯狂那无从解释的反复无常：我见他一连几个钟头凝望虚空，那姿态专注到极处，仿佛在倾听某种想象出来的声音。难怪他的状态骇人——难怪它感染了我。我觉得他那些狂幻而慑人的迷信，正缓慢却确凿地，一寸一寸爬上我的心头。

===Original===

It was, especially, upon retiring to bed late in the night of the seventh or eighth day after the placing of the lady Madeline within the donjon, that I experienced the full power of such feelings. Sleep came not near my couch﻿—while the hours waned and waned away. I struggled to reason off the nervousness which had dominion over me. I endeavored to believe that much, if not all of what I felt, was due to the bewildering influence of the gloomy furniture of the room﻿—of the dark and tattered draperies, which, tortured into motion by the breath of a rising tempest, swayed fitfully to and fro upon the walls, and rustled uneasily about the decorations of the bed. But my efforts were fruitless. An irrepressible tremor gradually pervaded my frame; and, at length, there sat upon my very heart an incubus of utterly causeless alarm. Shaking this off with a gasp and a struggle, I uplifted myself upon the pillows, and, peering earnestly within the intense darkness of the chamber, harkened﻿—I know not why, except that an instinctive spirit prompted me﻿—to certain low and indefinite sounds which came, through the pauses of the storm, at long intervals, I knew not whence. Overpowered by an intense sentiment of horror, unaccountable yet unendurable, I threw on my clothes with haste (for I felt that I should sleep no more during the night), and endeavored to arouse myself from the pitiable condition into which I had fallen, by pacing rapidly to and fro through the apartment.

I had taken but few turns in this manner, when a light step on an adjoining staircase arrested my attention. I presently recognised it as that of Usher. In an instant afterward he rapped, with a gentle touch, at my door, and entered, bearing a lamp. His countenance was, as usual, cadaverously wan﻿—but, moreover, there was a species of mad hilarity in his eyes﻿—an evidently restrained *hysteria* in his whole demeanor. His air appalled me﻿—but anything was preferable to the solitude which I had so long endured, and I even welcomed his presence as a relief.

“And you have not seen it?” he said abruptly, after having stared about him for some moments in silence﻿—“you have not then seen it?﻿—but, stay! you shall.” Thus speaking, and having carefully shaded his lamp, he hurried to one of the casements, and threw it freely open to the storm.

===Chinese===

尤其是在把玛德琳小姐安放进主堡地窖之后的第七天或第八天夜里，我上床就寝时，才充分领受了这类感觉的全部威力。睡意不肯近我的床——时辰一点一点消磨过去。我竭力想用道理驱散支配着我的神经紧张。我努力让自己相信：我所感到的，即便不是全部，也多半出自屋里阴森的家具那令人迷乱的影响——出自那些深色破烂的帷幔：它们被渐渐升起的暴风的气息折磨得动了起来，在墙上断断续续地前后摆动，绕着床的饰物窸窣作响，全无安宁。但我的努力全然无用。一阵压抑不住的战栗渐渐漫过我的全身；到末了，一团全然无端的惊悸，竟像梦魇一样坐上了我的心头。我喘着气，挣了一挣，把它甩脱，从枕上撑起身子，向屋内浓极的黑暗里细细张望，侧耳倾听——我不知为何，只觉有一种本能的冲动怂恿着我——去听某种低微而模糊的声响：它们穿过风暴的间歇，隔许久传来一阵，我不知来自何方。一种强烈的恐怖之感压倒了我，无端，却难耐；我慌忙披上衣裳（因为我觉得这一夜再也睡不着了），想在屋里疾步来回踱走，把自己从陷落其中的可悯境地拽起来。我这样来回没走几趟，相邻楼梯上一阵轻快的脚步声就攫住了我的注意。我立刻听出那是厄舍。转眼间，他轻轻叩了叩我的门，举着一盏灯走了进来。他的脸色一如平日，惨白如死灰——可他眼里还多了一层疯狂的欢快——整个举止间透着一种显然强自抑住的*歇斯底里*。他的神气叫我胆寒——可怎么也好过我久已忍受的孤独，我甚至把他的到来当作一种解脱来欢迎。「你还没见到它？」他默然向四下里瞪视了片刻，突兀地说——「这么说你还没见到？——可，慢着！你会见到的。」说着，他把灯仔细遮严，急步走向一扇窗，把它向风暴豁然洞开。

===Original===

The impetuous fury of the entering gust nearly lifted us from our feet. It was, indeed, a tempestuous yet sternly beautiful night, and one wildly singular in its terror and its beauty. A whirlwind had apparently collected its force in our vicinity; for there were frequent and violent alterations in the direction of the wind; and the exceeding density of the clouds (which hung so low as to press upon the turrets of the house) did not prevent our perceiving the lifelike velocity with which they flew careering from all points against each other, without passing away into the distance. I say that even their exceeding density did not prevent our perceiving this﻿—yet we had no glimpse of the moon or stars﻿—nor was there any flashing forth of the lightning. But the under surfaces of the huge masses of agitated vapor, as well as all terrestrial objects immediately around us, were glowing in the unnatural light of a faintly luminous and distinctly visible gaseous exhalation which hung about and enshrouded the mansion.

“You must not﻿—you shall not behold this!” said I, shudderingly, to Usher, as I led him, with a gentle violence, from the window to a seat. “These appearances, which bewilder you, are merely electrical phenomena not uncommon﻿—or it may be that they have their ghastly origin in the rank miasma of the tarn. Let us close this casement;﻿—the air is chilling and dangerous to your frame. Here is one of your favorite romances. I will read, and you shall listen;﻿—and so we will pass away this terrible night together.”

The antique volume which I had taken up was the *Mad Trist* of Sir Launcelot Canning; but I had called it a favorite of Usher’s more in sad jest than in earnest; for, in truth, there is little in its uncouth and unimaginative prolixity which could have had interest for the lofty and spiritual ideality of my friend. It was, however, the only book immediately at hand; and I indulged a vague hope that the excitement which now agitated the hypochondriac, might find relief (for the history of mental disorder is full of similar anomalies) even in the extremeness of the folly which I should read. Could I have judged, indeed, by the wild overstrained air of vivacity with which he harkened, or apparently harkened, to the words of the tale, I might well have congratulated myself upon the success of my design.

===Chinese===

闯进来的狂风其势汹汹，几乎把我们从地上掀起来。那确乎是一个风暴怒号、却又严峻得美丽的夜，一个恐怖与美俱极怪异的夜。旋风显然已在我们左近积足了势力：风频频改向，而且猛烈；云密到极点（低得直压在宅子的塔楼上），却挡不住我们看见它们从四面八方相互狂冲疾撞时那虎虎如生的速度——它们撞作一团，并不飘散远去。我说，连它们那极度的浓密都不能妨碍我们看到这景象——然而我们看不见月亮，也看不见星星——也没有闪电的迸现。但是，那一大团一大团翻腾水汽的底面，连同我们四周紧邻的地上万物，都泛着一种不自然的光——那是一层微微发亮、清晰可见的气状瘴霭，悬在宅子四周，把它裹在其中。「你不能——你不可看这个！」我打着颤对厄舍说，一面半是强扶半是拉地把他从窗边引到座位上。「这些叫你迷乱的景象，不过是并不罕见的电光现象罢了——要不然，便是从那小湖的浊瘴里升起的可怖之物。咱们把这窗关上；——寒气正砭骨，对你身子有害。喏，这是你心爱的一部传奇。我来念，你听着；——咱们就这样一起熬过这个可怕的夜。」我拿起的那部古书，是朗斯洛特·坎宁爵士的《疯狂的特里斯特》；我称它是厄舍的心爱之书，与其说当真，不如说是含哀的戏言；因为实情是，它那粗笨乏味、毫无想象力的冗长文字，实在没有什么能合得上我朋友那高迈空灵的理想气质。可它是手边唯一的一部书；我也姑且抱着一丝模糊的希望：眼下搅动这位忧郁症患者的兴奋，说不定能从我即将念出的极端愚蠢里寻得解脱（精神失常的病史里，这类反常之事比比皆是）。的确，倘若单凭他听故事时——或者表面听着故事时——那副狂乱而绷到极处的活泼劲儿来判断，我满可以庆幸自己计策得成了。

===Original===

I had arrived at that well-known portion of the story where Ethelred, the hero of the Trist, having sought in vain for peaceable admission into the dwelling of the hermit, proceeds to make good an entrance by force. Here, it will be remembered, the words of the narrative run thus:

“And Ethelred, who was by nature of a doughty heart, and who was now mighty withal, on account of the powerfulness of the wine which he had drunken, waited no longer to hold parley with the hermit, who, in sooth, was of an obstinate and maliceful turn, but, feeling the rain upon his shoulders, and fearing the rising of the tempest, uplifted his mace outright, and, with blows, made quickly room in the plankings of the door for his gauntleted hand; and now pulling therewith sturdily, he so cracked, and ripped, and tore all asunder, that the noise of the dry and hollow-sounding wood alarummed and reverberated throughout the forest.”

At the termination of this sentence I started, and for a moment, paused; for it appeared to me (although I at once concluded that my excited fancy had deceived me)﻿—it appeared to me that, from some very remote portion of the mansion, there came, indistinctly, to my ears, what might have been, in its exact similarity of character, the echo (but a stifled and dull one certainly) of the very cracking and ripping sound which Sir Launcelot had so particularly described. It was, beyond doubt, the coincidence alone which had arrested my attention; for, amid the rattling of the sashes of the casements, and the ordinary commingled noises of the still increasing storm, the sound, in itself, had nothing, surely, which should have interested or disturbed me. I continued the story:

“But the good champion Ethelred, now entering within the door, was sore enraged and amazed to perceive no signal of the maliceful hermit; but, in the stead thereof, a dragon of a scaly and prodigious demeanor, and of a fiery tongue, which sat in guard before a palace of gold, with a floor of silver; and upon the wall there hung a shield of shining brass with this legend enwritten﻿—

Who entereth herein, a conqueror hath bin;

Who slayeth the dragon, the shield he shall win;

===Chinese===

我念到了故事里尽人皆知的一段：特里斯特的主人公埃塞尔雷德，求和平进入隐士的居所而不得，便索性以武力闯入。这里，诸位当还记得，书中的文字是这样的：「且说埃塞尔雷德，天性便是一副骁勇的心肠，此刻又仗着饮下的烈酒之力，气壮万分，再不与那隐士多费唇舌——那隐士实属顽固恶毒之辈——他觉出肩头落雨，又惧风暴将起，索性抡起钉头锤，一顿猛砸，在门板上为戴盔的手砸出个孔来；随即抓紧使劲一拉，噼里啪啦，那干木空洞之声，直震得满林回响，惊动四野。」这句话念完，我吃了一惊，怔了片刻；因为在我看来（虽然我当即断定是亢奋的幻想骗了我）——在我看来，从宅子极远的某处，隐约传来我耳中的，似乎正是朗斯洛特爵士着力描写的那劈裂之声的回声（自然，是隔闷而低沉的），其性质分毫不差。毋庸置疑，单是这份巧合便攫住了我的注意；因为在那越刮越猛的风暴中，在窗框的格格声与种种混杂的声响之间，那声音本身，实在没有什么能引我留意、扰我心神的。我接着念故事：「但那好汉埃塞尔雷德进门之后，却见不到那恶隐士的半点踪影，不禁又惊又怒；出现在眼前的，是一条鳞甲峥嵘、气势骇人、口吐烈焰的巨龙，盘守在一座黄金宫殿之前，殿中铺着白银的地；墙上悬着一面亮铮铮的黄铜盾牌，上镌铭文——

进得此门者，乃是克胜之雄；
斩得此龙者，此盾归其手中；

===Original===

And Ethelred uplifted his mace, and struck upon the head of the dragon, which fell before him, and gave up his pesty breath, with a shriek so horrid and harsh, and withal so piercing, that Ethelred had fain to close his ears with his hands against the dreadful noise of it, the like whereof was never before heard.”

Here again I paused abruptly, and now with a feeling of wild amazement﻿—for there could be no doubt whatever that, in this instance, I did actually hear (although from what direction it proceeded I found it impossible to say) a low and apparently distant, but harsh, protracted, and most unusual screaming or grating sound﻿—the exact counterpart of what my fancy had already conjured up for the dragon’s unnatural shriek as described by the romancer.

Oppressed, as I certainly was, upon the occurrence of this second and most extraordinary coincidence, by a thousand conflicting sensations, in which wonder and extreme terror were predominant, I still retained sufficient presence of mind to avoid exciting, by any observation, the sensitive nervousness of my companion. I was by no means certain that he had noticed the sounds in question; although, assuredly, a strange alteration had, during the last few minutes, taken place in his demeanor. From a position fronting my own, he had gradually brought round his chair, so as to sit with his face to the door of the chamber; and thus I could but partially perceive his features, although I saw that his lips trembled as if he were murmuring inaudibly. His head had dropped upon his breast﻿—yet I knew that he was not asleep, from the wide and rigid opening of the eye as I caught a glance of it in profile. The motion of his body, too, was at variance with this idea﻿—for he rocked from side to side with a gentle yet constant and uniform sway. Having rapidly taken notice of all this, I resumed the narrative of Sir Launcelot, which thus proceeded:

===Chinese===

「埃塞尔雷德举起钉头锤，一锤打在龙头上；龙倒在他面前，发出一声厉叫，断送了它那瘟疫般的性命——那叫声何等可怖刺耳，又尖利穿心，埃塞尔雷德只得双手掩耳，抵挡那骇人的声浪，那是旷古未闻之声。」这里我又猛然停住，心中是一阵狂乱的惊愕——因为这一回，千真万确，我当真听见了（虽说从哪个方向传来，我全然说不上）一种低沉而显然遥远的、却刺耳、拖长、极端反常的尖啸或磨锉之声——同我方才为那传奇作家笔下巨龙的非自然厉叫所幻想出的，分毫不差。这第二桩、也是最非同寻常的一桩巧合发生时，我自然被千百种纷乱交战的感觉压着，其中惊异与极度的恐怖占了上风；但我仍保住了足够的心神，不吐一言，免得撩动我同伴敏感的神经。我绝不敢断定他注意到了那些声音；尽管就在方才那几分钟里，他的举止确实起了古怪的变化。他原本与我对面而坐，却渐渐把椅子挪转，变成脸朝着屋门的方向；因此我只能看见他面孔的一部分，虽然我看见他嘴唇颤动，仿佛在无声地喃喃低语。他的头已垂到胸前——然而我知道他没有睡着：我从侧面瞥见他的眼睛，睁得大大的，僵直不动。他身体的动作也与睡着之说相悖——他以一种轻柔却持续而均匀的摇晃，左右摇摆着。我迅速留意到这一切，便接着念朗斯洛特爵士的故事；故事是这样往下进行的：

===Original===

“And now, the champion, having escaped from the terrible fury of the dragon, bethinking himself of the brazen shield, and of the breaking up of the enchantment which was upon it, removed the carcass from out of the way before him, and approached valorously over the silver pavement of the castle to where the shield was upon the wall; which in sooth tarried not for his full coming, but fell down at his feet upon the silver floor, with a mighty great and terrible ringing sound.”

No sooner had these syllables passed my lips, than﻿—as if a shield of brass had indeed, at the moment, fallen heavily upon a floor of silver﻿—I became aware of a distinct, hollow, metallic, and clangorous, yet apparently muffled reverberation. Completely unnerved, I leaped to my feet; but the measured rocking movement of Usher was undisturbed. I rushed to the chair in which he sat. His eyes were bent fixedly before him, and throughout his whole countenance there reigned a stony rigidity. But, as I placed my hand upon his shoulder, there came a strong shudder over his whole person; a sickly smile quivered about his lips; and I saw that he spoke in a low, hurried, and gibbering murmur, as if unconscious of my presence. Bending closely over him, I at length drank in the hideous import of his words.

===Chinese===

「如今，那勇士既已逃出巨龙的可怕凶焰，心里记挂着那面铜盾，记挂着破解附在盾上的魔法，便把龙的尸体从面前挪开，勇猛地踏过城堡的白银地面，走向墙上悬盾之处；那盾却不等他走到近前，便带着一声洪大可怖的铿锵之音，落在他脚边的银地上。」这几个字才离我的唇——就像一面铜盾当真在那一刻重重落在银地之上似的——我立时察觉一阵清晰、空洞、金属性、铿然作响、却又显然隔着什么的回荡。我心力俱溃，一跃而起；可厄舍那有节奏的摇晃纹丝未乱。我冲到他坐的椅子前。他双眼直勾勾望着前面，整张脸上凝着一种石头的僵硬。可是，当我的手按上他的肩，他整个人猛地一阵强颤；一丝病态的微笑在他唇边抽动；我看见他正低声、急促、含混不清地咕哝着什么，仿佛全然不觉我在跟前。我俯身凑近他，终于听清了他话中骇人的含义。

===Original===

“Not hear it?﻿—yes, I hear it, and *have* heard it. Long﻿—long﻿—long﻿—many minutes, many hours, many days, have I heard it﻿—yet I dared not﻿—oh, pity me, miserable wretch that I am!﻿—I dared not﻿—I *dared* not speak! *We have put her living in the tomb!* Said I not that my senses were acute? I *now* tell you that I heard her first feeble movements in the hollow coffin. I heard them﻿—many, many days ago﻿—yet I dared not﻿—*I dared not speak!* And now﻿—tonight﻿—Ethelred﻿—ha! ha!﻿—the breaking of the hermit’s door, and the death-cry of the dragon, and the clangor of the shield!﻿—say, rather, the rending of her coffin, and the grating of the iron hinges of her prison, and her struggles within the coppered archway of the vault! Oh whither shall I fly? Will she not be here anon? Is she not hurrying to upbraid me for my haste? Have I not heard her footstep on the stair? Do I not distinguish that heavy and horrible beating of her heart? Madman!”﻿—here he sprang furiously to his feet, and shrieked out his syllables, as if in the effort he were giving up his soul﻿—“*Madman! I tell you that she now stands without the door!*”

As if in the superhuman energy of his utterance there had been found the potency of a spell﻿—the huge antique panels to which the speaker pointed, threw slowly back, upon the instant, their ponderous and ebony jaws. It was the work of the rushing gust﻿—but then without those doors there *did* stand the lofty and enshrouded figure of the lady Madeline of Usher. There was blood upon her white robes, and the evidence of some bitter struggle upon every portion of her emaciated frame. For a moment she remained trembling and reeling to and fro upon the threshold﻿—then, with a low moaning cry, fell heavily inward upon the person of her brother, and in her violent and now final death-agonies, bore him to the floor a corpse, and a victim to the terrors he had anticipated.

===Chinese===

「没听见？——不，我听见了，而且*早就*听见了。很久——很久——很久——许多分钟，许多钟头，许多天，我一直听见——可我不敢——哦，怜悯我吧，我这可悲的可怜虫！——我不敢——我*不敢*说！*我们把她活生生放进了坟墓！*我不是说过我感官敏锐吗？我*现在*告诉你，她在那空洞的棺材里最初的微弱动静，我听见了。我听见了——许多许多天以前——可我不敢——*我不敢说！*而现在——今夜——埃塞尔雷德——哈！哈！——隐士门的碎裂，龙的死嚎，盾的铿锵！——不如说，是棺材的迸裂，是她牢狱铁铰链的轧轧，是她在那包铜地窖拱道里的挣扎！哦，我往哪里逃？她不是马上就要到吗？她不是正急急赶来，责骂我的性急吗？我没有听见她在楼梯上的脚步吗？我没有分辨出她那沉重可怕的心的跳动吗？疯子！」——说到这里，他狂怒地一跃而起，尖声喊出这几个字，仿佛这一声要把他的魂魄都喊出去——「*疯子！我告诉你，她现在就站在门外！*」仿佛他话语里那超人的元力中真藏着符咒的效力——说话人手指着的那两扇高大古老的门板，顷刻间，缓缓张开了它们乌黑沉重的巨口。那是疾风所作——可门外，也确实立着厄舍家的玛德琳小姐那裹着衾衣的高高身影。她白袍上带着血，她那枯瘦躯体的每一处，都留着一场惨烈挣扎的痕迹。有一刻，她在门槛上颤着、摇晃着——然后，一声低低的呜咽，重重地向内扑倒在她哥哥身上；在她那狂暴的、也是最后的死亡挣扎中，把他拖倒在地板上——他成了一具尸首，成了他所预惧的那些恐怖的牺牲品。

===Original===

From that chamber, and from that mansion, I fled aghast. The storm was still abroad in all its wrath as I found myself crossing the old causeway. Suddenly there shot along the path a wild light, and I turned to see whence a gleam so unusual could have issued; for the vast house and its shadows were alone behind me. The radiance was that of the full, setting, and bloodred moon, which now shone vividly through that once barely-discernible fissure, of which I have before spoken as extending from the roof of the building, in a zigzag direction, to the base. While I gazed, this fissure rapidly widened﻿—there came a fierce breath of the whirlwind﻿—the entire orb of the satellite burst at once upon my sight﻿—my brain reeled as I saw the mighty walls rushing asunder﻿—there was a long tumultuous shouting sound like the voice of a thousand waters﻿—and the deep and dank tarn at my feet closed sullenly and silently over the fragments of the “*House of Usher*.”

===Chinese===

从那间屋子，从那座宅邸，我魂飞魄散地逃了出来。当我发觉自己正跨过那道旧堤时，风暴仍在四处发泄着全部的狂怒。忽然，一道野异的光沿着堤道疾射而来，我回头去看这异样的光究竟从何而出；因为身后只有那片巨宅和它的暗影。那光，来自一轮圆圆满满、正在西沉、血红血红的月亮；此刻，它正透过那道先前几乎无法察觉的裂缝，鲜亮地照出来——我先前说过，那裂缝从楼顶曲曲折折直裂到墙基。我正望着，那裂缝迅速扩开——旋风送来一股猛烈的气息——那轮满月整个儿迸现在我的眼前——当我看见巍峨的墙轰然崩裂、向两侧奔溃时，我的头脑晕眩了——一声悠长喧腾的呼啸腾起，如千道流水齐吼——而我脚边那幽深湿冷的小湖，阴沉沉、静悄悄地，在「厄舍府」的断壁残垣上合拢了。

## William Wilson / 威廉·威尔逊
===Original===

What say of it? what say of **conscience** grim,

That spectre in my path?

> Chamberlayne’s *Pharronida*

Let me call myself, for the present, William Wilson. The fair page now lying before me need not be sullied with my real appellation. This has been already too much an object for the scorn﻿—for the horror﻿—for the detestation of my race. To the uttermost regions of the globe have not the indignant winds bruited its unparalleled infamy? Oh, outcast of all outcasts most abandoned!﻿—to the earth art thou not forever dead? to its honors, to its flowers, to its golden aspirations?﻿—and a cloud, dense, dismal, and limitless, does it not hang eternally between thy hopes and heaven?

I would not, if I could, here or today, embody a record of my later years of unspeakable misery, and unpardonable crime. This epoch﻿—these later years﻿—took unto themselves a sudden elevation in turpitude, whose origin alone it is my present purpose to assign. Men usually grow base by degrees. From me, in an instant, all virtue dropped bodily as a mantle. From comparatively trivial wickedness I passed, with the stride of a giant, into more than the enormities of an Elah-Gabalus. What chance﻿—what one event brought this evil thing to pass, bear with me while I relate. Death approaches; and the shadow which foreruns him has thrown a softening influence over my spirit. I long, in passing through the dim valley, for the sympathy﻿—I had nearly said for the pity﻿—of my fellow men. I would fain have them believe that I have been, in some measure, the slave of circumstances beyond human control. I would wish them to seek out for me, in the details I am about to give, some little oasis of *fatality* amid a wilderness of error. I would have them allow﻿—what they cannot refrain from allowing﻿—that, although temptation may have erewhile existed as great, man was never *thus*, at least, tempted before﻿—certainly, never *thus* fell. And is it therefore that he has never thus suffered? Have I not indeed been living in a dream? And am I not now dying a victim to the horror and the mystery of the wildest of all sublunary visions?

===Chinese===

你们对它说什么？对那冷峻的**良心**说什么，

我路上的那个幽灵？

——钱伯莱恩《法罗尼达》（*Pharronida*）

暂且，容我自称威廉·威尔逊（William Wilson）。此刻摊在我面前的这一页净纸，不必让我的真名玷污。那名字早已遭受太多我的同类的蔑视——恐惧——憎恶。在世界的极远处，愤怒的风不是还传扬着它无与伦比的丑名吗？哦，弃儿中的弃儿，最被弃绝的一个！——你不是对这尘世永远死了吗？对它的荣誉，它的花朵，它金色的憧憬？——而一朵浓密、阴惨、无边无际的云，不是永远悬在你的希望与上天之间吗？

我不愿意——即便能够——在今天在这里，把我后来那些年不可言说的苦难和不可饶恕的罪行写成实录。这个时期——这些后来的年月——在堕落的陡坡上骤然拔起，而它的源头，正是我此刻的目的所要指明的。人通常是逐渐变坏的。从我身上，一切德性却在顷刻之间整个脱落，像一件斗篷。我从相对微不足道的恶行，以巨人的跨步，直入胜过埃拉加巴卢斯（Elah-Gabalus）的穷凶极恶。是什么机缘——什么单独的事件造成这件恶事，请容忍我讲来。死亡临近了；先行于他的阴影，已给我的精神投下一种柔化的影响。我在穿过这昏暗幽谷的时候，渴望着——我险些说了怜悯——我同类人的同情。我巴不得他们相信：我在某种程度上，是人力无法驾驭的环境的奴隶。我但愿他们在我即将给出的细节里，在错误的荒野中，为我寻出一小块*宿命*的绿洲。我但愿他们承认——他们不由得不承认的——诱惑从前或许同样巨大，但人从来不曾*这样*、至少不曾被这样诱惑过——自然，也从不曾*这样*堕落过。那么，是不是正因如此他才不曾这样受苦？难道我不是当真活在一梦之中？而此刻，我不是正作为一切人间幻象中最狂野的那一场的恐怖与神秘的一个牺牲品，垂死着吗？

===Original===

I am the descendant of a race whose imaginative and easily excitable temperament has at all times rendered them remarkable; and, in my earliest infancy, I gave evidence of having fully inherited the family character. As I advanced in years it was more strongly developed; becoming, for many reasons, a cause of serious disquietude to my friends, and of positive injury to myself. I grew self-willed, addicted to the wildest caprices, and a prey to the most ungovernable passions. Weak-minded, and beset with constitutional infirmities akin to my own, my parents could do but little to check the evil propensities which distinguished me. Some feeble and ill-directed efforts resulted in complete failure on their part, and, of course, in total triumph on mine. Thenceforward my voice was a household law; and at an age when few children have abandoned their leading-strings, I was left to the guidance of my own will, and became, in all but name, the master of my own actions.

My earliest recollections of a school-life, are connected with a large, rambling, Elizabethan house, in a misty-looking village of England, where were a vast number of gigantic and gnarled trees, and where all the houses were excessively ancient. In truth, it was a dreamlike and spirit-soothing place, that venerable old town. At this moment, in fancy, I feel the refreshing chilliness of its deeply-shadowed avenues, inhale the fragrance of its thousand shrubberies, and thrill anew with undefinable delight, at the deep hollow note of the church-bell, breaking, each hour, with sullen and sudden roar, upon the stillness of the dusky atmosphere in which the fretted Gothic steeple lay imbedded and asleep.

It gives me, perhaps, as much of pleasure as I can now in any manner experience, to dwell upon minute recollections of the school and its concerns. Steeped in misery as I am﻿—misery, alas! only too real﻿—I shall be pardoned for seeking relief, however slight and temporary, in the weakness of a few rambling details. These, moreover, utterly trivial, and even ridiculous in themselves, assume, to my fancy, adventitious importance, as connected with a period and a locality when and where I recognise the first ambiguous monitions of the destiny which afterwards so fully overshadowed me. Let me then remember.

===Chinese===

我是一个种族的后裔，他们那富于想象、容易激动的气质，历来使他们卓然出众；而在最早的孩提时代，我便显出十足承袭了家族性格的证据。年岁渐长，这天性愈发强烈地发展；出于种种缘故，成了我的亲友们严重的忧心，也成了我自己确凿的损害。我变得刚愎任性，沉溺于最狂放的怪想，受制于最难驾驭的激情。我的父母心智软弱，又被与我相类的体质上的毛病缠身，对我那些出格的恶习所能做的管束微乎其微。他们几番软弱无方的努力归于彻底失败，自然，便换得我的全胜。从那时起，我的声音便是一家之法；在极少几个孩子脱离襁褓牵带的年纪，我便被交给自己的意志去引导，除了名义之外，成了自己行动的主人。

我对学生时代最早的记忆，连着英国一座雾气迷蒙的村庄里一幢庞大蜿蜒的伊丽莎白时代的宅子，那里有许多虬曲的巨树，所有的房屋都异常古老。实在说，那座古老可敬的老镇，是一个如梦的、安魂的地方。此刻，我在想象里还感到它深荫夹道沁人的凉意，嗅到千百丛灌木的芬芳，并在教堂钟深沉空洞的鸣响里，重新激起说不清的欢愉——那钟声每一小时一次，阴郁而骤然地爆发，打进昏暗大气间的寂静里；那镌花哥特式的尖塔，正嵌睡在其中。

把学校及其中种种琐事细细追忆，或许给了我如今以任何方式所能体验的最大乐趣。我浸在苦难里——唉！苦得太真——为求解脱，哪怕些微而短暂，在几段闲琐细节的软弱里寻求安慰，该得宽恕。况且这些琐事本身极其无谓，甚至可笑，在我的幻想里却平添了额外的分量：连着那个时期、那个地方——我在其中认出日后如此全然笼罩我的命运最早那些含混先兆的时期与地方。容我记起它们吧。

===Original===

The house, I have said, was old and irregular. The grounds were extensive, and a high and solid brick wall, topped with a bed of mortar and broken glass, encompassed the whole. This prison-like rampart formed the limit of our domain; beyond it we saw but thrice a week﻿—once every Saturday afternoon, when, attended by two ushers, we were permitted to take brief walks in a body through some of the neighbouring fields﻿—and twice during Sunday, when we were paraded in the same formal manner to the morning and evening service in the one church of the village. Of this church the principal of our school was pastor. With how deep a spirit of wonder and perplexity was I wont to regard him from our remote pew in the gallery, as, with step solemn and slow, he ascended the pulpit! This reverend man, with countenance so demurely benign, with robes so glossy and so clerically flowing, with wig so minutely powdered, so rigid and so vast﻿—could this be he who, of late, with sour visage, and in snuffy habiliments, administered, ferule in hand, the Draconian laws of the academy? Oh, gigantic paradox, too utterly monstrous for solution!

At an angle of the ponderous wall frowned a more ponderous gate. It was riveted and studded with iron bolts, and surmounted with jagged iron spikes. What impressions of deep awe did it inspire! It was never opened save for the three periodical egressions and ingressions already mentioned; then, in every creak of its mighty hinges, we found a plenitude of mystery﻿—a world of matter for solemn remark, or for more solemn meditation.

The extensive enclosure was irregular in form, having many capacious recesses. Of these, three or four of the largest constituted the playground. It was level, and covered with fine hard gravel. I well remember it had no trees, nor benches, nor anything similar within it. Of course it was in the rear of the house. In front lay a small parterre, planted with box and other shrubs, but through this sacred division we passed only upon rare occasions indeed﻿—such as a first advent to school or final departure thence, or perhaps, when a parent or friend having called for us, we joyfully took our way home for the Christmas or Midsummer holidays.

===Chinese===

宅子，我说过，又老又不规整。园地广阔，一堵高而坚实的砖墙，墙头抹一层灰浆、嵌着碎玻璃，围住全部。这道监狱式的壁垒便是我们领地的边界；墙外我们一周只见三次——每星期六下午一次，由两位助教押着，获准集体在邻近的几片田野里散一会儿步——星期日两次，同式的列队，去村里唯一的教堂做早晚礼拜。这教堂的本堂牧师，正是我们学校的主事人。我惯常怀着何等深沉的惊异与困惑，从楼上我们那偏远的座席望着他，一步一步庄严而迟缓地登上讲坛！这位可敬的人，面貌如此端庄慈祥，袍服如此光洁、如此具有教士的飘逸，假发扑粉扑得如此精细、如此板正、如此庞大——这可能就是不久前那个板着面孔、穿着鼻烟渍斑斑的衣装、手里拿着戒尺、执行学塾严刑峻法的人吗？哦，巨大的悖论，怪异到无从解答！

沉重的墙的一角，皱着一扇更沉重的门。门上铆着钉、缀着铁钉，门顶竖着参差的铁刺。它给人的敬畏何等深刻！除了前面说过的三次定期的出与进，它从不开启；那时，它巨大合页的每一声吱呀，在我们听来都满是神秘——满是值得郑重谈论、或更郑重沉思的素材。

宽阔的围场形状不规整，有许多宽大的凹处。其中三四处最大的构成了操场。操场地平，铺着细硬的砾石。我记得清楚，场内没有树，没有长凳，也没有任何类似的东西。它自然在宅后。宅前铺着一小方花坛，种着黄杨和其他灌木；但只有在极难得的场合，我们才经过那片神圣的地界——比如初到学校或最终离校，或者，当父母或朋友来接我们，我们欢欢喜喜回家过圣诞节或仲夏节假的时候。

===Original===

But the house!﻿—how quaint an old building was this!﻿—to me how veritably a palace of enchantment! There was really no end to its windings﻿—to its incomprehensible subdivisions. It was difficult, at any given time, to say with certainty upon which of its two stories one happened to be. From each room to every other there were sure to be found three or four steps either in ascent or descent. Then the lateral branches were innumerable﻿—inconceivable﻿—and so returning in upon themselves, that our most exact ideas in regard to the whole mansion were not very far different from those with which we pondered upon infinity. During the five years of my residence here, I was never able to ascertain with precision, in what remote locality lay the little sleeping apartment assigned to myself and some eighteen or twenty other scholars.

The schoolroom was the largest in the house﻿—I could not help thinking, in the world. It was very long, narrow, and dismally low, with pointed Gothic windows and a ceiling of oak. In a remote and terror-inspiring angle was a square enclosure of eight or ten feet, comprising the sanctum, “during hours,” of our principal, the Reverend Dr. Bransby. It was a solid structure, with massy door, sooner than open which in the absence of the “Dominie,” we would all have willingly perished by the peine forte et dure. In other angles were two other similar boxes, far less reverenced, indeed, but still greatly matters of awe. One of these was the pulpit of the “classical” usher, one of the “English and mathematical.” Interspersed about the room, crossing and recrossing in endless irregularity, were innumerable benches and desks, black, ancient, and timeworn, piled desperately with much-bethumbed books, and so beseamed with initial letters, names at full length, grotesque figures, and other multiplied efforts of the knife, as to have entirely lost what little of original form might have been their portion in days long departed. A huge bucket with water stood at one extremity of the room, and a clock of stupendous dimensions at the other.

===Chinese===

可是这宅子！——多古怪的一座老房子！——在我眼里实实在在是一座魔宫！它的曲折没有尽头——它的不可理解的分隔没有尽头。任何时候都难说准自己身在它两层楼的哪一层。从每一间屋子到另外每一间，必有三级四级台阶，或升或降。侧翼的岔道无穷无尽——不可设想——又各自折回自身，以致我们对于全宅最精确的观念，同我们沉思无穷时的观念相去不远。在这里住了五年，我始终未能确知，分给我和另外十八九二十个同学的宿舍，究竟藏在什么偏远的角落。

教室是宅里最大的屋子——我不由得想，也是世上最大的。很长，很窄，低得阴惨，嵌着尖拱哥特窗，天花板是橡木的。在偏远的、令人生畏的一角，有一个八或十英尺见方的围栏，构成我们的主事人布兰斯比（Bransby）博士牧师「课时」内的圣所。那是一座结实的构筑，门很厚重；与其在「塾师」不在时打开它，我们宁愿全体甘受强制重刑（peine forte et dure）而死。其他角落里另有两座类似的围箱，尊敬当然少得多，却仍然极令人生畏。一座是「古典」助教的讲坛，一座是「英文与数学」助教的。教室里散布着无数长凳和书桌，纵横交错、毫无规律，黑色，古老，磨旧，绝望地堆满翻得起了毛边的书，又给刻满姓名首字母、全名、怪诞的图形和刀子的其他种种成绩，以致早年间或许分给它们的那么一点点原形，已经荡然无存。屋子一头立着一只带水的大桶，另一头是一座尺寸惊人的钟。

===Original===

Encompassed by the massy walls of this venerable academy, I passed, yet not in tedium or disgust, the years of the third lustrum of my life. The teeming brain of childhood requires no external world of incident to occupy or amuse it; and the apparently dismal monotony of a school was replete with more intense excitement than my riper youth has derived from luxury, or my full manhood from crime. Yet I must believe that my first mental development had in it much of the uncommon﻿—even much of the outré. Upon mankind at large the events of very early existence rarely leave in mature age any definite impression. All is gray shadow﻿—a weak and irregular remembrance﻿—an indistinct regathering of feeble pleasures and phantasmagoric pains. With me this is not so. In childhood I must have felt with the energy of a man what I now find stamped upon memory in lines as vivid, as deep, and as durable as the exergues of the Carthaginian medals.

Yet in fact﻿—in the fact of the world’s view﻿—how little was there to remember! The morning’s awakening, the nightly summons to bed; the connings, the recitations; the periodical half-holidays, and perambulations; the playground, with its broils, its pastimes, its intrigues;﻿—these, by a mental sorcery long forgotten, were made to involve a wilderness of sensation, a world of rich incident, an universe of varied emotion, of excitement the most passionate and spirit-stirring. “Oh, le bon temps, que ce siècle de fer!”

===Chinese===

围在这座可敬学塾的重墙之内，我度过了我人生的第三个五年，却并不厌倦，也不厌恶。孩童那丰饶的头脑不需要外部事件的世界去占用或取悦；学校表面阴郁的单调，所充满的强烈兴奋，比我较成熟的少年从奢华里得到的、比我成年从罪行里得到的更多。然而我必须相信，我最初的心智发展里有不少非常——甚至不少古怪。对全人类而言，极幼年时代的事件很少在成年留下任何确定的印象。一切都是灰影——微弱而不规则的追忆——对薄弱欢乐和幻影痛苦的模糊重聚。于我却不然。在孩提时代，我必是以成人的力量感受了如今印在记忆里的东西，那些印痕像迦太基钱币边缘上的铭文一样鲜明、一样深、一样持久。

可是事实上——按世人所见的事实——可记的又何其少！晨起，夜间的就寝召唤；背诵，诵读；定期的半日假和散步；操场，连同它的吵闹、它的消遣、它的勾心斗角；——这些，借一种早已忘却的心灵魔法，竟被织成一片感觉的荒野、一个富饶事件的世界、一个诸种情绪的宇宙，兴奋最炽烈、最动人心魄。「啊，多好的时光，这铁的世纪！」

===Original===

In truth, the ardor, the enthusiasm, and the imperiousness of my disposition, soon rendered me a marked character among my schoolmates, and by slow, but natural gradations, gave me an ascendancy over all not greatly older than myself;﻿—over all with a single exception. This exception was found in the person of a scholar, who, although no relation, bore the same christian and surname as myself;﻿—a circumstance, in fact, little remarkable; for, notwithstanding a noble descent, mine was one of those everyday appellations which seem, by prescriptive right, to have been, time out of mind, the common property of the mob. In this narrative I have therefore designated myself as William Wilson﻿—a fictitious title not very dissimilar to the real. My namesake alone, of those who in school phraseology constituted “our set,” presumed to compete with me in the studies of the class﻿—in the sports and broils of the playground﻿—to refuse implicit belief in my assertions, and submission to my will﻿—indeed, to interfere with my arbitrary dictation in any respect whatsoever. If there is on earth a supreme and unqualified despotism, it is the despotism of a mastermind in boyhood over the less energetic spirits of its companions.

===Chinese===

实在说，我性情的热情、炽烈与专横，很快使我在同学中间成了一个瞩目的人物，并借缓慢而自然的阶梯，给了我一种对一切不比我大许多的人的支配权；——对一切，单单一个人除外。这个例外见于一个同学身上，他虽非亲族，却与我同名同姓；——这情形实在不算稀奇；因为，尽管出身名门，我的名字属于那类司空见惯的称呼，仿佛凭着惯例的权利，自古以来便是平民的公共财产。因此在这篇叙述里，我把自己题作威廉·威尔逊——一个与真名相去不远的假名。在学校用语里构成「我们一伙」的那些人当中，唯有这位同名人，敢于在课业上同我争衡——在操场的游戏和吵闹中同我争衡——拒绝绝对相信我的断言、服从我的意志——的确，在任何方面干扰我的专横指挥。倘若世上有什么至高无上、毫无限度的专制，那便是少年时代一个主宰心灵的头脑，对其同伴们较为孱弱的灵魂的专制。

===Original===

Wilson’s rebellion was to me a source of the greatest embarrassment; the more so as, in spite of the bravado with which in public I made a point of treating him and his pretensions, I secretly felt that I feared him, and could not help thinking the equality which he maintained so easily with myself, a proof of his true superiority; since not to be overcome cost me a perpetual struggle. Yet this superiority﻿—even this equality﻿—was in truth acknowledged by no one but myself; our associates, by some unaccountable blindness, seemed not even to suspect it. Indeed, his competition, his resistance, and especially his impertinent and dogged interference with my purposes, were not more pointed than private. He appeared to be destitute alike of the ambition which urged, and of the passionate energy of mind which enabled me to excel.
