In his rivalry he might have been supposed actuated solely by a whimsical desire to thwart, astonish, or mortify myself; although there were times when I could not help observing, with a feeling made up of wonder, abasement, and pique, that he mingled with his injuries, his insults, or his contradictions, a certain most inappropriate, and assuredly most unwelcome *affectionateness* of manner. I could only conceive this singular behavior to arise from a consummate self-conceit assuming the vulgar airs of patronage and protection.

Perhaps it was this latter trait in Wilson’s conduct, conjoined with our identity of name, and the mere accident of our having entered the school upon the same day, which set afloat the notion that we were brothers, among the senior classes in the academy. These do not usually inquire with much strictness into the affairs of their juniors. I have before said, or should have said, that Wilson was not, in the most remote degree, connected with my family. But assuredly if we *had* been brothers we must have been twins; for, after leaving Dr. Bransby’s, I casually learned that my namesake was born on the nineteenth of January, 1813﻿—and this is a somewhat remarkable coincidence; for the day is precisely that of my own nativity.

===Chinese===

威尔逊的反抗，是我极大的窘迫之源；尤其因为，尽管当众我摆足架势蔑视他和他的自命，暗中我却感到自己怕他，并且不由得把他这样轻易与我保持的平等，看作他真正优越的证明；因为不被压倒，在我须付出永久的挣扎。然而这份优越——甚至这份平等——实在除我自己无人承认；我们的同伴们，出于某种莫名的盲视，似乎连疑心也不疑。的确，他的竞争，他的抵抗，尤其是他对我意图那种无礼而固执的干扰，不但不张扬，反而全是私下的。他似乎全然缺乏那种鞭策我的野心，也缺乏使我得以出众的那种炽烈的心智能量。在他的争衡里，或许可以设想，驱使他的单单是一种古怪的欲望：挫败我，惊骇我，羞辱我；虽然有些时候，我怀着惊异、屈辱与恼恨交织的心情，不免注意到，他在他的伤害、侮辱或顶撞里，掺着某种极不合适、也确实极不受欢迎的*亲爱*神情。我只能设想这古怪的行为出于一种十足的自负，摆出庇护与保护的老俗气派。

或许正是威尔逊品行中后一种特点，加上我们名字的同一，加上我们同一天入学的纯然巧合，在学塾高年级里浮起了我们是兄弟的说法。高年级通常并不严格究问低年级的事务。我前面说过，或者本该说过：威尔逊与我的家庭毫无瓜葛。但可以断言，倘若我们*当真*是兄弟，我们必定是孪生；因为离开布兰斯比博士的学塾之后，我偶然得知我的同名人生于1813年1月19日——这是一个相当可观的巧合；因为那一天正是我自己的生日。

===Original===

It may seem strange that in spite of the continual anxiety occasioned me by the rivalry of Wilson, and his intolerable spirit of contradiction, I could not bring myself to hate him altogether. We had, to be sure, nearly every day a quarrel in which, yielding me publicly the palm of victory, he, in some manner, contrived to make me feel that it was he who had deserved it; yet a sense of pride on my part, and a veritable dignity on his own, kept us always upon what are called “speaking terms,” while there were many points of strong congeniality in our tempers, operating to awake me in a sentiment which our position alone, perhaps, prevented from ripening into friendship. It is difficult, indeed, to define, or even to describe, my real feelings towards him. They formed a motley and heterogeneous admixture;﻿—some petulant animosity, which was not yet hatred, some esteem, more respect, much fear, with a world of uneasy curiosity. To the moralist it will be unnecessary to say, in addition, that Wilson and myself were the most inseparable of companions.

It was no doubt the anomalous state of affairs existing between us, which turned all my attacks upon him, (and they were many, either open or covert) into the channel of banter or practical joke (giving pain while assuming the aspect of mere fun) rather than into a more serious and determined hostility. But my endeavours on this head were by no means uniformly successful, even when my plans were the most wittily concocted; for my namesake had much about him, in character, of that unassuming and quiet austerity which, while enjoying the poignancy of its own jokes, has no heel of Achilles in itself, and absolutely refuses to be laughed at. I could find, indeed, but one vulnerable point, and that, lying in a personal peculiarity, arising, perhaps, from constitutional disease, would have been spared by any antagonist less at his wit’s end than myself;﻿—my rival had a weakness in the faucal or guttural organs, which precluded him from raising his voice at any time *above a very low whisper*. Of this defect I did not fail to take what poor advantage lay in my power.

===Chinese===

说来也许奇怪：尽管威尔逊的争衡和他那不可容忍的顶撞脾气不断给我焦虑，我却不能使自己全然恨他。诚然，我们几乎天天有一场争吵，在争吵里，他当众把胜利的桂冠让给我，却总设法叫我感到受之有愧的是他；但我一方的骄傲，和他一方真正的尊严，使我们始终保持在所谓「见面说话」的关系上，同时我们性情里有好些强烈的相投之点，起着作用，在我心里唤起一种情感——或许单单是我们的处境阻止它成熟为友谊而已。实在难于界定，甚至难于描述我对他的真实感情。那是一种斑驳杂糅的混合；——几分浮躁的敌意，还不是恨；几分器重，更多的尊敬，许多畏惧，加上一大片不安的好奇。对道德家，此外无须再说：威尔逊和我，是同伴中最不可分的一对。

无疑，是我们之间存在的这种反常局面，把我对他的一切攻击（攻击很多，或公开或隐蔽）引到了嘲弄或恶作剧的渠道里（以纯粹取乐的面目给以疼痛），而没有引向更严肃、更坚决的敌意。但我在这方面的努力绝不全然成功，即便我的计划编排得最巧妙；因为我的同名人性格里有许多那种谦和安静的古板——自己享用自己玩笑的辛辣，自身却没有阿喀琉斯之踵，绝对拒绝被人取笑。的确，我找得出的弱点只有一个；那弱点出于一种个人的特异，或许源于体质上的疾病，任何对手只要不像我这样技穷，原该放过它不碰；——我的对手咽喉发音器官有缺陷，任何时候都无法把声音提到*很低的耳语之上*。这缺陷，我尽了我可怜的本事加以利用。

===Original===

Wilson’s retaliations in kind were many; and there was one form of his practical wit that disturbed me beyond measure. How his sagacity first discovered at all that so petty a thing would vex me, is a question I never could solve; but, having discovered, he habitually practised the annoyance. I had always felt aversion to my uncourtly patronymic, and its very common, if not plebeian praenomen. The words were venom in my ears; and when, upon the day of my arrival, a second William Wilson came also to the academy, I felt angry with him for bearing the name, and doubly disgusted with the name because a stranger bore it, who would be the cause of its twofold repetition, who would be constantly in my presence, and whose concerns, in the ordinary routine of the school business, must inevitably, on account of the detestable coincidence, be often confounded with my own.

The feeling of vexation thus engendered grew stronger with every circumstance tending to show resemblance, moral or physical, between my rival and myself. I had not then discovered the remarkable fact that we were of the same age; but I saw that we were of the same height, and I perceived that we were even singularly alike in general contour of person and outline of feature. I was galled, too, by the rumor touching a relationship, which had grown current in the upper forms. In a word, nothing could more seriously disturb me (although I scrupulously concealed such disturbance), than any allusion to a similarity of mind, person, or condition existing between us. But, in truth, I had no reason to believe that (with the exception of the matter of relationship, and in the case of Wilson himself), this similarity had ever been made a subject of comment, or even observed at all by our schoolfellows. That *he* observed it in all its bearings, and as fixedly as I, was apparent; but that he could discover in such circumstances so fruitful a field of annoyance, can only be attributed, as I said before, to his more than ordinary penetration.

===Chinese===

威尔逊以其人之道还治的次数很多；他有一种实际的机锋，搅得我不得安宁，无以复加。他的精明最初究竟怎样发现这么一件小事会惹恼我，是我始终解不开的问题；但一经发现，他便惯常练习这桩骚扰。我一向厌恶我这土气的姓氏，也厌恶它那极其寻常、近乎市井的名。这两个词在我耳中便是毒液；而当我入学那天，第二个威廉·威尔逊也来到学塾，我便对他顶着这名字生气，对这名字加倍嫌恶，因为一个陌生人顶着它，此人将成为它双重重复的原因，将时时在我眼前，而他因这可憎的巧合，在学校日常事务的寻常轮转里，必然时时与我的事务混作一团。

这样生出的恼怒，随着每一件显示我的对手与我之间精神或形貌相似的事而增强。那时我尚未发现我们是同岁这一显著事实；但我看见我们身高相同，并且察觉我们在体形轮廓、五官线条上甚至出奇地相像。上年级里流传的那种关于亲缘的谣言，也刺痛着我。一句话，任何暗示我们之间存在心智、形体或处境的相似的话，最能严重地搅扰我（虽然我小心翼翼地遮掩这种搅扰）。但实在说，我没有任何理由相信（亲缘一节除外，威尔逊本人亦除外），这相似曾被我们的同学谈论过，甚至被他们注意过。*他*从一切方面注意它、像我一样定定地注意它，是显然的；但他竟能在这种情形里发现一片如此丰饶的骚扰的沃土，只能如我前面所说，归因于他超乎寻常的洞察。

===Original===

His cue, which was to perfect an imitation of myself, lay both in words and in actions; and most admirably did he play his part. My dress it was an easy matter to copy; my gait and general manner were, without difficulty, appropriated; in spite of his constitutional defect, even my voice did not escape him. My louder tones were, of course, unattempted, but then the key﻿—it was identical; *and his singular whisper, it grew the very echo of my own*.

How greatly this most exquisite portraiture harassed me (for it could not justly be termed a caricature), I will not now venture to describe. I had but one consolation﻿—in the fact that the imitation, apparently, was noticed by myself alone, and that I had to endure only the knowing and strangely sarcastic smiles of my namesake himself. Satisfied with having produced in my bosom the intended effect, he seemed to chuckle in secret over the sting he had inflicted, and was characteristically disregardful of the public applause which the success of his witty endeavours might have so easily elicited. That the school, indeed, did not feel his design, perceive its accomplishment, and participate in his sneer, was, for many anxious months, a riddle I could not resolve. Perhaps the *gradation* of his copy rendered it not so readily perceptible; or, more possibly, I owed my security to the master air of the copyist, who, disdaining the letter (which in a painting is all the obtuse can see), gave but the full spirit of his original for my individual contemplation and chagrin.

===Chinese===

他的拿手好戏是把我模仿到惟妙惟肖，言语举止一概在内；他把他那角色演得妙到极点。我的衣着容易照样；我的步态和整个举止，毫不费力地被他挪用；尽管体质的缺陷，连我的嗓音也没能逃过他。我较高的音调自然不去尝试；可是那调门——一模一样；*而他那奇特的耳语，长成了我自己耳语的回声*。

这幅最精妙的写照怎样地折磨我（因为它无法公正地称作漫画），我此刻不敢描绘。我只有一种安慰——在于这样的情形：那模仿显然只被我自己注意到，我只须忍受我同名人自己那会心而怪诞地讥诮的微笑。他在我胸中造成了预期的效果便已满足，似乎在暗自为刺出的那一针窃喜，并且很有性格地无视他那机智的努力的成功本可轻易博得的公众喝彩。学校当真不曾觉察他的设计、看出他的完成、分受他的冷笑——有好多个月，这是我解不开的一个谜。也许他那摹本的*层层递进*使它不易觉察；或者，更可能的是，我的安全得归功于摹写者的师法：他鄙视字面（字面在画里是迟钝的眼睛所见的全部），只为我的独自观照与苦恼，给出他原本的全部精神。

===Original===

I have already more than once spoken of the disgusting air of patronage which he assumed toward me, and of his frequent officious interference with my will. This interference often took the ungracious character of advice; advice not openly given, but hinted or insinuated. I received it with a repugnance which gained strength as I grew in years. Yet, at this distant day, let me do him the simple justice to acknowledge that I can recall no occasion when the suggestions of my rival were on the side of those errors or follies so usual to his immature age and seeming inexperience; that his moral sense, at least, if not his general talents and worldly wisdom, was far keener than my own; and that I might, today, have been a better, and thus a happier man, had I less frequently rejected the counsels embodied in those meaning whispers which I then but too cordially hated and too bitterly despised.

As it was, I at length grew restive in the extreme under his distasteful supervision, and daily resented more and more openly what I considered his intolerable arrogance. I have said that, in the first years of our connection as schoolmates, my feelings in regard to him might have been easily ripened into friendship; but, in the latter months of my residence at the academy, although the intrusion of his ordinary manner had, beyond doubt, in some measure, abated, my sentiments, in nearly similar proportion, partook very much of positive hatred. Upon one occasion he saw this, I think, and afterwards avoided, or made a show of avoiding me.

===Chinese===

我已经不止一次说过他对我摆出的那副令人作呕的庇护架子，和他对我意志频频多事的干涉。这种干涉往往取忠告的不受欢迎的形态；忠告不公开给出，而是暗示，或旁敲侧击。我怀着一种随年岁增长的嫌恶接受它。然而，在这遥远的日子，让我给他一点朴素的公道：我记不起有任何一次，我对手的建议是站在他那不成熟的年纪、他那貌似缺乏历练通常犯的那些过失或愚行一边的；他的道德感——即便不是他的一般才能和处世智慧——远比我的锐利；倘若我较少拒绝那些凝在意味深长的耳语里的忠告——那些我当年怀着何等热烈的憎恨、何等苦涩的轻蔑的耳语——我今天原可能是一个更好的人，因而也更幸福。

可是事实上，我到底在他那令人不快的监护下变得烦躁到极点，日益公开地愤懑于我所认为的他那不可容忍的傲慢。我说过，在我们同学之谊的最初几年里，我对他的感情原可能轻易成熟为友谊；但在我寄居学塾的最后几个月里，虽然他寻常姿态的侵扰无疑已在某种程度上收敛，我的情绪却以几乎相似的比例，染上十足的正恨。有一个场合，我想他看出了这个，此后便回避我，或做出回避的样子。

===Original===

It was about the same period, if I remember aright, that, in an altercation of violence with him, in which he was more than usually thrown off his guard, and spoke and acted with an openness of demeanor rather foreign to his nature, I discovered, or fancied I discovered, in his accent, his air, and general appearance, a something which first startled, and then deeply interested me, by bringing to mind dim visions of my earliest infancy﻿—wild, confused and thronging memories of a time when memory herself was yet unborn. I cannot better describe the sensation which oppressed me than by saying that I could with difficulty shake off the belief of my having been acquainted with the being who stood before me, at some epoch very long ago﻿—some point of the past even infinitely remote. The delusion, however, faded rapidly as it came; and I mention it at all but to define the day of the last conversation I there held with my singular namesake.

The huge old house, with its countless subdivisions, had several large chambers communicating with each other, where slept the greater number of the students. There were, however (as must necessarily happen in a building so awkwardly planned), many little nooks or recesses, the odds and ends of the structure; and these the economic ingenuity of Dr. Bransby had also fitted up as dormitories; although, being the merest closets, they were capable of accommodating but a single individual. One of these small apartments was occupied by Wilson.

===Chinese===

大约在同一时期，如果我记得不错，在同他一场激烈的争执里——他比平常更失了常态，言谈举止带出一种与他本性相当疏远的坦率——我在他的口音、神气、总体的外貌里，发现或者自以为发现了一点什么，它先叫我吃了一惊，继而深深引起我的兴趣，因为它唤起我最早婴孩时代的朦胧幻象——狂乱、纷乱、纷至沓来的记忆，关于记忆本身尚未诞生的时代。压制着我的这种感觉，我无法描述得更贴切，只好说：我很难摆脱这样一个信念——站在我面前的这个存在，在很久很久以前的某个时代，某个甚至无限遥远的过去之点上，我曾与之相识。然而这错觉随生随灭，转瞬即逝；我提起它，不过是借此划定我在那里同我古怪的同名人最后一次交谈的日子。

那座无数分隔的巨大老宅，有几间互相连通的大屋，多数学生睡在那里。然而（在一座规划得如此笨拙的建筑里必然如此）有许多小角落、小凹处，构造的零头碎脑；布兰斯比博士经济的巧思也把它们布置成了寝室；虽是彻底的壁橱，却只能容纳单独一个人。这些小间之一，由威尔逊住着。

===Original===

One night, about the close of my fifth year at the school, and immediately after the altercation just mentioned, finding everyone wrapped in sleep, I arose from bed, and, lamp in hand, stole through a wilderness of narrow passages from my own bedroom to that of my rival. I had long been plotting one of those ill-natured pieces of practical wit at his expense in which I had hitherto been so uniformly unsuccessful. It was my intention, now, to put my scheme in operation, and I resolved to make him feel the whole extent of the malice with which I was imbued. Having reached his closet, I noiselessly entered, leaving the lamp, with a shade over it, on the outside. I advanced a step, and listened to the sound of his tranquil breathing. Assured of his being asleep, I returned, took the light, and with it again approached the bed. Close curtains were around it, which, in the prosecution of my plan, I slowly and quietly withdrew, when the bright rays fell vividly upon the sleeper, and my eyes, at the same moment, upon his countenance. I looked;﻿—and a numbness, an iciness of feeling instantly pervaded my frame. My breast heaved, my knees tottered, my whole spirit became possessed with an objectless yet intolerable horror. Gasping for breath, I lowered the lamp in still nearer proximity to the face. Were these﻿—*these* the lineaments of William Wilson? I saw, indeed, that they were his, but I shook as if with a fit of the ague in fancying they were not. What *was* there about them to confound me in this manner? I gazed;﻿—while my brain reeled with a multitude of incoherent thoughts. Not thus he appeared﻿—assuredly not *thus*﻿—in the vivacity of his waking hours. The same name! the same contour of person! the same day of arrival at the academy! And then his dogged and meaningless imitation of my gait, my voice, my habits, and my manner! Was it, in truth, within the bounds of human possibility, that *what I now saw* was the result, merely, of the habitual practice of this sarcastic imitation? Awestricken, and with a creeping shudder, I extinguished the lamp, passed silently from the chamber, and left, at once, the halls of that old academy, never to enter them again.

===Chinese===

一晚，约在我到校第五年将尽、恰恰在刚才说的那场争执之后，见人人裹在睡眠里，我下了床，提着灯，穿过一片窄巷的荒野，从自己的寝室偷进对手的寝室。我谋划以他为牺牲的一桩恶意恶作剧，已谋划许久，而至今一贯失败。此刻我打算付诸实行，并决意叫他感到灌注在我身上的恶意的全部分量。到了他的壁橱，我悄无声息进去，把灯罩上罩子留在外面。我进了一步，听他平静的呼吸。确信他睡着，我回身取了灯，再走近床前。床四面垂着严实的帐子；我按计划的进行，缓缓而轻轻地拉开，明亮的灯光便鲜明地照在睡着的人身上，而我的眼睛也同时照在他的脸上。我看了；——一阵麻木，一种冰冷的战栗，霎时浸透我的身躯。我的胸膛起伏，我的膝盖打颤，我整个的灵魂被一种无目的然而不堪忍受的恐怖攫住。喘着气，我把灯放得更近，凑近那张脸。这——*这*是威廉·威尔逊的五官吗？我确实看出是他的，但我抖得像打摆子，总觉得不是。这里面究竟有什么，这样把我搅乱？我凝视着；——头脑在无数不相连贯的思绪里晕眩。他醒着的活泼时辰里不是这样——确实不*是*这样的相貌。同样的名字！同样的体形轮廓！同一天到学塾报到！然后还有他对我步态、嗓音、习惯、举止那固执而毫无意义的模仿！*我此刻看见的*，当真在人类可能的疆界之内，仅仅是这讥诮模仿的惯常练习的结果吗？惊骇之下，带着一阵爬行的寒颤，我灭掉灯，悄悄走出那间屋子，随即离开了那座老学塾的厅堂，从此再不踏进。

===Original===

After a lapse of some months, spent at home in mere idleness, I found myself a student at Eton. The brief interval had been sufficient to enfeeble my remembrance of the events at Dr. Bransby’s, or at least to effect a material change in the nature of the feelings with which I remembered them. The truth﻿—the tragedy﻿—of the drama was no more. I could now find room to doubt the evidence of my senses; and seldom called up the subject at all but with wonder at extent of human credulity, and a smile at the vivid force of the imagination which I hereditarily possessed. Neither was this species of scepticism likely to be diminished by the character of the life I led at Eton. The vortex of thoughtless folly into which I there so immediately and so recklessly plunged, washed away all but the froth of my past hours, engulfed at once every solid or serious impression, and left to memory only the veriest levities of a former existence.

I do not wish, however, to trace the course of my miserable profligacy here﻿—a profligacy which set at defiance the laws, while it eluded the vigilance of the institution. Three years of folly, passed without profit, had but given me rooted habits of vice, and added, in a somewhat unusual degree, to my bodily stature, when, after a week of soulless dissipation, I invited a small party of the most dissolute students to a secret carousal in my chambers. We met at a late hour of the night; for our debaucheries were to be faithfully protracted until morning. The wine flowed freely, and there were not wanting other and perhaps more dangerous seductions; so that the gray dawn had already faintly appeared in the east, while our delirious extravagance was at its height. Madly flushed with cards and intoxication, I was in the act of insisting upon a toast of more than wonted profanity, when my attention was suddenly diverted by the violent, although partial unclosing of the door of the apartment, and by the eager voice of a servant from without. He said that some person, apparently in great haste, demanded to speak with me in the hall.

===Chinese===

在家虚度了几个月之后，我发觉自己成了伊顿的学生。短短的间隔已足以削弱我对布兰斯比学塾诸事件的记忆，或至少使我回忆它们时的感情性质发生实质的变化。那出戏的真相——悲剧——不再存在。如今我有了余地怀疑我的感官的证据；我极少重提那桩事，提起来也只惊叹人类轻信的程度之广，讪笑我承袭而来的想象力的鲜明之力。我在伊顿过的生活的性质，也不太可能削弱这类怀疑。我在那里一头扎进的、不计后果的愚行的漩涡，把我过去时日的渣滓以外的一切冲刷净尽，把每个坚实或严肃的印象一举吞没，只留给记忆前生那点最不足道的轻浮。

然而我不想在这里追述我可怜的放荡的历程——那放荡藐视学校的法规，同时躲过学校的督察。三年虚掷的愚行，没有给我益处，只给了我扎了根的恶习，并在我身体的个头上添了颇不寻常的高度；这时，在一周没有灵魂的放纵之后，我邀了一小伙最荒唐的同学，到我的住所里秘密痛饮。我们深夜聚齐；因为我们的纵酒必须忠实延续到早晨。酒畅流着，也不缺别的也许更危险的诱惑；以致灰白的曙光已隐约出现在东方，我们疯狂的奢华正到顶点。我在纸牌与醉意的疯狂涨红里，正坚持一句比平素更亵渎的祝酒，忽然注意力被岔开：屋门猛烈地、虽然只是局部地打开，门外传来仆人急切的声音。他说有个人，样子极匆忙，要求在大厅里同我说话。

===Original===

Wildly excited with wine, the unexpected interruption rather delighted than surprised me. I staggered forward at once, and a few steps brought me to the vestibule of the building. In this low and small room there hung no lamp; and now no light at all was admitted, save that of the exceedingly feeble dawn which made its way through the semicircular window. As I put my foot over the threshold, I became aware of the figure of a youth about my own height, and habited in a white kerseymere morning frock, cut in the novel fashion of the one I myself wore at the moment. This the faint light enabled me to perceive; but the features of his face I could not distinguish. Upon my entering he strode hurriedly up to me, and, seizing me by the arm with a gesture of petulant impatience, whispered the words “William Wilson” in my ear.

I grew perfectly sober in an instant.

There was that in the manner of the stranger, and in the tremulous shake of his uplifted finger, as he held it between my eyes and the light, which filled me with unqualified amazement; but it was not this which had so violently moved me. It was the pregnancy of solemn admonition in the singular, low, hissing utterance; and, above all, it was the character, the tone, *the key*, of those few, simple, and familiar, yet *whispered* syllables, which came with a thousand thronging memories of bygone days, and struck upon my soul with the shock of a galvanic battery. Ere I could recover the use of my senses he was gone.

===Chinese===

酒的狂烈兴奋之下，这意外的打断与其说使我吃惊，不如说使我高兴。我立刻踉跄向前，几步便到了门厅。这间低矮的小屋里没有挂灯；此刻也毫无光亮进来，只有极微弱的曙光，从半圆的窗挤进来。我的脚踏过门槛时，我觉察到一个青年的人影，约我自己那么高，穿一件白色克尔赛梅呢晨衣，剪裁的时新样式正是我此刻穿着的那一件。微光使我得以看出这些；但他的面貌我却分辨不出。我一进门，他急忙大步走到我跟前，以一阵浮躁的不耐的手势攥住我的胳膊，把「威廉·威尔逊」几个字耳语进我的耳朵。

顷刻之间，我完全醒了酒。

那陌生人的神情里，以及他举起的指头在我两眼与灯光之间颤抖地一晃里，有某种东西使我充满十足的惊愕；但如此猛烈撼动我的并不是这个。是那奇特、低微、嘶嘶的吐音里庄严告诫的分量；而尤其，是那几个简单、寻常、然而*耳语*出来的音节的特征、腔调、*调门*——它们带着千百个既往时日纷至沓来的记忆，以电瓶般的震荡击在我的灵魂上。我还没来得及恢复感官的运用，他已经去了。

===Original===

Although this event failed not of a vivid effect upon my disordered imagination, yet was it evanescent as vivid. For some weeks, indeed, I busied myself in earnest inquiry, or was wrapped in a cloud of morbid speculation. I did not pretend to disguise from my perception the identity of the singular individual who thus perseveringly interfered with my affairs, and harassed me with his insinuated counsel. But who and what was this Wilson?﻿—and whence came he?﻿—and what were his purposes? Upon neither of these points could I be satisfied; merely ascertaining, in regard to him, that a sudden accident in his family had caused his removal from Dr. Bransby’s academy on the afternoon of the day in which I myself had eloped. But in a brief period I ceased to think upon the subject; my attention being all absorbed in a contemplated departure for Oxford. Thither I soon went; the uncalculating vanity of my parents furnishing me with an outfit and annual establishment, which would enable me to indulge at will in the luxury already so dear to my heart﻿—to vie in profuseness of expenditure with the haughtiest heirs of the wealthiest earldoms in Great Britain.

Excited by such appliances to vice, my constitutional temperament broke forth with redoubled ardor, and I spurned even the common restraints of decency in the mad infatuation of my revels. But it were absurd to pause in the detail of my extravagance. Let it suffice, that among spendthrifts I out-Heroded Herod, and that, giving name to a multitude of novel follies, I added no brief appendix to the long catalogue of vices then usual in the most dissolute university of Europe.

===Chinese===

虽然这件事在我纷乱的想象上不曾缺少鲜明的效果，但它鲜明一如它的短暂。有几个星期，我果然忙于恳切的查问，或者裹在病态思虑的云里。我不假装在我自己的知觉前遮掩这个奇特人物——他这样执拗地干预我的事务、用他旁敲侧击的忠告搅扰我——的同一性。但这威尔逊是谁、是什么？——他从哪里来？——他的目的是什么？这几点的任何一点我都无法满足；关于他，我仅仅查明：他家一场突然的变故，使他在我自己私逃那天的下午，从布兰斯比博士的学塾离去了。但很短一段时间后我便不再想这件事；我的注意力全被一次计划的牛津之行吸住。我不久便去了；我父母不计后果的虚荣供给我一套行头和一年的开销，足以使我随心所欲地沉溺于已经对我心弥足珍贵的奢华——在花销的阔绰上同大不列颠最富有的伯爵领地最骄傲的继承人们一较短长。

被这样的作恶的凭据撩拨着，我体质里的气质以加倍的炽烈迸发出来，在纵酒的疯狂痴迷里，我连体面的一般约束也踩在脚下。然而在我的奢华的细节上停留是可笑的。说这么一句尽够了：在挥霍者中间，我把希律王也比了下去；并且给一大群新式的愚行命名，在欧洲最荒淫的大学当时通行的恶行的长目里，添了一篇不短的附录。

===Original===

It could hardly be credited, however, that I had, even here, so utterly fallen from the gentlemanly estate, as to seek acquaintance with the vilest arts of the gambler by profession, and, having become an adept in his despicable science, to practise it habitually as a means of increasing my already enormous income at the expense of the weak-minded among my fellow-collegians. Such, nevertheless, was the fact. And the very enormity of this offence against all manly and honourable sentiment proved, beyond doubt, the main if not the sole reason of the impunity with which it was committed. Who, indeed, among my most abandoned associates, would not rather have disputed the clearest evidence of his senses, than have suspected of such courses, the gay, the frank, the generous William Wilson﻿—the noblest and most liberal commoner at Oxford﻿—him whose follies (said his parasites) were but the follies of youth and unbridled fancy﻿—whose errors but inimitable whim﻿—whose darkest vice but a careless and dashing extravagance?

I had been now two years successfully busied in this way, when there came to the university a young parvenu nobleman, Glendinning﻿—rich, said report, as Herodes Atticus﻿—his riches, too, as easily acquired. I soon found him of weak intellect, and, of course, marked him as a fitting subject for my skill. I frequently engaged him in play, and contrived, with the gambler’s usual art, to let him win considerable sums, the more effectually to entangle him in my snares. At length, my schemes being ripe, I met him (with the full intention that this meeting should be final and decisive) at the chambers of a fellow-commoner (Mr. Preston), equally intimate with both, but who, to do him justice, entertained not even a remote suspicion of my design. To give to this a better coloring, I had contrived to have assembled a party of some eight or ten, and was solicitously careful that the introduction of cards should appear accidental, and originate in the proposal of my contemplated dupe himself. To be brief upon a vile topic, none of the low finesse was omitted, so customary upon similar occasions that it is a just matter for wonder how any are still found so besotted as to fall its victim.

===Chinese===

然而，几乎叫人不能相信：我竟在这里也全然堕落到这样的地步，去结交职业赌徒的那些最卑污的技艺，并且在他那可鄙的科学里成了行家之后，惯常地操持它，作为从我的大学同伴中间心智软弱者身上增大我已极庞大的进项的手段。然而事实如此。而这桩对一切男子气与荣誉感的罪的极大本身，无疑证明了它得以不受惩罚的主要的——即便不是唯一的——原因。的确，在我那些最堕落的伙伴中间，谁肯宁可争议他感官最明白的证据，而疑心到这样行径的头上——快活的、坦率的、慷慨的威廉·威尔逊头上——牛津最高贵最豪爽的公费生头上——他的愚行（他的寄生虫们说）不过是青春和不羁幻想的愚行——他的过失不过是无从模仿的怪想——他最暗的恶习不过是大手大脚、满不在乎的挥霍？

我照这样顺利地干了两年，这时大学里来了一位年轻的暴发户贵族，格伦丁宁（Glendinning）——据传说富得像希罗德·阿提库斯（Herodes Atticus），而这财富得来也同样容易。我很快发现他智力孱弱，自然把他标作我的技艺合宜的对象。我频频同他赌，并且借赌棍惯常的手段，设法让他赢进可观的数目，以便更有效地把他缠进我的罗网。终于，我的盘算成熟，我在一位公费生同学（普雷斯顿（Preston）先生）的住所里同他会局——那人与两人都同样亲厚，但凭良心说，他连我设计的影子也没有疑到。为给这设计添一层更好的颜色，我设法聚拢了八九个人的一伙，并且极其小心地使纸牌的引入显得出于偶然，出自我的预期的受骗者本人的提议。这桩卑污的话题不必细说：类似的场合惯用的种种低级手腕一概未曾省略，以致竟是一件正当令人惊异的事：居然还有人蠢到落进它的牺牲。

===Original===

We had protracted our sitting far into the night, and I had at length effected the manoeuvre of getting Glendinning as my sole antagonist. The game, too, was my favorite écarté! The rest of the company, interested in the extent of our play, had abandoned their own cards, and were standing around us as spectators. The parvenu, who had been induced by my artifices in the early part of the evening, to drink deeply, now shuffled, dealt, or played, with a wild nervousness of manner for which his intoxication, I thought, might partially, but could not altogether account. In a very short period he had become my debtor to a large amount, when, having taken a long draught of port, he did precisely what I had been coolly anticipating﻿—he proposed to double our already extravagant stakes. With a well-feigned show of reluctance, and not until after my repeated refusal had seduced him into some angry words which gave a color of pique to my compliance, did I finally comply. The result, of course, did but prove how entirely the prey was in my toils: in less than an hour he had quadrupled his debt. For some time his countenance had been losing the florid tinge lent it by the wine; but now, to my astonishment, I perceived that it had grown to a pallor truly fearful. I say to my astonishment. Glendinning had been represented to my eager inquiries as immeasurably wealthy; and the sums which he had as yet lost, although in themselves vast, could not, I supposed, very seriously annoy, much less so violently affect him. That he was overcome by the wine just swallowed, was the idea which most readily presented itself; and, rather with a view to the preservation of my own character in the eyes of my associates, than from any less interested motive, I was about to insist, peremptorily, upon a discontinuance of the play, when some expressions at my elbow from among the company, and an ejaculation evincing utter despair on the part of Glendinning, gave me to understand that I had effected his total ruin under circumstances which, rendering him an object for the pity of all, should have protected him from the ill offices even of a fiend.

===Chinese===

我们把局拖到深夜，我终于演成了让格伦丁宁单独做我的对手的那一手。牌也是我的心爱——埃卡泰（écarté）！其余的人，被我们赌注的规模勾起兴趣，丢开自己的牌，围拢来作观客。那位暴发户，晚上早些时候被我的手段灌了大量酒，如今发牌、洗牌、出牌，手式里带一种狂乱的紧张，我以为他的醉意可以部分地、却不能全部地说明。很短时间他已欠下我一大笔数目，这时他灌下满满一杯波尔图酒，做的恰恰是我冷冷料定的事——提议把我们已经荒唐的赌注加倍。我摆出以假乱真的勉强，直到我屡次的拒绝把他诱出几句恼怒的话、给我的应允添上一层赌气的色彩之后，才终于应允。结果自然只证明猎物全然在我的罗网里：不到一小时，他的债务翻了四倍。有一阵子他的脸色一直在失去酒借给它的那层红晕；而此刻，令我惊异的是，我察觉它已长成一种真正骇人的苍白。我说令我惊异。我热切的查问所得的报告说格伦丁宁富得无可计量；而他到那时为止输掉的数目，虽然本身巨大，我以为本不能很严重地搅扰他，更不用说这样剧烈地震动他。他被刚灌下的酒压倒了——这是最先现出来的念头；于是，与其说出于任何较少自利的动机，毋宁为了在同伴们眼里保全我自己的体面，我正要断然坚持停局，这时我臂肘边人群里的一些言语，和格伦丁宁一声显出彻底绝望的惊呼，使我明白：我已经在这样一些情形下造成了他全盘的毁灭——那些情形使他成了众人怜悯的对象，本该保护他不受哪怕恶鬼的恶手。

===Original===

What now might have been my conduct it is difficult to say. The pitiable condition of my dupe had thrown an air of embarrassed gloom over all; and, for some moments, a profound silence was maintained, during which I could not help feeling my cheeks tingle with the many burning glances of scorn or reproach cast upon me by the less abandoned of the party. I will even own that an intolerable weight of anxiety was for a brief instant lifted from my bosom by the sudden and extraordinary interruption which ensued. The wide, heavy folding doors of the apartment were all at once thrown open, to their full extent, with a vigorous and rushing impetuosity that extinguished, as if by magic, every candle in the room. Their light, in dying, enabled us just to perceive that a stranger had entered, about my own height, and closely muffled in a cloak. The darkness, however, was now total; and we could only *feel* that he was standing in our midst. Before any one of us could recover from the extreme astonishment into which this rudeness had thrown all, we heard the voice of the intruder.

“Gentlemen,” he said, in a low, distinct, and never-to-be-forgotten *whisper* which thrilled to the very marrow of my bones, “Gentlemen, I make no apology for this behaviour, because in thus behaving, I am but fulfilling a duty. You are, beyond doubt, uninformed of the true character of the person who has tonight won at écarté a large sum of money from Lord Glendinning. I will therefore put you upon an expeditious and decisive plan of obtaining this very necessary information. Please to examine, at your leisure, the inner linings of the cuff of his left sleeve, and the several little packages which may be found in the somewhat capacious pockets of his embroidered morning wrapper.”

===Chinese===

此刻我本会怎样行事，难说。我的受骗者那可怜的处境给一切罩上一层尴尬的阴郁；有片刻，一种深沉的沉默保持着，沉默里我不由得感到两颊火辣辣的，被那一伙里较未堕落的人掷到我身上来的那许多灼人的轻蔑或责难的目光。我甚至承认，接踵而来的那突然而非常的打断，把一副不堪忍受的焦虑的重担，从我的胸口卸下了短短一瞬。屋子那些宽大的、沉重的折叠门，霎时以一股猛冲的蛮力开到全幅，像魔法一样熄灭了屋里每支蜡烛。它们的光在熄灭时使我们恰好看出：一个陌生人进来了，约我自己的高度，斗篷裹得严严实实。然而黑暗此刻全然；我们只能*感到*他站在我们中间。我们任何一人还没从这场粗暴投下的极端惊愕里恢复过来，我们听见了闯入者的声音。

「先生们，」他说，用一种低微、清晰、永世难忘的*耳语*——那耳语一直震到我的骨髓，「先生们，我为这举动不辩解，因为这样举动，我不过尽一分责任。你们无疑还不知道今晚在埃卡泰牌上从格伦丁宁勋爵那里赢去一大笔钱的这个人真是什么货色。因此我要教你们一个迅速而决定性的办法，去取得这份十分必要的情报。请诸位得便时查看他左袖口里面的衬里，以及在他那件刺绣晨袍颇为宽大的口袋里可以找到的几个小包。」

===Original===

While he spoke, so profound was the stillness that one might have heard a pin drop upon the floor. In ceasing, he departed at once, and as abruptly as he had entered. Can I﻿—shall I describe my sensations? Must I say that I felt all the horrors of the damned? Most assuredly I had little time given for reflection. Many hands roughly seized me upon the spot, and lights were immediately reprocured. A search ensued. In the lining of my sleeve were found all the court cards essential in écarté, and, in the pockets of my wrapper, a number of packs, facsimiles of those used at our sittings, with the single exception that mine were of the species called, technically, *arrondees*; the honours being slightly convex at the ends, the lower cards slightly convex at the sides. In this disposition, the dupe who cuts, as customary, at the length of the pack, will invariably find that he cuts his antagonist an honor; while the gambler, cutting at the breadth, will, as certainly, cut nothing for his victim which may count in the records of the game.

Any burst of indignation upon this discovery would have affected me less than the silent contempt, or the sarcastic composure, with which it was received.

“Mr. Wilson,” said our host, stooping to remove from beneath his feet an exceedingly luxurious cloak of rare furs, “Mr. Wilson, this is your property.” (The weather was cold; and, upon quitting my own room, I had thrown a cloak over my dressing wrapper, putting it off upon reaching the scene of play.) “I presume it is supererogatory to seek here (eyeing the folds of the garment with a bitter smile) for any farther evidence of your skill. Indeed, we have had enough. You will see the necessity, I hope, of quitting Oxford﻿—at all events, of quitting instantly my chambers.”

===Chinese===

他说话时，屋里静到一个人可以听见一枚针落在地板上。说完，他立刻离去，同他进来一样突兀。我能否——我该不该描述我的感觉？我必须说我感到了被罚入地狱者的全部恐怖吗？的确，我几乎没有获准反省的时间。许多只手当场粗鲁地抓住我，灯烛立刻重新取来。一场搜查接踵而至。在我袖子的衬里，搜出了埃卡泰牌所必需的全部花牌；在我晨袍的口袋里，搜出好几副牌，同我们局上用的那几副一模一样，唯一的例外是我的这些属于技术上称作圆角牌（arrondees）的一类：花牌牌头两端微微凸起，下牌两侧微微凸起。这样布置之下，受骗的人照惯例从牌的长边起牌，就必然给对手起出一张花牌；而赌棍从牌的宽边起牌，也就必然给他的牺牲起不出任何在牌局的记录里算数的牌。

这一发现上任何一阵义愤的爆发，都不会像它所受的这种沉默的轻蔑，或讥诮的镇定那样影响我。

「威尔逊先生，」我们的主人说，弯腰从脚下拾起一件极其华贵的稀珍毛皮斗篷，「威尔逊先生，这是您的财产。」（天气冷；我离开自己房间时在晨袍外面罩了斗篷，到赌局场所便脱下了。）「我想在这里再找您技艺的进一步证据（他苦笑着盯住那件衣裳的褶襞），是多余的。的确，我们领教够了。我希望您看得出必要的结论：离开牛津——无论如何，立刻离开我的住所。」

===Original===

Abased, humbled to the dust as I then was, it is probable that I should have resented this galling language by immediate personal violence, had not my whole attention been at the moment arrested by a fact of the most startling character. The cloak which I had worn was of a rare description of fur; how rare, how extravagantly costly, I shall not venture to say. Its fashion, too, was of my own fantastic invention; for I was fastidious to an absurd degree of coxcombry, in matters of this frivolous nature. When, therefore, Mr. Preston reached me that which he had picked up upon the floor, and near the folding doors of the apartment, it was with an astonishment nearly bordering upon terror, that I perceived my own already hanging on my arm (where I had no doubt unwittingly placed it), and that the one presented me was but its exact counterpart in every, in even the minutest possible particular. The singular being who had so disastrously exposed me, had been muffled, I remembered, in a cloak; and none had been worn at all by any of the members of our party with the exception of myself. Retaining some presence of mind, I took the one offered me by Preston; placed it, unnoticed, over my own; left the apartment with a resolute scowl of defiance; and, next morning ere dawn of day, commenced a hurried journey from Oxford to the continent, in a perfect agony of horror and of shame.

*I fled in vain.* My evil destiny pursued me as if in exultation, and proved, indeed, that the exercise of its mysterious dominion had as yet only begun. Scarcely had I set foot in Paris ere I had fresh evidence of the detestable interest taken by this Wilson in my concerns. Years flew, while I experienced no relief. Villain!﻿—at Rome, with how untimely, yet with how spectral an officiousness, stepped he in between me and my ambition! At Vienna, too﻿—at Berlin﻿—and at Moscow! Where, in truth, had I *not* bitter cause to curse him within my heart? From his inscrutable tyranny did I at length flee, panic-stricken, as from a pestilence; and to the very ends of the earth *I fled in vain*.

===Chinese===

我那时蒙羞受辱，被踩进尘土；倘若我的全副注意力不曾当场被一桩最惊人心性的事实摄住，我很可能要以即时的暴力回敬这刺人的言语。我穿的那件斗篷是一种稀有的毛皮；怎样稀有、怎样贵得离谱，我不敢说。它的式样也出自我自己幻想的发明；因为我在这类轻浮的事情上挑剔到荒唐的花花公子程度。因此，当普雷斯顿先生把他从地板上、从那屋子折叠门附近拾起的东西递到我手里，我是带着几乎濒于恐怖的惊异，察觉我自己那件已经挂在我的臂上（我毫不怀疑是无意间挂的），而递给我的那一件，是它在每一处、甚至最微细的可能细节上的精确副本。那位把我败露得如此之惨的奇特存在，我记得是裹在斗篷里的；而我们一伙的成员，除我之外，谁也没有穿斗篷。我保住若干心神，接下普雷斯顿递来的那件；不动声色地把它罩在自己那件上；带着一副决绝的、挑衅的凶相离开屋子；次日黎明未到，便踏上从牛津往大陆的仓皇旅程，怀着恐怖与羞耻的十足的绞痛。

*我白白地逃了。*我的恶运追逐着我，仿佛在欣幸，并且确实证明：它那神秘统治的行使，至此不过刚刚开始。我刚踏上巴黎（Paris）的地土，便有了新的证据，证明这位威尔逊对我的事务怀着可憎的关切。岁月飞逝，我并未得到宽解。恶棍！——在罗马，带着何等不识时务、然而何等幽灵般的多事，他插进我和我的雄心之间！在维也纳也一样——在柏林——在莫斯科！真的，我何尝*不*有苦涩的理由在心里咒他？我终于从他那不可测的暴政下逃出来，惊惶失措，像逃一场瘟疫；逃到地极——*我白白地逃了*。

===Original===

And again, and again, in secret communion with my own spirit, would I demand the questions “Who is he?﻿—whence came he?﻿—and what are his objects?” But no answer was there found. And then I scrutinized, with a minute scrutiny, the forms, and the methods, and the leading traits of his impertinent supervision. But even here there was very little upon which to base a conjecture. It was noticeable, indeed, that, in no one of the multiplied instances in which he had of late crossed my path, had he so crossed it except to frustrate those schemes, or to disturb those actions, which, if fully carried out, might have resulted in bitter mischief. Poor justification this, in truth, for an authority so imperiously assumed! Poor indemnity for natural rights of self-agency so pertinaciously, so insultingly denied!

I had also been forced to notice that my tormentor, for a very long period of time (while scrupulously and with miraculous dexterity maintaining his whim of an identity of apparel with myself), had so contrived it, in the execution of his varied interference with my will, that I saw not, at any moment, the features of his face. Be Wilson what he might, *this*, at least, was but the veriest of affectation, or of folly. Could he, for an instant, have supposed that, in my admonisher at Eton﻿—in the destroyer of my honor at Oxford﻿—in him who thwarted my ambition at Rome, my revenge at Paris, my passionate love at Naples, or what he falsely termed my avarice in Egypt﻿—that in this, my arch-enemy and evil genius, could fail to recognise the William Wilson of my school boy days﻿—the namesake, the companion, the rival﻿—the hated and dreaded rival at Dr. Bransby’s? Impossible!﻿—But let me hasten to the last eventful scene of the drama.

===Chinese===

于是，一次又一次，在同我自己精神秘密交契之中，我提出那些问题：「他是谁？——他从哪里来？——他的目的是什么？」但答案一个也寻不见。于是我以极细密的审视，检查他那些无礼监护的形态、方法和主导的特征。但就在这里，可资揣想的也很少。确实可以注意到：在他晚近多次横在我的路上的例子里，他无一例外地只为挫败那些计划、搅扰那些行动而横过来——那些计划行动倘若完全实行，本会导致苦涩的祸害。为这样一个如此专横假定的权威，这真是可怜的辩护！对天赋的行动自主的权利，被这样执拗地、这样侮辱地否认，补偿多么可怜！

我也不得不注意到：我的折磨者，在很长一个时期里（一丝不苟地、以奇迹般的巧妙维持着他同我衣着同一的怪想），在他对我意志的种种干预的执行中，始终作了这样的安排，使我在任何时刻都看不见他面貌的五官。威尔逊无论是什么，*这*至少纯然是最不足道的做作，或者愚蠢。难道他会有片刻设想：在我的伊顿的训诫者里——在牛津毁我名誉的那个人里——在罗马阻我雄心、在巴黎破我报复、在那不勒斯断我热烈的爱情、或在埃及阻他所诬称的我的贪欲的那个人里——在这个我的大敌、我的恶灵里，会认不出我学生时代的威廉·威尔逊——那个同名人、同伴、对手——布兰斯比学塾里那个可恨可畏的对手吗？不可能！——但容我赶紧讲到这出戏最后的、决定命运的一幕。

===Original===

Thus far I had succumbed supinely to this imperious domination. The sentiment of deep awe with which I habitually regarded the elevated character, the majestic wisdom, the apparent omnipresence and omnipotence of Wilson, added to a feeling of even terror, with which certain other traits in his nature and assumptions inspired me, had operated, hitherto, to impress me with an idea of my own utter weakness and helplessness, and to suggest an implicit, although bitterly reluctant submission to his arbitrary will. But, of late days, I had given myself up entirely to wine; and its maddening influence upon my hereditary temper rendered me more and more impatient of control. I began to murmur﻿—to hesitate﻿—to resist. And was it only fancy which induced me to believe that, with the increase of my own firmness, that of my tormentor underwent a proportional diminution? Be this as it may, I now began to feel the inspiration of a burning hope, and at length nurtured in my secret thoughts a stern and desperate resolution that I would submit no longer to be enslaved.

It was at Rome, during the Carnival of 18﻿—, that I attended a masquerade in the palazzo of the Neapolitan Duke Di Broglio. I had indulged more freely than usual in the excesses of the wine-table; and now the suffocating atmosphere of the crowded rooms irritated me beyond endurance. The difficulty, too, of forcing my way through the mazes of the company contributed not a little to the ruffling of my temper; for I was anxiously seeking (let me not say with what unworthy motive) the young, the gay, the beautiful wife of the aged and doting Di Broglio. With a too unscrupulous confidence she had previously communicated to me the secret of the costume in which she would be habited, and now, having caught a glimpse of her person, I was hurrying to make my way into her presence. At this moment I felt a light hand placed upon my shoulder, and that ever-remembered, low, damnable *whisper* within my ear.

In an absolute frenzy of wrath, I turned at once upon him who had thus interrupted me, and seized him violently by the collar. He was attired, as I had expected, in a costume altogether similar to my own; wearing a Spanish cloak of blue velvet, begirt about the waist with a crimson belt sustaining a rapier. A mask of black silk entirely covered his face.

===Chinese===

到此为止，我一直仰面屈服于这专横的统治。我惯常怀着的那种深沉的敬畏——对威尔逊的高贵品格、庄严智慧、表观的无所不在与无所不能——加上他天性里、他自命里某些别的特质在我身上激起的甚至恐惧之情，至今一直在把我压进一个我自己极端软弱无力的念头里，并且唆使我对他专断的意志默默服从，虽然服从得痛切地不情愿。但近来，我把自己整个交给了酒；酒对我承袭性情的使人疯狂的影响，使我对控制越来越不耐。我开始咕哝——迟疑——抵抗。是不是单是幻想，诱使我相信：随着我自己坚韧的增长，我折磨者的坚韧经受着成比例的减缩？无论如何，此刻我开始感到一种灼热的希望的鼓舞，终于在我的秘念里养出一种严峻而绝望的决心：我不再屈服于被奴役。

那是罗马，18——年的狂欢节，我赴一场化装舞会，在那不勒斯的迪布罗利奥（Di Broglio）公爵的府邸。我在酒桌上比平常更放肆地纵酒；此刻满屋拥挤人群的令人窒息的空气，激得我再不能忍。在人群的迷宫里挤出一条路的困难，也大大助长了我脾气的恼怒；因为我正焦灼地寻觅（容我不说怀着怎样卑劣的动机）那年迈昏聩的迪布罗利奥公爵年轻、快活、美丽的妻子。她先前怀着过于轻率的自信，把她将要穿着的服装的秘密告诉过我；此刻，瞥见了她的人影，我正急急挤进她面前去。这一刻我觉出一只轻手搭上我的肩头，和那永志不忘的、低低的、可咒的*耳语*在我耳边。

在绝对狂怒的疯狂里，我立刻转身扑向这样打断我的人，狠狠攥住他的领口。他穿着，如我所预期的，一套同我全然相似的服装；披一件蓝丝绒的西班牙斗篷，腰间围着一条深红的腰带，悬着一柄轻剑。一幅黑丝绢的面具完全罩住他的脸。

===Original===

“Scoundrel!” I said, in a voice husky with rage, while every syllable I uttered seemed as new fuel to my fury, “scoundrel! impostor! accursed villain! you shall not﻿—you *shall not* dog me unto death! Follow me, or I stab you where you stand!”﻿—and I broke my way from the ballroom into a small antechamber adjoining, dragging him unresistingly with me as I went.

Upon entering, I thrust him furiously from me. He staggered against the wall, while I closed the door with an oath, and commanded him to draw. He hesitated but for an instant; then, with a slight sigh, drew in silence, and put himself upon his defence.

The contest was brief indeed. I was frantic with every species of wild excitement, and felt within my single arm the energy and power of a multitude. In a few seconds I forced him by sheer strength against the wainscoting, and thus, getting him at mercy, plunged my sword, with brute ferocity, repeatedly through and through his bosom.

At that instant some person tried the latch of the door. I hastened to prevent an intrusion, and then immediately returned to my dying antagonist. But what human language can adequately portray *that* astonishment, *that* horror which possessed me at the spectacle then presented to view? The brief moment in which I averted my eyes had been sufficient to produce, apparently, a material change in the arrangements at the upper or farther end of the room. A large mirror﻿—so at first it seemed to me in my confusion﻿—now stood where none had been perceptible before; and, as I stepped up to it in extremity of terror, mine own image, but with features all pale and dabbled in blood, advanced to meet me with a feeble and tottering gait.

Thus it appeared, I say, but was not. It was my antagonist﻿—it was Wilson, who then stood before me in the agonies of his dissolution. His mask and cloak lay, where he had thrown them, upon the floor. Not a thread in all his raiment﻿—not a line in all the marked and singular lineaments of his face which was not, even in the most absolute identity, *mine own*!

It was Wilson; but he spoke no longer in a whisper, and I could have fancied that I myself was speaking while he said:

===Chinese===

「恶棍！」我说，声音因暴怒而嘶哑，我吐出的每个字都仿佛添给我怒火的新柴，「恶棍！冒牌货！该死的匪徒！你休想——你*休想*把我纠缠到死！跟着我，不然我就当场把你捅个窟窿！」——我一面说，一面冲出舞厅，闯进毗邻的一间小前厅，一路把他毫无抵抗地拖在手里。

一进屋，我狂怒地把他推开。他踉跄着撞在墙上，我咒骂一声关上门，命令他拔剑。他迟疑不过一瞬；然后轻轻叹一口气，默默拔剑，摆好招架的姿势。

这场搏斗实在短促。我被种种狂野的兴奋激得发狂，觉得在我单独一条胳膊里，有一群人的精力和膂力。几秒钟之内，我纯凭气力把他逼到护壁板上，这样把他置于任我宰割的地步，便以野兽的凶残，把我的剑一刀又一刀反复捅进他的胸口。

就在那一瞬，有人试着拧门闩。我赶忙挡住闯入，随即回到我那垂死的对手跟前。但*那*惊愕，*那*恐怖——它们攫住我，面对此刻呈现在眼前的景象——人的语言哪能描画得尽？我移开眼睛的那短短一瞬，已经足以造成，看来如此，屋子高处或远端布置上的一种实质的变化。一面大镜子——最初在迷乱中我这样觉得——此刻立在先前并无镜子可辨的地方；当我以极端的恐怖走近它，我自己的形象，但五官惨白、血迹斑斑，迈着虚软踉跄的步子，迎上前来。

我说，看起来如此，但并非如此。那是我的对手——那是威尔逊，此刻站在我面前，在他弥留的痛苦里。他的面具和斗篷躺在他掷下的地板上。他全部衣装里没有一根线——他脸上所有那些显著而奇特的轮廓里没有一道线，不是，甚至在最绝对的同一里，*我自己的*！

那是威尔逊；但他不再用耳语说话，我可以猜想是我自己在说话，当他说：

===Original===

“*You have conquered, and I yield. Yet, henceforward art thou also dead﻿—dead to the World, to Heaven and to Hope! In me didst thou exist﻿—and, in my death, see by this image, which is thine own, how utterly thou hast murdered thyself.*”

===Chinese===

「*你战胜了，我认输。然而从此你也就死了——对世界死了，对上天死了，对希望死了！你曾在我之中存在——而，在我的死里，请借这副你自己的形象看看，你把自己谋杀得多么彻底。*」

## The Conversation of Eiros and Charmion / 艾罗斯与查米恩的对话
===Original===

Πυρ σοι προσοισω.

I will bring fire to thee.

> Euripides, *Androm.*

Eiros

Why do you call me Eiros?

Charmion

So henceforward will you always be called. You must forget too, *my* earthly name, and speak to me as Charmion.

Eiros

This is indeed no dream!

Charmion

Dreams are with us no more; but of these mysteries anon. I rejoice to see you looking lifelike and rational. The film of the shadow has already passed from off your eyes. Be of heart and fear nothing. Your allotted days of stupor have expired and, tomorrow, I will myself induct you into the full joys and wonders of your novel existence.

Eiros

True, I feel no stupor, none at all. The wild sickness and the terrible darkness have left me, and I hear no longer that mad, rushing, horrible sound, like the “voice of many waters.” Yet my senses are bewildered, Charmion, with the keenness of their perception of *the new*.

Charmion

A few days will remove all this;﻿—but I fully understand you, and feel for you. It is now ten earthly years since I underwent what you undergo﻿—yet the remembrance of it hangs by me still. You have now suffered all of pain, however, which you will suffer in Aidenn.

Eiros

In Aidenn?

Charmion

In Aidenn.

Eiros

Oh God!﻿—pity me, Charmion!﻿—I am overburdened with the majesty of all things﻿—of the unknown now known﻿—of the speculative Future merged in the august and certain Present.

Charmion

Grapple not now with such thoughts. Tomorrow we will speak of this. Your mind wavers, and its agitation will find relief in the exercise of simple memories. Look not around, nor forward﻿—but back. I am burning with anxiety to hear the details of that stupendous event which threw you among us. Tell me of it. Let us converse of familiar things, in the old familiar language of the world which has so fearfully perished.

Eiros

Most fearfully, fearfully!﻿—this is indeed no dream.

Charmion

Dreams are no more. Was I much mourned, my Eiros?

Eiros

Mourned, Charmion?﻿—oh deeply. To that last hour of all, there hung a cloud of intense gloom and devout sorrow over your household.

Charmion

===Chinese===

Πυρ σοι προσοισω.

我将以火予你。

——欧里庇得斯《安德洛墨达》

艾罗斯

你为什么叫我艾罗斯？

查米恩

从此以后，你就永远叫这个名字了。你也必须忘掉「我」尘世的名字，叫我查米恩。

艾罗斯

这当真不是梦！

查米恩

梦于我们已不复存在；这些奥妙回头再讲。见你面色如生、神志清明，我很欢喜。影子的那层翳，已从你眼前退去。鼓起心来，什么也不必怕。你派定的昏迷之日已经期满，明天，我将亲自引你进入你那崭新存在的全部欢愉与奇观。

艾罗斯

真的，我不觉昏迷了，一点也不。那狂乱的病和可怕的黑暗都离开了我，我再也听不见那疯狂的、奔涌的、可怕的声音了——那「众水的声音」。只是我的感官，查米恩，为它们感知「新异」的敏锐而迷乱了。

查米恩

几天之后，这一切都会消散；——可我全然懂你，也体恤你。从我经受你此刻所经受的，至今已过了尘世的十年——而那记忆仍缠着我。不过你在爱甸要受的苦，你已经受完了。

艾罗斯

在爱甸？

查米恩

在爱甸。

艾罗斯

哦，上帝！——怜悯我，查米恩！——万物的威严压得我承担不起——那未知的如今已知了——那思辨的将来，汇入了威严而确凿的现在。

查米恩

此刻且不必同这些念头搏斗。明天我们再谈。你的心神在摇曳，一用到单纯的回忆上，它的激动便得宽解。不要环顾，不要前瞻——要回顾。我焦灼得很，想听那桩把你抛到我们中间来的赫赫大事的详情。讲给我听。让我们用旧日尘世那熟悉的语言，谈谈熟悉的事——那个已经那样可怕地灭亡了的世界。

艾罗斯

可怕之至，可怕之至！——这当真不是梦。

查米恩

梦已不再。人们很哀悼我么，我的艾罗斯？

艾罗斯

哀悼，查米恩？——哦，深沉极了。直到最后的时辰，一片浓重的阴云和虔诚的悲恸，始终罩着你的家。

查米恩

===Original===

And that last hour﻿—speak of it. Remember that, beyond the naked fact of the catastrophe itself, I know nothing. When, coming out from among mankind, I passed into Night through the Grave﻿—at that period, if I remember aright, the calamity which overwhelmed you was utterly unanticipated. But, indeed, I knew little of the speculative philosophy of the day.

Eiros

The individual calamity was as you say entirely unanticipated; but analogous misfortunes had been long a subject of discussion with astronomers. I need scarce tell you, my friend, that, even when you left us, men had agreed to understand those passages in the most holy writings which speak of the final destruction of all things by fire, as having reference to the orb of the earth alone. But in regard to the immediate agency of the ruin, speculation had been at fault from that epoch in astronomical knowledge in which the comets were divested of the terrors of flame. The very moderate density of these bodies had been well established. They had been observed to pass among the satellites of Jupiter, without bringing about any sensible alteration either in the masses or in the orbits of these secondary planets. We had long regarded the wanderers as vapory creations of inconceivable tenuity, and as altogether incapable of doing injury to our substantial globe, even in the event of contact. But contact was not in any degree dreaded; for the elements of all the comets were accurately known. That among *them* we should look for the agency of the threatened fiery destruction had been for many years considered an inadmissible idea. But wonders and wild fancies had been, of late days, strangely rife among mankind; and, although it was only with a few of the ignorant that actual apprehension prevailed, upon the announcement by astronomers of a *new* comet, yet this announcement was generally received with I know not what of agitation and mistrust.

===Chinese===

那么说说那最后的时辰罢。记住，除了那场大祸本身的赤裸事实，我一无所知。当我从人间走出来、经坟墓入了长夜——那段时候，如果我记得不错，吞没你们的那场灾难还全然无人料及。不过，说真的，当日的思辨哲学，我本就懂得不多。

艾罗斯

个人的灾祸诚如你所说，全无人料及；可类似的凶事，天文学家们久已引为论题。我几乎不必告诉你，我的朋友，你离开我们时，人们已经一致这样理解至圣书卷里讲到万物终将于火中毁灭的那些段落——说它们指的仅仅是地这一球。至于那毁灭的直接作手，自从天文学把彗星们身上火的恐怖剥除以来，种种悬测一直落空。这些天体的密度极低，早已考实。人们观察到它们从木星的卫星中间穿过，却不论对这些次级行星的质量还是轨道，都不曾带来任何可觉的变动。我们久已把这些游星看作稀薄得不可想象的蒸气造物，全然无力伤害我们坚实的地球，哪怕相触。而相触也无半分可惧；因为所有彗星的诸元都已精确得知。到「它们」中间去寻那预警的火焚之灾的作手——多年来这想法一直被斥为不可。可是近来，奇谈怪想在人间奇怪地盛起；天文学家们一宣布一颗「新」彗星，虽然真正的惶恐只握住少数无知的人，这消息却普遍叫人生出一种我说不出的骚动与疑惧。

===Original===

The elements of the strange orb were immediately calculated, and it was at once conceded by all observers, that its path, at perihelion, would bring it into very close proximity with the earth. There were two or three astronomers, of secondary note, who resolutely maintained that a contact was inevitable. I cannot very well express to you the effect of this intelligence upon the people. For a few short days they would not believe an assertion which their intellect so long employed among worldly considerations could not in any manner grasp. But the truth of a vitally important fact soon makes its way into the understanding of even the most stolid. Finally, all men saw that astronomical knowledge lied not, and they awaited the comet. Its approach was not, at first, seemingly rapid; nor was its appearance of very unusual character. It was of a dull red, and had little perceptible train. For seven or eight days we saw no material increase in its apparent diameter, and but a partial alteration in its color. Meantime, the ordinary affairs of men were discarded and all interests absorbed in a growing discussion, instituted by the philosophic, in respect to the cometary nature. Even the grossly ignorant aroused their sluggish capacities to such considerations. The learned *now* gave their intellect﻿—their soul﻿—to no such points as the allaying of fear, or to the sustenance of loved theory. They sought﻿—they panted for right views. They groaned for perfected knowledge. *Truth* arose in the purity of her strength and exceeding majesty, and the wise bowed down and adored.

===Chinese===

那颗怪星的诸元立刻算了出来；所有观测者当即承认：它的轨道在近日点处，将同地球极为相近。有两三位二流的天文学家，坚决主张相触在所难免。这消息对民众的效力，我难以向你表达。短短几天，人们还不肯相信这断言——他们的智力久在尘俗的算计里打转，怎么也提不住它。可一个攸关存亡的事实的真，很快就扎进最迟钝的理解里去。末了，人人都看见天文学的知识不曾撒谎，人们便等着那颗彗星。起初，它的来势看着并不迅疾；相貌也不很特别。暗红色，尾迹几乎看不见。有七八天，我们看不出它视直径有什么实质的增长，颜色也只有局部的变化。其间，人间寻常事务尽废，一切兴味都吸进一场由哲人们发起的、日益高涨的争论里——论彗星的本性。连极端无知的人，也把他们迟钝的才力唤起来想这些。学者们「此刻」不再把才智与灵魂花在平息恐惧或喂养心爱的旧说上。他们寻求——他们渴望正确的见解。他们为圆满的知识而呻吟。「真理」在她纯净的伟力与无比的威仪中升起，智者们躬身崇拜。

===Original===

That material injury to our globe or to its inhabitants would result from the apprehended contact, was an opinion which hourly lost ground among the wise; and the wise were now freely permitted to rule the reason and the fancy of the crowd. It was demonstrated, that the density of the comet’s nucleus was far less than that of our rarest gas; and the harmless passage of a similar visitor among the satellites of Jupiter was a point strongly insisted upon, and which served greatly to allay terror. Theologists with an earnestness fear-enkindled, dwelt upon the biblical prophecies, and expounded them to the people with a directness and simplicity of which no previous instance had been known. That the final destruction of the earth must be brought about by the agency of fire, was urged with a spirit that enforced everywhere conviction; and that the comets were of no fiery nature (as all men now knew) was a truth which relieved all, in a great measure, from the apprehension of the great calamity foretold. It is noticeable that the popular prejudices and vulgar errors in regard to pestilences and wars﻿—errors which were wont to prevail upon every appearance of a comet﻿—were now altogether unknown. As if by some sudden convulsive exertion, reason had at once hurled superstition from her throne. The feeblest intellect had derived vigor from excessive interest.

What minor evils might arise from the contact were points of elaborate question. The learned spoke of slight geological disturbances, of probable alterations in climate, and consequently in vegetation, of possible magnetic and electric influences. Many held that no visible or perceptible effect would in any manner be produced. While such discussions were going on, their subject gradually approached, growing larger in apparent diameter, and of a more brilliant lustre. Mankind grew paler as it came. All human operations were suspended.

===Chinese===

说所惧的相触会给我们的地球或其居民带来实质的伤害——这见解在智者中日甚一日地失势；而智者如今被放手去统治大众的理性与想象。已经证明：那彗星核的密度，远低于我们最稀薄的气体；而一个同类的过客从木星卫星间无害穿行，是被着力坚持的一点，大大平息了恐怖。神学家们怀着恐惧点燃的热忱，反复讲论圣经的预言，向民众讲解得那样直截而简明，先例全无。说地球的最终毁灭必出于火之力——这论点到处都带着一股叫人不得不服的气势；而彗星并无火的性质（如众人此时皆知的），这一条真理，又大大解脱了众人对那预言的大灾的忧惧。值得注意：彗星每现，必盛行的那些关于瘟疫与刀兵的民间成见与流俗谬说，如今全然绝迹。仿佛理性一阵痉挛式的猛力，登时把迷信掀下了宝座。最弱的智力，也从过度的关切里得了气力。

至于相触会生出什么小灾，则是细密的论题。学者们讲起轻微的地动、气候因而植被的可能改变、可能的磁与电的影响。许多人坚持：不会生出任何可见可觉的效应。这些讨论进行之际，它们的话题渐渐逼近，视直径越来越大，光焰越来越亮。它来近，人就变得更苍白。人间的一切运转都停了。

===Original===

There was an epoch in the course of the general sentiment when the comet had attained, at length, a size surpassing that of any previously recorded visitation. The people now, dismissing any lingering hope that the astronomers were wrong, experienced all the certainty of evil. The chimerical aspect of their terror was gone. The hearts of the stoutest of our race beat violently within their bosoms. A very few days sufficed, however, to merge even such feelings in sentiments more unendurable We could no longer apply to the strange orb any *accustomed* thoughts. Its *historical* attributes had disappeared. It oppressed us with a hideous *novelty* of emotion. We saw it not as an astronomical phenomenon in the heavens, but as an incubus upon our hearts, and a shadow upon our brains. It had taken, with inconceivable rapidity, the character of a gigantic mantle of rare flame, extending from horizon to horizon.

Yet a day, and men breathed with greater freedom. It was clear that we were already within the influence of the comet; yet we lived. We even felt an unusual elasticity of frame and vivacity of mind. The exceeding tenuity of the object of our dread was apparent; for all heavenly objects were plainly visible through it. Meantime, our vegetation had perceptibly altered; and we gained faith, from this predicted circumstance, in the foresight of the wise. A wild luxuriance of foliage, utterly unknown before, burst out upon every vegetable thing.

Yet another day﻿—and the evil was not altogether upon us. It was now evident that its nucleus would first reach us. A wild change had come over all men; and the first sense of *pain* was the wild signal for general lamentation and horror. This first sense of pain lay in a rigorous constriction of the breast and lungs, and an insufferable dryness of the skin. It could not be denied that our atmosphere was radically affected; the conformation of this atmosphere and the possible modifications to which it might be subjected, were now the topics of discussion. The result of investigation sent an electric thrill of the intensest terror through the universal heart of man.

===Chinese===

在普遍情绪的进程中，有一个时期，彗星的尺寸终于超过了史载一切先例。民众这时抛开了「天文学家们错了」的最后指望，把凶事的确定尝了个满口。他们恐怖中的虚幻色彩消失了。我们族中最刚强的心，也在胸膛里狂跳。然而不过几天，连这样的情绪也淹没在更难堪的感觉里。我们再不能拿任何「惯熟的」念头去看那颗怪星了。它「史册上的」一切属性都消失了。它以一种可憎的「新奇」的情绪压着我们。我们看见的不再是天上的一桩天文现象，而是压在心头的一个梦魇、罩在脑上的一道影。它已以一种不可想象的速度，变成一件稀薄火焰织成的巨大披氅，从天际到天际。

又过一日，人们呼吸得自在了些。显然，我们已处于彗星的影响之内；可我们还活着。我们甚至感到一种非常的身轻与心智的活泼。我们那恐惧对象的无比稀薄，一目了然；因为一切天体都透过它清清楚楚地显出来。其间，我们的草木已可觉地变了样；从这预言过的情形里，我们对智者们的先见生了信心。一种先前全然未知的、狂野繁茂的枝叶，在每一株草木上迸发出来。

再过一日——大祸还没有整个临头。这时显然，它的核将先抵达我们。所有的人都起了狂变；而「痛」的初感，便是普遍哀号与恐怖的狂乱信号。这最初的痛感，在于胸肺的紧束和皮肤难忍的干燥。无可否认，我们的大气已受了根本的影响；这大气的构造和它可能遭受的种种改变，成了当前的话题。研究的结果，把一道极度恐怖的电颤，送进了全人类的共同的心。

===Original===

It had been long known that the air which encircled us was a compound of oxygen and nitrogen gases, in the proportion of twenty-one measures of oxygen, and seventy-nine of nitrogen in every one hundred of the atmosphere. Oxygen, which was the principle of combustion, and the vehicle of heat, was absolutely necessary to the support of animal life, and was the most powerful and energetic agent in nature. Nitrogen, on the contrary, was incapable of supporting either animal life or flame. An unnatural excess of oxygen would result, it had been ascertained in just such an elevation of the animal spirits as we had latterly experienced. It was the pursuit, the extension of the idea, which had engendered awe. What would be the result of *a total extraction of the nitrogen*? A combustion irresistible, all-devouring, omni-prevalent, immediate;﻿—the entire fulfilment, in all their minute and terrible details, of the fiery and horror-inspiring denunciations of the prophecies of the Holy Book.

Why need I paint, Charmion, the now disenchained frenzy of mankind? That tenuity in the comet which had previously inspired us with hope, was now the source of the bitterness of despair. In its impalpable gaseous character we clearly perceived the consummation of Fate. Meantime a day again passed﻿—bearing away with it the last shadow of Hope. We gasped in the rapid modification of the air. The red blood bounded tumultuously through its strict channels. A furious delirium possessed all men; and, with arms rigidly outstretched towards the threatening heavens, they trembled and shrieked aloud. But the nucleus of the destroyer was now upon us; even here in Aidenn, I shudder while I speak. Let me be brief﻿—brief as the ruin that overwhelmed. For a moment there was a wild lurid light alone, visiting and penetrating all things. Then﻿—let us bow down, Charmion, before the excessive majesty of the great God!﻿—then, there came a shouting and pervading sound, as if from the mouth itself of **him**; while the whole incumbent mass of ether in which we existed, burst at once into a species of intense flame, for whose surpassing brilliancy and all-fervid heat even the angels in the high Heaven of pure knowledge have no name. Thus ended all.

===Chinese===

人们早已知道，环裹我们的空气是氧和氮两种气体的混合物：每一百份大气里，氧气占二十一，氮气占七十九。氧是燃烧的原理、热的载体，是维持动物生命所绝对必需的，也是自然界最强有力的动因。氮则相反，既不能维持动物生命，也不能维持火焰。氧的不自然的过量，其后果——已查明——正是我们近来经历的那种动物性精神的昂奋。而正是这一想法的追索与推展，生出了敬畏。「若把氮全部抽去」，其结果将如何？一场不可抗拒、吞噬一切、无所不在、立时的燃烧；——圣书预言里那些火的、令人胆寒的警告，将在一切微末而可怕的细节里全部应验。

查米恩，我何必描画人类此刻挣脱了锁链的狂乱？那彗星的稀薄，先前给过我们希望，如今成了绝望的苦源。在它那不可触的气体品性里，我们清楚地看见了命运的完成。其间又过去一日——带走了希望的最后一道影。我们在空气的急变里喘息。鲜红的血在它严密的管道里奔涌咆哮。一种狂暴的谵妄攝住了所有的人；他们双臂僵直地伸向威逼的天空，发着抖，放声尖叫。可那毁灭者的核已临到我们头上；即便在这里，在爱甸，我一开口还要发抖。让我简短罢——简短得像那吞没一切的覆灭。有一瞬，只有一片狂乱的惨白的光，照彻万物、透入万物。随后——查米恩，让我们在大上帝的无比威仪前躬身罢！——随后，来了一阵弥漫的呼喊，仿佛出自「他」的口；而我们置身其中的、整个覆压的以太，霎时迸作一种炽烈之火——那火的辉煌之至、炽热之至，连纯知高天里的天使，也唤不出它的名。一切就这样完了。

## Why the Little Frenchman Wears His Hand in a Sling / 小法国佬为什么用绷带吊着手
===Original===

It’s on my visiting cards sure enough (and it’s them that’s all o’ pink satin paper) that inny gintleman that plases may behould the intheristhin’ words, “Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, 39 Southampton Row, Russell Square, Parrish o’ Bloomsbury.” And shud ye be wantin’ to diskiver who is the pink of purliteness quite, and the laider of the hot tun in the houl city o’ Lonon﻿—why it’s jist mesilf. And fait that same is no wonder at all at all (so be plased to stop curlin’ your nose), for every inch o’ the six wakes that I’ve been a gintleman, and left aff wid the bog-throthing to take up wid the Barronissy, it’s Pathrick that’s been living like a houly imperor, and gitting the iddication and the graces. Och! and wouldn’t it be a blessed thing for your spirrits if ye cud lay your two peepers jist, upon Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, when he is all riddy drissed for the hopperer, or stipping into the Brisky for the drive into the Hyde Park. But it’s the illigant big figgur that I ’ave, for the rason o’ which all the ladies fall in love wid me. Isn’t it my own swate silf now that’ll missure the six fut, and the three inches more nor that, in me stockins, and that am excadingly will proportioned all over to match? And it is ralelly more than three fut and a bit that there is, inny how, of the little ould furrener Frinchman that lives jist over the way, and that’s a-oggling and a-goggling the houl day, (and bad luck to him,) at the purty widdy Misthress Tracle that’s my own nixt-door neighbor, (God bliss her!) and a most particuller frind and acquaintance? You percave the little spalpeen is summat down in the mouth, and wears his lift hand in a sling, and it’s for that same thing, by yur lave, that I’m going to give you the good rason.

===Chinese===

那话儿在我拜客的名片上写得明明白白——全是粉红缎面子纸的名片——哪位高兴的先生都可以瞧见那叫人瞧着起劲的字眼儿：「帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士（Sir Pathrick O'Grandison, Barronitt），从男爵，南安普敦路39号，罗素广场，布卢姆斯伯里教区。」您要是想晓得谁才是全伦敦最最斯文的尖子、全城时髦人物的魁首——嘿，那正是俺老帕本人。这话说来一点儿也不稀奇（劳驾您别皱鼻子），因为打俺当上绅士、撇下泥塘子营生改行做从男爵的这六个礼拜里，帕特里克俺过的可是圣上一般的日子，学问和气派一齐往身上长。哦！您要是能把两只眼珠子搁在帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士身上——看他穿戴齐整预备赴舞、或者跨进布鲁厄姆马车预备上海德公园兜风——那才叫您心花怒放哩。俺有一副漂亮大个儿的身板，太太们个个为俺害相思，就为这个。俺自己的小甜身板，穿袜量足有六英尺，外加三英寸多，浑身上下匀称得服服帖帖，这难道不是吗？可是住在街对面那个小老外来路子——法国佬——真个够三英尺还带零头，整天贼眉贼眼地盯，（他倒好运气！）盯的是俺紧隔壁的好邻居特蕾克尔（Tracle）小寡妇（上帝保佑她！），还是俺顶顶要好的知己朋友？您瞧见那小无赖耷拉着脑袋，左手吊在绷带里；得了您老的准许，俺这就把那桩事的好缘由讲给您听。

===Original===

The truth of the houl matter is jist simple enough; for the very first day that I com’d from Connaught, and showd my swate little silf in the strait to the widdy, who was looking through the windy, it was a gone case althegither with the heart o’ the purty Misthress Tracle. I percaved it, ye see, all at once, and no mistake, and that’s God’s truth. First of all it was up wid the windy in a jiffy, and thin she threw open her two peepers to the itmost, and thin it was a little gould spyglass that she clapped tight to one o’ them and divil may burn me if it didn’t spake to me as plain as a peeper cud spake, and says it, through the spyglass: “Och! the tip o’ the mornin’ to ye, Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, mavourneen; and it’s a nate gintleman that ye are, sure enough, and it’s mesilf and me forten jist that’ll be at yur sarvice, dear, inny time o’ day at all at all for the asking.” And it’s not mesilf ye wud have to be bate in the purliteness; so I made her a bow that wud ha’ broken yur heart altegither to behould, and thin I pulled aff me hat with a flourish, and thin I winked at her hard wid both eyes, as much as to say, “True for you, yer a swate little crature, Mrs. Tracle, me darlint, and I wish I may be drownthed dead in a bog, if it’s not mesilf, Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, that’ll make a houl bushel o’ love to yur leddyship, in the twinkling o’ the eye of a Londonderry purraty.”

And it was the nixt mornin’, sure, jist as I was making up me mind whither it wouldn’t be the purlite thing to sind a bit o’ writin’ to the widdy by way of a love-litter, when up com’d the delivery servant wid an illigant card, and he tould me that the name on it (for I niver could rade the copperplate printin’ on account of being lift handed) was all about Mounseer, the Count, A Goose, Look-aisy, Maiter-di-dauns, and that the houl of the divilish lingo was the spalpeeny long name of the little ould furrener Frinchman as lived over the way.

===Chinese===

实情的全部就是这般简单；就在俺从康诺特（Connaught）来的头一天，把俺的小甜身子往街上一亮，寡妇正打窗户里往外瞧，好特蕾克尔太太的心就整个儿完蛋了。您瞧，俺一眼就看出来，错不了，天底下真真如此。头一件，窗子噌地推上去；跟着她两只眼珠子睁到最大；跟着又把一只小小的金色望远镜紧紧扣在一只眼上——天打雷劈，那玩意儿跟我说起话来，跟眼珠子能说话一样明白，透过望远镜说：「哦！早上好呀，帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士，从男爵，我的心肝儿；您是位呱呱叫的体面先生，错不了；我跟我这点福气，亲爱的，只管开口，白天黑夜随时听您差遣。」论斯文您可别想赢俺；于是俺朝她鞠了一躬，那躬您瞧了心都得断成两截；跟着把帽子一甩摘下；跟着冲她两只眼一齐狠狠地挤了挤，那意思无非说：「说得真对，您是位小甜心儿，特蕾克尔太太，我的乖乖，俺要不是帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士、从男爵本人，甘愿淹死在泥塘里，也定要趁您老人家的明眸一眨眼的工夫，给您老人家献上一蒲式耳的爱情。」

第二天早上，俺正拿不定主意，要不要写张字条儿当情书给寡妇送去才算斯文，送信的仆人却递上来一张漂亮名片；他告诉我，名片上的名字（铜版印的字俺认不得，因为俺是左撇子）全是「芒瑟尔，康特（伯爵），阿·鹅斯，卢克艾西，梅特迪当斯先生」这一套，满纸鬼话便是街对面住的那个小老外来路子——法国佬的又长又刁的名字。

===Original===

And jist wid that in cum’d the little willian himself, and then he made me a broth of a bow, and thin he said he had ounly taken the liberty of doing me the honor of the giving me a call, and thin he went on to palaver at a great rate, and divil the bit did I comprehind what he wud be afther the tilling me at all at all, excipting and saving that he said “pully wou, woolly wou,” and tould me, among a bushel o’ lies, bad luck to him, that he was mad for the love o’ my widdy Misthress Tracle, and that my widdy Mrs. Tracle had a puncheon for *him*.

At the hearin’ of this, ye may swear, though, I was as mad as a grasshopper, but I remimbered that I was Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, and that it wasn’t althegither gentaal to lit the anger git the upper hand o’ the purliteness, so I made light o’ the matter and kipt dark, and got quite sociable wid the little chap, and afther a while what did he do but ask me to go wid him to the widdy’s, saying he wud give me the feshionable inthroduction to her leddyship.

“Is it there ye are?” said I thin to mesilf, “and it’s thrue for you, Pathrick, that ye’re the fortunittest mortal in life. We’ll soon see now whither it’s your swate silf, or whither it’s little Mounseer Maiter-di-dauns, that Misthress Tracle is head and ears in the love wid.”

Wid that we wint aff to the widdy’s, next door, and ye may well say it was an illigant place; so it was. There was a carpet all over the floor, and in one corner there was a forty-pinny and a jews-harp and the divil knows what ilse, and in another corner was a sofy, the beautifullest thing in all natur, and sitting on the sofy, sure enough, there was the swate little angel, Misthress Tracle.

“The tip o’ the mornin’ to ye,” says I, “Mrs. Tracle,” and thin I made sich an illigant obaysance that it wud ha quite althegither bewildered the brain o’ ye.

“Wully woo, pully woo, plump in the mud,” says the little furrenner Frinchman, “and sure Mrs. Tracle,” says he, that he did, “isn’t this gintleman here jist his reverence Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, and isn’t he althegither and entirely the most particular frind and acquaintance that I have in the houl world?”

===Chinese===

说着说着，那小宝贝儿本人进来了；他朝俺鞠了一钵子粥似的躬，跟着说他不过冒昧行个方便，赏脸来拜访俺；跟着他唾沫横飞地闲扯起来，他到底在跟俺说什么俺一个字也没抓着，只除得他说的「扑利乌，乌利乌」，还夹在一大蒲式耳谎话里告诉俺——他倒好运气——说他是为爱俺的寡妇特蕾克尔太太疯魔了，还说俺的寡妇特蕾克尔太太对他有心。

听了这话，您敢赌咒，俺气得像只蚂蚱；可俺记起俺是帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士，从男爵，让火气压过斯文不大合乎体统，于是俺把事情轻轻揭过，按住不表，跟那小家伙处得满和气；过了一阵儿，他干的什么？竟请俺陪他去寡妇家，说要给俺做一次时髦的引见。

「原来您在这儿啊！」俺心里说，「帕特里克，你真是世上顶有福气的人。这就瞧吧，到底是你的小甜身子，还是小芒瑟梅特迪当斯，才是特蕾克尔太太从头到脚爱着的人。」

于是俺们一块儿到隔壁寡妇家去；您尽可以说那地方漂亮，真个漂亮。地板满铺地毯；一个角落里立着一架四十基尼的钢琴，一只口簧琴，天晓得还有什么别的；另一个角落里摆着一张沙发，天底下顶美的宝贝；沙发上坐着，错不了，那位小甜天使，特蕾克尔太太。

「早上好呀，」俺说，「特蕾克尔太太，」跟着俺行了一个漂亮大礼，行得您老的脑袋都要发昏。

「乌利乌，扑利乌，一跤栽泥里，」小外来路子法国佬说；「特蕾克尔太太，」他说——他真说了——「这位先生不就是可敬的帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士、从男爵吗？他不就是我在这世上顶顶要好的知己朋友吗？」

===Original===

And wid that the widdy, she gits up from the sofy, and makes the swatest curthchy nor iver was seen; and thin down she sits like an angel; and thin, by the powers, it was that little spalpeen Mounseer Maiter-di-dauns that plumped his silf right down by the right side of her. Och hon! I ixpicted the two eyes o’ me wud ha cum’d out of my head on the spot, I was so dispirate mad! Howiver, “Bait who!” says I, after awhile. “Is it there ye are, Mounseer Maiter-di-dauns?” and so down I plumped on the lift side of her leddyship, to be aven with the willain. Botheration! it wud ha done your heart good to percave the illigant double wink that I gived her jist thin right in the face with both eyes.

But the little ould Frinchman he niver beginned to suspict me at all at all, and disperate hard it was he made the love to her leddyship. “Woully wou,” says he, “Pully wou,” says he, “Plump in the mud,” says he.

“That’s all to no use, Mounseer Frog, mavourneen,” thinks I; and I talked as hard and as fast as I could all the while, and throth it was mesilf jist that divarted her leddyship complately and intirely, by rason of the illigant conversation that I kipt up wid her all about the dear bogs of Connaught. And by and by she gived me such a swate smile, from one ind of her mouth to the ither, that it made me as bould as a pig, and I jist took hould of the ind of her little finger in the most dilikittest manner in natur, looking at her all the while out o’ the whites of my eyes.

And then ounly percave the cuteness of the swate angel, for no sooner did she obsarve that I was afther the squazing of her flipper, than she up wid it in a jiffy, and put it away behind her back, jist as much as to say, “Now thin, Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, there’s a bitther chance for ye, mavourneen, for it’s not altogether the gentaal thing to be afther the squazing of my flipper right full in the sight of that little furrenner Frinchman, Mounseer Maiter-di-dauns.”

===Chinese===

话音未落，寡妇从沙发上起身，行了一个天底下再没见过的甜屈膝礼；跟着像天使一般坐下；跟着，老天爷，那个小无赖芒瑟梅特迪当斯一屁股在她右手边坐了下来。哎哟！俺当时气得发昏，俺的两只眼珠子险些当场蹦出脑壳！不过，「好嘛！」俺隔了一会儿说。「原来您在这儿啊，芒瑟梅特迪当斯？」于是在她左手边一屁股坐下，跟那恶棍扯平。哎哟哟！俺当时冲她脸上两只眼睛一齐挤的那个漂亮的双眼媚，够叫您心里舒坦到底。

可那小老法国佬压根儿没起一点疑心，硬是跟她的太太大人热烈求起爱来。「乌利乌，」他说，「扑利乌，」他说，「一跤栽泥里，」他说。

「白搭，青蛙先生，我的心肝儿，」俺心里想；俺一面拼足了劲儿说个不停，说个不停，实话俺一个人把太太大人款待得服服帖帖、完完全全，就靠俺同她絮叨的康诺特可爱的泥塘子的那场漂亮谈吐。不多时她冲俺笑了，从嘴的这一头一直甜到那一头，笑得俺胆子壮得像头猪，俺便以天底下顶讲究的方式捏住她小手指头的尖儿，一面翻着两只眼白瞧她。

然后您瞧瞧那小甜天使的机灵劲儿：她一瞧见俺捏她的小手儿，霎时把手一抬，背到身后头，那意思无非说：「得了吧，帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士，我的心肝儿，您的运气糟透啦，当着那个小老外来路子法国佬、芒瑟梅特迪当斯的面捏我的小手儿，可不大合体统哩。」

===Original===

Wid that I giv’d her a big wink jist to say, “lit Sir Pathrick alone for the likes o’ them thricks,” and thin I wint aisy to work, and you’d have died wid the divarsion to behould how cliverly I slipped my right arm betwane the back o’ the sofy, and the back of her leddyship, and there, sure enough, I found a swate little flipper all a waiting to say, “the tip o’ the mornin’ to ye, Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt.” And wasn’t it mesilf, sure, that jist giv’d it the laste little bit of a squaze in the world, all in the way of a commincement, and not to be too rough wid her leddyship? and och, botheration, wasn’t it the gentaalest and dilikittest of all the little squazes that I got in return? “Blood and thunder, Sir Pathrick, mavourneen,” thinks I to mesilf, “fait it’s jist the mother’s son of you, and nobody else at all at all, that’s the handsomest and the fortunittest young bog-throtter that ever cum’d out of Connaught!” And with that I givd the flipper a big squaze, and a big squaze it was, by the powers, that her leddyship giv’d to me back. But it would ha split the seven sides of you wid the laffin’ to behould, jist then all at once, the consated behavior of Mounseer Maiter-di-dauns. The likes o’ sich a jabbering, and a smirking, and a parley-wouing as he begin’d wid her leddyship, niver was known before upon arth; and divil may burn me if it wasn’t me own very two peepers that cotch’d him tipping her the wink out of one eye. Och, hon! if it wasn’t mesilf thin that was mad as a Kilkenny cat I shud like to be tould who it was!

===Chinese===

俺冲她使了个老大的眼色，意思是「这种把戏，有俺老帕在，您甭管」；然后俺轻轻地、悄悄地用起功来——您瞧见俺怎样伶俐地把右胳膊插进沙发背和太太大人的后背中间，准会笑死过去；那儿，错不了，一只小甜手儿正等着说「早上好呀，帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士，从男爵」。那俺当然——谁还不是俺——只是轻轻捏了世上顶顶小的一下，算个开场，好不冲撞太太大人；哦，天哪，她回捏俺的那一下，不是顶斯文、顶叫人心里发甜的小捏吗？「血流成河，帕特里克爵士，我的心肝儿，」俺心里想，「老天为证，出康诺特的顶漂亮、顶有福气的年轻泥塘客，天下再没有第二个，正是您娘养的您本人！」想到这里，俺把手儿重重一捏，而老天爷在上，太太大人回敬俺的那一捏，才是真格的大捏。可是您要是瞧见芒瑟梅特迪当斯那会儿的得意劲儿，保管七个侧面都要笑裂了。他对太太大人那副唠叨、嘻嘻、扑利乌的做派，天底下头一回有；俺自家的两只眼珠子亲眼瞧见他挤着一只眼给她递眼色，天打雷劈也赖不掉。哦哟！那会儿要是发疯发成基尔肯尼猫的不是俺本人，您说说是谁！

===Original===

“Let me infarm you, Mounseer Maiter-di-dauns,” said I, as purlite as iver ye seed, “that it’s not the gintaal thing at all at all, and not for the likes o’ you inny how, to be afther the oggling and a-goggling at her leddyship in that fashion,” and jist wid that such another squaze as it was I giv’d her flipper, all as much as to say, “isn’t it Sir Pathrick now, my jewel, that’ll be able to the protectin’ o’ you, my darlint?” and then there cum’d another squaze back, all by way of the answer. “Thrue for you, Sir Pathrick,” it said as plain as iver a squaze said in the world, “Thrue for you, Sir Pathrick, mavourneen, and it’s a proper nate gintleman ye are﻿—that’s God’s truth,” and with that she opened her two beautiful peepers till I belaved they wud ha’ cum’d out of her hid althegither and intirely, and she looked first as mad as a cat at Mounseer Frog, and thin as smiling as all out o’ doors at mesilf.

“Thin,” says he, the willian, “Och hon! and a wolly-wou, pully-wou,” and then wid that he shoved up his two shoulders till the divil the bit of his hid was to be diskivered, and then he let down the two corners of his purraty-trap, and thin not a haporth more of the satisfaction could I git out o’ the spalpeen.

Belave me, my jewel, it was Sir Pathrick that was unreasonable mad thin, and the more by token that the Frinchman kipt an wid his winking at the widdy; and the widdy she kept an wid the squazing of my flipper, as much as to say, “At him again, Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, mavourneen;” so I just ripped out wid a big oath, and says I:

“Ye little spalpeeny frog of a bog-throtting son of a bloody noun!”﻿—and jist thin what d’ye think it was that her leddyship did? Troth she jumped up from the sofy as if she was bit, and made off through the door, while I turned my head round afther her, in a complate bewilderment and botheration, and followed her wid me two peepers. You percave I had a reason of my own for knowing that she couldn’t git down the stares althegither and intirely; for I knew very well that I had hould of her hand, for the divil the bit had I iver lit it go. And says I:

===Chinese===

「容我奉告，芒瑟梅特迪当斯，」俺说，说得您老人家从没见过的斯文，「像您那样贼眉贼眼盯着太太大人，一点儿也不合体统，压根儿轮不到您这种人。」话音未落，俺把她的手儿又是一捏，那意思无非说：「现在能护着您的，我的宝贝儿，不就是俺帕特里克爵士吗？」跟着手儿里又回来一捏，权当回答。「说得真对，帕特里克爵士，」它说得比世上任何一捏都明白，「说得真对，帕特里克爵士，我的心肝儿，您是位呱呱叫的体面先生——天底下真真如此。」跟着她把两只美丽的眼珠子睁到俺以为要整个儿、彻底儿蹦出她脑壳的地步；先冲青蛙先生狠狠瞪了一眼，跟着又冲俺笑得满园子春光似的。

「那么，」那恶棍说，「哦哟！乌利乌，扑利乌，」跟着耸起两肩，耸得脑壳都瞧不见一星半点，跟着把嘴的两角耷拉下来；那小无赖身上，俺再榨不出半文钱的下文。

相信俺，我的宝贝儿，俺老帕那会儿气得没道理了；更别说那法国佬还冲寡妇挤眼不停；寡妇捏俺的手儿也不停，那意思无非说：「再顶他一下，帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士，我的心肝儿。」于是俺一串大誓咒骂出来，说道：

「你这泥塘客的小青蛙杂碎、血糊淋剌的名词儿养的！」——就在这时您猜她老人家干了什么？真的，她从沙发上蹦起来，像叫蝎子蜇了，夺门而去；俺把她抛在脑后，落个彻底的懵懂与狼狈，两只眼珠子追着她。您瞧明白，俺自有俺的道理知道她跑不完整座楼梯；因为俺知道得清清楚楚，她的手还在俺手里攥着，天打雷劈，俺压根儿没松过。于是俺说：

===Original===

“Isn’t it the laste little bit of a mistake in the world that ye’ve been afther the making, yer leddyship? Come back now, that’s a darlint, and I’ll give ye yur flipper.” But aff she wint down the stairs like a shot, and thin I turned round to the little Frinch furrenner. Och hon! if it wasn’t his spalpeeny little paw that I had hould of in my own﻿—why thin﻿—thin it wasn’t﻿—that’s all.

And maybe it wasn’t mesilf that jist died then outright wid the laffin’, to behold the little chap when he found out that it wasn’t the widdy at all at all that he had had hould of all the time, but only Sir Pathrick O’Grandison. The ould divil himself niver behild sich a long face as he pet an! As for Sir Pathrick O’Grandison, Barronitt, it wasn’t for the likes of his riverence to be afther the minding of a thrifle of a mistake. Ye may jist say, though (for it’s God’s thruth), that afore I left hould of the flipper of the spalpeen (which was not till afther her leddyship’s futman had kicked us both down the stairs), I giv’d it such a nate little broth of a squaze as made it all up into raspberry jam.

“Wouly-wou,” says he, “pully-wou,” says he﻿—“Cot tam!”

And that’s jist the thruth of the rason why he wears his lift hand in a sling.

===Chinese===

「您老人家莫不是弄岔了世上最小的一丁点儿？回来呀，好乖乖，我把您的手儿还您。」可她嗖的一声下了楼梯，俺便转身对着那小法国佬。哦哟！俺手里攥的要是他那小无赖的小爪子——那就——那就不是——就这么回事。

您要是瞧见那小家伙发觉他攥了一路的压根儿不是寡妇，而只是帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士，您保管当场笑断气。老魔鬼本人也憋不出他拉的那张长脸！至于帕特里克·奥格兰迪森爵士、从男爵，他老人家犯不着惦记一星半点儿小误会。不过您可以只管说（这是天底下真真的话）：在俺松开那小无赖的手爪儿之前——直到她老人家家的脚夫把俺们俩踢下楼梯才松——俺给它来了一个漂亮的小捏，捏得它整个儿成了一罐子山莓酱。

「乌利乌，」他说，「扑利乌，」他说——「高当！」

这就是他左手吊在绷带里的缘由的真真下场。

## The Business Man / 生意人
===Original===

Method is the soul of business.

> Old saying

I am a business man. I am a methodical man. Method is the thing, after all. But there are no people I more heartily despise than your eccentric fools who prate about method without understanding it; attending strictly to its letter, and violating its spirit. These fellows are always doing the most out-of-the-way things in what they call an orderly manner. Now here, I conceive, is a positive paradox. True method appertains to the ordinary and the obvious alone, and cannot be applied to the outré. What definite idea can a body attach to such expressions as “methodical Jack o’ Dandy,” or “a systematical Will o’ the Wisp”?

My notions upon this head might not have been so clear as they are, but for a fortunate accident which happened to me when I was a very little boy. A good-hearted old Irish nurse (whom I shall not forget in my will) took me up one day by the heels, when I was making more noise than was necessary, and swinging me round two or three times, d﻿—﻿—﻿d my eyes for “a skreeking little spalpeen,” and then knocked my head into a cocked hat against the bedpost. This, I say, decided my fate, and made my fortune. A bump arose at once on my sinciput, and turned out to be as pretty an organ of *order* as one shall see on a summer’s day. Hence that positive appetite for system and regularity which has made me the distinguished man of business that I am.

===Chinese===

方法乃事业之魂。

> 古谚

我是个生意人。我是个有条理的人。说到底，条理就是一切。可再没有哪种人，比我更打心底里瞧不起你们那些怪僻的傻瓜——他们大谈条理而不懂条理；死守它的字面，违背它的精神。这班人，总是以他们所谓的井然有序，去做最荒唐透顶的事。而这，依我看，是一个十足的悖论。真正的方法，只属于寻常与显然，不能用于怪诞。「有条理的花花公子」「有体系的风火鬼火」这样的话，能叫人联想起什么明确的观念？

我在这方面的见地，原本未必这样清楚，多亏我幼小时遇上一桩侥幸的事故。一位好心的爱尔兰老保姆（我的遗嘱里不会忘了她）见我嚎得超过了必要的份量，有一天拎起我的双脚，抡了两三圈，骂我这「吱哇乱叫的小兔崽子」瞎了眼，随后把我的脑袋往床柱上磕出个三角帽。这一下，我说，定了我的命，成了我的业。我的前囟顿时鼓起一个包，后来证明，那是顶漂亮的一只*秩序*器官，大白天走遍天下也难见到第二只。由此，才有我对体系与规矩的那份绝对的胃口——正是它，造成了今日这位鼎鼎大名的生意人我。

===Original===

If there is anything on earth I hate, it is a genius. Your geniuses are all arrant asses﻿—the greater the genius the greater the ass﻿—and to this rule there is no exception whatever. Especially, you cannot make a man of business out of a genius, any more than money out of a Jew, or the best nutmegs out of pine-knots. The creatures are always going off at a tangent into some fantastic employment, or ridiculous speculation, entirely at variance with the “fitness of things,” and having no business whatever to be considered as a business at all. Thus you may tell these characters immediately by the nature of their occupations. If you ever perceive a man setting up as a merchant or a manufacturer, or going into the cotton or tobacco trade, or any of those eccentric pursuits; or getting to be a drygoods dealer, or soap-boiler, or something of that kind; or pretending to be a lawyer, or a blacksmith, or a physician﻿—anything out of the usual way﻿—you may set him down at once as a genius, and then, according to the rule-of-three, he’s an ass.

===Chinese===

世上若有我恨的东西，那就是天才。你们的天才个个是不折不扣的蠢驴——天才越大，蠢驴越大——此律绝无例外。尤其是，天才做不成生意人，正如犹太人身上榨不出钱，松木疙瘩里榨不出上等肉豆蔻。这班造物，动不动就斜刺里冲进什么稀奇的营生、可笑的投机，全然不合「事物的宜称」，根本算不得一宗生意。所以，看职业就知道这种人。你若见谁当起商人或厂主，或贩棉花烟草，或干任何那类怪营生；或做绸布商、煮皂商，诸如此类；或冒充律师、铁匠、医生——凡出常轨的——你都可立刻断定他是天才；再按三率法一推，他就是一头驴。
