Boats, yachts, and ships have been carried away by not guarding against it before they were within its reach. It likewise happens frequently, that whales come too near the stream, and are overpowered by its violence; and then it is impossible to describe their howlings and bellowings in their fruitless struggles to disengage themselves. A bear once, attempting to swim from Lofoden to Moskoe, was caught by the stream and borne down, while he roared terribly, so as to be heard on shore. Large stocks of firs and pine trees, after being absorbed by the current, rise again broken and torn to such a degree as if bristles grew upon them. This plainly shows the bottom to consist of craggy rocks, among which they are whirled to and fro. This stream is regulated by the flux and reflux of the sea﻿—it being constantly high and low water every six hours. In the year 1645, early in the morning of Sexagesima Sunday, it raged with such noise and impetuosity that the very stones of the houses on the coast fell to the ground.”

===Chinese===

「罗弗敦与莫斯肯之间，」他说，「水深三十六至四十英寻；可另一面朝武尔格那边，水浅得船只不能安稳通过，随时有触岩碎裂之虞，哪怕最风平浪静的天气也难幸免。涨潮时，水流在罗弗敦与莫斯肯之间向内陆奔涌，湍急狂暴；而它退回海里的怒号，差不多连最响最可怕的大瀑布也及不上：几里格外便听得见声。那些漩涡或深坑又那样大、那样深，船只一旦入了它的吸力，便无可避免地被吸下去带到水底，在岩上撞得粉碎；待水势一缓，碎块又被抛回上来。可这些平息的间隙，只在潮水回转之际、天气晴好之时才有，长不过一刻钟，其后猛势渐渐又回。水流最狂、再添风暴助虐之时，靠近它一挪威里之内都是危险。小艇、快船、帆船，都因不及提防，没等到不了它的势力圈就已被掳去。也常有鲸靠得太近，被它的狂力压倒；那时它们挣扎脱身而不得，那种嚎叫吼鸣，无从描画。有一回，一头熊想从罗弗敦游去莫斯肯，被水流逮住卷了下去，一路惨嗥，岸上都听得见。大片大片的枞树松树，被急流吞没之后再浮起来时，断的断、裂的裂，毛刺丛生，仿佛浑身长出了鬃毛。这明白地说明，水底尽是嶙峋乱岩，树干就在其间被搅来搅去。这股水流随海潮涨落而动——每六小时必有一次高低水位。一六四五年七旬主日（Sexagesima Sunday）清晨，它咆哮奔涌得那样凶猛，连海岸上房屋的石头都震落到了地上。」

===Original===

In regard to the depth of the water, I could not see how this could have been ascertained at all in the immediate vicinity of the vortex. The “forty fathoms” must have reference only to portions of the channel close upon the shore either of Moskoe or Lofoden. The depth in the centre of the Moskoe-ström must be immeasurably greater; and no better proof of this fact is necessary than can be obtained from even the sidelong glance into the abyss of the whirl which may be had from the highest crag of Helseggen. Looking down from this pinnacle upon the howling Phlegethon below, I could not help smiling at the simplicity with which the honest Jonas Ramus records, as a matter difficult of belief, the anecdotes of the whales and the bears; for it appeared to me, in fact, a self-evident thing, that the largest ship of the line in existence, coming within the influence of that deadly attraction, could resist it as little as a feather the hurricane, and must disappear bodily and at once.

===Chinese===

至于水的深度，我看不出紧挨漩涡的地方，这深浅究竟是如何测得的。「四十英寻」必定只指紧靠莫斯肯或罗弗敦岸边的那几段水道。莫斯肯漩涡中央的深度，必定深得不可测量；要证明这一点，只消从赫尔塞根最高的峭岩上朝那漩涡的深渊侧里瞥一眼，就尽够了。从这绝顶俯瞰脚底咆哮的弗莱格桑冥河，我不禁失笑——老实的约拿斯·拉穆斯把鲸和熊的逸闻当作难以置信之事记录下来，那份天真实在好笑；因为在我看来，这实在是自明之理：现世最大的战列舰，一入那致命吸力的范围，同羽毛之于飓风一样毫无抵抗，必定整个儿霎时消失。

===Original===

The attempts to account for the phenomenon﻿—some of which, I remember, seemed to me sufficiently plausible in perusal﻿—now wore a very different and unsatisfactory aspect. The idea generally received is that this, as well as three smaller vortices among the Ferroe islands, “have no other cause than the collision of waves rising and falling, at flux and reflux, against a ridge of rocks and shelves, which confines the water so that it precipitates itself like a cataract; and thus the higher the flood rises, the deeper must the fall be, and the natural result of all is a whirlpool or vortex, the prodigious suction of which is sufficiently known by lesser experiments.”﻿—These are the words of the *Encyclopaedia Britannica*. Kircher and others imagine that in the centre of the channel of the Maelström is an abyss penetrating the globe, and issuing in some very remote part﻿—the Gulf of Bothnia being somewhat decidedly named in one instance. This opinion, idle in itself, was the one to which, as I gazed, my imagination most readily assented; and, mentioning it to the guide, I was rather surprised to hear him say that, although it was the view almost universally entertained of the subject by the Norwegians, it nevertheless was not his own. As to the former notion he confessed his inability to comprehend it; and here I agreed with him﻿—for, however conclusive on paper, it becomes altogether unintelligible, and even absurd, amid the thunder of the abyss.

“You have had a good look at the whirl now,” said the old man, “and if you will creep round this crag, so as to get in its lee, and deaden the roar of the water, I will tell you a story that will convince you I ought to know something of the Moskoe-ström.”

I placed myself as desired, and he proceeded.

===Chinese===

为这现象寻找解释的种种尝试——我记得其中有些当初读来还颇为可信——如今在这实景面前，显得多么不同、多么不能令人满意。流行的看法是：这一处，连同法罗群岛三处较小的漩涡，「别无成因，不过是涨落之潮撞上一道岩脊与暗滩而生起的波浪互击；岩脊拦住水，水便如瀑布般直跌下去；潮涨得越高，跌落便越深；这一切的自然结果，便是一个漩涡或涡流，其惊人的吸力，由较小的实验已充分知晓」——这是《不列颠百科全书》的话。基歇尔（Kircher）等人则设想，梅尔斯特罗姆水道的正中央有一个穿透地球的深渊，在极遥远的地方出口——有一处相当肯定的指名，说的便是波的尼亚湾。这意见本身荒唐，可我望着望着，想象力偏偏最容易接受的就是它；说给向导听，我倒有点惊讶地听他说，挪威人几乎众口一词地信这个，他却不然。至于前一种说法，他承认自己无法理解；这一点我同他一致——在纸上无论多么完满的论证，一到这深渊的雷鸣中间，便全然不可解，甚至荒唐了。

「这漩涡你已经看得够仔细了，」老人说，「你要是肯绕到这块岩后面背风的地方，把水声压一压，我就给你讲一段故事，叫你信服：关于莫斯肯漩涡，我理应知道一二。」

我依言坐好，他便讲了起来。

===Original===

“Myself and my two brothers once owned a schooner-rigged smack of about seventy tons burden, with which we were in the habit of fishing among the islands beyond Moskoe, nearly to Vurrgh. In all violent eddies at sea there is good fishing, at proper opportunities, if one has only the courage to attempt it; but among the whole of the Lofoden coastmen, we three were the only ones who made a regular business of going out to the islands, as I tell you. The usual grounds are a great way lower down to the southward. There fish can be got at all hours, without much risk, and therefore these places are preferred. The choice spots over here among the rocks, however, not only yield the finest variety, but in far greater abundance; so that we often got in a single day, what the more timid of the craft could not scrape together in a week. In fact, we made it a matter of desperate speculation﻿—the risk of life standing instead of labor, and courage answering for capital.

“We kept the smack in a cove about five miles higher up the coast than this; and it was our practice, in fine weather, to take advantage of the fifteen minutes’ slack to push across the main channel of the Moskoe-ström, far above the pool, and then drop down upon anchorage somewhere near Otterholm, or Sandflesen, where the eddies are not so violent as elsewhere. Here we used to remain until nearly time for slack-water again, when we weighed and made for home. We never set out upon this expedition without a steady side wind for going and coming﻿—one that we felt sure would not fail us before our return﻿—and we seldom made a miscalculation upon this point. Twice, during six years, we were forced to stay all night at anchor on account of a dead calm, which is a rare thing indeed just about here; and once we had to remain on the grounds nearly a week, starving to death, owing to a gale which blew up shortly after our arrival, and made the channel too boisterous to be thought of. Upon this occasion we should have been driven out to sea in spite of everything, (for the whirlpools threw us round and round so violently, that, at length, we fouled our anchor and dragged it) if it had not been that we drifted into one of the innumerable cross currents﻿—here today and gone tomorrow﻿—which drove us under the lee of Flimen, where, by good luck, we brought up.

===Chinese===

「我和我的两个兄弟，从前合有一条双桅小帆船，七十吨上下，我们惯常驾着它在莫斯肯以远、几乎到武尔格的一带岛屿间打鱼。海上凡有猛涡流的地方，只要时机对头，鱼汛都好，只要人有胆子去碰；可在整个罗弗甸海岸，照例出海到岛边以此为业的，只有我们兄弟三个，这话我告诉你。寻常的渔场，远在往南很远的低处。那里的鱼随时可捕，风险不大，所以人们都拣那些地方。可这边岩间的几处宝地，不但鱼的品种最贵，数量也多得多；我们常常一天里打到的东西，胆小的同行一星期也凑不齐。说实在的，我们把它当作一桩玩命的投机——拿性命的险当本钱使，拿胆量充资本。

「帆船寄泊的小湾，在沿岸再往上五英里左右的地方；天气好时，我们的做法是，趁着十五分钟的平潮，抢渡莫斯肯漩涡的主水道——远远赶到漩涡的上头——然后在奥特尔霍尔姆或桑德弗勒森附近什么地方下锚，那两处的涡流不似别处凶。我们常在那里守到将近下一次平潮，起锚回家。凡做这趟远行，没有一次不等着稳稳的侧风来去——一阵我们拿得准回来之前绝不断的风——这一点上我们很少失算。六年里，有两回赶上风全然不动，不得不在锚地过夜——在这一带这真是稀罕事；还有一回，到渔场不久便起了一场大风，水道闹得不可复想，我们被迫在渔场困了差不多一星期，几乎饿死。那一回，若不是漂进了一股数不清的横流——今日在、明日无——被它送到弗利门的背风面，侥幸在那里停住，我们早被卷出海去了（因为漩涡把船团团转得那样猛，到后来锚索绞缠，锚也拖走了）。

===Original===

“I could not tell you the twentieth part of the difficulties we encountered ‘on the grounds’﻿—it is a bad spot to be in, even in good weather﻿—but we made shift always to run the gauntlet of the Moskoe-ström itself without accident; although at times my heart has been in my mouth when we happened to be a minute or so behind or before the slack. The wind sometimes was not as strong as we thought it at starting, and then we made rather less way than we could wish, while the current rendered the smack unmanageable. My eldest brother had a son eighteen years old, and I had two stout boys of my own. These would have been of great assistance at such times, in using the sweeps, as well as afterward in fishing﻿—but, somehow, although we ran the risk ourselves, we had not the heart to let the young ones get into the danger﻿—for, after all is said and done, it *was* a horrible danger, and that is the truth.

“It is now within a few days of three years since what I am going to tell you occurred. It was on the tenth day of July, 18﻿—, a day which the people of this part of the world will never forget﻿—for it was one in which blew the most terrible hurricane that ever came out of the heavens. And yet all the morning, and indeed until late in the afternoon, there was a gentle and steady breeze from the southwest, while the sun shone brightly, so that the oldest seaman among us could not have foreseen what was to follow.

“The three of us﻿—my two brothers and myself﻿—had crossed over to the islands about two o’clock p.m., and had soon nearly loaded the smack with fine fish, which, we all remarked, were more plenty that day than we had ever known them. It was just seven, *by my watch*, when we weighed and started for home, so as to make the worst of the Ström at slack water, which we knew would be at eight.

===Chinese===

「我们在『渔场』遇到的难处，二十分之一也讲不完给你听——那地方，即使好天气也不是久待之处——但我们总能闯过莫斯肯漩涡这一关而不失事，虽然有几回赶在平潮前后差了一分来钟，我的心都提到了嗓子眼。风有时不像出发时估量的那样劲，船便走得比心愿的慢些，水流又把船弄得难于驾驭。我大哥有个十八岁的儿子，我自己也有两个壮实的男孩。赶上这种时候，让他们帮着摇橹，过后帮着下线，原是得力不过的——可是不知怎么，虽然我们自己舍命，却狠不下心叫小的们蹈这个险——因为归根结底，这实实在在是个可怕的险，一点不假。

「离我此刻要讲的事发生，只差几天就满三年了。那是七月十日，一八——年，这一带的人永远不会忘记的一天——因为那一天刮起了开天辟地以来天上放出的最可怕的一场飓风。可是整整一个上午，直到下半晌，西南风温温顺顺、匀匀净净地吹着，太阳又亮，连我们中间最老的水手也断不能料到接下去的事。

「我们三个——我的两个兄弟和我——下午两点左右渡到了岛边，不多时便几乎给小帆船装满了上好的鱼；我们都留意到，那天的鱼比我们记忆里任何时候都多。七点整——照我的表——我们起锚回家，好赶在八点的平潮闯过漩涡最凶的一段，这个钟点我们是有数的。」

===Original===

“We set out with a fresh wind on our starboard quarter, and for some time spanked along at a great rate, never dreaming of danger, for indeed we saw not the slightest reason to apprehend it. All at once we were taken aback by a breeze from over Helseggen. This was most unusual﻿—something that had never happened to us before﻿—and I began to feel a little uneasy, without exactly knowing why. We put the boat on the wind, but could make no headway at all for the eddies, and I was upon the point of proposing to return to the anchorage, when, looking astern, we saw the whole horizon covered with a singular copper-colored cloud that rose with the most amazing velocity.

“In the meantime the breeze that had headed us off fell away, and we were dead becalmed, drifting about in every direction. This state of things, however, did not last long enough to give us time to think about it. In less than a minute the storm was upon us﻿—in less than two the sky was entirely overcast﻿—and what with this and the driving spray, it became suddenly so dark that we could not see each other in the smack.

“Such a hurricane as then blew it is folly to attempt describing. The oldest seaman in Norway never experienced anything like it. We had let our sails go by the run before it cleverly took us; but, at the first puff, both our masts went by the board as if they had been sawed off﻿—the mainmast taking with it my youngest brother, who had lashed himself to it for safety.

“Our boat was the lightest feather of a thing that ever sat upon water. It had a complete flush deck, with only a small hatch near the bow, and this hatch it had always been our custom to batten down when about to cross the Ström, by way of precaution against the chopping seas. But for this circumstance we should have foundered at once﻿—for we lay entirely buried for some moments. How my elder brother escaped destruction I cannot say, for I never had an opportunity of ascertaining. For my part, as soon as I had let the foresail run, I threw myself flat on deck, with my feet against the narrow gunwale of the bow, and with my hands grasping a ring-bolt near the foot of the foremast. It was mere instinct that prompted me to do this﻿—which was undoubtedly the very best thing I could have done﻿—for I was too much flurried to think.

===Chinese===

「出发时一股新风送在右舷侧后方，有一阵子船走得飞快，我们压根儿没想到危险，实在也看不出丝毫该当提防的因由。冷不防，一阵从赫尔塞根那边刮过来的风打得我们措手不及。这太反常了——从来没在我们身上出过这样的事——我心里开始有点发毛，又说不清为什么。我们转舵迎风，却因为涡流一团团搅着，半点也前进不得。我正打算提议退回锚地去，朝船尾一望，只见整个地平线上腾起一片古怪的铜色云，上升的速度骇人。

「这时候，顶头的那阵风息了，我们落在完全的死静里，四面八方地漂。这光景持续得又短，短得不容我们细想。不到一分钟，风暴扑到了身上——不到两分钟，天全然阴合一一再加上横扫的浪沫，天色骤然黑下来，船上彼此都看不见了。

「那时刮起的那场飓风，想描画它是痴心妄想。挪威最老的水手也不曾经历过那样的。我们没等它正式逮住，早已一放了帆；可第一阵狂风打来，两根桅杆便一齐折断落水，仿佛锯断的一般——主桅带走了我最小的兄弟，他为了保险把自己绑在桅杆上了。

「我们这条船，是浮在水上的东西里最轻飘的一根羽毛。它通体是齐平的甲板，只在船头附近留一个小舱口；每逢要渡漩涡，照老规矩把这个舱口钉死，防备碎乱的浪头。若没有这一着，我们当场就沉了——因为有一阵子船整个儿埋在水里。我大哥怎么逃过这一劫的，我说不上，一直无从打听。至于我自己，前帆一放，我就整个人平贴在甲板上，双脚抵住船头窄窄的舷缘，双手攥住前桅脚旁的一枚系环螺栓。这么做什么纯出本能——而它无疑是我所能做的再好不过的事——因为我早已慌得失了思考。」

===Original===

“For some moments we were completely deluged, as I say, and all this time I held my breath, and clung to the bolt. When I could stand it no longer I raised myself upon my knees, still keeping hold with my hands, and thus got my head clear. Presently our little boat gave herself a shake, just as a dog does in coming out of the water, and thus rid herself, in some measure, of the seas. I was now trying to get the better of the stupor that had come over me, and to collect my senses so as to see what was to be done, when I felt somebody grasp my arm. It was my elder brother, and my heart leaped for joy, for I had made sure that he was overboard﻿—but the next moment all this joy was turned into horror﻿—for he put his mouth close to my ear, and screamed out the word ‘*Moskoe-ström!*’

“No one ever will know what my feelings were at that moment. I shook from head to foot as if I had had the most violent fit of the ague. I knew what he meant by that one word well enough﻿—I knew what he wished to make me understand. With the wind that now drove us on, we were bound for the whirl of the Ström, and nothing could save us!

“You perceive that in crossing the Ström *channel*, we always went a long way up above the whirl, even in the calmest weather, and then had to wait and watch carefully for the slack﻿—but now we were driving right upon the pool itself, and in such a hurricane as this! ‘To be sure,’ I thought, ‘we shall get there just about the slack﻿—there is some little hope in that’﻿—but in the next moment I cursed myself for being so great a fool as to dream of hope at all. I knew very well that we were doomed, had we been ten times a ninety-gun ship.

“By this time the first fury of the tempest had spent itself, or perhaps we did not feel it so much, as we scudded before it, but at all events the seas, which at first had been kept down by the wind, and lay flat and frothing, now got up into absolute mountains. A singular change, too, had come over the heavens. Around in every direction it was still as black as pitch, but nearly overhead there burst out, all at once, a circular rift of clear sky﻿—as clear as I ever saw﻿—and of a deep bright blue﻿—and through it there blazed forth the full moon with a lustre that I never before knew her to wear. She lit up everything about us with the greatest distinctness﻿—but, oh God, what a scene it was to light up!

===Chinese===

「有一阵子，如我所说，我们整个儿没在水里；这全部时间我屏住呼吸，攥着螺栓。憋不住时，我双膝撑起身子，两手仍不放，头才探出了水。不多时，我们的小船自己一抖，像狗出水时那样，多少甩掉了些海水。我正想压下麻木、收拢神智看看该做什么，忽觉有人攥住我的臂膀。是我大哥；我的心欢喜得直跳，我还道他早落了水——可下一刻，欢喜尽数变成了恐怖——他把嘴贴到我耳边，尖声喊出一个词：『莫斯肯漩涡！』

「谁也不会知道我那一刻的心情。我从头到脚抖起来，像打最凶的寒战。他这一个词的意思，我懂得再透不过——他要我明白的是什么，我懂得。照如今送着我们跑的这风，我们正对着漩涡的旋口去，什么也救不了我们！

「你晓得，往常渡漩涡水道时，哪怕最静的天，我们也总先赶到漩涡上方老远的地方，再仔细候着平潮——可现在，我们竟是直往涡口上冲，又顶着这样一场飓风！『也好，』我想，『我们赶到的时辰大约正在平潮——这总算有一点指望』——可下一刻我就咒骂自己，骂自己蠢到竟还做梦指望。我清楚得很，我们是定了死罪的，哪怕我们是一条九十炮战列舰的十倍。

「到这时，风暴最初一股狂劲已经泄了——也许是我们顺风逃着，不很觉得了——但不管怎样，起初被风压平、伏着白沫的海面，如今耸成了实实在在的群山。天上也起了一番奇异的变化。四下里依旧黑得像沥青，可头顶近处，蓦地绽开一圈晴空——晴得我从没见过——深湛、明亮的一片蓝——满月从那里迸射出来，带着我从不曾见它有过的光华。它把我们四周的一切照得纤毫毕现——可是，上帝啊，它照亮的是怎样一幅景象！」

===Original===

“I now made one or two attempts to speak to my brother﻿—but, in some manner which I could not understand, the din had so increased that I could not make him hear a single word, although I screamed at the top of my voice in his ear. Presently he shook his head, looking as pale as death, and held up one of his fingers, as if to say *‘listen!’*

“At first I could not make out what he meant﻿—but soon a hideous thought flashed upon me. I dragged my watch from its fob. It was not going. I glanced at its face by the moonlight, and then burst into tears as I flung it far away into the ocean. *It had run down at seven o’clock! We were behind the time of the slack, and the whirl of the Ström was in full fury!*

“When a boat is well built, properly trimmed, and not deep laden, the waves in a strong gale, when she is going large, seem always to slip from beneath her﻿—which appears very strange to a landsman﻿—and this is what is called *riding*, in sea phrase.

“Well, so far we had ridden the swells very cleverly; but presently a gigantic sea happened to take us right under the counter, and bore us with it as it rose﻿—up﻿—up﻿—as if into the sky. I would not have believed that any wave could rise so high. And then down we came with a sweep, a slide, and a plunge, that made me feel sick and dizzy, as if I was falling from some lofty mountaintop in a dream. But while we were up I had thrown a quick glance around﻿—and that one glance was all sufficient. I saw our exact position in an instant. The Moskoe-Ström whirlpool was about a quarter of a mile dead ahead﻿—but no more like the everyday Moskoe-Ström than the whirl, as you now see it, is like a millrace. If I had not known where we were, and what we had to expect, I should not have recognised the place at all. As it was, I involuntarily closed my eyes in horror. The lids clenched themselves together as if in a spasm.

===Chinese===

「我这时想跟大哥说一两句话——可不知怎么，喧声涨得那样厉害，我把嗓门叫到顶，贴着他耳朵喊，他也听不见一个字。不久他摇了摇头，脸白得像死人，竖起一根手指，像是在说『听！』

「起初我明白不过来他的意思——可紧跟着，一个可怖的念头闪过。我从表袋里拽出表。表停了。我借月光看了一眼表盘，随即含着泪把它远远抛进了大海。它七点钟就停了！我们误过了平潮的时辰，莫斯肯漩涡正当全盛的狂怒！

「一条船，只要造得好、配载匀、吃水不深，在大风里顺风疾走时，浪仿佛总从船底滑脱开去——在岸上人看来非常奇怪——这就是海上话里说的『骑浪』。

「我们就这样一直很巧妙地骑在浪头上；可猛然间，一道天大的浪从船尾底下把船兜住，托着它一道升起——升——升——仿佛要升进天里。我从不知道浪能起这样高。随即我们一滑一坠地泻下来，坠得我又晕又恶心，像梦里从高山顶上跌落。可趁船在浪尖上时，我飞快朝四下一扫——就这一眼，尽够了。我霎时看清了我们的准确位置。莫斯肯大漩涡在正前方四分之一英里——可它同平日的莫斯肯漩涡，再无一分相像，正如你此刻见的这个大旋流同一条磨坊水道不相像一样。若不是我早知道身在何处、当有何等下场，我根本认不得这地方。即便认得，我也吓得不由自主闭上眼。眼皮像痉挛似的死死阖住。」

===Original===

“It could not have been more than two minutes afterward until we suddenly felt the waves subside, and were enveloped in foam. The boat made a sharp half turn to larboard, and then shot off in its new direction like a thunderbolt. At the same moment the roaring noise of the water was completely drowned in a kind of shrill shriek﻿—such a sound as you might imagine given out by the waste-pipes of many thousand steam-vessels, letting off their steam all together. We were now in the belt of surf that always surrounds the whirl; and I thought, of course, that another moment would plunge us into the abyss, down which we could only see indistinctly on account of the amazing velocity with which we wore borne along. The boat did not seem to sink into the water at all, but to skim like an air-bubble upon the surface of the surge. Her starboard side was next the whirl, and on the larboard arose the world of ocean we had left. It stood like a huge writhing wall between us and the horizon.

“It may appear strange, but now, when we were in the very jaws of the gulf, I felt more composed than when we were only approaching it. Having made up my mind to hope no more, I got rid of a great deal of that terror which unmanned me at first. I suppose it was despair that strung my nerves.

“It may look like boasting﻿—but what I tell you is truth﻿—I began to reflect how magnificent a thing it was to die in such a manner, and how foolish it was in me to think of so paltry a consideration as my own individual life, in view of so wonderful a manifestation of God’s power. I do believe that I blushed with shame when this idea crossed my mind. After a little while I became possessed with the keenest curiosity about the whirl itself. I positively felt a *wish* to explore its depths, even at the sacrifice I was going to make; and my principal grief was that I should never be able to tell my old companions on shore about the mysteries I should see. These, no doubt, were singular fancies to occupy a man’s mind in such extremity﻿—and I have often thought since, that the revolutions of the boat around the pool might have rendered me a little lightheaded.

===Chinese===

「此后决计不过两分钟，我们忽然觉得浪平了，四围裹满了白沫。船向左舷猛地掉转半个身位，随即像雷霆一样朝新方向射去。同一刻，水的咆哮全然淹灭在一种锐利的啸声里——那声音，你可以想象成几千条轮船的排水管一齐放开蒸汽。我们这时进了终日环绕漩涡的那圈浪沫带；我自然以为下一刻便要坠进深渊——因为船被带走得快极，深渊底下只能迷迷糊糊望见。船似乎全然不是往水里沉，倒像一颗气泡在浪面上滑掠。右舷朝着漩涡，左舷一侧耸立着我们离开的那片海洋世界。它像一堵扭动的高墙，立在我们与天际线之间。

「说来奇怪，如今身在海湾的正咽喉里，我反倒比将到未到的时候镇定了。横下心不再指望，起初那种卸掉人胆的恐怖倒去了一大半。想是绝望绷紧了我的神经。

「这听着像吹嘘——可我告诉你的是实话——我开始琢磨，这样死去是多么壮丽的一件事；在上帝威力这样一场奇观面前，还惦记我自己这条微不足道的性命，又是多么愚蠢。这个念头掠过心头时，我相信自己是羞红了脸。过不多时，我对漩涡本身起了最强烈的好奇。我当真生出一个愿望，想去探一探它的深底，哪怕拿我即将付出的牺牲来换；而我最大的悲哀是，我将永远不能把亲眼所见的奥秘，讲给我岸上的老伙计们听了。这些，无疑是一个人身临绝境时最古怪的念头——后来我常想，小船绕着涡口那一圈圈转，怕是把我转得有些头轻了。」

===Original===

“There was another circumstance which tended to restore my self-possession; and this was the cessation of the wind, which could not reach us in our present situation﻿—for, as you saw yourself, the belt of surf is considerably lower than the general bed of the ocean, and this latter now towered above us, a high, black, mountainous ridge. If you have never been at sea in a heavy gale, you can form no idea of the confusion of mind occasioned by the wind and spray together. They blind, deafen, and strangle you, and take away all power of action or reflection. But we were now, in a great measure, rid of these annoyances﻿—just as death-condemned felons in prison are allowed petty indulgences, forbidden them while their doom is yet uncertain.

“How often we made the circuit of the belt it is impossible to say. We careered round and round for perhaps an hour, flying rather than floating, getting gradually more and more into the middle of the surge, and then nearer and nearer to its horrible inner edge. All this time I had never let go of the ring-bolt. My brother was at the stern, holding on to a small empty water-cask which had been securely lashed under the coop of the counter, and was the only thing on deck that had not been swept overboard when the gale first took us. As we approached the brink of the pit he let go his hold upon this, and made for the ring, from which, in the agony of his terror, he endeavored to force my hands, as it was not large enough to afford us both a secure grasp. I never felt deeper grief than when I saw him attempt this act﻿—although I knew he was a madman when he did it﻿—a raving maniac through sheer fright. I did not care, however, to contest the point with him. I knew it could make no difference whether either of us held on at all; so I let him have the bolt, and went astern to the cask. This there was no great difficulty in doing; for the smack flew round steadily enough, and upon an even keel﻿—only swaying to and fro, with the immense sweeps and swelters of the whirl. Scarcely had I secured myself in my new position, when we gave a wild lurch to starboard, and rushed headlong into the abyss. I muttered a hurried prayer to God, and thought all was over.

===Chinese===

「还有一桩情形帮我找回了自己的镇定：风停了——我们如今的位置，风已经够不着——因为你自己也看见了，那圈浪沫带比大洋的一般床面低得多，此刻海面高高耸在我们头顶，成了一道黑黑的高山脊。你若没在大风里出过海，便想不来风和浪沫合起来能叫人多糊涂。它们叫你瞎、叫你聋、叫你喘不上气，夺走你行动和思考的一切力气。可这些苦恼我们如今大半免了——正如定了死罪的囚犯，在刑期未定之前不许的那些小宽纵，倒许给了他们。

「这条浪带我们绕了多少圈，说不清。我们飞转了约莫一个钟头——是飞，不是浮——渐渐进入浪带的中部，又渐渐挨近那可怖的内缘。这全部时间我没撒过那枚系环螺栓。我兄弟在船尾，抱着一只捆牢在尾舱顶下的小空水桶——全船甲板上，初遭风袭时唯一没扫下海去的东西。挨到深渊的口沿，他撒开桶，扑向那枚环，在恐怖的极痛里，硬掰我抓环的手——环不够大，容不得两个人抓牢。我看他这般行事，心里的悲恸再没有更深过——虽然我明白，他这样做时是个疯子——一个纯然吓出来的狂人。可我不愿同他争这个。我晓得我们两个抓不抓，结局毫无二致；我便把螺栓让给他，自己到船尾去抱桶。这并不难办到；小船转得相当平稳，龙骨也平——只是随漩涡巨大的扫荡与翻滚来回摇摆。我刚在新位置上站稳，船便向右舷疯狂地一侧，一头栽进了深渊。我匆匆向上帝念了一句祷词，心想一切都完了。」

===Original===

“As I felt the sickening sweep of the descent, I had instinctively tightened my hold upon the barrel, and closed my eyes. For some seconds I dared not open them﻿—while I expected instant destruction, and wondered that I was not already in my death-struggles with the water. But moment after moment elapsed. I still lived. The sense of falling had ceased; and the motion of the vessel seemed much as it had been before, while in the belt of foam, with the exception that she now lay more along. I took courage, and looked once again upon the scene.

“Never shall I forget the sensations of awe, horror, and admiration with which I gazed about me. The boat appeared to be hanging, as if by magic, midway down, upon the interior surface of a funnel vast in circumference, prodigious in depth, and whose perfectly smooth sides might have been mistaken for ebony, but for the bewildering rapidity with which they spun around, and for the gleaming and ghastly radiance they shot forth, as the rays of the full moon, from that circular rift amid the clouds which I have already described, streamed in a flood of golden glory along the black walls, and far away down into the inmost recesses of the abyss.

“At first I was too much confused to observe anything accurately. The general burst of terrific grandeur was all that I beheld. When I recovered myself a little, however, my gaze fell instinctively downward. In this direction I was able to obtain an unobstructed view, from the manner in which the smack hung on the inclined surface of the pool. She was quite upon an even keel﻿—that is to say, her deck lay in a plane parallel with that of the water﻿—but this latter sloped at an angle of more than forty-five degrees, so that we seemed to be lying upon our beam-ends. I could not help observing, nevertheless, that I had scarcely more difficulty in maintaining my hold and footing in this situation, than if we had been upon a dead level; and this, I suppose, was owing to the speed at which we revolved.

===Chinese===

「坠落的那阵眩晕恶心袭来时，我本能地把桶搂得更紧，闭上了眼。有几秒钟我不敢睁开——只等着立时的毁灭，奇怪自己怎么还没有在水里作垂死的挣扎。可一刻又一刻过去了。我还活着。坠落的感觉停了；船的动静同先前在泡沫带里时差不多，只是船身更侧了些。我壮起胆，再朝景象看了一眼。

「我四下仰望时那种敬畏、恐怖与赞叹交缠的感受，永远不会忘记。小船像着了魔法，悬在这漏斗内壁的半腰上——那漏斗周围浩阔、深不可测，内壁光滑得同乌木一般，要不是它旋得那样炫目地快，要不是满月从我已说过那圈云间裂口泼下来的光，顺着黑墙泻成一道金辉，直透进深渊最深的隐处，映得四壁幽幽放光，你真会把它错当成乌木。

「起初我慌乱得看不清什么。只看见一片惊心动魄的壮阔。等我稍稍定住，目光便本能地落向下方。多亏小船悬在倾斜的涡面上，这个方向我看得毫无遮拦。船身相当平——就是说，甲板与水面平行——可水面斜得过了四十五度，我们像是船梁着地侧躺着一样。饶是这样，我发觉在这位置上把稳抓牢，竟同站在死平地上差不多一样不难；我想，这是全亏我们旋转得快。」

===Original===

“The rays of the moon seemed to search the very bottom of the profound gulf; but still I could make out nothing distinctly, on account of a thick mist in which everything there was enveloped, and over which there hung a magnificent rainbow, like that narrow and tottering bridge which Mussulmen say is the only pathway between Time and Eternity. This mist, or spray, was no doubt occasioned by the clashing of the great walls of the funnel, as they all met together at the bottom﻿—but the yell that went up to the Heavens from out of that mist, I dare not attempt to describe.

“Our first slide into the abyss itself, from the belt of foam above, had carried us a great distance down the slope; but our farther descent was by no means proportionate. Round and round we swept﻿—not with any uniform movement﻿—but in dizzying swings and jerks, that sent us sometimes only a few hundred yards﻿—sometimes nearly the complete circuit of the whirl. Our progress downward, at each revolution, was slow, but very perceptible.

“Looking about me upon the wide waste of liquid ebony on which we were thus borne, I perceived that our boat was not the only object in the embrace of the whirl. Both above and below us were visible fragments of vessels, large masses of building timber and trunks of trees, with many smaller articles, such as pieces of house furniture, broken boxes, barrels and staves. I have already described the unnatural curiosity which had taken the place of my original terrors. It appeared to grow upon me as I drew nearer and nearer to my dreadful doom. I now began to watch, with a strange interest, the numerous things that floated in our company. I *must* have been delirious, for I even sought *amusement* in speculating upon the relative velocities of their several descents toward the foam below. ‘This fir tree,’ I found myself at one time saying, ‘will certainly be the next thing that takes the awful plunge and disappears,’﻿—and then I was disappointed to find that the wreck of a Dutch merchant ship overtook it and went down before. At length, after making several guesses of this nature, and being deceived in all﻿—this fact﻿—the fact of my invariable miscalculation, set me upon a train of reflection that made my limbs again tremble, and my heart beat heavily once more.

===Chinese===

「月光仿佛一直照透了深渊的底；可我仍旧什么也辨不清，因为底下的一切裹在一层浓雾里，雾顶上悬着一道壮丽的虹，正像穆斯林说的那座窄而摇摇欲坠的桥——光阴与永恒之间唯一的路径。这雾，或者说浪沫，无疑是漏斗四壁在渊底相撞而生；可从那雾里冲上天的嚎声，我不敢试着描画。

「从上面的泡沫带滑进深渊的第一下，把我们送下了斜坡好远；可再往下的降坠，就全不成比例了。我们一圈圈地绕——并不匀净——一阵晕眩的摆荡和颠动，有时只送出几百码，有时几乎绕满整整一圈。每绕一转，向下的路都慢，却看得清清楚楚。

「我扫视这片驮着我们的黑玉般的茫茫水面，发觉陷在漩涡怀抱里的，不止我们一条船。上上下下，都漂着船的碎块、大堆的建筑木料和整根的树干，还有许多零碎物件——家具的残件、破箱子、桶和桶板。我已说过，早先的恐怖让位给了一种反常的好奇；越临近我可怕的下场，它仿佛越盛。我开始怀着一种怪异的兴味，端详同我们一起漂的这许多东西。我必定是疯了，因为我竟拿它们各自坠向下头白沫的快慢打趣取乐。『这棵枞树，』我发现自己有一回说，『必定是下一个栽下去没顶的。』——随后我便失望地发现，一条荷兰商船的残骸赶过了它，先沉了下去。这样猜了几回，回回落空——正是这个事实——我一向失算的这个事实，引出我一路思索，使我四肢重新发抖，心重新沉重地跳。」

===Original===

“It was not a new terror that thus affected me, but the dawn of a more exciting *hope*. This hope arose partly from memory, and partly from present observation. I called to mind the great variety of buoyant matter that strewed the coast of Lofoden, having been absorbed and then thrown forth by the Moskoe-ström. By far the greater number of the articles were shattered in the most extraordinary way﻿—so chafed and roughened as to have the appearance of being stuck full of splinters﻿—but then I distinctly recollected that there were *some* of them which were not disfigured at all. Now I could not account for this difference except by supposing that the roughened fragments were the only ones which had been *completely absorbed*﻿—that the others had entered the whirl at so late a period of the tide, or, for some reason, had descended so slowly after entering, that they did not reach the bottom before the turn of the flood came, or of the ebb, as the case might be. I conceived it possible, in either instance, that they might thus be whirled up again to the level of the ocean, without undergoing the fate of those which had been drawn in more early, or absorbed more rapidly. I made, also, three important observations. The first was, that, as a general rule, the larger the bodies were, the more rapid their descent﻿—the second, that, between two masses of equal extent, the one spherical, and the other *of any other shape*, the superiority in speed of descent was with the sphere﻿—the third, that, between two masses of equal size, the one cylindrical, and the other of any other shape, the cylinder was absorbed the more slowly. Since my escape, I have had several conversations on this subject with an old schoolmaster of the district; and it was from him that I learned the use of the words ‘cylinder’ and ‘sphere.’ He explained to me﻿—although I have forgotten the explanation﻿—how what I observed was, in fact, the natural consequence of the forms of the floating fragments﻿—and showed me how it happened that a cylinder, swimming in a vortex, offered more resistance to its suction, and was drawn in with greater difficulty than an equally bulky body, of any form whatever.18

===Chinese===

「教我如此震动的，不是新的恐怖，而是一种更教人兴奋的希望的萌动。这希望，一半来自记忆，一半来自眼前的观察。我想起罗弗敦沿岸散布的那许多浮物——都是被莫斯肯漩涡吞下又吐出来的。其中绝大多数碎裂得不可想象——磨得毛毛糙糙，浑身像插满了木刺——可我又分明记得，其中有一些竟毫无损伤。这差别，我只能这样解释：磨伤的碎片是彻底吞到过底的；另一些，或是入涡时潮时已晚，或是入涡后坠得慢，不等洪潮回转——或按情形，不等落潮回转——便没到得了底。我设想，无论哪种情形，它们都可能这样被重新旋上海面，免掉那些入涡早、被吸得快的东西的命运。我还作了三项重要的观察。第一，大体而论，物体越大，坠得越快；第二，两块等大的东西，一块球形，另一块无论什么形状，先坠下去的是球；第三，两块等大的东西，一块圆柱形，另一块无论什么形状，圆柱被吸得最慢。脱险以后，我就这个题目同本乡一位老塾师谈过几回；圆柱、球体这些词，就是从他那里学来的。他给我讲解过——尽管讲解我已忘了——我所观察到的，实是漂浮物形状的自然结果；他还指点我，为什么一条圆柱在漩涡里，对吸力的抵抗比任何同等大小的别种形体都大，被吸入也更难。［18］

===Original===

“There was one startling circumstance which went a great way in enforcing these observations, and rendering me anxious to turn them to account, and this was that, at every revolution, we passed something like a barrel, or else the yard or the mast of a vessel, while many of these things, which had been on our level when I first opened my eyes upon the wonders of the whirlpool, were now high up above us, and seemed to have moved but little from their original station.

“I no longer hesitated what to do. I resolved to lash myself securely to the water cask upon which I now held, to cut it loose from the counter, and to throw myself with it into the water. I attracted my brother’s attention by signs, pointed to the floating barrels that came near us, and did everything in my power to make him understand what I was about to do. I thought at length that he comprehended my design﻿—but, whether this was the case or not, he shook his head despairingly, and refused to move from his station by the ring-bolt. It was impossible to reach him; the emergency admitted of no delay; and so, with a bitter struggle, I resigned him to his fate, fastened myself to the cask by means of the lashings which secured it to the counter, and precipitated myself with it into the sea, without another moment’s hesitation.

===Chinese===

「还有一桩触目的情形，大大印证了这些观察，教我一心想拿它们派上用场：船每绕一转，我们都要超过一只桶，或者一根船的横桁、桅杆之类的东西；而其中许多，在我睁眼初见这奇观时分明同我们一般高低的，如今已高悬在我们上方，似乎还不曾怎么挪离原位。

「我不再迟疑该做什么了。我决意把自己牢牢绑在怀里这只水桶上，把它从船尾割断，连同自己一起抛进海里。我打手势唤起我兄弟的注意，指给他看漂近我们的那些桶，使出浑身解数叫他明白我要做什么。后来我以为他懂了我的打算——可是懂也罢，不懂也罢，他绝望地摇了摇头，不肯离开那枚系环螺栓半步。够也够不着他；事急不容再拖；于是，经历一场惨痛的挣扎，我把他交给了他的命——用拴桶的索子把自己缚在桶上，毫不迟疑，连人带桶扑进了大海。」

===Original===

“The result was precisely what I had hoped it might be. As it is myself who now tell you this tale﻿—as you see that I *did* escape﻿—and as you are already in possession of the mode in which this escape was effected, and must therefore anticipate all that I have farther to say﻿—I will bring my story quickly to conclusion. It might have been an hour, or thereabout, after my quitting the smack, when, having descended to a vast distance beneath me, it made three or four wild gyrations in rapid succession, and, bearing my loved brother with it, plunged headlong, at once and forever, into the chaos of foam below. The barrel to which I was attached sunk very little farther than half the distance between the bottom of the gulf and the spot at which I leaped overboard, before a great change took place in the character of the whirlpool. The slope of the sides of the vast funnel became momently less and less steep. The gyrations of the whirl grew, gradually, less and less violent. By degrees, the froth and the rainbow disappeared, and the bottom of the gulf seemed slowly to uprise. The sky was clear, the winds had gone down, and the full moon was setting radiantly in the west, when I found myself on the surface of the ocean, in full view of the shores of Lofoden, and above the spot where the pool of the Moskoe-ström *had been*. It was the hour of the slack﻿—but the sea still heaved in mountainous waves from the effects of the hurricane. I was borne violently into the channel of the Ström, and in a few minutes was hurried down the coast into the ‘grounds’ of the fishermen. A boat picked me up﻿—exhausted from fatigue﻿—and (now that the danger was removed) speechless from the memory of its horror. Those who drew me on board were my old mates and daily companions﻿—but they knew me no more than they would have known a traveller from the spirit-land. My hair which had been raven-black the day before, was as white as you see it now. They say too that the whole expression of my countenance had changed. I told them my story﻿—they did not believe it. I now tell it to *you*﻿—and I can scarcely expect you to put more faith in it than did the merry fishermen of Lofoden.”

===Chinese===

「结果正同我指望的一样。既然如今讲述这段故事的是我本人——既然你看见我确实脱了险——既然脱险的门道你已了然，往下要说的你自然也能料到——我便把故事快快收梢。离船大约一个钟头，也许还不到，小船在我脚下极深的深处，急速地打了三四个疯转，载着我亲爱的兄弟，一头栽进下方的泡沫乱阵，永劫不复了。我绑着的那只桶，沉到跳海处与渊底距离的一半稍多，还不到底，漩涡的性质便起了大变。巨漏斗四壁的坡度，一刻缓似一刻；漩涡的回旋，渐渐一缓一缓地弱下去。泡沫和虹先后隐去，渊底仿佛缓缓隆起。天上晴了，风息了，满月在西天明晃晃地沉落，这时我发觉自己已浮上海面，罗弗敦的岸望得清清楚楚，正罩在莫斯肯漩涡方才盘踞的位置上。正是平潮的时辰——飓风过后的海，还耸着山一样的浪。我被凶猛地卷进漩涡水道，不出几分钟，便顺流被赶下海岸，进了渔人们的『渔场』。一条船把我捞了上去——我已力竭——（险既已过）一想起那恐怖，便说不出话。把我拖上船的，是我多年的老伙计、朝夕的同伴——可他们认不得我了，同认不得一个从阴间来的客不相上下。我的头发，前一天还是鸦黑的，已白得同你现在见的一样。他们还说，我整张脸的神情都变了。我把我的故事讲给他们听——他们不信。如今我讲给你听——我也很难指望你，比罗弗敦那些快活的渔人更多信我几分。」

## The Island of the Fay / 仙灵岛
===Original===

Nullus enim locus sine genio est.

> Servius

“La musique,” says Marmontel, in those *Contes Moraux*19 which in all our translations, we have insisted upon calling *Moral Tales*, as if in mockery of their spirit﻿—“la musique est le seul des talents qui jouissent de lui même; tous les autres veulent des temoins.” He here confounds the pleasure derivable from sweet sounds with the capacity for creating them. No more than any other talent, is that for music susceptible of complete enjoyment, where there is no second party to appreciate its exercise. And it is only in common with other talents that it produces *effects* which may be fully enjoyed in solitude. The idea which the raconteur has either failed to entertain clearly, or has sacrificed in its expression to his national love of *point*, is, doubtless, the very tenable one that the higher order of music is the most thoroughly estimated when we are exclusively alone. The proposition, in this form, will be admitted at once by those who love the lyre for its own sake, and for its spiritual uses. But there is one pleasure still within the reach of fallen mortality and perhaps only one﻿—which owes even more than does music to the accessory sentiment of seclusion. I mean the happiness experienced in the contemplation of natural scenery. In truth, the man who would behold aright the glory of God upon earth must in solitude behold that glory. To me, at least, the presence﻿—not of human life only, but of life in any other form than that of the green things which grow upon the soil and are voiceless﻿—is a stain upon the landscape﻿—is at war with the genius of the scene.

===Chinese===

没有一处地方没有它的精灵。

——塞尔维乌斯（Servius）

「音乐，」马蒙泰尔（Marmontel）在他那部*Contes Moraux*〔19〕里说——在我们全部的译本里，我们一味坚持把它称作《道德故事》，仿佛存心嘲弄它们的精神——「音乐是唯一以自身为乐的才能；其余一切才能都要有见证人。」他在这里把悦耳之声可得的快乐，同创造它们的能力混为一谈。同任何其他才能一样，音乐的才能若没有第二个人来领略它的运用，便无从得到完全的享受。它同其他才能共同的地方，只在它产生那种可以在孤独中充分享受的*效果*。这位说故事的人或者不曾清晰地怀有那个念头，或者在表达时把它牺牲给他那个民族对*俏皮*的酷爱——那念头无疑极站得住：高级的音乐，在我们全然独自一人时，才得到最彻底的领会。这个命题，凡为竖琴本身、为它精神的用途而爱它的人，会立刻承认。但仍有一种快乐，堕落的人性还够得着——或许仅此一种——它比音乐更亏欠隐逸这份助成的情味。我说的是观照自然景色时体验到的幸福。实在说，要在地上正当地看见上帝的荣耀，人必须在孤独里看那荣耀。至少对我，在场的东西——不但人类生命，而且任何非青绿之物、任何有声的生命形式的存在——都是景致上的一块污渍——都是同这场景的精灵交战。

===Original===

I love, indeed, to regard the dark valleys, and the gray rocks, and the waters that silently smile, and the forests that sigh in uneasy slumbers, and the proud watchful mountains that look down upon all﻿—I love to regard these as themselves but the colossal members of one vast animate and sentient whole﻿—a whole whose form (that of the sphere) is the most perfect and most inclusive of all; whose path is among associate planets; whose meek handmaiden is the moon, whose mediate sovereign is the sun; whose life is eternity, whose thought is that of a God; whose enjoyment is knowledge; whose destinies are lost in immensity, whose cognizance of ourselves is akin with our own cognizance of the animalculae which infest the brain﻿—a being which we, in consequence, regard as purely inanimate and material much in the same manner as these animalculae must thus regard us.

===Chinese===

我实在爱把幽暗的山谷、灰白的岩石、无声微笑的流水、不安的睡眠里叹息的森林、俯瞰一切的高傲而警醒的群山——我实在爱把这些看作不过是一具浩大的、活的、有感觉的整体的巨大肢体——一个整体，它的形状（球形）在一切形状里最完全、最包罗；它的路径在结伴的行星之间；它谦卑的侍女是月亮，它居间的君主是太阳；它的生命是永恒，它的思想是一位神的思想；它的享受是知识；它的命运消失在浩瀚里，它对我们的认识，同我们对我们脑中滋生的微生物的认识相仿——因而我们把它看作纯然无生命、纯然物质的东西，正如这些微生物想必这样看我们。

===Original===

Our telescopes and our mathematical investigations assure us on every hand﻿—notwithstanding the cant of the more ignorant of the priesthood﻿—that space, and therefore that bulk, is an important consideration in the eyes of the Almighty. The cycles in which the stars move are those best adapted for the evolution, without collision, of the greatest possible number of bodies. The forms of those bodies are accurately such as, within a given surface, to include the greatest possible amount of matter;﻿—while the surfaces themselves are so disposed as to accommodate a denser population than could be accommodated on the same surfaces otherwise arranged. Nor is it any argument against bulk being an object with God, that space itself is infinite; for there may be an infinity of matter to fill it. And since we see clearly that the endowment of matter with vitality is a principle﻿—indeed, as far as our judgments extend, the *leading* principle in the operations of Deity﻿—it is scarcely logical to imagine it confined to the regions of the minute, where we daily trace it, and not extending to those of the august. As we find cycle within cycle without end﻿—yet all revolving around one far-distant centre which is the Godhead, may we not analogically suppose in the same manner, life within life, the less within the greater, and all within the Spirit Divine? In short, we are madly erring, through self-esteem, in believing man, in either his temporal or future destinies, to be of more moment in the universe than that vast “clod of the valley” which he tills and contemns, and to which he denies a soul for no more profound reason than that he does not behold it in operation.20

===Chinese===

我们的望远镜和数学研究处处向我们保证——尽管教会里较无知的人士一味唱高调——空间，从而体积，在全能者眼里是一个重要的考虑。星辰运行的诸轨道，正是最适于使尽可能多的天体不碰撞地演化的轨道。那些天体的形状，精确地是这样一些形状：在给定的表面之内，包含最大可能量的物质；——而这些表面本身又安排成能容纳比任何别的安排所容纳的更稠密的居民。空间本身无限，并不能反驳体积是上帝的一个对象；因为或许有无限多的物质去充满它。既然我们清楚看见，赋予物质以生命是一条原则——就我们的判断所及，是神的运作里的*首要*原则——设想它限于我们每日在其中追踪它的微小区域，而不伸展到那些庄严的区域，是不合逻辑的。既然我们发现轨道之内有轨道，无有穷尽——却都绕着一个遥远的中心旋转，那中心便是神性——我们何不依此类推，设想生命之内有生命，小的在大的之内，一切都在神圣的灵之内？一句话，我们因自负而狂谬地错了：相信人，或他现世的或将来的命运，在宇宙里比他耕种又轻贱的那一大块「谷中的土块」更要紧，否认它有灵魂，理由之浅薄，无非是他在运作里看不见那灵魂。〔20〕

===Original===

These fancies, and such as these, have always given to my meditations among the mountains and the forests, by the rivers and the ocean, a tinge of what the everyday world would not fail to term fantastic. My wanderings amid such scenes have been many, and far-searching, and often solitary; and the interest with which I have strayed through many a dim, deep valley, or gazed into the reflected Heaven of many a bright lake, has been an interest greatly deepened by the thought that I have strayed and gazed alone. What flippant Frenchman21 was it who said in allusion to the well-known work of Zimmerman, that, “la solitude est une belle chose; mais il faut quelqu’un pour vous dire que la solitude est une belle chose?” The epigram cannot be gainsayed; but the necessity is a thing that does not exist.

It was during one of my lonely journeyings, amid a far distant region of mountain locked within mountain, and sad rivers and melancholy tarn writhing or sleeping within all﻿—that I chanced upon a certain rivulet and island. I came upon them suddenly in the leafy June, and threw myself upon the turf, beneath the branches of an unknown odorous shrub, that I might doze as I contemplated the scene. I felt that thus only should I look upon it﻿—such was the character of phantasm which it wore.

On all sides﻿—save to the west, where the sun was about sinking﻿—arose the verdant walls of the forest. The little river which turned sharply in its course, and was thus immediately lost to sight, seemed to have no exit from its prison, but to be absorbed by the deep green foliage of the trees to the east﻿—while in the opposite quarter (so it appeared to me as I lay at length and glanced upward) there poured down noiselessly and continuously into the valley, a rich golden and crimson waterfall from the sunset fountains of the sky.

About midway in the short vista which my dreamy vision took in, one small circular island, profusely verdured, reposed upon the bosom of the stream.

So blended bank and shadow there

That each seemed pendulous in air﻿—

so mirror-like was the glassy water, that it was scarcely possible to say at what point upon the slope of the emerald turf its crystal dominion began.

===Chinese===

这些幻想，以及这类幻想，始终给我在山与林之间、河与海之间的冥想，添上一层日常世界必定要叫作幻想的色彩。我在这类景致里的漫游很多，很远，常常独自；我徘徊过许多幽暗的深谷，凝望过许多明亮的湖里映着的天，那种兴趣，因徘徊与凝望都是独自一人而大大加深。那轻薄的法国人〔21〕是谁——他在提到齐默尔曼（Zimmerman）那部名著时说：「孤独是一件美事；可总得有个人对你说孤独是一件美事？」警句无可辩驳；但那桩必要并不存在。

是在我一次孤独的旅途中——在山锁着山的极远的地方，哀伤的河与忧郁的湖在一切之内蠕动或沉睡——我偶然遇到一条小溪和一座岛。枝叶繁茂的六月，我突然撞见它们，扑倒在草皮上，在一丛不知名的芳香的灌木的枝条下，好一边打盹一边观照那景致。我觉得唯其这样才该看它——它披着的幻影的品格如此。

四面八方——除西边，太阳正要沉落——立起森林的翠墙。小河在行程里陡然一折，立刻没了踪影，似乎没有出口可以逃出它的囚牢，而是被东边树木的深绿枝叶吸了去——而对面一侧（我直挺挺躺着仰望时，它显得这样）一道金黄与绯红的瀑布，从天上的落日泉里，无声而不断地倾泻进山谷。

在我梦一般的眼力所及的短短纵深的中段，一座小小的圆岛，绿得丰饶，安卧在溪流的胸口。

岸与影在那里融作一片，

仿佛彼此悬在空中——

水明净如镜，以致几乎说不出，在翠玉草皮的哪一点上，它水晶的统治开始了。

===Original===

My position enabled me to include in a single view both the eastern and western extremities of the islet; and I observed a singularly-marked difference in their aspects. The latter was all one radiant harem of garden beauties. It glowed and blushed beneath the eyes of the slant sunlight, and fairly laughed with flowers. The grass was short, springy, sweet-scented, and asphodel-interspersed. The trees were lithe, mirthful, erect﻿—bright, slender, and graceful﻿—of Eastern figure and foliage, with bark smooth, glossy, and parti-colored. There seemed a deep sense of life and joy about all; and although no airs blew from out the heavens, yet everything had motion through the gentle sweepings to and fro of innumerable butterflies, that might have been mistaken for tulips with wings.22

The other or eastern end of the isle was whelmed in the blackest shade. A sombre, yet beautiful and peaceful gloom here pervaded all things. The trees were dark in color, and mournful in form and attitude, wreathing themselves into sad, solemn, and spectral shapes that conveyed ideas of mortal sorrow and untimely death. The grass wore the deep tint of the cypress, and the heads of its blades hung droopingly, and hither and thither among it were many small unsightly hillocks, low and narrow, and not very long, that had the aspect of graves, but were not; although over and all about them the rue and the rosemary clambered. The shade of the trees fell heavily upon the water, and seemed to bury itself therein, impregnating the depths of the element with darkness. I fancied that each shadow, as the sun descended lower and lower, separated itself sullenly from the trunk that gave it birth, and thus became absorbed by the stream; while other shadows issued momently from the trees, taking the place of their predecessors thus entombed.

===Chinese===

我的位置使我在一个视野里收尽小岛东西两端；我观察出它们面貌上奇异分明的差别。西端整个是一座光华灿烂的后宫花园之美。它在斜阳的眼下红晕焕发，简直笑着满身的花。草短、有弹性、芳香，间以日影兰。树轻盈、欢悦、挺直——明亮、纤细、优雅——东方式的样子和叶，树皮光滑，有光泽，五彩斑斓。一切之上似乎有生命与欢乐的深沉意味；虽然天上不吹一丝风，万物却在无数蝴蝶往复的轻扫里运动，那些蝴蝶会叫人错认作生了翅膀的郁金香。〔22〕

岛的另一端——东端——淹在最黑的阴影里。一种阴沉、然而美丽而和平的幽暗，弥漫着这里的一切。树颜色深暗，形相姿态哀伤，把自己缠成悲戚、庄严、幽灵似的样子，传达着人间悲恻与夭亡的意念。草披着柏树的深色，叶尖低垂；草丛里到处有许多不好看的小丘，又低又窄，不太长，一副坟茔的神气，却并不是坟；虽然芸香和迷迭香攀满它们的上面和四围。树的影子沉重地压在水上，似乎把自己埋进水里，把黑暗灌进这元素的深处。我幻想，随着太阳越沉越低，每一道影子阴沉地从生它的树干上分离，就这样被溪流吸收；同时别的影子时时刻刻从树里出来，接替那些这样入了土的前辈。

===Original===

This idea, having once seized upon my fancy, greatly excited it, and I lost myself forthwith in revery. “If ever island were enchanted,” said I to myself, “this is it. This is the haunt of the few gentle Fays who remain from the wreck of the race. Are these green tombs theirs?﻿—or do they yield up their sweet lives as mankind yield up their own? In dying, do they not rather waste away mournfully, rendering unto God, little by little, their existence, as these trees render up shadow after shadow, exhausting their substance unto dissolution? What the wasting tree is to the water that imbibes its shade, growing thus blacker by what it preys upon, may not the life of the Fay be to the death which engulfs it?”

As I thus mused, with half-shut eyes, while the sun sank rapidly to rest, and eddying currents careered round and round the island, bearing upon their bosom large, dazzling, white flakes of the bark of the sycamore﻿—flakes which, in their multiform positions upon the water, a quick imagination might have converted into anything it pleased﻿—while I thus mused, it appeared to me that the form of one of those very Fays about whom I had been pondering made its way slowly into the darkness from out the light at the western end of the island. She stood erect in a singularly fragile canoe, and urged it with the mere phantom of an oar. While within the influence of the lingering sunbeams, her attitude seemed indicative of joy﻿—but sorrow deformed it as she passed within the shade. Slowly she glided along, and at length rounded the islet and reentered the region of light. “The revolution which has just been made by the Fay,” continued I, musingly, “is the cycle of the brief year of her life. She has floated through her winter and through her summer. She is a year nearer unto Death; for I did not fail to see that, as she came into the shade, her shadow fell from her, and was swallowed up in the dark water, making its blackness more black.”

===Chinese===

这念头一经攫住我的幻想，便大大撩动它，我随即迷失在遐想里。「倘若有过一座受魔法的岛，」我对自己说，「便是这座。这是大劫之后残存的少数温柔的仙灵的出没之地。这些绿坟是它们的吗？——还是它们像人类交出自己的生命那样交出它们的甜生命？它们死时不肯一下子死，倒宁可哀哀地凋谢，一点一点把存在归还给上帝，正如这些树把影子一道一道归还给溪流，把自己的实体耗到消散？浪费着的树之于吸它影子的水——水吃了它的贡物愈见其黑——仙灵的生命之于吞没它的死，何尝不如此？」

我这样沉思着，眼睛半闭，太阳迅速沉下去歇息，漩涡的水流绕着小岛团团回旋，把大片炫目的白色的梧桐树皮薄片载在胸前——那些薄片在水上姿态万变，一个敏捷的想象尽可把它们随心所欲变作任何东西——我这样沉思着，我方才冥想的那一类仙灵之一，似乎从岛的西端的光里，缓缓走进黑暗。她笔直立在一叶异样脆弱的独木舟里，用一支影幻似的桨推它。在流连的日光的势力之内，她的姿态显出欢乐——但她一进阴影，愁容便毁了它。她缓缓滑行，终于绕过小岛，重进光域。「仙灵方才的这一周旋，」我继续出神地说，「便是她短促的生命的年轮。她已浮过她的冬天和她的夏天。她离死更近一年了；因为我不曾看不见：她进阴影时，影子从她身上落了下来，被黑水吞没，使那黑更黑。」

===Original===

And again the boat appeared, and the Fay; but about the attitude of the latter there was more of care and uncertainty and less of elastic joy. She floated again from out the light and into the gloom (which deepened momently) and again her shadow fell from her into the ebony water, and became absorbed into its blackness. And again and again she made the circuit of the island, (while the sun rushed down to his slumbers), and at each issuing into the light there was more sorrow about her person, while it grew feebler and far fainter and more indistinct, and at each passage into the gloom there fell from her a darker shade, which became whelmed in a shadow more black. But at length when the sun had utterly departed, the Fay, now the mere ghost of her former self, went disconsolately with her boat into the region of the ebony flood﻿—and that she issued thence at all I cannot say, for darkness fell over all things and I beheld her magical figure no more.

===Chinese===

船又出现了，仙灵又出现了；但后者的姿态里多了些忧与无定，少了些弹性的欢乐。她又一次从光里浮出，进到幽暗里（幽暗时时刻刻加深），影子又一次从她身上落进黑檀的水里，被它的黑吸收。她一次又一次绕岛巡行（太阳正奔向他的安眠），每次进光时她身上更多一些悲哀，同时变得更弱，更淡，更模糊；每次进幽暗时，落下一道更暗的影，那影子被一片更黑的暗吞没。但终于，太阳全然去后，仙灵——如今只是她前身的幽灵——悻悻地带着她的船进了黑水之域——她是否还从那里出来过，我说不上，因为黑暗罩住万物，我再也不曾望见她那魔幻的身影。

## The Colloquy of Monos and Una / 莫诺斯与尤娜的对话
===Original===

Μελλοντα ταυτα.

“These things are in the near future.”

> Sophocles, *Antig.*

Una

“Born again?”

Monos

Yes, fairest and best beloved Una, “born again.” These were the words upon whose mystical meaning I had so long pondered, rejecting the explanations of the priesthood, until Death himself resolved for me the secret.

Una

Death!

Monos

How strangely, sweet Una, you echo my words! I observe, too, a vacillation in your step﻿—a joyous inquietude in your eyes. You are confused and oppressed by the majestic novelty of the Life Eternal. Yes, it was of Death I spoke. And here how singularly sounds that word which of old was wont to bring terror to all hearts﻿—throwing a mildew upon all pleasures!

Una

Ah, Death, the spectre which sat at all feasts! How often, Monos, did we lose ourselves in speculations upon its nature! How mysteriously did it act as a check to human bliss﻿—saying unto it “thus far, and no farther!” That earnest mutual love, my own Monos, which burned within our bosoms﻿—how vainly did we flatter ourselves, feeling happy in its first upspringing, that our happiness would strengthen with its strength! Alas! as it grew, so grew in our hearts the dread of that evil hour which was hurrying to separate us forever! Thus, in time, it became painful to love. Hate would have been mercy then.

Monos

Speak not here of these griefs, dear Una﻿—mine, mine, forever now!

Una

But the memory of past sorrow﻿—is it not present joy? I have much to say yet of the things which have been. Above all, I burn to know the incidents of your own passage through the dark Valley and Shadow.

Monos

And when did the radiant Una ask anything of her Monos in vain? I will be minute in relating all﻿—but at what point shall the weird narrative begin?

Una

At what point?

Monos

You have said.

Una

Monos, I comprehend you. In Death we have both learned the propensity of man to define the indefinable. I will not say, then, commence with the moment of life’s cessation﻿—but commence with that sad, sad instant when, the fever having abandoned you, you sank into a breathless and motionless torpor, and I pressed down your pallid eyelids with the passionate fingers of love.

Monos

===Chinese===

Μελλοντα ταυτα.

「这些事就在眼前。」

> 索福克勒斯《安提戈涅》

尤娜

「再生了么？」

莫诺斯

再生了，最美、最亲爱的尤娜，「再生了」。这几个字里的玄义，我苦想了那样久，拒受祭司们的解说，直到死神他亲自替我解开了这秘密。

尤娜

死！

莫诺斯

亲爱的尤娜，你把我的话回得多奇异！我还看出你歩子里的踌躇——你眼睛里欢喜的不安。你被永恒生命那庄严的新奇弄得又困惑、又沉重了。是，我说的是死。而这字眼，从前惯于把恐怖带给一切心、把霉晦罩上一切欢乐，此刻响起来又多么奇异！

尤娜

啊，死——坐在一切筵席上的幽灵！莫诺斯，我们曾多少次沉迷于对它本性的玄想！它何等神秘地掣住人的至福——对它说：「到此为止，不得再往！」我自己的莫诺斯，我们胸中燃烧的那份生死不渝的爱——起初它萌发时我们自觉幸福，便多么徒然地自喜，以为幸福会随爱的增长而增长！唉！爱越深，那个凶险时辰的恐惧也在我们心里越深——它正急着把我们永远分开！于是，爱终于成了痛苦。那时，恨反倒慈悲了。

莫诺斯

别在这里说这些悲伤，亲爱的尤娜——如今是我的，永远是我的！

尤娜

可对旧日悲伤的追忆——不正是眼下的欢乐么？那往昔的事，我还有许多要讲。最要紧的，我急着要知道你自己穿过黑暗的死亡谷与幽影的种种。

莫诺斯

光艳的尤娜向她的莫诺斯求告，几时空手回过？我愿细细说个周全——只是这段神异的叙述，从哪里起头呢？

尤娜

从哪里起头？

莫诺斯

你说出来了。

尤娜

莫诺斯，我懂你。在死里，我们都学会了人类那股要界说不可界说之物的痼癖。那么，我不说从生命停止的一刻起——就从那个凄凄惶惶的时辰起：热病抛下了你，你沉入无息无动的僵眠，我用爱情的烈手指，合下你惨白的眼皮。

莫诺斯

===Original===

One word first, my Una, in regard to man’s general condition at this epoch. You will remember that one or two of the wise among our forefathers﻿—wise in fact, although not in the world’s esteem﻿—had ventured to doubt the propriety of the term “improvement,” as applied to the progress of our civilization. There were periods in each of the five or six centuries immediately preceding our dissolution, when arose some vigorous intellect, boldly contending for those principles whose truth appears now, to our disenfranchised reason, so utterly obvious﻿—principles which should have taught our race to submit to the guidance of the natural laws, rather than attempt their control. At long intervals some masterminds appeared, looking upon each advance in practical science as a retro-gradation in the true utility. Occasionally the poetic intellect﻿—that intellect which we now feel to have been the most exalted of all﻿—since those truths which to us were of the most enduring importance could only be reached by that *analogy* which speaks in proof tones to the imagination alone and to the unaided reason bears no weight﻿—occasionally did this poetic intellect proceed a step farther in the evolving of the vague idea of the philosophic, and find in the mystic parable that tells of the tree of knowledge, and of its forbidden fruit, death-producing, a distinct intimation that knowledge was not meet for man in the infant condition of his soul. And these men, the poets, living and perishing amid the scorn of the “utilitarians”﻿—of rough pedants, who arrogated to themselves a title which could have been properly applied only to the scorned﻿—these men, the poets, pondered piningly, yet not unwisely, upon the ancient days when our wants were not more simple than our enjoyments were keen﻿—days when *mirth* was a word unknown, so solemnly deep-toned was happiness﻿—holy, august and blissful days, when blue rivers ran undammed, between hills unhewn, into far forest solitudes, primeval, odorous, and unexplored.

===Chinese===

先说一句，我的尤娜，关于那个时代人类的总体境况。你当记得，我们的先辈中有一两位智者——事实上智，只是世间不这么看——曾斗胆怀疑「改进」一词用在我们文明的进程上是否得当。在我们死去的五六个世纪之前，每一段时期里都崛起过一些旺盛的头脑，为那些原则据理力争；如今，这些原则的真理，在我们这些免除了桎梏的理性看来，明摆得那样彻底——它们本该教导我们的种族顺服自然法则的引导，而不是妄图驾驭它们。隔上许久，会有几位大心智出现，把实用科学的每一步前进，看作真正效用上的倒退。偶尔，那诗性的心智——我们如今觉得它才是最高贵的心智，因为那些对我们最关紧要的真理，唯有借那种*类比*才能抵达，而类比只以证明的口吻对想象说话，对无助的理性毫无分量——偶尔，这诗性的心智也会在哲思的模糊观念的展开里再进一歩，从那则讲述知识之树及其致死禁果的神秘寓言中，读出一个分明的暗示：知识并不配处于灵魂婴孩期的人类。这些人，诗人，在「功利之徒」的讥嘲里生、死——那是一班粗鄙的学究，僭用了一个只配加在他们所讥嘲者头上的名号——这些人，诗人，苦苦地、却并非不明智地，悬想着远古的日子：那时我们的所需，不多于我们享受之锐——那时「欢闹」是个无人知晓的词，幸福深沉肃穆到那个地歩——神圣、庄严、至福的日子：蓝色的河流未被拦断，穿行于未凿的丘山之间，流入遥远的森林幽寂——太初的、芳馨的、未曾探明的幽寂。

===Original===

Yet these noble exceptions from the general misrule served but to strengthen it by opposition. Alas! we had fallen upon the most evil of all our evil days. The great “movement”﻿—that was the cant term﻿—went on: a diseased commotion, moral and physical. Art﻿—the Arts﻿—arose supreme, and, once enthroned, cast chains upon the intellect which had elevated them to power. Man, because he could not but acknowledge the majesty of Nature, fell into childish exultation at his acquired and still-increasing dominion over her elements. Even while he stalked a God in his own fancy, an infantine imbecility came over him. As might be supposed from the origin of his disorder, he grew infected with system, and with abstraction. He enwrapped himself in generalities. Among other odd ideas, that of universal equality gained ground; and in the face of analogy and of God﻿—in despite of the loud warning voice of the laws of *gradation* so visibly pervading all things in Earth and Heaven﻿—wild attempts at an omni-prevalent Democracy were made. Yet this evil sprang necessarily from the leading evil﻿—Knowledge. Man could not both know and succumb. Meantime huge smoking cities arose, innumerable. Green leaves shrank before the hot breath of furnaces. The fair face of Nature was deformed as with the ravages of some loathsome disease. And methinks, sweet Una, even our slumbering sense of the forced and of the far-fetched might have arrested us here. But now it appears that we had worked out our own destruction in the perversion of our *taste*, or rather in the blind neglect of its culture in the schools. For, in truth, it was at this crisis that taste alone﻿—that faculty which, holding a middle position between the pure intellect and the moral sense, could never safely have been disregarded﻿—it was now that taste alone could have led us gently back to Beauty, to Nature, and to Life. But alas for the pure contemplative spirit and majestic intuition of Plato! Alas for the *μουσικη* which he justly regarded as an all-sufficient education for the soul! Alas for him and for it!﻿—since both were most desperately needed when both were most entirely forgotten or despised.23

===Chinese===

然而这些挣脱普世败政的高贵例外，只因与它相抗，反倒加固了它。唉！我们落进了我们一切坏日子里最坏的日子。大「运动」——行话是这样叫的——在进行：一场道德与肉体的病态的骚动。艺术——诸艺——崛起了，至尊至上；一旦登上宝座，便把那抬举它们登座的智能锁进锁链。人呢，因为不得不承认自然的庄严，又为自己所赢得的、且仍在扩张的对自然元素的统治，陷入了孩子气的狂喜。他一面在自己的幻想里昂首阔步如同神明，一面一阵婴儿式的低能罩上他来。可想而知——既然病根如彼——他染上了体系，染上了抽象。他把自己裹进泛论里。在种种怪念头中间，「人人平等」的念头得了势；于是当着类比的面、当着上帝的面——不顾*等第*法则响亮的警告，那法则明明白白贯满大地与上天的万物——他们做出了种种狂妄的尝试，求一个无所不在的民主。然而这一恶，必然出自为首的那一恶——知识。人不能既认识、又屈从。与此同时，浓烟滚滚的大城市崛起，数不胜数。绿叶在熔炉的热气里枯缩。自然的姣容，毁得像害了恶疮。亲爱的尤娜，我想，哪怕我们那迟钝的、对牵强与强求之物的感觉，也本可以在这里拦住我们。可如今看来，我们是把自己的毁灭，做进了我们*趣味*的败坏里——或者说，做进了学校对趣味培养的盲目疏忽里。因为，实情是：正当此关头，唯有趣味——那门居于纯粹理智与道德感之间的官能，忽略它从来不会有好下场——唯有趣味，本可以温柔地领我们回去，回到美，回到自然，回到生命。可柏拉图那纯粹的静观之灵、庄严的直觉，可惜了呀！他正当地视为灵魂全然足够的教育的*μουσικη*（音乐），可惜了呀！他可惜，它也可惜——因为两者在最被需要的时候，最被彻底遗忘或鄙弃。23

===Original===

Pascal, a philosopher whom we both love, has said, how truly!﻿—“*que tout notre raisonnement se réduit à céder au sentiment*;” and it is not impossible that the sentiment of the natural, had time permitted it, would have regained its old ascendancy over the harsh mathematical reason of the schools. But this thing was not to be. Prematurely induced by intemperance of knowledge the old age of the world drew on. This the mass of mankind saw not, or, living lustily although unhappily, affected not to see. But, for myself, the Earth’s records had taught me to look for widest ruin as the price of highest civilization. I had imbibed a prescience of our Fate from comparison of China the simple and enduring, with Assyria the architect, with Egypt the astrologer, with Nubia, more crafty than either, the turbulent mother of all Arts. In history24 of these regions I met with a ray from the Future. The individual artificialities of the three latter were local diseases of the Earth, and in their individual overthrows we had seen local remedies applied; but for the infected world at large I could anticipate no regeneration save in death. That man, as a race, should not become extinct, I saw that he must be “*born again*.”

And now it was, fairest and dearest, that we wrapped our spirits, daily, in dreams. Now it was that, in twilight, we discoursed of the days to come, when the Art-scarred surface of the Earth, having undergone that purification25 which alone could efface its rectangular obscenities, should clothe itself anew in the verdure and the mountain-slopes and the smiling waters of Paradise, and be rendered at length a fit dwelling-place for man:﻿—for man the Death purged﻿—for man to whose now exalted intellect there should be poison in knowledge no more﻿—for the redeemed, regenerated, blissful, and now immortal, but still for the *material*, man.

Una

===Chinese===

帕斯卡——你我同爱的一位哲人——说过，说得多真！——「*我们全部的推理，归结起来不过是向情感让歩*」；倘若时间许可，「自然」的情感，原非没有可能重新压倒学院里那严苛的数学理性。可这件事偏偏不成。知识的无度，催得世界的暮年早到了。世人对此视而不见；或者，活得热辣辣却并不幸福，装作不见。可就我自己而言，大地的记载教导过我：最高的文明，其代价是最广的毁灭。比较着质朴而持久的中华、营造者的亚述、占星家的埃及，还有比两者更狡黠的努比亚——一切技艺的骚动的母亲——我早吸取了对我们命运的预感。在这些地域的历史24里，我遇上了未来投来的一线光。后三者各自的人为，是大地局部的地方病；它们各自的倾覆，我们见过局部疗方的施用；可是对于这个染遍了的大世界，除死之外，我不指望任何再生。我明白：人类要不成批地绝灭，就必须「*再生*」。

而正是这时候，最美、最亲的，我们天天把灵魂裹进梦里。正是这时候，在暮色里，我们谈论着将来的日子：大地这张为艺术所创的面，经过那唯一能拭去其直角淫秽的净化25，重新披上乐园的青葱、山坡和笑水，终于成为配得上人的居所——配得上被死涤净的人——配得上那如今高举的智能、知识于他不再为毒的人——配得上得赎、重生、至福、而不朽，却仍旧是*物质的*人。

尤娜

===Original===

Well do I remember these conversations, dear Monos; but the epoch of the fiery overthrow was not so near at hand as we believed, and as the corruption you indicate did surely warrant us in believing. Men lived; and died individually. You yourself sickened, and passed into the grave; and thither your constant Una speedily followed you. And though the century which has since elapsed, and whose conclusion brings us thus together once more, tortured our slumbering senses with no impatience of duration, yet, my Monos, it was a century still.

Monos

Say, rather, a point in the vague infinity. Unquestionably, it was in the Earth’s dotage that I died. Wearied at heart with anxieties which had their origin in the general turmoil and decay, I succumbed to the fierce fever. After some few days of pain, and many of dreamy delirium replete with ecstasy, the manifestations of which you mistook for pain, while I longed but was impotent to undeceive you﻿—after some days there came upon me, as you have said, a breathless and motionless torpor; and this was termed *Death* by those who stood around me.

Words are vague things. My condition did not deprive me of sentience. It appeared to me not greatly dissimilar to the extreme quiescence of him, who, having slumbered long and profoundly, lying motionless and fully prostrate in a midsummer noon, begins to steal slowly back into consciousness, through the mere sufficiency of his sleep, and without being awakened by external disturbances.

===Chinese===

这些谈话我记得清楚，亲爱的莫诺斯；可烈火覆灭的时代，并不像我们以为的那样近，也不像你指出的那种腐坏所确凿担保的那样近。人们活着；一个个地死去。你自己病倒了，进了坟；你忠贞的尤娜随后很快跟了去。此后流逝的那个百年——它的终结此刻又把我们这样聚到一处——并没有以漫长煎熬我们沉睡的感官；然而，我的莫诺斯，那终究是一个百年。

莫诺斯

不如说，是浩渺无限里的一点。毫无疑问，我死在大地的风烛残年里。为普世的骚乱与衰败而生的种种焦劳，叫我心力交瘁，倒在剧烈的热病里。痛了几天、又沉溺在满盈狂喜的谵妄里许多天——那谵妄的种种表现，你误认作了疼痛，而我想让你明白却无能为力——这样一些天之后，如你所说，一阵无息无动的僵眠罩住了我；围在我身边的人，管它叫*死*。

词是含糊的东西。我的境况并没有剥夺我的知觉。在我看来，它同那样一个人的至极安宁相去不远：他睡得又长又深，仲夏的正午直挺挺躺着，纹丝不动，单凭睡眠已足，并未被外界的搅扰唤醒，便开始缓缓偷回意识里来。

===Original===

I breathed no longer. The pulses were still. The heart had ceased to beat. Volition had not departed, but was powerless. The senses were unusually active, although eccentrically so﻿—assuming often each other’s functions at random. The taste and the smell were inextricably confounded, and became one sentiment, abnormal and intense. The rose-water with which your tenderness had moistened my lips to the last, affected me with sweet fancies of flowers﻿—fantastic flowers, far more lovely than any of the old Earth, but whose prototypes we have here blooming around us. The eyelids, transparent and bloodless, offered no complete impediment to vision. As volition was in abeyance, the balls could not roll in their sockets but all objects within the range of the visual hemisphere were seen with more or less distinctness; the rays which fell upon the external retina, or into the corner of the eye, producing a more vivid effect than those which struck the front or interior surface. Yet, in the former instance, this effect was so far anomalous that I appreciated it only as *sound*﻿—sound sweet or discordant as the matters presenting themselves at my side were light or dark in shade﻿—curved or angular in outline. The hearing, at the same time, although excited in degree, was not irregular in action﻿—estimating real sounds with an extravagance of precision, not less than of sensibility. Touch had undergone a modification more peculiar. Its impressions were tardily received, but pertinaciously retained, and resulted always in the highest physical pleasure. Thus the pressure of your sweet fingers upon my eyelids, at first only recognised through vision, at length, long after their removal, filled my whole being with a sensual delight immeasurable. I say with a sensual delight. *All* my perceptions were purely sensual. The materials furnished the passive brain by the senses were not in the least degree wrought into shape by the deceased understanding. Of pain there was some little; of pleasure there was much; but of moral pain or pleasure none at all.

===Chinese===

我不再呼吸。脉搏停了。心脏不再跳。意志没有去，只是无力。感官异乎寻常地活跃，虽然活跃得古怪——常常彼此随机地代行对方的职司。味与嗅纠缠不清，成了一种单一的、异样而强烈的情感。你以温柔润过我唇边的最后一刻的玫瑰水，叫我生出花的甜幻——奇幻的花，远比旧大地上任何一种可爱，它们的样子，此刻正在我们四周开放。眼皮透明无血，对视觉不构成完全的障碍。意志既已停摆，眼球不能在眼窝里转，但视觉半球范围内的一切物象，都看得或清或模糊；落到外视网膜上、或斜落进眼角的那些光线，比直射正面或内面的，效果更鲜明。然而在后一情形，这效果又反常得厉害，我只把它领会为*声音*——随着身旁之物的明暗、轮廓的曲直，声音或甜或涩。同时，听觉虽在程度上亢奋，行动却并不乱——估量真实的声音，精确与敏感都到了夸张的地步。触觉经历了一种更 peculiar 的改变。它的印象来得迟，却执拗地留住，而且总归于最高的肉体欢愉。所以你甜蜜的手指压在我眼皮上，起初只透过视觉被认出，而在手指移去许久之后，终于灌满我整个的存在，以一种不可度量的感官的欢愉。我说的是感官的欢愉。我*一切*的知觉都纯粹是感官的。感官供给被动的头脑的材料，没有被那死去的悟性加工成任何形状。痛有一些；乐有很多；但道德的痛或乐，丝毫没有。

===Original===

Thus your wild sobs floated into my ear with all their mournful cadences, and were appreciated in their every variation of sad tone; but they were soft musical sounds and no more; they conveyed to the extinct reason no intimation of the sorrows which gave them birth; while the large and constant tears which fell upon my face, telling the bystanders of a heart which broke, thrilled every fibre of my frame with ecstasy alone. And this was in truth the *Death* of which these bystanders spoke reverently, in low whispers﻿—you, sweet Una, gaspingly, with loud cries.

They attired me for the coffin﻿—three or four dark figures which flitted busily to and fro. As these crossed the direct line of my vision they affected me as *forms*; but upon passing to my side their images impressed me with the idea of shrieks, groans, and other dismal expressions of terror, of horror, or of wo. You alone, habited in a white robe, passed in all directions musically about me.

===Chinese===

于是你狂乱的呜咽，带着全部哀伤的抑扬，飘进我的耳朵；每一种悲调的变化都被我领味；可它们只是柔美的乐音，仅此而已；它们不再向那熄灭的理性通报生它们的那些悲伤；而那不断落在我脸上的大颗大颗的泪，向旁观者诉说着一颗碎裂的心，却只用欢愉震颤我的每一根纤维。这才是旁观者低声敬言的*死*——是你，亲爱的尤娜，喘着气高声哭喊的那个死。

他们给我穿寿衣——三四个黑影忙忙碌碌地来来去去。这些影子穿过我视线的正线时，给我的感觉是*形*；可一转到我的身侧，它们的影像给我的感觉便是尖叫、呻吟，同恐惧、惊骇或悲苦的别样阴惨的声音。唯有你，一装白袍，从四面八方音乐般绕着我走。

===Original===

The day waned; and, as its light faded away, I became possessed by a vague uneasiness﻿—an anxiety such as the sleeper feels when sad real sounds fall continuously within his ear﻿—low distant bell-tones, solemn, at long but equal intervals, and mingling with melancholy dreams. Night arrived; and with its shadows a heavy discomfort. It oppressed my limbs with the oppression of some dull weight, and was palpable. There was also a moaning sound, not unlike the distant reverberation of surf, but more continuous, which, beginning with the first twilight, had grown in strength with the darkness. Suddenly lights were brought into the room, and this reverberation became forthwith interrupted into frequent unequal bursts of the same sound, but less dreary and less distinct. The ponderous oppression was in a great measure relieved; and, issuing from the flame of each lamp, (for there were many,) there flowed unbrokenly into my ears a strain of melodious monotone. And when now, dear Una, approaching the bed upon which I lay outstretched, you sat gently by my side, breathing odor from your sweet lips, and pressing them upon my brow, there arose tremulously within my bosom, and mingling with the merely physical sensations which circumstances had called forth, a something akin to sentiment itself﻿—a feeling that, half appreciating, half responded to your earnest love and sorrow; but this feeling took no root in the pulseless heart, and seemed indeed rather a shadow than a reality, and faded quickly away, first into extreme quiescence, and then into a purely sensual pleasure as before.

===Chinese===

天色晚了；它的光褪去时，一种模糊的不安攫住了我——一种焦虑，像睡者耳畔连续落进真实而悲哀的声音时感到的那种——低远而庄严的钟声，间隔长而均匀，混进忧郁的梦里。夜来了；随着夜的阴影，一层沉重的不适。它像什么沉钝的重量压在我四肢上，而且是可触的。还有一阵呜咽似的声音，不很远处的浪的回响，只是更连续；从初薄的暮色起，随黑暗渐渐增势。忽然，灯烛端进了屋；这回响随即断作同一声音的、频繁而不匀的迸发，只是不那么凄沉、不那么分明。那沉重的压迫大为宽解；而从每一盏灯的火苗里（灯有许多盏），一缕旋律的单音，不间断地流进我的耳朵。而此刻，亲爱的尤娜，你走近我直躺的床，温柔地坐在我身旁，吐着香唇的气息，把它们压上我的额头——我的胸中颤颤地升起一样什么，同情境唤起的纯肉体感觉混在一处，近乎情感本身的东西——一种半领味、半回应你恳切的爱与悲的感觉；可这感觉在无脉的心里扎不下根，实在更像一道影子，而非实体，很快便隐去了：先隐入至极的安宁，随后又隐入先前那种纯粹的感官的欢愉。

===Original===

And now, from the wreck and the chaos of the usual senses, there appeared to have arisen within me a sixth, all perfect. In its exercise I found a wild delight﻿—yet a delight still physical, inasmuch as the understanding had in it no part. Motion in the animal frame had fully ceased. No muscle quivered; no nerve thrilled; no artery throbbed. But there seemed to have sprung up in the brain, *that* of which no words could convey to the merely human intelligence even an indistinct conception. Let me term it a mental pendulous pulsation. It was the moral embodiment of man’s abstract idea of *Time*. By the absolute equalization of this movement﻿—or of such as this﻿—had the cycles of the firmamental orbs themselves, been adjusted. By its aid I measured the irregularities of the clock upon the mantel, and of the watches of the attendants. Their tickings came sonorously to my ears. The slightest deviations from the true proportion﻿—and these deviations were omni-prevalent﻿—affected me just as violations of abstract truth were wont, on earth, to affect the moral sense. Although no two of the timepieces in the chamber struck the individual seconds accurately together, yet I had no difficulty in holding steadily in mind the tones, and the respective momentary errors of each. And this﻿—this keen, perfect, self-existing sentiment of *duration*﻿—this sentiment existing (as man could not possibly have conceived it to exist) independently of any succession of events﻿—this idea﻿—this sixth sense, upspringing from the ashes of the rest, was the first obvious and certain step of the intemporal soul upon the threshold of the temporal Eternity.

===Chinese===

而今，从寻常诸感官的残骸与混沌里，我体内似乎升起了一种第六感，完美无缺。运用它，我寻到一种狂野的欢喜——却仍是肉体的欢喜，因为悟性在其中无份。动物躯架里的运动已全然停止。没有一条肌肉颤动；没有一根神经震栗；没有一条动脉搏跳。可脑子里仿佛生出了*那样一样东西*，言语无法向纯粹的人类智能传达它的哪怕一个模糊概念。让我把它称作心智的摆式脉动吧。它是人的*时间*抽象观念的道德化身。正是凭这种运动——或这类运动——的绝对均齐，诸天体本身的周期才得校准。借它的帮助，我量出了壁炉架上时钟和侍者们怀表的误差。它们的滴答洪亮地落进我的耳朵。对真正比例的最细微的偏离——而这偏差无处不在——作用于我，正如抽象真理的被违犯，从前在大地上作用于道德感。屋里没有两只钟表能把各自的秒敲得完全同时；可我毫不费力，便把每一只的音调、以及各自的瞬时误差，稳稳握在心里。而这——这敏锐、完美、自存的*绵延*之感——这感觉（人绝设想不到它能这样存在）独立于任何事件的相续而存在——这个观念——这从其余诸感的灰烬里跃起的第六感，是超时间的灵魂，踏上时间性永恒的门槛时，头一步显明而确凿的台阶。

===Original===

It was midnight; and you still sat by my side. All others had departed from the chamber of Death. They had deposited me in the coffin. The lamps burned flickeringly; for this I knew by the tremulousness of the monotonous strains. But, suddenly these strains diminished in distinctness and in volume. Finally they ceased. The perfume in my nostrils died away. Forms affected my vision no longer. The oppression of the Darkness uplifted itself from my bosom. A dull shock like that of electricity pervaded my frame, and was followed by total loss of the idea of contact. All of what man has termed sense was merged in the sole consciousness of entity, and in the one abiding sentiment of duration. The mortal body had been at length stricken with the hand of the deadly *Decay*.

Yet had not all of sentience departed; for the consciousness and the sentiment remaining supplied some of its functions by a lethargic intuition. I appreciated the direful change now in operation upon the flesh, and, as the dreamer is sometimes aware of the bodily presence of one who leans over him, so, sweet Una, I still dully felt that you sat by my side. So, too, when the noon of the second day came, I was not unconscious of those movements which displaced you from my side, which confined me within the coffin, which deposited me within the hearse, which bore me to the grave, which lowered me within it, which heaped heavily the mould upon me, and which thus left me, in blackness and corruption, to my sad and solemn slumbers with the worm.

And here, in the prison-house which has few secrets to disclose, there rolled away days and weeks and months; and the soul watched narrowly each second as it flew, and, without effort, took record of its flight﻿—without effort and without object.

===Chinese===

是午夜；你仍坐在我身旁。别的人都已离开死的内室。他们已把我安放进棺材。灯烛明灭地燃着；这我是凭那单音乐音的颤动知道的。可是忽然，这些乐音的清晰与音量低下去。末了它们停了。鼻中的香气散了。形不再作用于我的视觉。黑暗的重压从我胸上抬起了自己。一阵迟钝的电似的震荡漫过我的躯架，随之是接触观念的全部丧失。人所谓的感官，尽数融进单一的实体意识，和单一的、恒驻的绵延之感。有死的躯体，终于挨了致命的*朽*的手。

然而知觉没有全部离去；因为残剩的意识与情感，以一种昏沉的直觉，代行了它的几分职司。我领味着此刻肉体上正进行的可怖之变；正如梦者有时能觉出俯在他身上那人的身体的临在，亲爱的尤娜，我也还昏昏地觉出你坐在我身旁。同样，到第二天的正午，那些动作也不曾全出我的知觉：它们把你从我身边移开，把我关进棺木，把我安进柩车，把我抬到坟场，把我放进墓穴，把湿土重重堆上我，就这样把我留给黑暗与腐朽，去同蛆虫作我凄凉而庄严的长眠。

在这里，在这座几乎没有秘密可泄的牢宅里，天、周、月滚了过去；灵魂紧紧盯住飞逝的每一秒，毫不费力地录下它的飞——毫不费力，也毫无目的。

===Original===

A year passed. The consciousness of *being* had grown hourly more indistinct, and that of mere *locality* had, in great measure, usurped its position. The idea of entity was becoming merged in that of *place*. The narrow space immediately surrounding what had been the body, was now growing to be the body itself. At length, as often happens to the sleeper (by sleep and its world alone is *Death* imaged)﻿—at length, as sometimes happened on Earth to the deep slumberer, when some flitting light half startled him into awaking, yet left him half enveloped in dreams﻿—so to me, in the strict embrace of the *Shadow* came *that* light which alone might have had power to startle﻿—the light of enduring *Love*. Men toiled at the grave in which I lay darkling. They upthrew the damp earth. Upon my mouldering bones there descended the coffin of Una.

And now again all was void. That nebulous light had been extinguished. That feeble thrill had vibrated itself into quiescence. Many lustra had supervened. Dust had returned to dust. The worm had food no more. The sense of being had at length utterly departed, and there reigned in its stead﻿—instead of all things﻿—dominant and perpetual﻿—the autocrats *Place* and *Time*. For *that* which *was not*﻿—for that which had no form﻿—for that which had no thought﻿—for that which had no sentience﻿—for that which was soulless, yet of which matter formed no portion﻿—for all this nothingness, yet for all this immortality, the grave was still a home, and the corrosive hours, co-mates.

===Chinese===

一年过去了。*存在*的意识，一个钟头一个钟头地淡下去；单是*方位*的意识，大半篡了它的位。实体的观念，正化进*场所*的观念。紧围着那曾是身体的四周的窄狭空间，如今渐渐便成了身体本身。到末了——正如常见于睡者的（唯有凭睡眠及其世界，才能给*死*造像）——到末了，正如从前在大地上偶尔见于沉睡者的：一点掠过的光，半惊他入醒，却仍留他半裹在梦里——这样，在*幽影*紧严的怀抱里，向我来了那唯一也许能惊动我的光——持久之*爱*的光。人们在我暗卧的坟上劳作。他们掘开湿土。我的朽骨之上，落下了尤娜的棺。

而后又是一片虚空。那星云似的光熄了。那微弱的震颤，颤到静了。许多个五年过去了。尘归于尘。蛆虫再无食。存在的意识终于彻底离去；代替它君临一切、且永久的，是两位专制者——*场所*与*时间*。因为那*不是*的——那无形的——那无思的——那无觉的——那无灵魂而物质又不占其丝毫的——为这整个的虚无，也为这整个的不朽，坟仍是一个家，而侵蚀的时辰，是它的同居人。

## Never Bet the Devil Your Head / 千万别拿脑袋同魔鬼打赌
===Original===

A Tale with a Moral

“*Con tal que las costumbres de un autor*,” says Don Thomas de las Torres, in the preface to his *Amatory Poems* “*sean puras y castas, importo muy poco que no sean igualmente severas sus obras*”﻿—meaning, in plain English, that, provided the morals of an author are pure personally, it signifies nothing what are the morals of his books. We presume that Don Thomas is now in Purgatory for the assertion. It would be a clever thing, too, in the way of poetical justice, to keep him there until his *Amatory Poems* get out of print, or are laid definitely upon the shelf through lack of readers. Every fiction *should have* a moral; and, what is more to the purpose, the critics have discovered that every fiction *has*. Philip Melanchthon, some time ago, wrote a commentary upon the *Batrachomyomachia*, and proved that the poet’s object was to excite a distaste for sedition. Pierre la Seine, going a step farther, shows that the intention was to recommend to young men temperance in eating and drinking. Just so, too, Jacobus Hugo has satisfied himself that, by Euenis, Homer meant to insinuate John Calvin; by Antinous, Martin Luther; by the Lotophagi, Protestants in general; and, by the Harpies, the Dutch. Our more modern Scholiasts are equally acute. These fellows demonstrate a hidden meaning in “The Antediluvians,” a parable in Powhatan, “new views in Cock Robin,” and transcendentalism in “Hop O’ My Thumb.” In short, it has been shown that no man can sit down to write without a very profound design. Thus to authors in general much trouble is spared. A novelist, for example, need have no care of his moral. It is there﻿—that is to say, it is somewhere﻿—and the moral and the critics can take care of themselves. When the proper time arrives, all that the gentleman intended, and all that he did not intend, will be brought to light, in the *Dial*, or the *Down-Easter*, together with all that he ought to have intended, and the rest that he clearly meant to intend:﻿—so that it will all come very straight in the end.

===Chinese===

一篇有寓意的故事

「*只要一位作者的风俗私德*，」托马斯·德·拉斯托雷斯大人在他的《恋歌集》序言里说，「*是纯洁贞正的，他的作品不同样严正，也就无关紧要了*」——用明白的英语说，就是：只要作者本人道德纯洁，他书里的道德如何，无关痛痒。我们推想，托马斯大人如今正在炼狱里，为这一句高论还债。倘若叫他一直蹲到他的《恋歌集》绝版、或者因无人问津而正式束之高阁为止，那在诗化正义一门，也算得一件妙事。每一篇小说*都应该有*寓意；更要紧的是，批评家们已经发现每一篇小说*都有*。菲利普·梅兰希顿前些年给《蛙鼠之战》作注，证明诗人的用意是唤起人们对暴乱的厌恶。皮埃尔·拉塞纳更进一歩，指出其用意在于劝青年饮食有节。同样，雅各布斯·雨果也使自己满意了：荷马笔下的尤厄尼斯，暗指约翰·加尔文；安提诺乌斯，暗指马丁·路德；食莲人，泛指新教徒；鸟身女妖，则指荷兰人。我们更近代的注家们一样尖。这班人从《洪水前的人》里读出微言，从《波瓦坦》里读出寓言，从《知更鸟科克》里读出新见，从《大拇指》里读出超验主义。总之，已经证明：任何人提起笔，必有一个十分深沉的用意。如此，一般作家们省了多少麻烦。譬如小说家，大可不必为寓意操心。寓意在那里——就是说，在某个地方——寓意同批评家自会彼此照应。时辰一到，这位先生想过的、没想过的，统统都会曝光，登在《日晷》或《唐易斯特》上，连同他本该想过的，以及他显然存心想过的其余种种：——所以末了一切都会妥妥帖帖。

===Original===

There is no just ground, therefore, for the charge brought against me by certain ignoramuses﻿—that I have never written a moral tale, or, in more precise words, a tale with a moral.
