亲王站在蓝屋里，身旁簇拥着一群脸色发白的朝臣。起初，他一开口，这一群人便有一阵轻轻的冲向那闯入者的移动——那人此刻也在近旁，正迈着从容而威严的步子，向说话的人走近。但由于那化装者的疯狂的僭妄在全体的心里激起的一种无名的敬畏，竟找不到一个人伸手去抓他；于是他畅通无阻，走到离亲王之身一码之内；而那庞大的人群仿佛被同一个冲动驱使，从屋子中央缩到墙边，他便一路不间断地——带着他从头显出的那种庄严而均匀的步子——穿过蓝屋到紫屋——穿过紫屋到绿屋——穿过绿屋到橙屋——再从橙屋到白屋——甚至从那里又到紫屋，才有人下定决心动手拦他。然而这时，普洛斯佩罗亲王——被暴怒和片刻怯懦的羞耻逼疯了——匆匆冲过那六间屋子；一个人也不曾跟着他，因为一种致命的恐怖攫住了所有的人。他高举一柄出鞘的短剑，以疾速的狂怒，逼近到那后退的身影三英尺四英尺之内，后者恰已走到绒厅的尽头，突然转过身来，面对他的追逐者。一声尖利的叫喊——短剑闪着光落在黑檀的地毯上，紧接着，普洛斯佩罗亲王也在那地毯上扑倒死去。于是，绝望之下的狂勇一经召唤，一大群狂欢者立刻冲进那间黑屋，抓住那化装的人——那高大的身影一动不动，笔直立在黑檀钟的阴影里——当他们以这样粗暴的蛮劲抓住那尸衣与尸状的假面，发觉里面空无一物、没有任何有形之体时，不由得发出一阵无法言说的恐怖的抽气。

===Original===

And now was acknowledged the presence of the Red Death. He had come like a thief in the night. And one by one dropped the revellers in the blood-bedewed halls of their revel, and died each in the despairing posture of his fall. And the life of the ebony clock went out with that of the last of the gay. And the flames of the tripods expired. And Darkness and Decay and the Red Death held illimitable dominion over all.

===Chinese===

于是红死魔的存在被公认了。他像夜里的贼一样来了。狂欢者们一个接一个倒在他们作乐的血露淋漓的厅堂里，各自保持着跌倒时那绝望的姿势死去。黑檀钟的生命随最后一个快活人的生命熄灭。三脚架的火焰熄灭。黑暗与朽烂与红死魔，握着无边的统治，君临一切。

## The Landscape Garden / 山水园林
===Original===

The garden like a lady fair was cut,

That lay as if she slumbered in delight,

And to the open skies her eyes did shut.

The azure fields of Heaven were ’sembled right

In a large round, set with the flow’rs of light.

The flowers de luce, and the sparks of dew

That hung upon their azure leaves did show

Like twinkling stars that sparkle in the ev’ning blue.

> Giles Fletcher

No more remarkable man ever lived than my friend, the young Ellison. He was remarkable in the entire and continuous profusion of good gifts ever lavished upon him by fortune. From his cradle to his grave, a gale of the blandest prosperity bore him along. Nor do I use the word Prosperity in its mere wordly or external sense. I mean it as synonymous with happiness. The person of whom I speak, seemed born for the purpose of foreshadowing the wild doctrines of Turgot, Price, Priestley, and Condorcet﻿—of exemplifying, by individual instance, what has been deemed the mere chimera of the perfectionists. In the brief existence of Ellison, I fancy, that I have seen refuted the dogma﻿—that in man’s physical and spiritual nature, lies some hidden principle, the antagonist of Bliss. An intimate and anxious examination of his career, has taught me to understand that, in general, from the violation of a few simple laws of Humanity, arises the Wretchedness of mankind; that, as a species, we have in our possession the as yet unwrought elements of Content﻿—and that even now, in the present blindness and darkness of all idea on the great question of the Social Condition, it is not impossible that Man, the individual, under certain unusual and highly fortuitous conditions, may be happy.

===Chinese===

那花园裁剪得像一位淑女，

她躺着，仿佛在欢愉中沉睡，

把双眼闭向敞开的天宇。

天堂蔚蓝的田野，被如实模仿

在一个巨大的圆环里，缀满光的花朵。

鸢尾花，同露的微芒

悬在蔚蓝的叶上，宛如

黄昏碧空里闪闪眨眼的星。

——贾尔斯·弗莱彻（Giles Fletcher）

再没有谁比我朋友年轻的埃利森（Ellison）活得更异乎寻常。他的异乎寻常，在于命运倾泻在他身上的好礼物，既完全，又连续不断。从摇篮到坟墓，一阵最温和的顺遂之风，把他一路吹送。我用的「顺遂」，也不仅取其尘世的、外表的意义。我拿它作幸福的同义语。我说的这个人，生来就像是为预演蒂尔戈、普赖斯、普里斯特利与孔多塞的狂放学说——为以一己的实例，验证那被当作完普论者的呓语的东西。在埃利森短短的一生里，我自以为看见了那条教条的反证——那条教条说：人的肉体与精神的天性里，藏着某种与福祉为敌的隐秘原理。对他的生涯作了一番亲密而焦虑的检视之后，我才懂得：人类的悲惨，大体出于对几条简单的人道之律的违犯；我们这个物种，手里原本握着尚未加工的知足的元素；而且即便此刻，在这大地上一切关于社会状况的伟大问题全都昏盲无见的时候，个人的人，在某些非常而大碰运气的境况之下，也未必不能幸福。

===Original===

With opinions such as these was my young friend fully imbued; and thus is it especially worthy of observation that the uninterrupted enjoyment which distinguished his life was in great part the result of preconcert. It is, indeed evident, that with less of the instinctive philosophy which, now and then, stands so well in the stead of experience, Mr. Ellison would have found himself precipitated, by the very extraordinary successes of his life, into the common vortex of Unhappiness which yawns for those of preeminent endowments. But it is by no means my present object to pen an essay on Happiness. The ideas of my friend may be summed up in a few words. He admitted but four unvarying laws, or rather elementary principles, of Bliss. That which he considered chief, was (strange to say!) the simple and purely physical one of free exercise in the open air. “The health,” he said, “attainable by other means than this is scarcely worth the name.” He pointed to the tillers of the earth﻿—the only people who, as a class, are proverbially more happy than others﻿—and then he instanced the high ecstasies of the foxhunter. His second principle was the love of woman. His third was the contempt of ambition. His fourth was an object of unceasing pursuit; and he held that, other things being equal, the extent of happiness was proportioned to the spirituality of this object.

===Chinese===

我这位年轻的朋友满怀着这一类见解；因此格外值得注意：他一生不间断的享受，在很大程度上是有意预备的果。实在很明显：若不是他凭着那种时常能顶替经验的本能哲思，埃利森先生势必被自己一生非凡的成功，拋进那为禀赋超群者张着口的寻常不幸的漩涡。但写一篇论幸福的文章，决非我此刻的目的。我朋友的见解几句话就可说尽。他只承认四条不变的幸福之律，或者毋宁说四条基本原理。他认为居首的（说来奇怪！）竟是那条单纯而纯粹肉体的：在露天自由活动。「用别的法子换来的健康，」他说，「配不上健康这个名字。」他举猎狐人的狂喜为例，又指着耕田的人——唯一可以公认为整体上比别人更幸福的一类人。他的第二条原理是对女人的爱。第三条是对野心的鄙弃。第四条是一个可以追求不懈的目标；他认为，其余条件相等时，幸福的多少正比于这目标的精神性。

===Original===

I have said that Ellison was remarkable in the continuous profusion of good gifts lavished upon him by Fortune. In personal grace and beauty he exceeded all men. His intellect was of that order to which the attainment of knowledge is less a labor than a necessity and an intuition. His family was one of the most illustrious of the empire. His bride was the loveliest and most devoted of women. His possessions had been always ample; but, upon the attainment of his one and twentieth year, it was discovered that one of those extraordinary freaks of Fate had been played in his behalf which startle the whole social world amid which they occur, and seldom fail radically to alter the entire moral constitution of those who are their objects. It appears that about one hundred years prior to Mr. Ellison’s attainment of his majority, there had died, in a remote province, one Mr. Seabright Ellison. This gentlemen had amassed a princely fortune, and, having no very immediate connections, conceived the whim of suffering his wealth to accumulate for a century after his decease. Minutely and sagaciously directing the various modes of investment, he bequeathed the aggregate amount to the nearest of blood, bearing the name Ellison, who should be alive at the end of the hundred years. Many futile attempts had been made to set aside this singular bequest; their ex post facto character rendered them abortive; but the attention of a jealous government was aroused, and a decree finally obtained, forbidding all similar accumulations. This act did not prevent young Ellison, upon his twenty-first birthday, from entering into possession, as the heir of his ancestor, Seabright, of a fortune of *four hundred and fifty millions of dollars*.26

===Chinese===

我说过，埃利森异乎寻常之处，在于命运倾泻给他的好礼物连续不断。论仪表的优雅俊美，他超过所有人。他的心智属于那一类：求得知识不像劳作，倒像必需与直觉。他的门第是帝国最煊赫的门第之一。他的新娘是女人里最可爱、最忠贞的。他的家产一直充裕；可到他二十一岁成年的那一天，人们才发现：命运为他玩了一手那样罕见的奇招——这类奇招一出，震骇它发生的整个社会，而少有不彻底改换受它眷顾者的道德结构。原来在埃利森先生成年前一百年，有一个西布赖特·埃利森先生，死在一个边远的省份。这位先生积下了一份王侯的家私；因没有很近的亲支，起了一个怪念头：让财富在他死后滚利一百年。他把种种投资的路数一一精细而精明地安排好，然后把总额遗赠给百年期满时在世、血缘最近、姓埃利森的人。曾多次试图推翻这份奇特的遗赠；它们事后立法的性质使它们尽数落空；可一个猜忌的政府被惊动了，终于立下一法，禁止一切同样的滚积。然而这一法并没有拦住年轻的埃利森：二十一岁生日那天，他以先祖西布赖特继承人的身份，继承了*四亿五千万美元*的家产。〔26〕

===Original===

When it had become definitely known that such was the enormous wealth inherited, there were, of course, many speculations as to the mode of its disposal. The gigantic magnitude and the immediately available nature of the sum, dazzled and bewildered all who thought upon the topic. The possessor of any *appreciable* amount of money might have been imagined to perform any one of a thousand things. With riches merely surpassing those of any citizen, it would have been easy to suppose him engaging to supreme excess in the fashionable extravagances of his time; or busying himself with political intrigues; or aiming at ministerial power; or purchasing increase of nobility, or devising gorgeous architectural piles; or collecting large specimens of Virtu; or playing the munificent patron of Letters and Art; or endowing and bestowing his name upon extensive institutions of charity. But, for the inconceivable wealth in the actual possession of the young heir, these objects and all ordinary objects were felt to be inadequate. Recourse was had to figures; and figures but sufficed to confound. It was seen, that even at three percent, the annual income of the inheritance amounted to no less than thirteen millions and five hundred thousand dollars; which was one million and one hundred and twenty-five thousand per month; or thirty-six thousand, nine hundred and eighty-six per day, or one thousand five hundred and forty-one per hour, or six and twenty dollars for every minute that flew. Thus the usual track of supposition was thoroughly broken up. Men knew not what to imagine. There were some who even conceived that Mr. Ellison would divest himself forthwith of at least two-thirds of his fortune as of utterly superfluous opulence; enriching whole troops of his relatives by division of his superabundance.

===Chinese===

这笔巨额遗产一传开，自然众说纷纭，都在猜它怎样处置。这笔款的巨大与现成，难住了每一个想过这题目的人。凡握有*可观数目*金钱的人，都可以被想象去做一千件事里的任何一件。倘若他只是富过任何平民，尽可以设想他沉溺于当世的时髦挥霍到极顶；或热衷政治阴谋；或觊觎部长之权；或捐买爵位的晋阶；或设计辉煌的建筑巨构；或广收古玩巨藏；或扮演文艺的豪客恩主；或捐建大规模的慈善机构并以己名命名。可对于这位年轻继承人实际握有的难以想象的财富，这一切目标、一切寻常目标，都显得天地太窄。于是求助算术，算术也只够添乱。一算便知：即便按三厘利，这笔遗产的年入也不少于一千三百五十万美元——每月一百一十二万五千；每天三万六千九百八十六元；每小时一千五百四十一元；飞逝的每一分钟，二十六元。寻常猜想的轨道就此彻底冲垮。人们不知该怎么想象了。甚至有人设想，埃利森先生会立刻舍掉至少三分之二的家财，视之为全然多余的豪富——把盈余分掉，让整族整族的亲眷致富。

===Original===

I was not surprised, however, to perceive that he had long made up his mind upon a topic which had occasioned so much of discussion to his friends. Nor was I greatly astonished at the nature of his decision. In the widest and noblest sense, he was a poet. He comprehended, moreover, the true character, the august aims, the supreme majesty and dignity of the poetic sentiment. The proper gratification of the sentiment he instinctively felt to lie in the *creation of novel forms of Beauty*. Some peculiarities, either in his early education, or in the nature of his intellect, had tinged with what is termed materialism the whole cast of his ethical speculations; and it was this bias, perhaps, which imperceptibly led him to perceive that the most advantageous, if not the sole legitimate field for the exercise of the poetic sentiment, was to be found in the creation of novel moods of purely *physical* loveliness. Thus it happened that he became neither musician nor poet; if we use this latter term in its everyday acceptation. Or it might have been that he became neither the one nor the other, in pursuance of an idea of his which I have already mentioned﻿—the idea, that in the contempt of ambition lay one of the essential principles of happiness on earth. Is it not, indeed, possible that while a *high* order of genius is necessarily ambitious, the *highest* is invariably *above* that which is termed ambition? And may it not thus happen that many far greater than Milton, have contentedly remained “mute and inglorious?” I believe the world has never yet seen, and that, unless through some series of accidents goading the noblest order of mind into distasteful exertion, the world will *never* behold, that full extent of triumphant execution, in the richer productions of Art, of which the human nature is absolutely capable.

===Chinese===

至于那一点——那叫他的朋友们议论纷纷的一点——他早已打定主意，我并不惊讶。他那决断的性质，也不很出我意外。在最宽、最高的意义上，他是诗人。他还领会诗情真实的品格、庄严的鹄的、至高的威仪与尊贵。对这诗情的正当满足，他本能地感到，在于*创造新颖的美的形式*。他早年所受的教育，或他心智的本性，有某些特殊之处，给他全部的伦理玄思染上了所谓唯物主义的色彩；也许正是这一偏，不知不觉引他看出：诗情的演练，那最有利——即便不算唯一正当——的园地，在于创造纯然*肉体的*可爱的新气象。于是他既没有成为音乐家，也没有成为诗人——倘若这后一个字取它日常的意义。也可能是：他单单为贯彻自己的一个念头——我已经提过——幸福的根本之一在于鄙弃野心——才不屑于成为二者。天赋高者必野心勃勃，而*最高*的天才，*高*于所谓野心之上——这难道不是可能的么？而正因如此，多少远胜弥尔顿的人，岂不心甘情愿地「无声无闻，不见经传」了一世？我相信，世人从不曾见过——而且，除非一连串的意外，逼着最高贵的心智去做它厌烦的苦役，世人也将*永远*见不到——人性在艺术更丰饶的产品里所能达到的那全幅凯旋的作为。

===Original===

Mr. Ellison became neither musician nor poet; although no man lived more profoundly enamored both of Music and the Muse. Under other circumstances than those which invested him, it is not impossible that he would have become a painter. The field of sculpture, although in its nature rigidly poetical, was too limited in its extent and in its consequences, to have occupied, at any time, much of his attention. And I have now mentioned *all* the provinces in which even the most liberal understanding of the poetic sentiment has declared this sentiment capable of expatiating. I mean the most liberal public or recognized conception of the idea involved in the phrase “poetic sentiment.” But Mr. Ellison imagined that the richest, and altogether the most natural and most suitable province, had been blindly neglected. No definition had spoken of the *Landscape-Gardener*, as of the poet; yet my friend could not fail to perceive that the creation of the Landscape-Garden offered to the true muse the most magnificent of opportunities. Here was, indeed, the fairest field for the display of invention, or imagination, in the endless combining of forms of novel Beauty; the elements which should enter into combination being, at all times, and by a vast superiority, the most glorious which the earth could afford. In the multiform of the tree, and in the multicolor of the flower, he recognized the most direct and the most energetic efforts of Nature at physical loveliness. And in the direction or concentration of this effort, or, still more properly, in its adaption to the eyes which were to behold it upon earth, he perceived that he should be employing the best means﻿—laboring to the greatest advantage﻿—in the fulfilment of his destiny as Poet.

===Chinese===

埃利森没有成为音乐家，也没有成为诗人；虽然再没有谁比他更深地爱着音乐与诗神。倘若境遇不是那样，他未必不会成为画家。雕刻，虽然本性上彻头彻尾是诗的，格局与后果都太有限，任何时候都不至于占去他多少心思。至此，我已数尽了即便对诗情最宽的理解也承认它得以驰骋的一切疆域。我是指对「诗情」一语所含观念的那种最宽的、公认的或被承认的概念。可埃利森想象：最丰饶、而全然最自然、最相宜的那一疆域，被盲目地怠慢了。从没有哪一条定义把*造园家*同诗人并提；然而我的朋友不能不看出：风景园林的创造，献给真正的诗神的是最壮丽的机会。这里确是最美的园地，供发明或想象施展：无穷无尽地组合新颖的美的形式；而入组合的元素，任何时候都以绝大的优势，是大地所能提供的最辉煌的元素。在树木的千形、花卉的万色里，他认出自然朝肉体之美所作的最直接、最劲健的努力。而在导引或汇聚这努力——或说得更准，使它适配于那将要在大地上凝望它的眼睛——他看出自己将用着最好的手段——以最大的便宜劳作——成全他做诗人的天命。

===Original===

“Its adaptation to the eyes which were to behold it upon earth.” In his explanation of this phraseology, Mr. Ellison did much towards solving what has always seemed to me an enigma. I mean the fact (which none but the ignorant dispute), that no such combinations of scenery exist in Nature as the painter of genius has in his power to produce. No such Paradises are to be found in reality as have glowed upon the canvas of Claude. In the most enchanting of natural landscapes, there will always be found a defect or an excess﻿—many excesses and defects. While the component parts may exceed, individually, the highest skill of the artist, the arrangement of the parts will always be susceptible of improvement. In short, no position can be attained, from which an artistical eye, looking steadily, will not find matter of offence, in what is technically termed the *composition* of a natural landscape. And yet how unintelligible is this! In all other matters we are justly instructed to regard Nature as supreme. With her details we shrink from competition. Who shall presume to imitate the colors of the tulip, or to improve the proportions of the lily of the valley? The criticism which says, of sculpture or of portraiture, that “Nature is to be exalted rather than imitated,” is in error. No pictorial or sculptural combinations of *points* of human loveliness, do more than approach the living and breathing human beauty as it gladdens our daily path. Byron, who often erred, erred not in saying:

I’ve seen more living beauty, ripe and real,

Than all the nonsense of their stone ideal.

===Chinese===

「使它适配于那将要在大地上凝望它的眼睛。」埃利森对这一句的解释，大有助于解开在我看去始终是谜的一件事——即这样的事实（除无知者外无人争议）：自然里不存在天才画家所能造出的那种景色的组合。现实里找不到克劳德画布上燃烧过的那种乐园。在最醉人的自然风景里，总有一处缺陷或一处过剩——许多过剩与缺陷。组件单看，尽可令艺术家最高的技艺失色；可这些组件的排布，却永远有可改善的余地。总之，占不到一个位置，让艺术家的眼睛凝神望去，不在技术上称作自然风景的*构图*里发现刺目之处。而这多么不可解！在别的一切事上，我们都公正地受教：视自然为至高。同她的细部，我们避而不敢竞争。谁敢模仿郁金香的颜色，或改良铃兰的比例？那种批评——说雕刻或肖像「自然当被高举，而非被模仿」——是错的。人物画与雕刻里那些可爱的*点*的组合，至多不过是接近活的、呼吸着的人美——她使我们的日日之途生辉。拜伦常常出错，可在这句里没有错：

我见过更多活着的美，熟而真，

胜过他们石头的理想的那一切胡说。

===Original===

In landscape alone is the principle of the critic true; and, having felt its truth here, it is but the headlong spirit of generalization which has induced him to pronounce it true throughout *all* the domains of Art. Having, I say, *felt* its truth here. For the feeling is no affectation or chimera. The mathematics afford no more absolute demonstrations, than the *sentiment* of his Art yields to the artist. He not only believes, but positively knows, that such and such apparently arbitrary arrangements of matter, or form, constitute, and alone constitute, the true Beauty. Yet his reasons have not yet been matured into expression. It remains for a more profound analysis than the world has yet seen, fully to investigate and express them. Nevertheless is he confirmed in his instinctive opinions, by the concurrence of all his compeers. Let a composition be defective; let an emendation be wrought in its mere arrangement of form; let this emendation be submitted to every artist in the world; by each will its necessity be admitted. And even far more than this, in remedy of the defective composition, each insulated member of the fraternity will *suggest* the identical emendation.

===Chinese===

唯独在风景的排布里，批评家的原则才是真的；而他在这里尝到了它的真，又是那股子鲁莽的泛化劲，引得他宣布它通行于艺术*一切*的疆域。我说，他在这里*尝到*了它的真；因为这感觉不是矫饰，不是幻象。数学给不出比艺术家的艺术情感给他的更绝对的证明。他不但相信，而且确知：物质或形式这样那样看似任意的排布，构成、而且唯独构成真正的美。只是他的理由，还没有酝酿成语言。要充分考察并表述它们，还须待一种比世人迄今所见更深的分析。但凭全行同道的异口同声，他那本能的见解得到了确证。任取一幅有缺陷的构图；单在形的排布上做一处订正；把这订正呈给世上每一位艺术家；人人都会承认它确有必要。还不止此：为救这有缺陷的构图，同行中每一个孤立的人，*提的*都会是同一处订正。

===Original===

I repeat that in landscape arrangements, or collocations alone, is the *physical* Nature susceptible of “exaltation” and that, therefore, her susceptibility of improvement at this one point, was a mystery which, hitherto I had been unable to solve. It was Mr. Ellison who first suggested the idea that what we regarded as improvement or exaltation of the natural beauty, was really such, as respected only the mortal or human *point of view*; that each alteration or disturbance of the primitive scenery might possibly effect a blemish in the picture, if we could suppose this picture viewed *at large* from some remote point in the heavens. “It is easily understood,” says Mr. Ellison, “that what might improve a closely scrutinized detail, might, at the same time, injure a general and more distantly observed effect.” He spoke upon this topic with warmth: regarding not so much its immediate or obvious importance (which is little), as the character of the conclusions to which it might lead, or of the collateral propositions which it might serve to corroborate or sustain. There *might be* a class of beings, human once, but now to humanity invisible, for whose scrutiny and for whose refined appreciation of the beautiful, more especially than for our own, had been set in order by God the great landscape-garden of *the whole earth*.

In the course of our discussion, my young friend took occasion to quote some passages from a writer who has been supposed to have well treated this theme.

===Chinese===

我再说一遍：唯独在风景的排布或配置里，物质的*自然*才可被「高举」；因此，她在这一点上竟能被改善，一直是我不解的谜。是埃利森先生头一个提出这个念头：我们所谓自然美的改善或高举，就凡人或人类的*观点*而言才真是如此；倘若我们设想这幅画从天上的某个远点*全幅*望去，风景的每一改动或扰动，或许会在画上造成一处瑕疵。「不难明白，」埃利森先生说，「也许能改良一处细细审视的细节的东西，同时会伤害一个总体的、更远处观看的效果。」他谈这个题目谈得热切：他着眼的不那么是它眼前或明显的分量（那很小），而更在它可能引出的结论的品格，或它可能佐证或支撑的旁属命题。*可能有*一类存在者，曾为人身，而今对人类不可见；为了他们的审视、为了他们对美的精微的领略——尤甚于为了我们自己——上帝才把*整个大地*这座大风景园安排齐整。

在我们讨论的过程里，我这位年轻的朋友借机引用了一位作家的几段文字；人们一向认为，这作家把这题目处理得极好。

===Original===

“There are, properly,” he writes, “but two styles of landscape-gardening, the natural and the artificial. One seeks to recall the original beauty of the country, by adapting its means to the surrounding scenery; cultivating trees in harmony with the hills or plain of the neighboring land; detecting and bringing into practice those nice relations of size, proportion and color which, hid from the common observer, are revealed everywhere to the experienced student of nature. The result of the natural style of gardening, is seen rather in the absence of all defects and incongruities﻿—in the prevalence of a beautiful harmony and order, than in the creation of any special wonders or miracles. The artificial style has as many varieties as there are different tastes to gratify. It has a certain general relation to the various styles of building. There are the stately avenues and retirements of Versailles; Italian terraces; and a various mixed old English style, which bears some relation to the domestic Gothic or English Elizabethan architecture. Whatever may be said against the abuses of the artificial landscape-gardening, a mixture of pure art in a garden scene, adds to it a great beauty. This is partly pleasing to the eye, by the show of order and design, and partly moral. A terrace, with an old moss-covered balustrade, calls up at once to the eye, the fair forms that have passed there in other days. The slightest exhibition of art is an evidence of care and human interest.”

===Chinese===

「造园法式，」他写道，「严格说只有两种：自然的与人工的。前者力求唤回乡土的原本之美，把它的手段适配于四围的景物；培植林木，使之同近处的山丘或平原相谐；找出那些尺寸、比例、颜色的精微关系，并把它们付诸实行——这些关系瞒过寻常观者，却处处向有经验的研究自然的学生显形。自然式造园的结果，与其说见于创造任何特殊的奇迹，不如说见于一切缺陷与不谐的荡然无存——见于一种美的谐和与秩序的通体流行。人工式则有多少待餍足的趣味，便有多少变体。它同建筑的种种式样有某种总体的关联。有凡尔赛那些堂皇的林荫道与幽隐处；有意大利的露台；有一种驳杂的老英国式，它同家常哥特式或英国伊丽莎白时代的建筑有些瓜葛。无论对人工式造园的滥用可以说多少闲话，园景里掺入纯粹的艺术，总添一种大美。这美一半悦目，靠秩序与设计的排场；一半是道德的。一座露台，带一道旧而覆苔的栏楯，霎时便向眼睛唤起别的年代里曾在那里经过的美的身影。艺术的一点点展露，便是关怀与人间兴趣的凭证。」

===Original===

“From what I have already observed,” said Mr. Ellison, “you will understand that I reject the idea, here expressed, of ‘recalling the original beauty of the country.’ The original beauty is never so great as that which may be introduced. Of course, much depends upon the selection of a spot with *capabilities*. What is said in respect to the ‘detecting and bringing into practice those nice relations of size, proportion and color,’ is a mere vagueness of speech, which may mean much, or little, or nothing, and which guides in no degree. That the true ‘result of the natural style of gardening is seen rather in the absence of all defects and incongruities, than in the creation of any special wonders or miracles,’ is a proposition better suited to the grovelling apprehension of the herd, than to the fervid dreams of the man of genius. The merit suggested is, at best, negative, and appertains to that hobbling criticism which, in letters, would elevate Addison into apotheosis. In truth, while that merit which consists in the mere avoiding demerit, appeals directly to the understanding, and can thus be foreshadowed in *Rule*, the loftier merit, which breathes and flames in invention or creation, can be apprehended solely in its results. Rule applies but to the excellences of avoidance﻿—to the virtues which deny or refrain. Beyond these the critical art can but suggest. We may be instructed to build an Odyssey, but it is in vain that we are told *how* to conceive a *Tempest*, an *Inferno*, a *Prometheus Bound*, a *Nightingale*, such as that of Keats, or the *Sensitive Plant* of Shelley. But, the thing done, the wonder accomplished, and the capacity for apprehension becomes universal. The sophists of the *negative* school, who, through inability to create, have scoffed at creation, are now found the loudest in applause. What, in its chrysalis condition of principle, affronted their demure reason, never fails, in its maturity of accomplishment, to extort admiration from their instinct of the beautiful or of the sublime.

===Chinese===

「由我方才所说，」埃利森先生说，「您会明白：我拒绝这里表述的那个观念——『唤回乡土的原本之美』。原本之美从来不曾大过可以被引入的美。自然，许多取决于地点的挑选，看它有怎样的*潜质*。至于所谓『找出那些尺寸、比例、颜色的精微关系并把它们付诸实行』，那不过是话说的含混，可以解作多，可以解作少，可以解作无，一星半点也指不了路。至于说『自然式造园的真结果，与其说见于创造任何特殊的奇迹，不如说见于一切缺陷与不谐的荡然无存』——这个命题，更适合群氓的卑琐理解，不适合天才的炽热的梦。这里暗示的功绩，充其量是消极的，属于那种蹒跚的批评——它在文学里会把艾迪生捧上神坛。实在说，仅仅免于缺陷的那种功绩，直接向理解力呼吁，因此可以在*规则*里预先描出；而那在发明或创造里呼吸着、燃烧着的更高的功绩，却只能凭它的结果来领会。规则只管避让的美德——否认或节制的美德。除此之外，批评的艺术只能提示。我们可以受教去写一部《奥德赛》；可要我们构想一部《暴风雨》、一部《地狱篇》、一部《被缚的普罗米修斯》、一首济慈那样的《夜莺颂》、雪莱那样的《敏感的植物》，人家告诉我们*怎样*构想也是枉然。但事既成，奇迹既立，领会的才能便遍及人人。那*消极*一派的诡辩家，从前因无力创造而嘲笑创造，如今发现他们鼓起掌来最响。凡是还在原则的蛹里、曾冒犯他们端方理性之物，一旦长成业绩的成熟，从他们那对美或崇高的本能里，从来免不了榨出赞美。

===Original===

“Our author’s observations on the artificial style of gardening,” continued Mr. Ellison, “are less objectionable. ‘A mixture of pure art in a garden scene, adds to it a great beauty.’ This is just, and the reference to the sense of human interest is equally so. I repeat that the principle here expressed, is incontrovertible; but there *may be* something even beyond it. There may be an object in full keeping with the principle suggested﻿—an object unattainable by the means ordinarily in possession of mankind, yet which, if attained, would lend a charm to the landscape-garden immeasurably surpassing that which a merely *human* interest could bestow. The true poet possessed of very unusual pecuniary resources, might possibly, while retaining the necessary idea of *art* or *interest* or *culture*, so imbue his designs at once with extent and novelty of Beauty, as to convey the sentiment of *spiritual* interference. It will be seen that, in bringing about such result, he secures all the advantages of *interest* or *design*, while relieving his work of all the harshness and technicality of Art. In the most rugged of wildernesses﻿—in the most savage of the scenes of pure Nature﻿—there is apparent the *art* of a Creator; yet is *this* art apparent only to reflection; in no respect has it the obvious force of a feeling. Now, if we imagine this sense of the Almighty Design to be *harmonized* in a measurable degree, if we suppose a landscape whose combined *strangeness*, vastness, definitiveness, and magnificence, shall inspire the idea of culture, or care, or superintendence, on the part of intelligences superior yet akin to humanity﻿—then the sentiment of *interest* is preserved, while the Art is made to assume the air of an intermediate or secondary Nature﻿—a Nature which is not God, nor an emanation of God, but which still is Nature, in the sense that it is the handiwork of the angels that hover between man and God.”

===Chinese===

「我们的作者关于人工式造园的议论，」埃利森先生继续说，「较无可议。『园景里掺入纯粹的艺术，总添一种大美。』这话对；关涉人间兴趣之感的那层也对。我再说一遍：这里表述的原则无可辩驳；但它*之上*也许还有东西。也许存在一个与这原则完全相称的目标——个人凭寻常手段不可企及、而一旦企及，将赋风景园林以一层魅力，远过一个单是*人的*兴趣所能给的。一位拥有极不寻常财力的真诗人，一面保留*艺术*或*兴趣*或*栽培*的必需观念，一面却可以把自己的设计浸透以美的广度与新奇，浸透到传达出*神灵*干预之感。可以看出：成全这样的结果，他既得*兴趣*或*设计*的一切好处，又为作品卸去了艺术的一切粗硬与匠气。在最崎岖的荒野——在最蛮荒的纯自然之景里——也显见一位造物者的*艺术*；可*这*艺术唯反思可见；它丝毫没有一份情感的显豁的力量。现在，倘若我们设想这全能设计之感被*谐调*到可量的一阶，倘若我们假定这样一幅风景：它的兼有的*奇*、浩大、分明与壮丽，传达出关切、栽培、监临之意——出自一族优于人却近于人的存在——那么，*兴趣*之情保住了，而艺术便有了居间的或第二重自然的神气——这自然不是上帝，不是上帝的流射，却仍是自然——在它是悬于人神之间的众天使的手作这个意义上的自然。」

===Original===

It was in devoting his gigantic wealth to the practical embodiment of a vision such as this﻿—in the free exercise in the open air, which resulted from personal direction of his plans﻿—in the continuous and unceasing *object* which these plans afforded﻿—in the contempt of ambition which it enabled him more to feel than to affect﻿—and, lastly, it was in the companionship and sympathy of a devoted wife, that Ellison thought to find, *and found*, an exemption from the ordinary cares of Humanity, with a far greater amount of positive happiness than ever glowed in the rapt daydreams of De Stäel.

===Chinese===

正是把他的巨额财富，献给这样一个幻象的实际成形——在亲自督理计划所确保的露天自由活动里——在这些计划所供给的不懈的*目标*里——在它使他得以真心怀抱多过矫饰的对野心的鄙弃里——最后，还在一位忠贞妻子的相伴与同情里——埃利森以为他寻得、也*确已寻得*：对人寻常忧虑的豁免，以及一份远过于德·斯塔尔夫人销魂的白日梦里所燃的、实实在在的幸福。

## The Mystery of Marie Rogêt27 / 玛丽·罗热疑案
===Original===

A Sequel to “The Murders in the Rue Morgue”

Es giebt eine Reihe idealischer Begebenheiten, die der Wirklichkeit parallel lauft. Selten fallen sie zusammen. Menschen und zufalle modifieiren gewohulich die idealische Begebenheit, so dass sie unvollkommen erscheint, und ihre Folgen gleichfalls unvollkommen sind. So bei der Reformation; statt des Protestantismus kam das Lutherthum hervor.

There are ideal series of events which run parallel with the real ones. They rarely coincide. Men and circumstances generally modify the ideal train of events, so that it seems imperfect, and its consequences are equally imperfect. Thus with the Reformation; instead of Protestantism came Lutheranism.

> Novalis.28 *Moral Ansichten*

There are few persons, even among the calmest thinkers, who have not occasionally been startled into a vague yet thrilling half-credence in the supernatural, by *coincidences* of so seemingly marvellous a character that, as *mere* coincidences, the intellect has been unable to receive them. Such sentiments﻿—for the half-credences of which I speak have never the full force of *thought*﻿—such sentiments are seldom thoroughly stifled unless by reference to the doctrine of chance, or, as it is technically termed, the Calculus of Probabilities. Now this Calculus is, in its essence, purely mathematical; and thus we have the anomaly of the most rigidly exact in science applied to the shadow and spirituality of the most intangible in speculation.

The extraordinary details which I am now called upon to make public, will be found to form, as regards sequence of time, the primary branch of a series of scarcely intelligible *coincidences*, whose secondary or concluding branch will be recognized by all readers in the late murder of **Mary Cecila Rogers**, at New York.

===Chinese===

——「莫尔格街凶杀案」续篇

Es giebt eine Reihe idealischer Begebenheiten, die der Wirklichkeit parallel lauft. Selten fallen sie zusammen. Menschen und zufalle modifieiren gewohulich die idealische Begebenheit, so dass sie unvollkommen erscheint, und ihre Folgen gleichfalls unvollkommen sind. So bei der Reformation; statt des Protestantismus kam das Lutherthum hervor.

有一些理想的事件系列，与真实的事件系列并行。它们极少重合。人与际遇通常改变理想的事件进程，使它显得不完满，而它的后果也同样不完满。宗教改革便是如此；出来的不是新教，而是路德宗。

——诺瓦利斯（Novalis）《道德观》（Moral Ansichten）〔28〕

极少有人——即便在最沉静的思想者中间——不曾偶尔被一些表面惊人的*巧合*惊起一种模糊然而悸动的对超自然的半信；作为*单纯的*巧合，智力已无力容纳它们。这样的心绪——我说的半信从来不曾达到*思想*的全部力度——若不援引机会的学说，即技术上所谓概率演算，便很少被彻底压熄。而这演算，就其本质而言，纯是数学；于是我们有了这样一个反常：科学里最精确不过的东西，被应用在思辨里最不可捉摸的影与灵上面。

我此刻被召唤公之于众的这些离奇的细节，就时间的顺序而言，将构成一串几乎不可理解的*巧合*的主枝；这串巧合的次枝或结枝，一切读者都会在**玛丽·塞西拉·罗杰斯**新近在纽约被谋杀一案里认出来。

===Original===

When, in an article entitled “The Murders in the Rue Morgue,” I endeavored, about a year ago, to depict some very remarkable features in the mental character of my friend, the Chevalier C. Auguste Dupin, it did not occur to me that I should ever resume the subject. This depicting of character constituted my design; and this design was thoroughly fulfilled in the wild train of circumstances brought to instance Dupin’s idiosyncrasy. I might have adduced other examples, but I should have proven no more. Late events, however, in their surprising development, have startled me into some farther details, which will carry with them the air of extorted confession. Hearing what I have lately heard, it would be indeed strange should I remain silent in regard to what I both heard and saw so long ago.

Upon the winding up of the tragedy involved in the deaths of Madame L’Espanaye and her daughter, the Chevalier dismissed the affair at once from his attention, and relapsed into his old habits of moody reverie. Prone, at all times, to abstraction, I readily fell in with his humor; and, continuing to occupy our chambers in the Faubourg Saint Germain, we gave the Future to the winds, and slumbered tranquilly in the Present, weaving the dull world around us into dreams.

But these dreams were not altogether uninterrupted. It may readily be supposed that the part played by my friend, in the drama at the Rue Morgue, had not failed of its impression upon the fancies of the Parisian police. With its emissaries, the name of Dupin had grown into a household word. The simple character of those inductions by which he had disentangled the mystery never having been explained even to the Prefect, or to any other individual than myself, of course it is not surprising that the affair was regarded as little less than miraculous, or that the Chevalier’s analytical abilities acquired for him the credit of intuition. His frankness would have led him to disabuse every inquirer of such prejudice; but his indolent humor forbade all farther agitation of a topic whose interest to himself had long ceased. It thus happened that he found himself the cynosure of the political eyes; and the cases were not few in which attempt was made to engage his services at the Prefecture. One of the most remarkable instances was that of the murder of a young girl named Marie Rogêt.

===Chinese===

约一年前，我写过一篇题为「莫尔格街凶杀案」的文章，力图描画我的朋友C·奥古斯特·杜宾（C. Auguste Dupin）骑士心智品格的某些非常显著的特点；我那时不曾想到还会重提这个题目。描画品格是我的设计；而这设计，在那用以例证杜宾独特气质的狂放的情节之链里，得到了十足的完成。我本可以添上别的例子，但证明不了更多。然而晚近的事件，以其惊人的展开，把我惊起，逼出一些进一步的细节；这些细节将带着被榨出的供词的气味。既已听到我近来听到的一切，倘若我对久已既闻且见的事保持缄默，那才真正奇怪。

勒斯帕奈太太和她女儿之死所含的那场悲剧收场之后，骑士立刻把这件事从注意里抹去，重新沉入他阴郁遐想的老习惯。他向来容易出神，我欣然随他的兴致；继续占用圣日耳曼区的寓所，我们把未来交给风，安睡在现在里，把周遭枯燥的世界织成梦。

但这些梦并不全然不受搅扰。不难设想：我朋友在莫尔格街那出戏里扮演的角色，已在巴黎警察的想象上留下印象。同它的密探们在一起，杜宾的名字长成了家常的词。他借以解开那谜底的那些推断何等单纯，这层道理连总监也不曾获释，除我之外也没告诉任何别人；因此那案子被看作近乎神迹，骑士的分析能力为他博得直觉的名声——这自然不足为怪。他的坦率原会引他去打消每一个探询者的这种成见；但他慵懒的性情禁止他对一个自己久已无味的题目再作搅动。于是他发现自己成了政界众目所瞩的人物；求他出力的案子并不少。其中最显著的一例，便是一个名叫玛丽·罗热（Marie Rogêt）的少女被谋杀。

===Original===

This event occurred about two years after the atrocity in the Rue Morgue. Marie, whose Christian and family name will at once arrest attention from their resemblance to those of the unfortunate “cigar-girl,” was the only daughter of the widow Estelle Rogêt. The father had died during the child’s infancy, and from the period of his death, until within eighteen months before the assassination which forms the subject of our narrative, the mother and daughter had dwelt together in the Rue Pavée Saint Andrée;29 Madame there keeping a pension, assisted by Marie. Affairs went on thus until the latter had attained her twenty-second year, when her great beauty attracted the notice of a perfumer, who occupied one of the shops in the basement of the Palais Royal, and whose custom lay chiefly among the desperate adventurers infesting that neighborhood. Monsieur Le Blanc30 was not unaware of the advantages to be derived from the attendance of the fair Marie in his perfumery; and his liberal proposals were accepted eagerly by the girl, although with somewhat more of hesitation by Madame.

The anticipations of the shopkeeper were realized, and his rooms soon became notorious through the charms of the sprightly grisette. She had been in his employ about a year, when her admirers were thrown info confusion by her sudden disappearance from the shop. Monsieur Le Blanc was unable to account for her absence, and Madame Rogêt was distracted with anxiety and terror. The public papers immediately took up the theme, and the police were upon the point of making serious investigations, when, one fine morning, after the lapse of a week, Marie, in good health, but with a somewhat saddened air, made her reappearance at her usual counter in the perfumery. All inquiry, except that of a private character, was of course immediately hushed. Monsieur Le Blanc professed total ignorance, as before. Marie, with Madame, replied to all questions, that the last week had been spent at the house of a relation in the country. Thus the affair died away, and was generally forgotten; for the girl, ostensibly to relieve herself from the impertinence of curiosity, soon bade a final adieu to the perfumer, and sought the shelter of her mother’s residence in the Rue Pavée Saint Andrée.

===Chinese===

这件事发生在莫尔格街暴行之后约两年。玛丽——她的教名与姓氏，同那位不幸的「雪茄姑娘」的名字相似，会立刻引起注意——是寡妇埃斯特尔·罗热（Estelle Rogêt）的独生女。父亲在孩子幼年死去；从他死去的时候起，直到构成我们这篇叙述主题的那场凶杀之前的十八个月里，母女同住在帕韦圣安德烈街（Rue Pavée Saint Andrée）〔29〕；罗热太太在那里办一所包饭寄宿舍，玛丽作她的帮手。事情就这样进行，直到玛丽满了二十二岁：她那绝色的美，惊动了一位香水商；那人在皇宫广场（Palais Royal）底层的铺面里占着一间店，主顾多是在那一带出没的亡命的冒险家。勒布朗（Le Blanc）先生〔30〕并非不知道美丽的玛丽在他的香水铺里当差的好处；他慷慨的建议立刻被姑娘急切地接受，虽然太太那面稍有迟疑。

店主的预料应验了；他那几间屋子，很快因这活泼的灰衣女工的魅力而声名狼藉。她在他那里当差约一年，她的仰慕者们便因她从铺子里突然失踪而陷入纷乱。勒布朗先生无从解释她的不见，罗热太太焦虑与恐怖得心神无主。公众的报纸立刻抓住这个题目；警察正要着手认真的查究，一周之后，一个晴朗的早晨，玛丽气色很好、只带几分黯然的神情，重新出现在香水铺里她的老柜台上。一切查问，除了私人的性质，当然立刻平息。勒布朗先生照旧声称一无所知。玛丽同太太对一切问题都答道：那一星期是在乡下一位亲戚家里度过的。于是事情渐渐淡去，被普遍遗忘；因为这姑娘，表面为了摆脱好奇的冒犯，不久便向香水商作了最后的告别，回到她母亲在帕韦圣安德烈街的宅子里避风。

===Original===

It was about five months after this return home, that her friends were alarmed by her sudden disappearance for the second time. Three days elapsed, and nothing was heard of her. On the fourth her corpse was found floating in the Seine,31 near the shore which is opposite the Quartier of the Rue Saint Andrée, and at a point not very far distant from the secluded neighborhood of the Barrière du Roule.32

The atrocity of this murder (for it was at once evident that murder had been committed), the youth and beauty of the victim, and, above all, her previous notoriety, conspired to produce intense excitement in the minds of the sensitive Parisians. I can call to mind no similar occurrence producing so general and so intense an effect. For several weeks, in the discussion of this one absorbing theme, even the momentous political topics of the day were forgotten. The Prefect made unusual exertions; and the powers of the whole Parisian police were, of course, tasked to the utmost extent.

===Chinese===

这次回家之后约五个月，她的亲友们又被她第二次突然失踪惊动了。三天过去，音信全无。第四天，她的尸体被发现在塞纳河（Seine）〔31〕里漂浮，靠近正对圣安德烈区的河岸，离鲁莱关卡（Barrière du Roule）〔32〕那僻静的左近不远。

这桩谋杀的残暴（因为立刻便显然：谋杀已经行了），被害人的年轻与美丽，而尤其她先前的名声，联合起来，在敏感的巴黎人心里激起极度的骚动。我想不起任何类似的事件，产生过这样普遍、这样强烈的效应。好几个星期，人们讨论着这一个盘踞心头的题目，连当日头等重要的政治题目也被忘掉。总监作了非常的努力；整个巴黎警力的绳索，自然绷到了最紧。

===Original===

Upon the first discovery of the corpse, it was not supposed that the murderer would be able to elude, for more than a very brief period, the inquisition which was immediately set on foot. It was not until the expiration of a week that it was deemed necessary to offer a reward; and even then this reward was limited to a thousand francs. In the meantime the investigation proceeded with vigor, if not always with judgment, and numerous individuals were examined to no purpose; while, owing to the continual absence of all clue to the mystery, the popular excitement greatly increased. At the end of the tenth day it was thought advisable to double the sum originally proposed; and, at length, the second week having elapsed without leading to any discoveries, and the prejudice which always exists in Paris against the Police having given vent to itself in several serious émeutes, the Prefect took it upon himself to offer the sum of twenty thousand francs “for the conviction of the assassin,” or, if more than one should prove to have been implicated, “for the conviction of any one of the assassins.” In the proclamation setting forth this reward, a full pardon was promised to any accomplice who should come forward in evidence against his fellow; and to the whole was appended, wherever it appeared, the private placard of a committee of citizens, offering ten thousand francs, in addition to the amount proposed by the Prefecture. The entire reward thus stood at no less than thirty thousand francs, which will be regarded as an extraordinary sum when we consider the humble condition of the girl, and the great frequency, in large cities, of such atrocities as the one described.

===Chinese===

尸体初被发现时，人们不认为凶手能在一段很短的时期以外，躲开立刻设置的查究。直到一星期期满，才觉得有必要悬赏；即便那时，赏格也限于一千法郎。与此同时，查究进展得有力——纵不常有判断力——许多人被讯问而无结果；由于谜底的一切线索继续缺席，民众的激动大增。到第十天结束，觉得宜于把原定的数目加倍；终于，第二个星期过去而毫无发现，巴黎对警察素来的成见借几场严重的骚乱找到了出口，总监便自作主张，悬出两万法郎的赏格，「奖给把凶手定罪的人」，或，倘若证实不止一人被牵连，「奖给把任何一个凶手定罪的人」。在宣布这项赏格的告示里，允诺对任何出面作证控告同伙的从犯一概赦免；并且在全部告示的末尾，凡得张贴处，都附上一份市民委员会的私人招贴，在总监厅的数目之外，再加一万法郎。全部赏格于是不下三万法郎；考虑到这姑娘身份的卑微，又考虑到大都市里这类暴行的屡见，这将被看作一笔惊人的巨款。

===Original===

No one doubted now that the mystery of this murder would be immediately brought to light. But although, in one or two instances, arrests were made which promised elucidation, yet nothing was elicited which could implicate the parties suspected; and they were discharged forthwith. Strange as it may appear, the third week from the discovery of the body had passed, and passed without any light being thrown upon the subject, before even a rumor of the events which had so agitated the public mind, reached the ears of Dupin and myself. Engaged in researches which absorbed our whole attention, it had been nearly a month since either of us had gone abroad, or received a visitor, or more than glanced at the leading political articles in one of the daily papers. The first intelligence of the murder was brought us by G﻿—﻿—, in person. He called upon us early in the afternoon of the thirteenth of July, 18﻿—, and remained with us until late in the night. He had been piqued by the failure of all his endeavors to ferret out the assassins. His reputation﻿—so he said with a peculiarly Parisian air﻿—was at stake. Even his honor was concerned. The eyes of the public were upon him; and there was really no sacrifice which he would not be willing to make for the development of the mystery. He concluded a somewhat droll speech with a compliment upon what he was pleased to term the *tact* of Dupin, and made him a direct, and certainly a liberal proposition, the precise nature of which I do not feel myself at liberty to disclose, but which has no bearing upon the proper subject of my narrative.

===Chinese===

此刻没有人怀疑这桩凶杀的谜会立刻水落石出。但是，虽然有一两处作了似乎能够说明真相的逮捕，却没有任何东西问出来足以牵连被疑的人；他们随即被开释。说来也许奇怪：发现尸体的第三个星期已经过去，过去而毫无一线光亮投在案子上，这时关于那些如此搅动公众心绪的事件，连一点传闻也不曾传到杜宾和我的耳朵里。我们埋头于吸住我们全部注意的研究，近一个月来，谁也不曾出门，不曾接待来客，至多翻一眼一份日报的政治社论。凶杀的第一则消息是G——亲自带来的。他在18——年七月十三日下午早些时候来我们这里，一直留到深夜。他为他的种种努力一无所获而着恼。他的名声——他用一种极巴黎的腔调说——正押在这案子上。连他的名誉也有干系。公众的眼睛盯着他；为把这谜底揭开，实在没有他不愿作的牺牲。他以对杜宾*机巧*的一番恭维，结束了一篇颇为滑稽的演说，并且向他直接提出一个当然慷慨的建议；这建议的准确性质，我觉得无权披露，但它同我这篇叙述的正当主题没有关系。

===Original===

The compliment my friend rebutted as best he could, but the proposition he accepted at once, although its advantages were altogether provisional. This point being settled, the Prefect broke forth at once into explanations of his own views, interspersing them with long comments upon the evidence; of which latter we were not yet in possession. He discoursed much, and beyond doubt, learnedly; while I hazarded an occasional suggestion as the night wore drowsily away. Dupin, sitting steadily in his accustomed armchair, was the embodiment of respectful attention. He wore spectacles, during the whole interview; and an occasional signal glance beneath their green glasses, sufficed to convince me that he slept not the less soundly, because silently, throughout the seven or eight leaden-footed hours which immediately preceded the departure of the Prefect.

In the morning, I procured, at the Prefecture, a full report of all the evidence elicited, and, at the various newspaper offices, a copy of every paper in which, from first to last, had been published any decisive information in regard to this sad affair. Freed from all that was positively disproved, this mass of information stood thus:

Marie Rogêt left the residence of her mother, in the Rue Pavée St. Andrée, about nine o’clock in the morning of Sunday June the twenty-second, 18﻿—. In going out, she gave notice to a Monsieur Jacques St. Eustache,33 and to him only, of her intent intention to spend the day with an aunt who resided in the Rue des Drômes. The Rue des Drômes is a short and narrow but populous thoroughfare, not far from the banks of the river, and at a distance of some two miles, in the most direct course possible, from the pension of Madame Rogêt. St. Eustache was the accepted suitor of Marie, and lodged, as well as took his meals, at the pension. He was to have gone for his betrothed at dusk, and to have escorted her home. In the afternoon, however, it came on to rain heavily; and, supposing that she would remain all night at her aunt’s (as she had done under similar circumstances before), he did not think it necessary to keep his promise. As night drew on, Madame Rogêt (who was an infirm old lady, seventy years of age) was heard to express a fear “that she should never see Marie again;” but this observation attracted little attention at the time.

===Chinese===

我的朋友把恭维尽力驳回去，但那建议他立刻接受，虽然它的好处全然是暂定的。这一点既定，总监立刻倾泻出他自己见解的解释，中间掺着对证据的长篇评论；这证据我们那时还没有拿到手。他讲了许多，毫无疑问，讲得博学；我在夜色渐渐昏沉里偶尔冒出一两条建议。杜宾端坐在他惯常的扶手椅里，是恭敬注意的化身。整个会面他戴着眼镜；绿玻璃底下偶尔投出的一道锐利的目光，足以使我相信：在总监离去之前那七八个铅锤步的钟点里，他睡得并不少些——只是不出声罢了。

早晨，我在总监公署弄到了全部问出证据的完整报告，又在各报馆弄到了每一份从始至终登过这桩伤心案子的任何决定性消息的报纸。除去确被推翻的一切，这一大堆情报便成了下面这样：

18——年六月二十二日，星期日，早晨九点钟，玛丽·罗热离开她母亲在帕韦圣安德烈街的住宅。出门时，她向雅克·圣厄斯塔什（Jacques St. Eustache）〔33〕先生——并且只向他一人——通知她打算到德罗姆街（Rue des Drômes）一位姨妈家里过一天。德罗姆街是一条短而窄、然而人烟稠密的大道，离河岸不远，从罗热太太的寄宿舍取最直的路走，约两英里。圣厄斯塔什是玛丽公认的追求者，寄宿兼搭伙都在寄宿舍里。他本该在黄昏去接他的未婚妻，护送她回家。然而下午雨下大了；他猜想她会留在姨妈家过夜（像先前类似的情形她做过的那样），便不觉得有必要守他的约。夜幕渐临，罗热太太（她是位衰弱的老太太，七十岁）被听见说出一句忧惧：「她再也见不着玛丽了。」但这话当时没有引起多少注意。

===Original===

On Monday, it was ascertained that the girl had not been to the Rue des Drômes; and when the day elapsed without tidings of her, a tardy search was instituted at several points in the city, and its environs. It was not, however until the fourth day from the period of disappearance that anything satisfactory was ascertained respecting her. On this day (Wednesday, the twenty-fifth of June) a Monsieur Beauvais,34 who, with a friend, had been making inquiries for Marie near the Barrière du Roule, on the shore of the Seine which is opposite the Rue Pavée St. Andrée, was informed that a corpse had just been towed ashore by some fishermen, who had found it floating in the river. Upon seeing the body, Beauvais, after some hesitation, identified it as that of the perfumery-girl. His friend recognized it more promptly.

The face was suffused with dark blood, some of which issued from the mouth. No foam was seen, as in the case of the merely drowned. There was no discoloration in the cellular tissue. About the throat were bruises and impressions of fingers. The arms were bent over on the chest and were rigid. The right hand was clenched; the left partially open. On the left wrist were two circular excoriations, apparently the effect of ropes, or of a rope in more than one volution. A part of the right wrist, also, was much chafed, as well as the back throughout its extent, but more especially at the shoulder-blades. In bringing the body to the shore the fishermen had attached to it a rope; but none of the excoriations had been effected by this. The flesh of the neck was much swollen. There were no cuts apparent, or bruises which appeared the effect of blows. A piece of lace was found tied so tightly around the neck as to be hidden from sight; it was completely buried in the flesh, and was fastened by a knot which lay just under the left ear. This alone would have sufficed to produce death. The medical testimony spoke confidently of the virtuous character of the deceased. She had been subjected, it said, to brutal violence. The corpse was in such condition when found, that there could have been no difficulty in its recognition by friends.

===Chinese===

星期一，查明那姑娘没有去过德罗姆街；这一天过去而没有她的消息，城里和城郊的几个地点才迟迟地展开搜寻。然而直到失踪后第四天，关于她才查明一点满意的东西。这一天（六月二十五日，星期三），一位博韦（Beauvais）〔34〕先生同一个朋友一起，在鲁莱关卡左近——正对帕韦圣安德烈街的塞纳河岸——探问玛丽的下落，被告知一具尸体刚被几个渔人拖上岸，他们发现它在河里漂浮。一见到那尸身，博韦先生踌躇了一下，认出它就是香水铺的姑娘。他的朋友认出得更敏捷。

脸被深色的血糊满，有些血从嘴里流出来。没有像单是溺死的那种口沫。蜂窝组织里没有变色。喉咙四周有瘀伤和指头的印痕。两臂弯在胸前，僵直。右手攥紧；左手半开。左腕上有两道圆形的擦伤，显然是绳子的效果，或一根绳绕了不止一匝。右腕的一部分也磨得很重，还有整个背部，尤其肩胛一带。渔人把尸体拖上岸时曾系过一根绳；但那些擦伤没有一处是这绳造成的。颈子的肉肿得很。没有显著的刀伤，也没有像打击效果的瘀伤。发现一圈花边紧紧系在颈上，以致藏在肉里看不见；它完全埋进肉中，由一个结扣住，那结正在左耳下方。单是这个便足以致死。医学证词确凿地讲到死者的贞洁品格。据说，她曾遭受残暴的强力。尸体被发现时的状况，使朋友们认出它毫无困难。

===Original===

The dress was much torn and otherwise disordered. In the outer garment, a slip, about a foot wide, had been torn upward from the bottom hem to the waist, but not torn off. It was wound three times around the waist, and secured by a sort of hitch in the back. The dress immediately beneath the frock was of fine muslin; and from this a slip eighteen inches wide had been torn entirely out﻿—torn very evenly and with great care. It was found around her neck, fitting loosely, and secured with a hard knot. Over this muslin slip and the slip of lace, the strings of a bonnet were attached; the bonnet being appended. The knot by which the strings of the bonnet were fastened, was not a lady’s, but a slip or sailor’s knot.

After the recognition of the corpse, it was not, as usual, taken to the Morgue (this formality being superfluous), but hastily interred not far from the spot at which it was brought ashore. Through the exertions of Beauvais, the matter was industriously hushed up, as far as possible; and several days had elapsed before any public emotion resulted. A weekly paper,35 however, at length took up the theme; the corpse was disinterred, and a reexamination instituted; but nothing was elicited beyond what has been already noted. The clothes, however, were now submitted to the mother and friends of the deceased, and fully identified as those worn by the girl upon leaving home.

Meantime, the excitement increased hourly. Several individuals were arrested and discharged. St. Eustache fell especially under suspicion; and he failed, at first, to give an intelligible account of his whereabouts during the Sunday on which Marie left home. Subsequently, however, he submitted to Monsieur G﻿—﻿—, affidavits, accounting satisfactorily for every hour of the day in question. As time passed and no discovery ensued, a thousand contradictory rumors were circulated, and journalists busied themselves in suggestions. Among these, the one which attracted the most notice, was the idea that Marie Rogêt still lived﻿—that the corpse found in the Seine was that of some other unfortunate. It will be proper that I submit to the reader some passages which embody the suggestion alluded to. These passages are *literal* translations from *L’Etoile*,36 a paper conducted, in general, with much ability.

===Chinese===

衣着撕得极烂，此外一片纷乱。外衣上，一条约一英尺宽的布幅，从下摆向上撕到腰际，但没有撕脱。它在腰上绕了三匝，在背后用一种结扣住。紧贴外裙的衣裳是细纱的；从这上面一条十八英寸宽的布幅被整个撕掉——撕得极齐整，且极其经心。它被发现在她的颈上，松松围着，用一个死结扣紧。在这条纱幅和花边幅之上，系着帽带；帽子挂在那儿。系帽带的那个结，不是女人打的，是一个滑结，或水手结。

尸体被认出之后，没有照常例抬去陈尸所（这道手续是多余的），而在离它上岸处不远的地方匆匆下葬。靠博韦先生的尽力，这事被尽心竭力地压下；几天过去，才激起公众的动情。然而一份周刊〔35〕终于抓住这个题目；尸体被起出来，重新查验；但除已记下的以外，一无所获。可是衣物这回交给了死者的母亲和亲友，被完完全全认作那姑娘离家时穿的衣服。

与此同时，骚动一小时一小时地涨。几个人被逮捕又被开释。圣厄斯塔什尤其落到嫌疑底下；起初，他交代不清玛丽离家的那个星期日里他在何处。然而随后他向G——先生呈递了宣誓书，对那一天每个钟头的行踪都作了满意的交代。时间过去而没有发现，千百种互相矛盾的谣言流布起来，新闻记者们忙于出主意。其中最引人注意的，是玛丽·罗热还活着——塞纳河里发现的尸体是别的什么不幸者的那个想法。我宜于向读者提交几段文字，把这里暗示的意思收录在内。这些段落是从《星报》（L'Etoile）〔36〕逐字译出的；那份报纸总的来说办得很有本事。

===Original===

“Mademoiselle Rogêt left her mother’s house on Sunday morning, June the twenty-second, 18﻿—, with the ostensible purpose of going to see her aunt, or some other connection, in the Rue des Drômes. From that hour, nobody is proved to have seen her. There is no trace or tidings of her at all.

---

There has no person, whatever, come forward, so far, who saw her at all, on that day, after she left her mother’s door.

---

Now, though we have no evidence that Marie Rogêt was in the land of the living after nine o’clock on Sunday, June the twenty-second, we have proof that, up to that hour, she was alive. On Wednesday noon, at twelve, a female body was discovered afloat on the shore of the Barrière de Roule. This was, even if we presume that Marie Rogêt was thrown into the river within three hours after she left her mother’s house, only three days from the time she left her home﻿—three days to an hour. But it is folly to suppose that the murder, if murder was committed on her body, could have been consummated soon enough to have enabled her murderers to throw the body into the river before midnight. Those who are guilty of such horrid crimes choose darkness rather the light.

---

Thus we see that if the body found in the river was that of Marie Rogêt, it could only have been in the water two and a half days, or three at the outside. All experience has shown that drowned bodies, or bodies thrown into the water immediately after death by violence, require from six to ten days for decomposition to take place to bring them to the top of the water. Even where a cannon is fired over a corpse, and it rises before at least five or six days’ immersion, it sinks again, if let alone. Now, we ask, what was there in this case to cause a departure from the ordinary course of nature?

---

If the body had been kept in its mangled state on shore until Tuesday night, some trace would be found on shore of the murderers. It is a doubtful point, also, whether the body would be so soon afloat, even were it thrown in after having been dead two days. And, furthermore, it is exceedingly improbable that any villains who had committed such a murder as is here supposed, would have thrown the body in without weight to sink it, when such a precaution could have so easily been taken.”

===Chinese===

「罗热小姐于18——年六月二十二日星期日早晨离开她母亲的住宅，表面上是去德罗姆街看她姨妈或别的亲眷。从那一刻起，没有人被证明见过她。关于她没有丝毫踪迹或音信。

---

无论什么人，到目前为止，没有站出来说他在那一天、在她走出母亲家门之后见过她。

---

现在，虽然我们没有证据证明玛丽·罗热在六月二十二日星期日九点钟之后还活在人间，我们却有证据证明，到那一刻为止，她还活着。星期三中午十二点，一具女尸在鲁莱关卡岸边的漂浮中被发现。这，即便我们假定玛丽·罗热在离开母亲家门后三个钟头之内就被抛进河里，离她离家也才有三天——三天零一个钟头。可是设想这场凶杀——倘若凶杀果真落在她身上——能够足够快地办完、使她的凶手们在午夜以前把尸体抛进河里，是愚蠢的。犯这类可怕罪案的人，宁可要黑暗，不要光亮。

---

这样我们看到，倘若河里发现的尸体是玛丽·罗热的，它只可能在水里两天半，至多三天。一切经验表明：溺死的尸体，或死后被暴行立刻抛进水里的尸体，需要六到十天，腐烂才能使它们浮上水面。即便在尸体上空放过一炮，它如果在浸泡至少五六天之前浮起来，一放手便又沉下去。现在我们要问：这个案子里，有什么使自然的常轨出了偏差？

---

倘若尸体在被残害的状态里留在岸上直到星期二夜里，岸上会找到凶手们的某些踪迹。还有一点也难说：即使尸体是死后两天才抛进水里，它是否会这样快漂浮起来。此外，极难相信：犯下这里所设想的这样一场凶杀的恶棍，竟会把尸体抛下水而不系重物，既然这样的预防取起来如此容易。」

===Original===

The editor here proceeds to argue that the body must have been in the water “not three days merely, but, at least, five times three days,” because it was so far decomposed that Beauvais had great difficulty in recognizing it. This latter point, however, was fully disproved. I continue the translation:

“What, then, are the facts on which M. Beauvais says that he has no doubt the body was that of Marie Rogêt? He ripped up the gown sleeve, and says he found marks which satisfied him of the identity. The public generally supposed those marks to have consisted of some description of scars. He rubbed the arm and found *hair* upon it﻿—something as indefinite, we think, as can readily be imagined﻿—as little conclusive as finding an arm in the sleeve. M. Beauvais did not return that night, but sent word to Madame Rogêt, at seven o’clock, on Wednesday evening, that an investigation was still in progress respecting her daughter. If we allow that Madame Rogêt, from her age and grief, could not go over (which is allowing a great deal), there certainly must have been someone who would have thought it worth while to go over and attend the investigation, if they thought the body was that of Marie. Nobody went over. There was nothing said or heard about the matter in the Rue Pavée St. Andrée, that reached even the occupants of the same building. M. St. Eustache, the lover and intended husband of Marie, who boarded in her mother’s house, deposes that he did not hear of the discovery of the body of his intended until the next morning, when M. Beauvais came into his chamber and told him of it. For an item of news like this, it strikes us it was very coolly received.”

===Chinese===

报纸的编辑在这里接着论证：尸体必曾在水里「不止三天，至少五乘三——十五天」，因为它腐烂得那样厉害，博韦认出它来大费周章。但这后一点已被完全推翻。我继续翻译：

「那么，博韦先生凭哪些事实说他毫不怀疑那尸体是玛丽·罗热的？他撕开外裙的袖子，说他找到使他认为同一是玛丽的东西。公众一般以为那些东西是某种疤痕。他摩挲那条胳膊，在上面找到*毛发*——一种我们想不出比这更含糊、更不定形的东西——同在袖子里找到一条胳膊一样算不得结论。博韦先生那晚没有回去，却在星期三晚上七点给罗热太太捎话说，关于她女儿的查究还在进行。倘若我们承认罗热太太因年老与悲伤不能过去（这是承认了很多），那么必定有某个人，倘若他们认为那尸体是玛丽的，会想到值得过去照管那场查究。没有人过去。帕韦圣安德烈街里，关于这件事，没有任何说过的话或听到的动静传进同楼的住户耳朵里。圣厄斯塔什先生，玛丽的情人、拟议中的丈夫，寄宿在她母亲的家里，具结说：直到第二天早晨博韦先生走进他的卧室告诉他之前，他不曾听说他的未婚妻的尸体被发现的消息。对这样一条新闻，在我们看，受理得未免太冷。」

===Original===

In this way the journal endeavored to create the impression of an apathy on the part of the relatives of Marie, inconsistent with the supposition that these relatives believed the corpse to be hers. Its insinuations amount to this: that Marie, with the connivance of her friends, had absented herself from the city for reasons involving a charge against her chastity; and that these friends, upon the discovery of a corpse in the Seine, somewhat resembling that of the girl, had availed themselves of the opportunity to impress the public with the belief of her death. But *L’Etoile* was again overhasty. It was distinctly proved that no apathy, such as was imagined, existed; that the old lady was exceedingly feeble, and so agitated as to be unable to attend to any duty; that St. Eustache, so far from receiving the news coolly, was distracted with grief, and bore himself so frantically, that M. Beauvais prevailed upon a friend and relative to take charge of him, and prevent his attending the examination at the disinterment. Moreover, although it was stated by *L’Etoile*, that the corpse was re-interred at the public expense﻿—that an advantageous offer of private sculpture was absolutely declined by the family﻿—and that no member of the family attended the ceremonial;﻿—although, I say, all this was asserted by *L’Etoile* in furtherance of the impression it designed to convey﻿—yet *all* this was satisfactorily disproved. In a subsequent number of the paper, an attempt was made to throw suspicion upon Beauvais himself. The editor says:

“Now, then, a change comes over the matter. We are told that on one occasion, while a Madame B﻿—﻿— was at Madame Rogêt’s house, M. Beauvais, who was going out, told her that a gendarme was expected there, and she, Madame B., must not say anything to the gendarme until he returned, but let the matter be for him.

---

In the present posture of affairs, M. Beauvais appears to have the whole matter locked up in his head. A single step cannot be taken without M. Beauvais, for, go which way you will, you run against him.

---

For some reason, he determined that nobody shall have anything to do with the proceedings but himself, and he has elbowed the male relatives out of the way, according to their representations, in a very singular manner. He seems to have been very much averse to permitting the relatives to see the body.”

===Chinese===

这样，那份报纸竭力造成一种印象：玛丽的亲属们冷漠，同他们相信那尸体是她的这个假定不相容。它的影射归结起来便是：玛丽在亲友的默许下，为着牵涉她贞操的缘由，离开了城里；这些亲友在塞纳河里发现一具同那姑娘有些相似的尸体时，便利用这机会，把她的死印进公众的信念。但《星报》又急躁了。分明证明：所谓的那种冷漠并不存在；老太太衰弱到极点，心绪乱得任何事务也无从料理；圣厄斯塔什非但不曾冷冷受理那消息，反而悲痛得神志昏乱，举止狂乱到这样地步，以致博韦先生劝服一位朋友和亲戚看住他，不许他到场参加起尸复验。再者，虽然《星报》说尸体是以公费重新下葬的——虽然据说家里谢绝了私人雕像的一笔有利提议，家里没有一个成员到场参加葬仪——虽然，我说，这一切都是《星报》为扶植它要传达的印象而断言的——然而*这一切*都得到满意的推翻。在该报随后一期里，有人试图把嫌疑引到博韦本人头上。编辑说：

「于是，事情换了面目。有人告诉我们：某次，一位B太太在罗热太太家里，博韦先生正要出门，告诉她有一个警士要来，她，B太太，在他回来之前什么也不要对警士说，事情留给他办。

---

在事态目前的情况下，博韦先生似乎把整件事锁在他一个人的头脑里。没有博韦先生便一步也动不得，因为无论朝哪边走，都会撞上他。

---

由于某种缘由，他断定除了自己谁也不许过问这案子的进行，而照他们的说法，他把男性亲属用臂肘挤到一边去，样子非常古怪。他似乎极不愿意让亲属们看见尸体。」

===Original===

By the following fact, some color was given to the suspicion thus thrown upon Beauvais. A visitor at his office, a few days prior to the girl’s disappearance, and during the absence of its occupant, had observed *a rose* in the keyhole of the door, and the name “*Marie*” inscribed upon a slate which hung near at hand.

The general impression, so far as we were enabled to glean it from the newspapers, seemed to be, that Marie had been the victim of *a gang* of desperadoes﻿—that by these she had been borne across the river, maltreated and murdered. *Le Commerciel*,37 however, a print of extensive influence, was earnest in combating this popular idea. I quote a passage or two from its columns:

“We are persuaded that pursuit has hitherto been on a false scent, so far as it has been directed to the Barrière du Roule. It is impossible that a person so well known to thousands as this young woman was, should have passed three blocks without someone having seen her; and anyone who saw her would have remembered it, for she interested all who knew her. It was when the streets were full of people, when she went out.

---

It is impossible that she could have gone to the Barrière du Roule, or to the Rue des Drômes, without being recognized by a dozen persons; yet no one has come forward who saw her outside of her mother’s door, and there is no evidence, except the testimony concerning her *expressed intentions*, that she did go out at all. Her gown was torn, bound round her, and tied; and by that the body was carried as a bundle. If the murder had been committed at the Barrière du Roule, there would have been no necessity for any such arrangement. The fact that the body was found floating near the Barrière, is no proof as to where it was thrown into the water.

---

A piece of one of the unfortunate girl’s petticoats, two feet long and one foot wide, was torn out and tied under her chin around the back of her head, probably to prevent screams. This was done by fellows who had no pocket-handkerchief.”

===Chinese===

下面的一个事实，给这样掷到博韦身上的嫌疑添了几分颜色。姑娘失踪前几天，趁屋主不在，一个到他事务所去的访客看见*一朵玫瑰*插在门锁孔里，近旁挂着的一块石板上写着「*玛丽*」的名字。

就我们从报纸所能搜拾的，一般的印象似乎是：玛丽是一帮亡命徒的牺牲品——他们把她抬过河去，凌辱了她，谋杀了她。然而《商业报》（Le Commerciel）〔37〕，一份影响很广的报纸，却恳切地驳斥这种流行的想法。我从它的栏目里引一两段：

「我们确信：追索迄今一直循着一条错误的气味，就它指向鲁莱关卡而言。像这位年轻姑娘这样为千百人所熟识的人，走过三个街区而不被什么人看见，是不可能的；而看见她的任何人都会记得，因为她叫一切认识她的人动心。她出门时，正是街上人烟鼎盛的时候。

---

她不可能走到鲁莱关卡或德罗姆街而不被十几个人认出来；然而没有一个人站出来说在她母亲门外之外的地方见过她；除了关于她*所表明的意向*的证词，没有任何证据证明她到底出了门没有。她的外裙撕破了，绕在她身上，系起来；尸体便当作一件包裹那样被抬走。倘若凶杀是在鲁莱关卡行的，这样的安排便没有必要。尸体在关卡附近漂浮中被发现，证明不了它是从哪里抛进水里的。

---

那不幸的姑娘裙幅中的一条，两英尺长、一英尺宽，被撕下来，系在她下巴底下，绕到脑后，多半为着防她喊叫。干这事的家伙连口袋手帕也没有。」

===Original===

A day or two before the Prefect called upon us, however, some important information reached the police, which seemed to overthrow, at least, the chief portion of *Le Commerciel*’s argument. Two small boys, sons of a Madame Deluc, while roaming among the woods near the Barrière du Roule, chanced to penetrate a close thicket, within which were three or four large stones, forming a kind of seat, with a back and footstool. On the upper stone lay a white petticoat; on the second, a silk scarf. A parasol, gloves, and a pocket-handkerchief were also here found. The handkerchief bore the name “Marie Rogêt.” Fragments of dress were discovered on the brambles around. The earth was trampled, the bushes were broken, and there was every evidence of a struggle. Between the thicket and the river, the fences were found taken down, and the ground bore evidence of some heavy burden having been dragged along it.

A weekly paper, *Le Soleil*,38 had the following comments upon this discovery﻿—comments which merely echoed the sentiment of the whole Parisian press:

“The things had all evidently been there at least three or four weeks; they were all mildewed down hard with the action of the rain and stuck together from mildew. The grass had grown around and over some of them. The silk on the parasol was strong, but the threads of it were run together within. The upper part, where it had been doubled and folded, was all mildewed and rotten, and tore on its being opened.

---

The pieces of her frock torn out by the bushes were about three inches wide and six inches long. One part was the hem of the frock, and it had been mended; the other piece was part of the skirt, not the hem. They looked like strips torn off, and were on the thorn bush, about a foot from the ground.

---

There can be no doubt, therefore, that the spot of this appalling outrage has been discovered.”

===Chinese===

然而在总监来访我们前一两天，一项重要的消息到了警察手里，它似乎至少推翻了《商业报》论证的主要部分。德吕克太太的两个小儿子，在鲁莱关卡附近的树林里游荡时，偶然钻进一座密林丛，丛中有三四块大石头，构成一种带靠背和脚凳的座椅。上面那块石头上放着一条白裙；第二块上放着一条绸围巾。还找到一把阳伞、手套和一块口袋手帕。手帕上写着「玛丽·罗热」的名字。四围的荆棘上发现衣裳的碎片。地面被踏乱，树丛折断，处处是挣扎的证据。从密丛到河之间，栅栏的栏杆被拆了下来，地面带着某种重负曾被拖过的痕迹。

一份周刊，《太阳报》（Le Soleil）〔38〕，对这一发现作了下面的评论——评论不过把整个巴黎报界的意见应声重复一遍：

「这些东西显然全在那里至少三四个星期了；它们全被雨水浸得霉硬，因霉而粘作一团。草长起来，围着几件，盖住几件。阳伞的绸还结实，但伞里的线已经跑散。上半，折叠过的地方，全霉了，烂了，一打开就破。

---

她的外裙被树丛撕下的碎片，约三英寸宽、六英寸长。一块是外裙的裙边，补缀过；另一块是裙幅的一部分，不是裙边。它们看着像撕下来的布条，挂在荆棘丛上，离地约一英尺。

---

因此毫无可疑：这场骇人暴行的地点已经发现了。」

===Original===

Consequent upon this discovery, new evidence appeared. Madame Deluc testified that she keeps a roadside inn not far from the bank of the river, opposite the Barrière du Roule. The neighborhood is secluded﻿—particularly so. It is the usual Sunday resort of blackguards from the city, who cross the river in boats. About three o’clock, in the afternoon of the Sunday in question, a young girl arrived at the inn, accompanied by a young man of dark complexion. The two remained here for some time. On their departure, they took the road to some thick woods in the vicinity. Madame Deluc’s attention was called to the dress worn by the girl, on account of its resemblance to one worn by a deceased relative. A scarf was particularly noticed. Soon after the departure of the couple, a gang of miscreants made their appearance, behaved boisterously, ate and drank without making payment, followed in the route of the young man and girl, returned to the inn about dusk, and re-crossed the river as if in great haste.

It was soon after dark, upon this same evening, that Madame Deluc, as well as her eldest son, heard the screams of a female in the vicinity of the inn. The screams were violent but brief. Madame D. recognized not only the scarf which was found in the thicket, but the dress which was discovered upon the corpse. An omnibus driver, Valence,39 now also testified that he saw Marie Rogêt cross a ferry on the Seine, on the Sunday in question, in company with a young man of dark complexion. He, Valence, knew Marie, and could not be mistaken in her identity. The articles found in the thicket were fully identified by the relatives of Marie.

The items of evidence and information thus collected by myself, from the newspapers, at the suggestion of Dupin, embraced only one more point﻿—but this was a point of seemingly vast consequence. It appears that, immediately after the discovery of the clothes as above described, the lifeless, or nearly lifeless body of St. Eustache, Marie’s betrothed, was found in the vicinity of what all now supposed the scene of the outrage. A phial labelled “laudanum,” and emptied, was found near him. His breath gave evidence of the poison. He died without speaking. Upon his person was found a letter, briefly stating his love for Marie, with his design of self-destruction.

===Chinese===

这一发现之后，新的证据出现了。德吕克太太具结说：她在离河岸不远、正对鲁莱关卡的地方开一家路边客栈。那一带僻静——特别僻静。它是城里下流人星期日的寻常游地，他们坐船过河。在所说的那个星期日下午三点钟，一个年轻姑娘来到客栈，由一个深色脸膛的年轻人陪着。两人在这里待了一些时候。他们离开时，取道走向附近几座密林。德吕克太太的注意被那姑娘的衣裳引去了，因为它像她一位亡故亲戚穿过的一件。一条围巾被特别注意到。这一对刚走，一伙恶棍出现，吵吵嚷嚷，吃了喝了不付钱，循着那一男一女去的路跟了去，黄昏光景回到客栈，急忙忙地又过了河。

就在这同一晚，天黑之后不久，德吕克太太同她的大儿子听见客栈附近一个女人的尖叫。叫声剧烈而短促。德吕克太太不但认出密丛里发现的那条围巾，也认出尸体上发现的那件衣裳。公共马车夫瓦朗斯（Valence）〔39〕此刻也具结说，他看见玛丽·罗热在所说的那个星期日同深色脸膛的年轻人一起，坐渡船过了塞纳河。他，瓦朗斯，认识玛丽，认错她是不可能的。密丛里找到的那些物件，被玛丽的亲属完全认作她的。

这些证据和消息的条目，是我照杜宾的指点从报纸里搜辑的，此外只剩一点——但这一点看上去关涉极大。事情是：在如上所述的衣物被发现之后紧接着，圣厄斯塔什——玛丽的未婚夫——那没有生命的、或近乎没有生命的躯体，被发现在如今人人以为的暴行现场左近。一只标着「鸦片酊」的药瓶，空了，在他身旁找到。他的呼吸带着毒物的证据。他死了，一个字没说。他身上找到一封信，简短地说他对玛丽的爱，和他自尽的打算。

===Original===

“I need scarcely tell you,” said Dupin, as he finished the perusal of my notes, “that this is a far more intricate case than that of the Rue Morgue; from which it differs in one important respect. This is an *ordinary*, although an atrocious instance of crime. There is nothing peculiarly outré about it. You will observe that, for this reason, the mystery has been considered easy, when, for this reason, it should have been considered difficult, of solution. Thus; at first, it was thought unnecessary to offer a reward. The myrmidons of G﻿—﻿— were able at once to comprehend how and why such an atrocity *might have been* committed. They could picture to their imaginations a mode﻿—many modes﻿—and a motive﻿—many motives; and because it was not impossible that either of these numerous modes and motives *could* have been the actual one, they have taken it for granted that one of them *must*. But the case with which these variable fancies were entertained, and the very plausibility which each assumed, should have been understood as indicative rather of the difficulties than of the facilities which must attend elucidation. I have before observed that it is by prominences above the plane of the ordinary, that reason feels her way, if at all, in her search for the true, and that the proper question in cases such as this, is not so much ‘what has occurred?’ as ‘what has occurred that has never occurred before?’ In the investigations at the house of Madame L’Espanaye,40 the agents of G﻿—﻿— were discouraged and confounded by that very *unusualness* which, to a properly regulated intellect, would have afforded the surest omen of success; while this same intellect might have been plunged in despair at the ordinary character of all that met the eye in the case of the perfumery-girl, and yet told of nothing but easy triumph to the functionaries of the Prefecture.

===Chinese===

「不必我告诉你，」杜宾读罢我的札记说，「这案子比莫尔格街那桩错综得多；它与它在一个重要之点上不同。这是一桩*寻常的*，虽然凶残的罪案实例。关于它，没有一点特殊古怪之处。你会注意到：正因如此，这个谜被认为易解，而恰恰因此它本该被认为难解。于是：起初认为悬赏是不必要的。G——的那些爪牙立刻便能领会这样一场暴行*本来怎样、为何*能够行得。他们能在想象里描出一种方式——许多种方式——和一个动机——许多动机；因为这许多方式与动机里任何一种*可能*正是实际的那一种，他们便径直认定其中之一*必定*是。但这些游移的幻想被采纳得那样轻易，而每一种又摆出那样的像样，本该被理解为预兆着阐明此案所必经的困难，而非便利。我从前指出过：理性探求真，倘若它能，靠的是高出寻常平面的凸处；在这样的案子里，恰当的问题不那么是「发生了什么」，而更是「发生了什么从未发生过的」。在勒斯帕奈太太〔40〕宅中的查究里，G——的探员们正被那*非同寻常*本身泄了气，搅昏了头；而在一个调理得当的智力看来，那非同寻常本会提供成功最确凿的先兆；同一个智力，在香水铺姑娘一案里，面对入目的一切所带的寻常品格，本可能陷入绝望，而这对总监厅的官员们只诉说着轻易的凯旋。

===Original===

“In the case of Madame L’Espanaye and her daughter there was, even at the beginning of our investigation, no doubt that murder had been committed. The idea of suicide was excluded at once. Here, too, we are freed, at the commencement, from all supposition of self-murder. The body found at the Barrière du Roule, was found under such circumstances as to leave us no room for embarrassment upon this important point. But it has been suggested that the corpse discovered is not that of the Marie Rogêt for the conviction of whose assassin, or assassins, the reward is offered, and respecting whom, solely, our agreement has been arranged with the Prefect. We both know this gentleman well. It will not do to trust him too far. If, dating our inquiries from the body found, and thence tracing a murderer, we yet discover this body to be that of some other individual than Marie; or, if starting from the living Marie, we find her, yet find her unassassinated﻿—in either case we lose our labor; since it is Monsieur G﻿—﻿— with whom we have to deal. For our own purpose, therefore, if not for the purpose of justice, it is indispensable that our first step should be the determination of the identity of the corpse with the Marie Rogêt who is missing.

“With the public the arguments of *L’Etoile* have had weight; and that the journal itself is convinced of their importance would appear from the manner in which it commences one of its essays upon the subject﻿—‘Several of the morning papers of the day,’ it says, ‘speak of the *conclusive* article in Monday’s *Etoile*.’ To me, this article appears conclusive of little beyond the zeal of its inditer. We should bear in mind that, in general, it is the object of our newspapers rather to create a sensation﻿—to make a point﻿—than to further the cause of truth. The latter end is only pursued when it seems coincident with the former. The print which merely falls in with ordinary opinion (however well founded this opinion may be) earns for itself no credit with the mob. The mass of the people regard as profound only him who suggests *pungent contradictions* of the general idea. In ratiocination, not less than in literature, it is the *epigram* which is the most immediately and the most universally appreciated. In both, it is of the lowest order of merit.

===Chinese===

「在勒斯帕奈太太和她女儿的案子里，甚至在我们查究的开端，凶杀已经行下，这是没有疑问的。自杀的念头立刻被排除。在这里，我们同样在开端便从一切自戕的设想里解放出来。在鲁莱关卡发现的尸体，其被发现时的情形，使我们在这一要点上没有困窘的余地。但有人提示：被发现的尸体不是那个玛丽·罗热的——为了把她的凶手或凶手们定罪，赏格悬着；我们同总监立的约，也单为着她而设。这位先生我们俩都熟。把他信得太远是不行的。倘若我们把查究的起点放在尸体上，循此追出一个凶手，结果却发现这尸体是玛丽以外的什么人；或者，倘若我们从活着的玛丽出发，找到了她，却发现她未被谋杀——两种情形里任何一种，我们都白费力气；因为我们要打交道的，是G——先生。因此，即便不为正义的目的，单为我们自己的目的，我们第一步必须断定这尸体同失踪的玛丽·罗热是同一个人。

「《星报》的论证在公众那里有了分量；而该报自己也信它们的重要，这从它就此题所写的一篇文章的开头方式便可见——『今天早晨的几家报纸，』它说，「都谈到星期一《星报》上那篇*结论性的*文章。」在我看来，这篇文章除了写它的那位的热心，什么也没有证明。我们应当记住：我们的报纸，一般地说，目的在于制造轰动——立一个论点——而不在推进真理的事业。后一目的只在似乎与前一目的重合时才被追求。一份报纸单是随声附和寻常的意见（无论这意见根据多牢），在群氓中间便挣不到信用。民众只把提出对公意*尖刻的悖反*的人当作深刻。在推理里，不下于在文学里，最立即、最普遍地被赏识的，是那*警句*。在两者里，它都属于最低等的功绩。

===Original===

“What I mean to say is, that it is the mingled epigram and melodrame of the idea, that Marie Rogêt still lives, rather than any true plausibility in this idea, which have suggested it to *L’Etoile*, and secured it a favorable reception with the public. Let us examine the heads of this journal’s argument; endeavoring to avoid the incoherence with which it is originally set forth.

“The first aim of the writer is to show, from the brevity of the interval between Marie’s disappearance and the finding of the floating corpse, that this corpse cannot be that of Marie. The reduction of this interval to its smallest possible dimension, becomes thus, at once, an object with the reasoner. In the rash pursuit of this object, he rushes into mere assumption at the outset. ‘It is folly to suppose,’ he says, ‘that the murder, if murder was committed on her body, could have been consummated soon enough to have enabled her murderers to throw the body into the river before midnight.’ We demand at once, and very naturally, *why*? Why is it folly to suppose that the murder was committed *within five minutes* after the girl’s quitting her mother’s house? Why is it folly to suppose that the murder was committed at any given period of the day? There have been assassinations at all hours. But, had the murder taken place at any moment between nine o’clock in the morning of Sunday, and a quarter before midnight, there would still have been time enough ‘to throw the body into the river before midnight.’ This assumption, then, amounts precisely to this﻿—that the murder was not committed on Sunday at all﻿—and, if we allow *L’Etoile* to assume this, we may permit it any liberties whatever. The paragraph beginning ‘It is folly to suppose that the murder, etc.,’ however it appears as printed in *L’Etoile*, may be imagined to have existed actually *thus* in the brain of its inditer﻿—‘It is folly to suppose that the murder, if murder was committed on the body, could have been committed soon enough to have enabled her murderers to throw the body into the river before midnight; it is folly, we say, to suppose all this, and to suppose at the same time, (as we are resolved to suppose), that the body was *not* thrown in until *after* midnight’﻿—a sentence sufficiently inconsequential in itself, but not so utterly preposterous as the one printed.

===Chinese===

「我要说的是：使《星报》想出玛丽·罗热还活着这个念头的，与其说这念头本身有任何真的可信，不如说它那警句与情节剧的杂拌。让我们检查这份报纸论证的要点，竭力避开它原本陈述时的杂乱无章。

「这位作者的头一个目的，是借玛丽失踪与浮尸被发现之间间隔的短促，证明这尸体不可能是玛丽的。把这间隔缩到它最小可能的尺寸，于是立刻成了这推理者的一个目标。在鲁莽地追逐这目标时，他一开头便闯进纯粹的臆断。『设想，』他说，「这场凶杀——倘若凶杀果真落在她身上——能够足够快地办完、使她的凶手们在午夜以前把尸体抛进河里，是愚蠢的。」我们立刻——并且极自然地——要求回答*为什么*？设想凶杀在那姑娘走出她母亲家门之后*五分钟之内*便已行下，为什么是愚蠢？设想凶杀在一天里的任何给定时辰行下，为什么是愚蠢？凶杀在任何时辰都有过。但是，倘若凶杀发生在星期日早晨九点与午夜前一刻之间的任何一刻，仍然有足够的时间「在午夜以前把尸体抛进河里」。于是这个臆断恰恰归结为：凶杀在星期日根本没有行下；而倘若我们容许《星报》作这个臆断，我们便可以容许它作任何放肆。开头作「设想这场凶杀，等等」的那一段，无论它印在《星报》上是什么样子，可以设想它在那执笔者的头脑里实际上*这样*存在过——「设想这场凶杀，倘若凶杀果真落在她身上，能够足够快地行下、使她的凶手们在午夜以前把尸体抛进河里，是愚蠢的；设想这一切，是愚蠢的，我们说，同时（因为我们横下心要这样设想）还要设想那尸体*不是*在午夜*之后*才抛进水里的」——这句话本身够不上连贯，但还不至于像印出来的那一句那样全然荒谬。

===Original===

“Were it my purpose,” continued Dupin, “merely to *make out a case* against this passage of *L’Etoile*’s argument, I might safely leave it where it is. It is not, however, with *L’Etoile* that we have to do, but with the truth. The sentence in question has but one meaning, as it stands; and this meaning I have fairly stated; but it is material that we go behind the mere words, for an idea which these words have obviously intended, and failed to convey. It was the design of the journalist to say that, at whatever period of the day or night of Sunday this murder was committed, it was improbable that the assassins would have ventured to bear the corpse to the river before midnight. And herein lies, really, the assumption of which I complain. It is assumed that the murder was committed at such a position, and under such circumstances, that *the bearing it* to the river became necessary. Now, the assassination might have taken place upon the river’s brink, or on the river itself; and, thus, the throwing the corpse in the water might have been resorted to, at any period of the day or night, as the most obvious and most immediate mode of disposal. You will understand that I suggest nothing here as probable, or as coincident with my own opinion. My design, so far, has no reference to the *facts* of the case. I wish merely to caution you against the whole tone of *L’Etoile*’s suggestion, by calling your attention to its ex parte character at the outset.

“Having prescribed thus a limit to suit its own preconceived notions; having assumed that, if this were the body of Marie, it could have been in the water but a very brief time, the journal goes on to say:

“ ‘All experience has shown that drowned bodies, or bodies thrown into the water immediately after death by violence, require from six to ten days for sufficient decomposition to take place to bring them to the top of the water. Even when a cannon is fired over a corpse, and it rises before at least five or six days’ immersion, it sinks again if let alone.’

===Chinese===

「倘若我的目的只是*立一个案子*反对《星报》论证的这一段，我可以安然把它搁在那里。然而我们要打交道的不是《星报》，而是真理。所说的那句话，照它现在的样子，只有一个意思；这意思我已如实地陈述；但重要的是，我们应当走到单纯的字句背后，去寻那字句显然立意表达而未能传达的观念。这位记者的意思是想说：无论这场凶杀在星期日的白天或黑夜的哪一刻行下，凶手们不大敢在午夜以前把尸体抬到河边去。而这里面，实在，藏着我所抱怨的那个臆断。它假定凶杀行在这样一个位置、这样的情形之下，以至于*把它抬到河边*成了必要。然而凶杀可能就发生在河岸上，或在河上；这样，把尸体抛进水里，便可以在白天黑夜的任何时刻被采取，作为最显然、最直接的处置方式。你要明白，我在这里什么也没有提示为或然，或与我自己的意见相合。到此为止，我的设计同案子的*事实*毫无关系。我只想提醒你提防《星报》整个提示的腔调，请你在开端便注意它的单方性质。

「既这样给它自己的先入之见划定了一个界限；既假定了倘若这是玛丽的尸体，它在水里便只可能待极短的时间，这份报纸接着说：

「『一切经验表明：溺死的尸体，或死后被暴行立刻抛进水里的尸体，需要六到十天，腐烂才能充分进行，把它们送到水面。即便在尸体上空放过一炮，它如果在浸泡至少五六天之前浮起，一放手便又沉下去。』」

===Original===

“These assertions have been tacitly received by every paper in Paris, with the exception of *Le Moniteur*.41 This latter print endeavors to combat that portion of the paragraph which has reference to ‘drowned bodies’ only, by citing some five or six instances in which the bodies of individuals known to be drowned were found floating after the lapse of less time than is insisted upon by *L’Etoile*. But there is something excessively unphilosophical in the attempt on the part of *Le Moniteur*, to rebut the general assertion of *L’Etoile*, by a citation of particular instances militating against that assertion. Had it been possible to adduce fifty instead of five examples of bodies found floating at the end of two or three days, these fifty examples could still have been properly regarded only as exceptions to *L’Etoile*’s rule, until such time as the rule itself should be confuted. Admitting the rule, (and this *Le Moniteur* does not deny, insisting merely upon its exceptions,) the argument of *L’Etoile* is suffered to remain in full force; for this argument does not pretend to involve more than a question of the *probability* of the body having risen to the surface in less than three days; and this probability will be in favor of *L’Etoile*’s position until the instances so childishly adduced shall be sufficient in number to establish an antagonistical rule.

===Chinese===

「这些断言被巴黎每一家报纸默认地接受，唯《箴言报》（Le Moniteur）〔41〕例外。这后一种报纸力图驳斥那一段里涉及「溺死的尸体」的部分，引用了五六件实例：被证明溺死的人的尸体，在比《星报》所坚持的更短的时间里浮了起来。但《箴言报》试图以引用同该断言相抵触的特殊实例，来反驳《星报》的一般断言，这尝试里有某种极不哲学的东西。倘若可能举出五十件而不是五件尸体在两三天末漂浮的例子，这五十件例子仍旧只宜被看作《星报》规则的例外，直到那规则本身被推翻为止。承认了那规则（这一点《箴言报》并不否认，只坚持它的例外），《星报》的论证便被容许保持全部的力量；因为这论证并不装作涉及比一个*概率*问题更多的东西——即尸体在三日之内浮上水面的概率；而这概率一直有利于《星报》的立场，直到那些幼稚地引出的实例，数目上足以确立一条对抗的规则为止。

===Original===

“You will see at once that all argument upon this head should be urged, if at all, against the rule itself; and for this end we must examine the *rationale* of the rule.
