「此刻我们必须忙别的查究。你不能不注意到对尸体的查验的极端疏漏。诚然，同一的问题轻易便断定了，或者本该断定；但还有别的要点该查明。尸体可曾在任何方面被*劫掠*？死者离家时可曾随身带着什么首饰？倘若带着，被发现时可还带着？这些都是重要的、证据全然未曾触及的问题；还有别的一些同等紧要的问题，也不曾得着注意。我们必须竭力借亲自的询问满足自己。圣厄斯塔什的案子必须重审。我对这个人没有嫌疑；但让我们按部就班地进行。我们将确凿无疑地查明关于他那个星期日行踪的*宣誓书*是否有效。这一类宣誓书容易做成故弄玄虚的事。然而这里倘若没有不对，我们便把圣厄斯塔什从我们的查究里打发走。他的自杀，倘若宣誓书里查出欺诈，是佐证着嫌疑的；没有这样的欺诈，它在任何方面都不是无从解释的事，或一件需要我们偏离寻常分析的路线的事。

===Original===

“In that which I now propose, we will discard the interior points of this tragedy, and concentrate our attention upon its outskirts. Not the least usual error, in investigations such as this, is the limiting of inquiry to the immediate, with total disregard of the collateral or circumstantial events. It is the malpractice of the courts to confine evidence and discussion to the bounds of apparent relevancy. Yet experience has shown, and a true philosophy will always show, that a vast, perhaps the larger portion of truth, arises from the seemingly irrelevant. It is through the spirit of this principle, if not precisely through its letter, that modern science has resolved to *calculate upon the unforeseen*. But perhaps you do not comprehend me. The history of human knowledge has so uninterruptedly shown that to collateral, or incidental, or accidental events we are indebted for the most numerous and most valuable discoveries, that it has at length become necessary, in any prospective view of improvement, to make not only large, but the largest allowances for inventions that shall arise by chance, and quite out of the range of ordinary expectation. It is no longer philosophical to base, upon what has been, a vision of what is to be. *Accident* is admitted as a portion of the substructure. We make chance a matter of absolute calculation. We subject the unlooked for and unimagined to the mathematical *formulae* of the schools.

“I repeat that it is no more than fact, that the *larger* portion of all truth has sprung from the collateral; and it is but in accordance with the spirit of the principle involved in this fact, that I would divert inquiry, in the present case, from the trodden and hitherto unfruitful ground of the event itself, to the contemporary circumstances which surround it. While you ascertain the validity of the affidavits, I will examine the newspapers more generally than you have as yet done. So far, we have only reconnoitred the field of investigation; but it will be strange indeed if a comprehensive survey, such as I propose, of the public prints, will not afford us some minute points which shall establish a *direction* for inquiry.”

===Chinese===

「在我此刻提出的方案里，我们将抛开这出悲剧内部的要点，把注意集中在它的外缘。在这类查究里，最寻常不过的错误之一，是把查问限于切近的事情，全然不顾旁属的或随带的诸事件。把证据与讨论锁在表面相关的界限之内，是法庭的失当。然而经验表明，一种真正的哲学将永远表明：真理的一大部分——也许更大的一部分——出于那些看似不相干的东西。现代科学正是借着这一原则的精神——纵不恰是它的字面——决意*把未预见者算进计划*。但也许你不领会我。人类知识的历程不间断地表明：旁属的、偶然的事件，亏欠了我们最繁多、最宝贵的发现，以致在任何展望改进的眼光里，不但要给那些出于偶然、出于寻常预期之外的发明留出大的地步，而且要留出最大的地步，这终于成了必要。以已然者为基，去构建将然者的景象，已不再是哲学的。*偶然*已被承认为基座的一部分。我们把机会当作绝对计算的对象。我们把料不到、想不到的东西交给学院的数学*公式*。

「我再说一遍：一切真理的*较大部分*出于旁属，这是事实而不仅仅是猜测；而我所以要把这案子的查究，从事件本身那被踏熟的、迄今无收的园地，引向环绕着它的同代诸情形，正是循着这事实所含的原则的精神。当你去查明宣誓书是否有效，我便把报纸查得比你迄今所做的更普遍些。到此为止，我们只侦察了查究的园地；但倘若像我提议的那样对公共印刷品作一番综合的鸟瞰，竟不能供给我们一些细小的要点，为查究确立一个*方向*，那才真真奇怪。」

===Original===

In pursuance of Dupin’s suggestion, I made scrupulous examination of the affair of the affidavits. The result was a firm conviction of their validity, and of the consequent innocence of St. Eustache. In the meantime my friend occupied himself, with what seemed to me a minuteness altogether objectless, in a scrutiny of the various newspaper files. At the end of a week he placed before me the following extracts:

“About three years and a half ago, a disturbance very similar to the present, was caused by the disappearance of this same Marie Rogêt, from the *parfumerie* of Monsieur Le Blanc, in the Palais Royal. At the end of a week, however, she reappeared at her customary *comptoir*, as well as ever, with the exception of a slight paleness not altogether usual. It was given out by Monsieur Le Blanc and her mother, that she had merely been on a visit to some friend in the country; and the affair was speedily hushed up. We presume that the present absence is a freak of the same nature, and that, at the expiration of a week, or perhaps of a month, we shall have her among us again.”

> —﻿*Evening Paper*﻿—Monday, June 23.43

“An evening journal of yesterday, refers to a former mysterious disappearance of Mademoiselle Rogêt. It is well known that, during the week of her absence from Le Blanc’s *parfumerie*, she was in the company of a young naval officer, much noted for his debaucheries. A quarrel, it is supposed, providentially led to her return home. We have the name of the Lothario in question, who is, at present, stationed in Paris, but, for obvious reasons, forbear to make it public.”

> —﻿*Le Mercurie*﻿—Tuesday Morning, June 24.44

===Chinese===

循着杜宾的提示，我对宣誓书的案子作了不苟的查验。结果是对它们效力的坚定信念，以及对圣厄斯塔什无辜的随之而来的信念。与此同时，我的朋友忙于翻检各报的档案，那种细致在我看来全然没有对象。一星期之末，他把下面的摘录摆在我面前：

「约三年半以前，一场同眼下极相似的骚动，曾因这同一个玛丽·罗热从皇宫广场勒布朗先生的*香水铺*失踪而起。然而一星期之末，她照旧在惯常的*柜台*重新出现，健康如常，只带着一点不寻常的微微苍白。勒布朗先生和她母亲放出话来：她不过去乡下看一位朋友；事情很快被压下。我们推测：眼下的失踪是同样性质的一桩怪想，一星期之后，或者一个月之后，我们又将见她回到我们中间。」

——《晚报》——六月二十三日，星期一〔43〕

「昨天一份晚报提到罗热小姐从前一次神秘的失踪。众所周知，她离开勒布朗香水铺的那一星期里，是同一位年轻海军军官在一起；那人淫佚出名。据想是一场口角，天意使然，引她回家。我们掌有那位浪荡子的名字；他此刻驻在巴黎，但为着显见的缘由，不宜公开。」

——《水星报》（Le Mercurie）——六月二十四日，星期二早晨〔44〕

===Original===

“An outrage of the most atrocious character was perpetrated near this city the day before yesterday. A gentleman, with his wife and daughter, engaged, about dusk, the services of six young men, who were idly rowing a boat to and fro near the banks of the Seine, to convey him across the river. Upon reaching the opposite shore, the three passengers stepped out, and had proceeded so far as to be beyond the view of the boat, when the daughter discovered that she had left in it her parasol. She returned for it, was seized by the gang, carried out into the stream, gagged, brutally treated, and finally taken to the shore at a point not far from that at which she had originally entered the boat with her parents. The villains have escaped for the time, but the police are upon their trail, and some of them will soon be taken.”

> —﻿*Morning Paper*﻿—June 25.45

“We have received one or two communications, the object of which is to fasten the crime of the late atrocity upon Mennais;46 but as this gentleman has been fully exonerated by a loyal inquiry, and as the arguments of our several correspondents appear to be more zealous than profound, we do not think it advisable to make them public.”

> —﻿*Morning Paper*﻿—June 28.47

“We have received several forcibly written communications, apparently from various sources, and which go far to render it a matter of certainty that the unfortunate Marie Rogêt has become a victim of one of the numerous bands of blackguards which infest the vicinity of the city upon Sunday. Our own opinion is decidedly in favor of this supposition. We shall endeavor to make room for some of these arguments hereafter.”

> —﻿*Evening Paper*﻿—Tuesday, June 31.48

“On Monday, one of the bargemen connected with the revenue service, saw a empty boat floating down the Seine. Sails were lying in the bottom of the boat. The bargeman towed it under the barge office. The next morning it was taken from thence, without the knowledge of any of the officers. The rudder is now at the barge office.”

> —﻿*Le Diligence*﻿—Thursday, June 26.49

Upon reading these various extracts, they not only seemed to me irrelevant, but I could perceive no mode in which any one of them could be brought to bear upon the matter in hand. I waited for some explanation from Dupin.

===Chinese===

「前天，在这城左近，干下了一场性质最凶残的暴行。一位绅士带着他的妻子和女儿，在黄昏光景雇了六个年轻小伙子的劳役——他们正把一只小船在塞纳河边划来划去消闲——渡他过河。到对岸时，三个乘客下了船，走出船影之外，女儿发觉她把阳伞忘在船里。她回身去取，被那一伙抓住，抬进河心，堵了嘴，横遭凌辱，终于被带到离她同父母上船的地点不远的一点岸上。那些恶棍此刻逃掉了，但警察已循上他们的踪迹，其中几个不久便要落网。」

——《晨报》——六月二十五日〔45〕

「我们收到一两封来信，目的是把新近暴行的罪名钉在梅奈〔46〕头上；但既然这位先生已被一次忠诚的查究完全开脱，而我们几位通信人的论证又热心有余、深刻不足，我们不认为把它们公开是相宜的。」

——《晨报》——六月二十八日〔47〕

「我们收到几封写得有力的来信，显然出自不同的来源，它们足以使下面一点近乎成为定案：不幸的玛丽·罗热成了星期日滋扰城郊的无数下流团伙之一手的牺牲品。我们自己的意见断然倾向这个设想。此后我们当设法在这里腾出篇幅登载这些论证中的几篇。」

——《晚报》——六月三十一日，星期二〔48〕

「星期一，税务局的一个驳船水手看见一只空船顺塞纳河漂下。船底放着帆。那水手把船拖到驳船事务所底下。第二天早晨，它被从那里取走，任何值班的官员都不知情。舵此刻在驳船事务所。」

——《驿车报》（Le Diligence）——六月二十六日，星期四〔49〕

读着这些形形色色的摘录，它们不但似乎同本案无关，而且我看不出其中任何一件可以拿来对付手头的事。我等着杜宾的解释。

===Original===

“It is not my present design,” he said, “to *dwell* upon the first and second of those extracts. I have copied them chiefly to show you the extreme remissness of the police, who, as far as I can understand from the Prefect, have not troubled themselves, in any respect, with an examination of the naval officer alluded to. Yet it is mere folly to say that between the first and second disappearance of Marie there is no *supposable* connection. Let us admit the first elopement to have resulted in a quarrel between the lovers, and the return home of the betrayed. We are now prepared to view a second *elopement* (if we *know* that an elopement has again taken place) as indicating a renewal of the betrayer’s advances, rather than as the result of new proposals by a second individual﻿—we are prepared to regard it as a ‘making up’ of the old amour, rather than as the commencement of a new one. The chances are ten to one, that he who had once eloped with Marie, would again propose an elopement, rather than that she to whom proposals of elopement had been made by one individual, should have them made to her by another. And here let me call your attention to the fact, that the time elapsing between the first ascertained, and the second supposed elopement, is a few months more than the general period of the cruises of our men-of-war. Had the lover been interrupted in his first villany by the necessity of departure to sea, and had he seized the first moment of his return to renew the base designs not yet altogether accomplished﻿—or not yet altogether accomplished *by him*? Of all these things we know nothing.

===Chinese===

「我此刻的设计不是*细说*那些摘录的第一件和第二件。我把它们抄来，主要是给你看警察的极端疏忽——就我从总监那里所能领会的，他们对那位海军军官的查问，竟没有在任何方面费过心。然而说玛丽的第一次与第二次失踪之间没有*可设想的*关联，是十足的蠢话。让我们承认第一次的私奔引出情人之间的一场口角，和被诱者的回家。此刻我们便有准备去看第二次的*私奔*（倘若我们*知道*又私奔了一次）表明诱奸者旧调的重弹，而不是第二个个人的新提议的结果——我们便有准备把它看作一场旧欢的「重续」，而不是一场新欢的开端。十比一的机会是：曾同玛丽私奔过一次的那个人，会再提一次私奔的提议，而不是：私奔的提议既已被一个人向她提过，便由另一个人再提。这里让我请你注意一个事实：第一次确知的与第二次假想的私奔之间隔的时间，比我们的军舰一般巡航的周期，多出几个月。倘若那情人头一次的恶行因须出海而被打断，他抓住归来的最初一刻重续那不曾全然得逞——或尚未全然*由他*得逞——的卑污设计，又怎样呢？这一切我们一概不知。

===Original===

“You will say, however, that, in the second instance, there was *no* elopement as imagined. Certainly not﻿—but are we prepared to say that there was not the frustrated design? Beyond St. Eustache, and perhaps Beauvais, we find no recognized, no open, no honorable suitors of Marie. Of none other is there anything said. Who, then, is the secret lover, of whom the relatives (*at least most of them*) know nothing, but whom Marie meets upon the morning of Sunday, and who is so deeply in her confidence, that she hesitates not to remain with him until the shades of the evening descend, amid the solitary groves of the Barrière du Roule? Who is that secret lover, I ask, of whom, at least, *most* of the relatives know nothing? And what means the singular prophecy of Madame Rogêt on the morning of Marie’s departure?﻿—‘I fear that I shall never see Marie again.’

“But if we cannot imagine Madame Rogêt privy to the design of elopement, may we not at least suppose this design entertained by the girl? Upon quitting home, she gave it to be understood that she was about to visit her aunt in the Rue des Drômes and St. Eustache was requested to call for her at dark. Now, at first glance, this fact strongly militates against my suggestion;﻿—but let us reflect. That she *did* meet some companion, and proceed with him across the river, reaching the Barrière du Roule at so late an hour as three o’clock in the afternoon, is known. But in consenting so to accompany this individual, (*for whatever purpose﻿—to her mother known or unknown,*) she must have thought of her expressed intention when leaving home, and of the surprise and suspicion aroused in the bosom of her affianced suitor, St. Eustache, when, calling for her, at the hour appointed, in the Rue des Drômes, he should find that she had not been there, and when, moreover, upon returning to the pension with this alarming intelligence, he should become aware of her continued absence from home. She must have thought of these things, I say. She must have foreseen the chagrin of St. Eustache, the suspicion of all. She could not have thought of returning to brave this suspicion; but the suspicion becomes a point of trivial importance to her, if we suppose her *not* intending to return.

===Chinese===

「然而你会说，在第二次的事里，*并没有*所想象的那种私奔。自然没有——但我们就预备说没有那被挫败的设计吗？除圣厄斯塔什，或许除博韦，我们找不出玛丽的任何公认的、公开的、体面的追求者。旁的人只字不提。那么，那个秘密的情人是谁？她的亲属（至少大多数）一无所知，而玛丽在星期日的早晨同他相会，并且他对她的信任深到这样：她毫不迟疑地同他留在鲁莱关卡的孤林里，直到暮色的影子降下。我问：那个至少*大多数*亲属一无所知的秘密情人是谁？罗热太太在玛丽出门那天早晨那句奇特的谶语又是什么意思？——『我怕我再也见不着玛丽了。』

「但倘若我们不能设想罗热太太与私奔的设计有染，我们至少可以设想这设计存于那姑娘的心里吗？离家时，她让人明白她要去德罗姆街看姨妈，并且请圣厄斯塔什天黑时去接她。乍看之下，这个事实强烈地抵触我的提示；——但让我们想想。她*确实*遇见了某个同伴，同他过了河，在下午三点钟那样晚的时刻到达鲁莱关卡，这是知道的。但她既然答应陪这同一个人去（无论为了什么目的——她母亲知道也好，不知道也好），她必定想到过她离家时表明的意向，想到过她的未婚夫圣厄斯塔什——他按约定的时辰到德罗姆街去接她，发觉她并不在那里，并且带着这骇人的消息回到寄宿舍，发觉她仍旧不在家——胸中掀起的惊愕与怀疑。我再说，这些她必定想到过。她必定预见圣厄斯塔什的懊恼，众人的怀疑。她想不到回来面对这怀疑；但倘若我们设想她*不打算回来*，这怀疑对她便成了无关紧要的一点。

===Original===

“We may imagine her thinking thus﻿—‘I am to meet a certain person for the purpose of elopement, or for certain other purposes known only to myself. It is necessary that there be no chance of interruption﻿—there must be sufficient time given us to elude pursuit﻿—I will give it to be understood that I shall visit and spend the day with my aunt at the Rue des Drômes﻿—I will tell St. Eustache not to call for me until dark﻿—in this way, my absence from home for the longest possible period, without causing suspicion or anxiety, will be accounted for, and I shall gain more time than in any other manner. If I bid St. Eustache call for me at dark, he will be sure not to call before; but, if I wholly neglect to bid him call, my time for escape will be diminished, since it will be expected that I return the earlier, and my absence will the sooner excite anxiety. Now, if it were my design to return *at all*﻿—if I had in contemplation merely a stroll with the individual in question﻿—it would not be my policy to bid St. Eustache call; for, calling, he will be *sure* to ascertain that I have played him false﻿—a fact of which I might keep him forever in ignorance, by leaving home without notifying him of my intention, by returning before dark, and by then stating that I had been to visit my aunt in the Rue des Drômes. But, as it is my design *never* to return﻿—or not for some weeks﻿—or not until certain concealments are effected﻿—the gaining of time is the only point about which I need give myself any concern.’

===Chinese===

「我们可以设想她这样想——『我要同某个人相会，为着私奔，或为着只有我自己知道的别的目的。必须没有被打断的机会——必须给我们足够的时间摆脱追寻——我要让人明白我要去德罗姆街的姨妈家过一天——我要告诉圣厄斯塔什天黑前不必来接我——这样，我在家之外可能的长时间的缺席，便有了交代，不惹起怀疑或焦虑，我便赢得比任何别的法子都多的时间。倘若我叫圣厄斯塔什天黑来接，他天黑之前必定不来接；但倘若我全然不叫他来接，我逃走的时间便缩短了，因为人家会指望我回来得早些，我的不在也便更早惹起焦虑。好，倘若我根本*打算回来*——倘若我盘算的不过是同那个人散散步——叫圣厄斯塔什来接便不合我的策略；因为他一来接，*必定*会查明我骗了他——这个事实我原可以叫他永远蒙在鼓里：离家时不通知他我的意向，天黑前回来，然后说我去了德罗姆街的姨妈家。但既然我的设计是*永不*回来——或几个星期不回——或不到几件隐匿的事办妥不回——赢得时间便是我唯一需要操心的一点。』

===Original===

“You have observed, in your notes, that the most general opinion in relation to this sad affair is, and was from the first, that the girl had been the victim of *a gang* of blackguards. Now, the popular opinion, under certain conditions, is not to be disregarded. When arising of itself﻿—when manifesting itself in a strictly spontaneous manner﻿—we should look upon it as analogous with that *intuition* which is the idiosyncrasy of the individual man of genius. In ninety-nine cases from the hundred I would abide by its decision. But it is important that we find no palpable traces of *suggestion*. The opinion must be rigorously *the public’s own*; and the distinction is often exceedingly difficult to perceive and to maintain. In the present instance, it appears to me that this ‘public opinion’ in respect to *a gang*, has been superinduced by the collateral event which is detailed in the third of my extracts. All Paris is excited by the discovered corpse of Marie, a girl young, beautiful, and notorious. This corpse is found, bearing marks of violence, and floating in the river. But it is now made known that, at the very period, or about the very period, in which it is supposed that the girl was assassinated, an outrage similar in nature to that endured by the deceased, although less in extent, was perpetuated, by a gang of young ruffians, upon the person of a second young female. Is it wonderful that the one known atrocity should influence the popular judgment in regard to the other unknown? This judgment awaited direction, and the known outrage seemed so opportunely to afford it! Marie, too, was found in the river; and upon this very river was this known outrage committed. The connection of the two events had about it so much of the palpable, that the true wonder would have been a *failure* of the populace to appreciate and to seize it. But, in fact, the one atrocity, known to be so committed, is, if anything, evidence that the other, committed at a time nearly coincident, was *not* so committed. It would have been a miracle indeed, if, while a gang of ruffians were perpetrating, at a given locality, a most unheard-of wrong, there should have been another similar gang, in a similar locality, in the same city, under the same circumstances, with the same means and appliances, engaged in a wrong of precisely the same aspect, at precisely the same period of time!

===Chinese===

「你在你的札记里注意到：关于这桩伤心案子的最普遍的意见，从最初起便是——那姑娘是一伙下流坯的牺牲品。此刻，民众的意见，在某些条件之下，是不可漠视的。当它自发地兴起——当它以严格的自然的方式显示自己——我们应当把它看作同那*直觉*类似，而那直觉是天才的个人独具的气质。九十九件里我愿依从它的判决。但重要的是，我们找不出*暗示*的明白痕迹。这意见必须严格地*是公众自己的*；而这一区分常常极难察觉、极难保持。在眼前的例子里，依我看，关于*一伙*的这个「公众意见」，是被我摘录的第三件里详述的那件旁属事件叠加上去的。全巴黎为一个发现的尸体激动着——玛丽的尸体，年轻，美丽，出名。这尸体带着暴力的痕迹，在河里漂浮着被发现。但此刻被泄露出来：恰在人们以为那姑娘被谋杀的时期，或约在那一时期，一场性质同死者所受的相似、只是程度较轻的暴行，被一伙年轻的恶棍行在第二个年轻女人身上。一场已知的暴行影响公众对另一场未知的判断，有什么可怪？这判断等待着方向，而已知的暴行来得这样凑巧，给了它方向！玛丽也在河里被发现；而这场已知的暴行恰恰也行在这条河上。两件事的关联带着这么多表显的成分，真正的奇迹倒是民众*没有*领会它、抓住它。但事实上，已知的这场暴行既知是那样行的，倒是证据，证明几乎同时行的另一场*并不*是那样行的。倘若一伙恶棍正在一个给定的地点行着一件闻所未闻的恶，而在同一座城里、一个相似的地点、同样的情形之下、用着同样的手段与器械，竟另有一伙类似的恶棍，在同一时间的同一时期里，行着一件面貌恰正相同的恶——那才真真是奇迹！

===Original===

Yet in what, if not in this marvellous train of coincidence, does the accidentally *suggested* opinion of the populace call upon us to believe?

“Before proceeding farther, let us consider the supposed scene of the assassination, in the thicket at the Barrière du Roule. This thicket, although dense, was in the close vicinity of a public road. Within were three or four large stones, forming a kind of seat with a back and footstool. On the upper stone was discovered a white petticoat; on the second, a silk scarf. A parasol, gloves, and a pocket-handkerchief, were also here found. The handkerchief bore the name, ‘Marie Rogêt.’ Fragments of dress were seen on the branches around. The earth was trampled, the bushes were broken, and there was every evidence of a violent struggle.

===Chinese===

然而，民众那偶然被*暗示*的意见，叫我们去信的，倘若不是这奇妙的巧合之链，又是什么呢？

「在继续之前，让我们把所设想的凶杀现场——鲁莱关卡的密丛——考察一下。这座密丛虽然浓密，却紧挨着一条公共的路。丛中有三四块大石头，构成一种带靠背和脚凳的座椅。上面那块石头上放着一条白裙；第二块上放着一条绸围巾。还找到一把阳伞、手套和一块口袋手帕。手帕上写着「玛丽·罗热」的名字。四围的枝子上看得见衣裳的碎片。地面被踏乱，树丛折断，处处是一场剧烈挣扎的证据。

===Original===

“Notwithstanding the acclamation with which the discovery of this thicket was received by the press, and the unanimity with which it was supposed to indicate the precise scene of the outrage, it must be admitted that there was some very good reason for doubt. That it *was* the scene, I may or I may not believe﻿—but there was excellent reason for doubt. Had the *true* scene been, as *Le Commerciel* suggested, in the neighborhood of the Rue Pavée St. Andrée, the perpetrators of the crime, supposing them still resident in Paris, would naturally have been stricken with terror at the public attention thus acutely directed into the proper channel; and, in certain classes of minds, there would have arisen, at once, a sense of the necessity of some exertion to redivert this attention. And thus, the thicket of the Barrière du Roule having been already suspected, the idea of placing the articles where they were found, might have been naturally entertained. There is no real evidence, although *Le Soleil* so supposes, that the articles discovered had been more than a very few days in the thicket; while there is much circumstantial proof that they could not have remained there, without attracting attention, during the twenty days elapsing between the fatal Sunday and the afternoon upon which they were found by the boys. ‘They were all *mildewed* down hard,’ says *Le Soleil*, adopting the opinions of its predecessors, ‘with the action of the rain, and stuck together from *mildew*. The grass had grown around and over some of them. The silk of the parasol was strong, but the threads of it were run together within. The upper part, where it had been doubled and folded, was all *mildewed* and rotten, and tore on being opened.’ In respect to the grass having ‘grown around and over some of them,’ it is obvious that the fact could only have been ascertained from the words, and thus from the recollections, of two small boys; for these boys removed the articles and took them home before they had been seen by a third party. But grass will grow, especially in warm and damp weather (such as was that of the period of the murder), as much as two or three inches in a single day. A parasol lying upon a newly turfed ground, might, in a single week, be entirely concealed from sight by the upspringing grass.

===Chinese===

「尽管密丛的发现博得报界的一片喝彩，众口一词地认为它标明暴行的确切现场，却必须承认：怀疑有着极好的理由。它*是不是*现场，我可以信，也可以不信——但怀疑有着极好的理由。倘若*真正的*现场照《商业报》的提示，在帕韦圣安德烈街的左近，那么罪行的施行者们——倘若他们仍住在巴黎——自然会被公众的注意这样敏锐地投进正轨吓得魂飞；而在某几类头脑里，立刻会生出一种必要之感：得作些努力，把这注意重新引开。于是，鲁莱关卡的密丛既已被疑，把物件放在它们被发现的地方的念头，便可能自然地被想到。没有真正的证据——虽然《太阳报》这样设想——证明被发现的物件在密丛里待过比几天更多的时候；同时有许多旁证证明：它们不可能留在那里而不惹起注意，在那致命的星期日与孩子们发现它们的那个下午之间相隔的二十天里。『它们全被雨水浸得*霉硬*，』《太阳报》说，采纳它前辈们的意见，「因*霉*而粘作一团。草长起来，围着几件，盖住几件。阳伞的绸还结实，但伞里的线已经跑散。上半，折叠过的地方，全*霉*了，烂了，一打开就破。」至于草「长起来，围着几件，盖住几件」，显而易见，这事实只能从两个小男孩的话里、从而从他们的追忆里查明；因为这些孩子在被第三方看见之前，已把物件拿走带回了家。但草是会长——尤其在温暖潮湿的天气里（凶杀的那个时期的天气正是这样）——一天里便长两三英寸。一把阳伞躺在新铺的草地上，一个星期里便可能被蹿起的草完全遮出视野。

===Original===

And touching that *mildew* upon which the editor of *Le Soleil* so pertinaciously insists, that he employs the word no less than three times in the brief paragraph just quoted, is he really unaware of the nature of this *mildew*? Is he to be told that it is one of the many classes of fungus, of which the most ordinary feature is its upspringing and decadence within twenty-four hours?

===Chinese===

至于那*霉*——《太阳报》的编辑那样执拗地坚持的霉，在方才引的那短短一段里用了不下三次的那个字——他当真不知道这*霉*是什么性质的东西吗？需要有人告诉他：它是菌类众多种属中的一种，最寻常的特征便是二十四小时之内蹿起又衰亡吗？

===Original===

“Thus we see, at a glance, that what has been most triumphantly adduced in support of the idea that the articles had been ‘for at least three or four weeks’ in the thicket, is most absurdly null as regards any evidence of that fact. On the other hand, it is exceedingly difficult to believe that these articles could have remained in the thicket specified, for a longer period than a single week﻿—for a longer period than from one Sunday to the next. Those who know anything of the vicinity of Paris, know the extreme difficulty of finding seclusion unless at a great distance from its suburbs. Such a thing as an unexplored, or even an unfrequently visited recess, amid its woods or groves, is not for a moment to be imagined. Let anyone who, being at heart a lover of nature, is yet chained by duty to the dust and heat of this great metropolis﻿—let any such one attempt, even during the weekdays, to slake his thirst for solitude amid the scenes of natural loveliness which immediately surround us. At every second step, he will find the growing charm dispelled by the voice and personal intrusion of some ruffian or party of carousing blackguards. He will seek privacy amid the densest foliage, all in vain. Here are the very nooks where the unwashed most abound﻿—here are the temples most desecrate. With sickness of the heart the wanderer will flee back to the polluted Paris as to a less odious because less incongruous sink of pollution. But if the vicinity of the city is so beset during the working days of the week, how much more so on the Sabbath! It is now especially that, released from the claims of labor, or deprived of the customary opportunities of crime, the town blackguard seeks the precincts of the town, not through love of the rural, which in his heart he despises, but by way of escape from the restraints and conventionalities of society. He desires less the fresh air and the green trees, than the utter *license* of the country. Here, at the roadside inn, or beneath the foliage of the woods, he indulges, unchecked by any eye except those of his boon companions, in all the mad excess of a counterfeit hilarity﻿—the joint offspring of liberty and of rum.

===Chinese===

「这样，我们一眼便看出：被那样洋洋得意地引出来支持物件曾在密丛里『至少三四个星期』这一观念的东西，就那一事实的任何证据而言，荒谬地等于零。另一方面，极难相信这些物件曾在所说的密丛里留过比一个星期更长的时期——从一个星期日到下一个星期日。凡对巴黎左近有所了解的人，都知道除非离城郊很远，寻一处僻静是何等困难。在它的林间或树丛里，有这样一块未探过的、甚至少有人到的幽地，是一刻也想象不得的事。让任何人——心里原是自然的情人，却被责任锁在这大都会的尘土与炎热里——让任何这样一个人试试，即便在星期几里，到立刻环绕着我们的这些自然的美的景致里，解一解他孤独的渴。每走第二步，他便发觉生长中的魅力被某个恶棍或一伙饮酒喧闹的下流人的嗓音与现身驱散。他要在最密的叶幕里寻隐私，全归无用。这里正是脏人最云集的角落——这里正是最受亵渎的殿堂。怀着心的厌恶，这漂泊者逃回污秽的巴黎，当作一个不那么可惜、因为不那么不调和的污秽之潭。但倘若城郊在每周的做工的日子里便这样被包围着，在安息日又当怎样！此刻，尤其在此刻，脱了劳役的羁绊，或失了惯常的犯罪的机会，城里的下流坯便奔向城的四郊，不由于对乡野的爱——他心里是轻贱它的——而作为对社会的约束与常规的逃避。他要的少是新鲜空气和绿树，多是乡野的全然的*放任*。这里，在路边的客栈里，或在树林的叶幕下，他纵情于假冒的欢快的一切疯狂的放纵，不受任何眼睛的约束，除他酒友们的眼睛——那欢快是自由与朗姆酒的合生的孩子。

===Original===

I say nothing more than what must be obvious to every dispassionate observer, when I repeat that the circumstance of the articles in question having remained undiscovered, for a longer period than from one Sunday to another, in *any* thicket in the immediate neighborhood of Paris, is to be looked upon as little less than miraculous.

“But there are not wanting other grounds for the suspicion that the articles were placed in the thicket with the view of diverting attention from the real scene of the outrage. And, first, let me direct your notice to the *date* of the discovery of the articles. Collate this with the date of the fifth extract made by myself from the newspapers. You will find that the discovery followed, almost immediately, the urgent communications sent to the evening paper. These communications, although various and apparently from various sources, tended all to the same point﻿—viz., the directing of attention to *a gang* as the perpetrators of the outrage, and to the neighborhood of the Barrière du Roule as its scene. Now here, of course, the suspicion is not that, in consequence of these communications, or of the public attention by them directed, the articles were found by the boys; but the suspicion might and may well have been, that the articles were not *before* found by the boys, for the reason that the articles had not before been in the thicket; having been deposited there only at so late a period as at the date, or shortly prior to the date of the communications, by the guilty authors of these communications themselves.

===Chinese===

我说的不过是每一个冷静的观察者必觉得显然的话，当我再说一遍：所说的那些物件曾在巴黎紧邻的*任何*密丛里，留过比从一个星期日到另一个星期日更长的时期而不被发现，这情形只能被看作近乎奇迹。

===Original===

“This thicket was a singular﻿—an exceedingly singular one. It was unusually dense. Within its naturally walled enclosure were three extraordinary stones, *forming a seat with a back and footstool*. And this thicket, so full of a natural art, was in the immediate vicinity, *within a few rods*, of the dwelling of Madame Deluc, whose boys were in the habit of closely examining the shrubberies about them in search of the bark of the sassafras. Would it be a rash wager﻿—a wager of one thousand to one﻿—that *a day* never passed over the heads of these boys without finding at least one of them ensconced in the umbrageous hall, and enthroned upon its natural throne? Those who would hesitate at such a wager, have either never been boys themselves, or have forgotten the boyish nature. I repeat﻿—it is exceedingly hard to comprehend how the articles could have remained in this thicket undiscovered, for a longer period than one or two days; and that thus there is good ground for suspicion, in spite of the dogmatic ignorance of *Le Soleil*, that they were, at a comparatively late date, deposited where found.

===Chinese===

「但并不缺别的根据，可以怀疑那些物件是带着把注意从暴行真正现场引开的用意放进密丛的。第一，容我把你的注意引到物件被发现的*日期*上。把它同我照报纸做的第五件摘录的日期对勘。你将发现：这发现紧跟在投给晚报的那些急切的信件之后。这些信件虽然来源不一、又显然出自不同的来源，却都趋向同一点——即把注意引向*一伙*，作为暴行的凶手，把鲁莱关卡的左近引作现场。这里，当然，可疑的并不是：由于这些信件，或由于它们引动的公众注意，物件才被孩子们发现；可疑的可能是，而且很可以是：物件先前不曾被孩子们发现，缘由是物件先前并不在密丛里；它们是到那样晚的一个日期——通信的日期或略在前——才被这些通信的有罪的作者们自己放进那里去的。

===Original===

“But there are still other and stronger reasons for believing them so deposited, than any which I have as yet urged. And, now, let me beg your notice to the highly artificial arrangement of the articles. On the *upper* stone lay a white petticoat; on the *second* a silk scarf; scattered around, were a parasol, gloves, and a pocket-handkerchief bearing the name, ‘Marie Rogêt.’ Here is just such an arrangement as would *naturally* be made by a not-over-acute person wishing to dispose the articles *naturally*. But it is by no means a *really* natural arrangement. I should rather have looked to see the things *all* lying on the ground and trampled under foot. In the narrow limits of that bower, it would have been scarcely possible that the petticoat and scarf should have retained a position upon the stones, when subjected to the brushing to and fro of many struggling persons. ‘There was evidence,’ it is said, ‘of a struggle; and the earth was trampled, the bushes were broken,’﻿—but the petticoat and the scarf are found deposited as if upon shelves. ‘The pieces of the frock torn out by the bushes were about three inches wide and six inches long. One part was the hem of the frock and it had been mended. They *looked like strips torn off*.’ Here, inadvertently, *Le Soleil* has employed an exceedingly suspicious phrase. The pieces, as described, do indeed ‘look like strips torn off;’ but purposely and by hand. It is one of the rarest of accidents that a piece is ‘torn off,’ from any garment such as is now in question, by the agency *of a thorn*. From the very nature of such fabrics, a thorn or nail becoming entangled in them, tears them rectangularly﻿—divides them into two longitudinal rents, at right angles with each other, and meeting at an apex where the thorn enters﻿—but it is scarcely possible to conceive the piece ‘torn off.’ I never so knew it, nor did you. To tear a piece *off* from such fabric, two distinct forces, in different directions, will be, in almost every case, required. If there be two edges to the fabric﻿—if, for example, it be a pocket-handkerchief, and it is desired to tear from it a slip, then, and then only, will the one force serve the purpose. But in the present case the question is of a dress, presenting but one edge.

===Chinese===

「这座密丛是一座奇异的——异乎寻常地奇异的密丛。它异常浓密。在它天然围成的圈子里，有三块异样的石头，*构成一座带靠背和脚凳的座椅*。而这座充满天然的艺术的密丛，就紧邻着德吕克太太的住宅，*相距不过几杆*；她的孩子们习惯在四周的灌木丛里细细搜寻黄樟的树皮。打一个鲁莽的赌——一千比一的赌——*随便哪一天*在这些孩子们的头顶过去，而不见他们至少一个躲在那叶幕的厅堂里，坐在那天然的宝座上——这赌会轻率吗？对这样的赌踌躇的人，要么自己从来不曾做过孩子，要么忘了孩子的天性。我再说一遍——那些物件竟能留在这座密丛里一两天以上而不被发现，极难领会；因此，尽管《太阳报》武断的无知，它们是到比较晚近的日期才被放进那被发现的地方的，这一点有极好的根据可以怀疑。

===Original===

To tear a piece from the interior, where no edge is presented, could only be effected by a miracle through the agency of thorns, and no *one* thorn could accomplish it. But, even where an edge is presented, two thorns will be necessary, operating, the one in two distinct directions, and the other in one. And this in the supposition that the edge is unhemmed. If hemmed, the matter is nearly out of the question. We thus see the numerous and great obstacles in the way of pieces being ‘torn off’ through the simple agency of ‘thorns;’ yet we are required to believe not only that one piece but that many have been so torn. ‘And one part,’ too, ‘*was the hem of the frock*!’ Another piece was ‘*part of the skirt, not the hem*,’﻿—that is to say, was torn completely out through the agency of thorns, from the uncaged interior of the dress! These, I say, are things which one may well be pardoned for disbelieving; yet, taken collectedly, they form, perhaps, less of reasonable ground for suspicion, than the one startling circumstance of the articles’ having been left in this thicket at all, by any *murderers* who had enough precaution to think of removing the corpse. You will not have apprehended me rightly, however, if you suppose it my design to *deny* this thicket as the scene of the outrage. There might have been a wrong *here*, or, more possibly, an accident at Madame Deluc’s. But, in fact, this is a point of minor importance. We are not engaged in an attempt to discover the scene, but to produce the perpetrators of the murder. What I have adduced, notwithstanding the minuteness with which I have adduced it, has been with the view, first, to show the folly of the positive and headlong assertions of *Le Soleil*, but secondly and chiefly, to bring you, by the most natural route, to a further contemplation of the doubt whether this assassination has, or has not, been the work of *a gang*.

“We will resume this question by mere allusion to the revolting details of the surgeon examined at the inquest. It is only necessary to say that his published *inferences*, in regard to the number of ruffians, have been properly ridiculed as unjust and totally baseless, by all the reputable anatomists of Paris. Not that the matter *might not* have been as inferred, but that there was no ground for the inference:﻿—was there not much for another?

===Chinese===

「但还有别的、更强的理由，使我信它们是那样被放进去的，胜过我迄今已经提出的一切。此刻，容我求你注意那些物件的高度人工的排布。*上面*那块石头上放着一条白裙；*第二*块上一条绸围巾；散在四围的，是一把阳伞、手套和一块写着「玛丽·罗热」名字的口袋手帕。这正是那种排布：一个不过分机敏的人想把物件摆得*自然些*，便*自然地*作出这样的排布。但这绝不是一种*真正的*自然排布。我倒宁可期望看见那些东西*全都*躺在地上，被脚下踩过。在那小天地的狭窄界限里，裙和围巾要在许多挣扎的人来回的擦蹭之下，仍保住它们在石头上的位置，几乎不可能。据说「有挣扎的证据；地面被踏乱，树丛折断」，——可裙和围巾被发现安置着，仿佛搁在架子上。『外裙被树丛撕下的碎片约三英寸宽、六英寸长。一块是外裙的裙边，补缀过。它们*看着像撕下来的布条*。』这里，《太阳报》无意之间用了一个极可疑的短语。这些碎片，照描述，的确「看着像撕下来的布条」；但那是存心用手撕的。一件如今所说的这类衣裳，凭*一根刺*的作用，撕下一块「撕下来的布条」，是极罕见的偶然。照这类织物的本性，一根刺或一枚钉缠进它们，是把它们直角地撕开——把它们分作两道纵的裂口，彼此成直角，会合在刺进去的尖上——但要说一块布幅「被撕下来」，几乎无法设想。我从不曾知道这样的事，你也不曾。要从这样的织物上把一块*撕下来*，几乎每一回都需要两种不同的力，朝着不同的方向。倘若织物有两道边——比如，它是一块口袋手帕，想从它撕下一幅——那时，唯有那时，一种力便够了用。但眼前的问题是一件衣裳，只有一道边。

===Original===

“Let us reflect now upon ‘the traces of a struggle;’ and let me ask what these traces have been supposed to demonstrate. A gang. But do they not rather demonstrate the absence of a gang? What *struggle* could have taken place﻿—what struggle so violent and so enduring as to have left its ‘traces’ in all directions﻿—between a weak and defenceless girl and the *gang* of ruffians imagined? The silent grasp of a few rough arms and all would have been over. The victim must have been absolutely passive at their will. You will here bear in mind that the arguments urged against the thicket as the scene, are applicable in chief part, only against it as the scene of an outrage committed by *more than a single individual*. If we imagine but *one* violator, we can conceive, and thus only conceive, the struggle of so violent and so obstinate a nature as to have left the ‘traces’ apparent.

===Chinese===

要从没有边露出的内部撕下一块，借刺的作用只有奇迹可办，而且没有*一根*刺能办成。但即便有边露着，两根刺也属必要，一根朝两个不同的方向使力，另一根朝一个方向使力。这还假定那道边没有缝边。倘若缝了边，事情便几乎无从谈起。这样我们看到：布幅要凭「刺」的单纯作用「撕下来」，障碍既多且大；然而人们竟要求我们相信：不但一块，而且许多块这样撕了下来。『而且一块，』还是『*外裙的裙边*！』另一块是『*裙幅的一部分，不是裙边*』——就是说，是凭刺的作用，从那没有开边的衣裳的内部整个撕出来的！这些，我说，是一个人尽可以得着原谅去不信的东西；然而，合起来看，它们所形成的合理的怀疑根据，也许还不及那桩惊人的情形：那些物件居然被任何有足够的先见想到要搬走尸体的*凶手们*留在了这座密丛里。不过你倘若设想我的设计是*否认*这座密丛是暴行的现场，你便没有把握住我的意思。那里也许行过一件恶——或者，更有可能，在德吕克太太家里出过一件偶然。但实在说，这是一个次要的要点。我们从事的并不是发现现场的企图，而是找出凶手的企图。我举出的这一切，纵然我举得那样细，其用意，第一，在显出《太阳报》那些斩钉截铁、轻率断言的愚蠢；第二，也是主要的，在借最自然的路线，把你引到那个疑点的进一步的思索上去：这凶杀究竟是不是*一伙*人干下的。

===Original===

“And again. I have already mentioned the suspicion to be excited by the fact that the articles in question were suffered to remain *at all* in the thicket where discovered. It seems almost impossible that these evidences of guilt should have been accidentally left where found. There was sufficient presence of mind (it is supposed) to remove the corpse; and yet a more positive evidence than the corpse itself (whose features might have been quickly obliterated by decay), is allowed to lie conspicuously in the scene of the outrage﻿—I allude to the handkerchief with the *name* of the deceased. If this was accident, it was not the accident *of a gang*. We can imagine it only the accident of an individual. Let us see. An individual has committed the murder. He is alone with the ghost of the departed. He is appalled by what lies motionless before him. The fury of his passion is over, and there is abundant room in his heart for the natural awe of the deed. His is none of that confidence which the presence of numbers inevitably inspires. He is alone with the dead. He trembles and is bewildered. Yet there is a necessity for disposing of the corpse. He bears it to the river, but leaves behind him the other evidences of guilt; for it is difficult, if not impossible to carry all the burden at once, and it will be easy to return for what is left. But in his toilsome journey to the water his fears redouble within him. The sounds of life encompass his path. A dozen times he hears or fancies the step of an observer. Even the very lights from the city bewilder him. Yet, in time and by long and frequent pauses of deep agony, he reaches the river’s brink, and disposes of his ghastly charge﻿—perhaps through the medium of a boat. But *now* what treasure does the world hold﻿—what threat of vengeance could it hold out﻿—which would have power to urge the return of that lonely murderer over that toilsome and perilous path, to the thicket and its blood chilling recollections? He returns *not*, let the consequences be what they may. He *could* not return if he would. His sole thought is immediate escape. He turns his back *forever* upon those dreadful shrubberies and flees as from the wrath to come.

===Chinese===

「我们靠对验尸时受讯的外科医生的详情的仅止一提，重提这个问题。只消说：他发表的关于恶棍人数的*推断*，已被巴黎所有可敬的解剖学家恰当地讥为无据且全无根基。不是说那件事*不可能*如所推断的那样，而是说没有任何根据可以作出那样的推断：——难道没有更多的根据作出另一种推断吗？

「此刻让我们想想『挣扎的痕迹』；容我问一声：这些痕迹被设想证明了什么。一伙人。然而它们岂不更证明一伙人的不在？在一个柔弱无力的姑娘同所想象的那*一伙*恶棍之间，能有什么*挣扎*——什么挣扎剧烈而持久到在各个方向留下『痕迹』？几条粗胳膊的悄悄一攥，一切便完了。被害人必定全然被动地任凭他们摆布。你在这里要记住：反对那密丛作现场的那些论证，主要只反对它作为*不止一个人*所行暴行的现场。倘若我们设想只有*一个*施暴者，我们便能设想——唯有这样设想——那场剧烈而顽强的挣扎，足以留下那些显见的『痕迹』。

===Original===

“But how with a gang? Their number would have inspired them with confidence; if, indeed confidence is ever wanting in the breast of the arrant blackguard; and of arrant blackguards alone are the supposed *gangs* ever constituted. Their number, I say, would have prevented the bewildering and unreasoning terror which I have imagined to paralyze the single man. Could we suppose an oversight in one, or two, or three, this oversight would have been remedied by a fourth. They would have left nothing behind them; for their number would have enabled them to carry *all* at once. There would have been no need of *return*.

“Consider now the circumstance that in the outer garment of the corpse when found, ‘a slip, about a foot wide had been torn upward from the bottom hem to the waist wound three times round the waist, and secured by a sort of hitch in the back.’ This was done with the obvious design of affording *a handle* by which to carry the body. But would any *number* of men have dreamed of resorting to such an expedient? To three or four, the limbs of the corpse would have afforded not only a sufficient, but the best possible hold. The device is that of a single individual; and this brings us to the fact that ‘between the thicket and the river, the rails of the fences were found taken down, and the ground bore evident traces of some heavy burden having been dragged along it!’ But would a *number* of men have put themselves to the superfluous trouble of taking down a fence, for the purpose of dragging through it a corpse which they might have *lifted* over any fence in an instant? Would a number of men have so *dragged* a corpse at all as to have left evident *traces* of the dragging?

“And here we must refer to an observation of *Le Commerciel*; an observation upon which I have already, in some measure, commented. ‘A piece,’ says this journal, ‘of one of the unfortunate girl’s petticoats was torn out and tied under her chin, and around the back of her head, probably to prevent screams. This was done by fellows who had no pocket-handkerchiefs.’

===Chinese===

「再者。我已经提过那由以下事实激起的怀疑：所说的那些物件居然被容许*留在*它们被发现的密丛里。这些罪证竟被偶然地留在被发现的地方，几乎不可能。据设想，他们有足够的心神搬走尸体；却让一件比尸体本身（尸体的面目或许很快便被腐坏抹掉）更积极的证据，明晃晃地躺在暴行的现场——我指那块写着死者*名字*的手帕。倘若这是偶然，它也不是*一伙人*的偶然。我们只能设想它是一个个人的偶然。让我们看看。一个人行下了凶杀。他同死者的幽灵独自相对。他被眼前一动不动的东西吓住了。他情欲的狂焰已经过去，他心里有的是对这桩行为天然的敬畏。他绝没有人群的在场必然激起的那种信心。他同死者单独相对。他发抖，心神无主。然而处置尸体又有必要。他把它抬向河边，却把其余的罪证留在身后；因为把全部重负一次带全，困难，或者不可能，而回来取剩下的东西倒是容易的。但在他向水边的劳苦的路上，他的恐惧在他心里加倍地涨。生命的声息包围着他的路。他一次次听见，或自以为听见旁观者的脚步。连城里的灯火也叫他昏乱。然而他终于到了水边，处置了他那怕人的重负——或许借一只船的媒介。但*此刻*世上还握着什么珍宝——它能捧出什么报复的威吓——有力量催那孤独的凶手循那条劳苦而险恶的路回到那密丛和它彻骨的追忆？他不回来，任凭后果如何。纵然他肯，他也*不能*回来。他唯一的念头是立刻的逃遁。他*永远*转过身去，背着那些可怖的灌木，逃着，像逃避将来的天罚。

===Original===

“I have before suggested that a genuine blackguard is never *without* a pocket-handkerchief. But it is not to this fact that I now especially advert. That it was not through want of a handkerchief for the purpose imagined by *Le Commerciel*, that this bandage was employed, is rendered apparent by the handkerchief left in the thicket; and that the object was not ‘to prevent screams’ appears, also, from the bandage having been employed in preference to what would so much better have answered the purpose. But the language of the evidence speaks of the strip in question as ‘found around the neck, fitting loosely, and secured with a hard knot.’ These words are sufficiently vague, but differ materially from those of *Le Commerciel*. The slip was eighteen inches wide, and therefore, although of muslin, would form a strong band when folded or rumpled longitudinally. And thus rumpled it was discovered. My inference is this. The solitary murderer, having borne the corpse, for some distance (whether from the thicket or elsewhere) by means of the bandage *hitched* around its middle, found the weight, in this mode of procedure, too much for his strength. He resolved to drag the burden﻿—the evidence goes to show that it *was* dragged. With this object in view, it became necessary to attach something like a rope to one of the extremities. It could be best attached about the neck, where the head would prevent its slipping off. And, now, the murderer bethought him, unquestionably, of the bandage about the loins. He would have used this, but for its volution about the corpse, the *hitch* which embarrassed it, and the reflection that it had not been ‘torn off’ from the garment. It was easier to tear a new slip from the petticoat. He tore it, made it fast about the neck, and so *dragged* his victim to the brink of the river. That this ‘bandage,’ only attainable with trouble and delay, and but imperfectly answering its purpose﻿—that this bandage was employed *at all*, demonstrates that the necessity for its employment sprang from circumstances arising at a period when the handkerchief was no longer attainable﻿—that is to say, arising, as we have imagined, after quitting the thicket (if the thicket it was), and on the road between the thicket and the river.

===Chinese===

「但一伙人又怎样？他们的人数会给他们的胸膛里装上信心——倘若十足的恶棍的胸膛里居然缺过信心；而所设想的那些*团伙*，从来单由十足的恶棍构成。他们的人数，我说，会防止那种我曾设想足以瘫痪单个人的昏乱而无理性的恐怖。倘若我们能设想一个人、两个人、三个人里有一个疏忽，这疏忽会被第四个人补救。他们什么也不会留在身后；因为他们的人数会使他们能够*一次*带全。便不需要*回来*。

「此刻考虑这个情形：尸体被发现时，在它的外衣上，「一条约一英尺宽的布幅，从下摆向上撕到腰际，在腰上绕了三匝，在背后用一种结扣住」。这是带着显然的用意做的：给出一个*把柄*，借以抬运尸体。但任何*数目*的人会想到采用这样一种权宜吗？对三四个人，尸体的四肢便给着不但够用、而且最好的把柄。这一手是单个个人的；而这就把我们引到这个事实：『在密丛与河之间，栅栏的栏杆被发现拆了下来，地面带着明显的痕迹，某种重负曾被拖过它！』然而*一群*人肯给自己添这样多余的麻烦，拆一道栅栏，为着把一具尸体从栅栏那里拖过，而那尸体他们原可以*举*过任何栅栏，一瞬的事？一群人肯把一具尸体*拖*到留下拖的明显*痕迹*的地步吗？

「这里我们必须援引《商业报》的一个观察；那观察我已经多少评论过。『那不幸的姑娘裙幅中的一条，』这份报纸说，「被撕下来，系在她下巴底下，绕到脑后，多半为着防她喊叫。干这事的，是连口袋手帕也没有的家伙。」

===Original===

“But the evidence, you will say, of Madame Deluc (!) points especially to the presence of *a gang*, in the vicinity of the thicket, at or about the epoch of the murder. This I grant. I doubt if there were not a *dozen* gangs, such as described by Madame Deluc, in and about the vicinity of the Barrière du Roule at *or about* the period of this tragedy. But the gang which has drawn upon itself the pointed animadversion, although the somewhat tardy and very suspicious evidence of Madame Deluc, is the *only* gang which is represented by that honest and scrupulous old lady as having eaten her cakes and swallowed her brandy, without putting themselves to the trouble of making her payment. *Et hinc illae irae?*

“But what *is* the precise evidence of Madame Deluc? ‘A gang of miscreants made their appearance, behaved boisterously, ate and drank without making payment, followed in the route of the young man and girl, returned to the inn *about dusk*, and recrossed the river as if in great haste.’

“Now this ‘great haste’ very possibly seemed *greater* haste in the eyes of Madame Deluc, since she dwelt lingeringly and lamentingly upon her violated cakes and ale﻿—cakes and ale for which she might still have entertained a faint hope of compensation. Why, otherwise, since it was *about dusk*, should she make a point of the *haste*? It is no cause for wonder, surely, that even a gang of blackguards should make *haste* to get home, when a wide river is to be crossed in small boats, when storm impends, and when night *approaches*.

===Chinese===

「我从前提示过：一个道地的下流坯从来不*缺*口袋手帕。但我此刻特别要说的不是这个事实。系这条带子并非因为缺《商业报》所想象的那种用处的手帕，这一点由留在密丛里的那块手帕显出来；而那目的并不是『防喊叫』，这一点也由那带子竟被采用、而不采用远更能达此目的之物，显了出来。但证据的措辞说到所说的那条布幅，说它『发现围着颈子，松松地，用一个死结扣紧』。这些词够含糊，但同《商业报》的措辞大不相同。那布幅宽十八英寸，因此虽是细纱，纵着叠起或皱起便成一条结实的带。它被发现时便这样皱着。我的推断是这样。那孤独的凶手，借那条*打结*在尸体腰间的带子，把尸体抬了一段路（无论从密丛还是从别处），发觉在这种方式里，重量超出了他的膂力。他决意拖那重负——证据表明它*确实*被拖过。为着这个目的，有必要把一条类似绳子的东西系在尸身的一端。最好系在颈上，那里头颅可以防它滑脱。此刻，那凶手无疑想到了腰间那条布幅。他本会用它，若非它绕着尸身的那几匝、那条碍事的*结*，以及想到它不曾从衣裳上「撕下来」。从裙上撕一条新的更容易。他撕下它，把它牢系在颈上，便这样*拖*着他的被害人到河边。这条『带子』——得来费事费时，而效力又不完全——它居然被*用了*，证明用它之必要出于那样的情势：那时手帕已无从取得——就是说，如我们所设想的，出于离开密丛之后（倘若那真是密丛），在密丛与河之间的路上。

===Original===

“I say *approaches*; for the night had *not yet arrived*. It was only *about dusk* that the indecent haste of these ‘miscreants’ offended the sober eyes of Madame Deluc. But we are told that it was upon this very evening that Madame Deluc, as well as her eldest son, ‘heard the screams of a female in the vicinity of the inn.’ And in what words does Madame Deluc designate the period of the evening at which these screams were heard? ‘It was *soon after dark*,’ she says. But ‘soon *after* dark,’ is, at least, *dark*; and ‘*about dusk*’ is as certainly daylight. Thus it is abundantly clear that the gang quitted the Barrière du Roule *prior* to the screams overheard (?) by Madame Deluc. And although, in all the many reports of the evidence, the relative expressions in question are distinctly and invariably employed just as I have employed them in this conversation with yourself, no notice whatever of the gross discrepancy has, as yet, been taken by any of the public journals, or by any of the myrmidons of police.

“I shall add but one to the arguments against *a gang*; but this *one* has, to my own understanding at least, a weight altogether irresistible. Under the circumstances of large reward offered, and full pardon to any king’s evidence, it is not to be imagined, for a moment, that some member of *a gang* of low ruffians, or of any body of men, would not long ago have betrayed his accomplices. Each one of a gang so placed, is not so much greedy of reward, or anxious for escape, as *fearful of betrayal*. He betrays eagerly and early that *he may not himself be betrayed*. That the secret has not been divulged, is the very best of proof that it is, in fact, a secret. The horrors of this dark deed are known only to *one*, or two, living human beings, and to God.

===Chinese===

「但你会说，德吕克太太的证据（！）尤其指明凶杀之时或其前后，密丛左近有*一伙人*在场。这一点我承认。我怀疑在那场悲剧*前后*的时期里，鲁莱关卡一带岂止有*十二*伙德吕克太太所描述的那样的团伙。但惹起那尖刻指摘的那一伙——那照德吕克太太颇为迟缓、而非常可疑的证据——是那位诚实而一丝不苟的老太太所代表的*唯一*一伙：吃了她的糕点，喝了她的白兰地，不费心给她钱。*祸由此起乎？*（Et hinc illae irae?）

「然而德吕克太太的*确切的*证据是什么？『一伙恶棍出现，吵吵嚷嚷，吃了喝了不付钱，循着那一男一女去的路跟了去，*黄昏光景*回到客栈，急忙忙地又过了河。』

「这『急忙』，很可能在德吕克太太的眼里显得*更*急，因为她絮絮地哀叹着她那被糟蹋的糕点和麦酒——那糕点和麦酒，她也许还残存着得到补偿的一线希望。不然，既然是*黄昏光景*，她为什么偏要点出那*急忙*？当然不足为怪：纵然一伙下流坯，在一条宽河要用小船渡过、风雨欲来、夜*将至*的时候，也该*急忙*赶回家去。

===Original===

“Let us sum up now the meagre yet certain fruits of our long analysis. We have attained the idea either of a fatal accident under the roof of Madame Deluc, or of a murder perpetrated, in the thicket at the Barrière du Roule, by a lover, or at least by an intimate and secret associate of the deceased. This associate is of swarthy complexion. This complexion, the ‘hitch’ in the bandage, and the ‘sailor’s knot,’ with which the bonnet-ribbon is tied, point to a seaman. His companionship with the deceased, a gay, but not an abject young girl, designates him as above the grade of the common sailor. Here the well written and urgent communications to the journals are much in the way of corroboration. The circumstance of the first elopement, as mentioned by *Le Mercurie*, tends to blend the idea of this seaman with that of the ‘naval officer’ who is first known to have led the unfortunate into crime.

===Chinese===

「我说*将至*；因为夜*还没有到*。正是*黄昏光景*，那些「恶棍」的无礼的急忙，才冒犯了德吕克太太清醒的眼睛。但有人告诉我们，恰在这天晚上，德吕克太太同她的大儿子「听见客栈附近一个女人的尖叫」。而德吕克太太用什么话标明这些尖叫被听见的那晚上的时刻？『是*天黑之后不久*，』她说。但『天黑*之后*不久』至少是*黑*了；而『*黄昏光景*』确然还是白天。这样，明白之极：那一伙在德吕克太太（？）听见的尖叫*之先*，便已离开了鲁莱关卡。而且，虽然在关于证据的一切许多报告里，所说的那些相对的措辞，分明而且一律地，恰如我在这次同你的谈话里使用的那样被使用着，这巨大的出入却至今不曾得到任何公众报纸、或任何警界爪牙的注意。

「对反对*一伙*的论证，我只再添一条；但这一条，至少就我自己的理解，有一种全然无可抵御的分量。在赏格巨大、并对任何充任国证的人一概赦免的情形之下，一时一刻也不可设想：*一伙*下流恶棍、或任何一伙人当中的某个成员，不早已出卖他的同伙。这样处境的一伙里的每个人，与其说贪赏，或急于脱身，不如说*怕被出卖*。他早早地急切地出卖，为的是他自己不被人出卖。这秘密不曾泄露，恰是最好的证明：它实在是一个秘密。这件黑行的恐怖，只为*一个*或两个活人同上帝所知。

===Original===

“And here, most fitly, comes the consideration of the continued absence of him of the dark complexion. Let me pause to observe that the complexion of this man is dark and swarthy; it was no common swarthiness which constituted the *sole* point of remembrance, both as regards Valence and Madame Deluc. But why is this man absent? Was he murdered by the gang? If so, why are there only *traces* of the assassinated *girl*? The scene of the two outrages will naturally be supposed identical. And where is his corpse? The assassins would most probably have disposed of both in the same way. But it may be said that this man lives, and is deterred from making himself known, through dread of being charged with the murder. This consideration might be supposed to operate upon him now﻿—at this late period﻿—since it has been given in evidence that he was seen with Marie﻿—but it would have had no force at the period of the deed. The first impulse of an innocent man would have been to announce the outrage, and to aid in identifying the ruffians. This *policy* would have suggested. He had been seen with the girl. He had crossed the river with her in an open ferryboat. The denouncing of the assassins would have appeared, even to an idiot, the surest and sole means of relieving himself from suspicion. We cannot suppose him, on the night of the fatal Sunday, both innocent himself and incognizant of an outrage committed. Yet only under such circumstances is it possible to imagine that he would have failed, if alive, in the denouncement of the assassins.

===Chinese===

「此刻让我们把我们冗长分析的贫瘠然而确凿的果实总结一下。我们达到了这样一个观念：或者在德吕克太太的屋顶底下出了一桩致命的偶然，或者在鲁莱关卡的密丛里行了一场凶杀，凶手是一个情人，至少是死者一个亲密而秘密的相识。这相识是黝黑的肤色。这肤色，那条带上的『结』，以及系帽带用的那『水手结』，指向一个水手。他同死者的相伴——那是一个快活、却不卑贱的年轻姑娘——把他标为在寻常水手之上的品级。这里，投给报界的那些写得恳切而漂亮的长信，大可作佐证。第一次私奔的情形，照《水星报》所记，倾向于把这水手的观念，同那『海军军官』的观念混起来——那军官是最早被知道把不幸者引入罪中的人。

===Original===

“And what means are ours of attaining the truth? We shall find these means multiplying and gathering distinctness as we proceed. Let us sift to the bottom this affair of the first elopement. Let us know the full history of ‘the officer,’ with his present circumstances, and his whereabouts at the precise period of the murder. Let us carefully compare with each other the various communications sent to the evening paper, in which the object was to inculpate *a gang*. This done, let us compare these communications, both as regards style and MS., with those sent to the morning paper, at a previous period, and insisting so vehemently upon the guilt of Mennais. And, all this done, let us again compare these various communications with the known MSS. of the officer. Let us endeavor to ascertain, by repeated questionings of Madame Deluc and her boys, as well as of the omnibus driver, Valence, something more of the personal appearance and bearing of the ‘man of dark complexion.’ Queries, skilfully directed, will not fail to elicit, from some of these parties, information on this particular point (or upon others)﻿—information which the parties themselves may not even be aware of possessing. And let us now trace *the boat* picked up by the bargeman on the morning of Monday the twenty-third of June, and which was removed from the barge-office, without the cognizance of the officer in attendance, and *without the rudder*, at some period prior to the discovery of the corpse. With a proper caution and perseverance we shall infallibly trace this boat; for not only can the bargeman who picked it up identify it, but the *rudder is at hand*. The rudder *of a sailboat* would not have been abandoned, without inquiry, by one altogether at ease in heart. And here let me pause to insinuate a question. There was no *advertisement* of the picking up of this boat. It was silently taken to the barge-office, and as silently removed. But its owner or employer﻿—how *happened* he, at so early a period as Tuesday morning, to be informed, without the agency of advertisement, of the locality of the boat taken up on Monday, unless we imagine some connection with the *navy*﻿—some personal permanent connection leading to cognizance of its minute in interests﻿—its petty local news?

===Chinese===

“In speaking of the lonely assassin dragging his burden to the shore, I have already suggested the probability of his availing himself *of a boat*. Now we are to understand that Marie Rogêt *was* precipitated from a boat. This would naturally have been the case. The corpse could not have been trusted to the shallow waters of the shore. The peculiar marks on the back and shoulders of the victim tell of the bottom ribs of a boat. That the body was found without weight is also corroborative of the idea. If thrown from the shore a weight would have been attached. We can only account for its absence by supposing the murderer to have neglected the precaution of supplying himself with it before pushing off. In the act of consigning the corpse to the water, he would unquestionably have noticed his oversight; but then no remedy would have been at hand. Any risk would have been preferred to a return to that accursed shore. Having rid himself of his ghastly charge, the murderer would have hastened to the city. There, at some obscure wharf, he would have leaped on land. But the boat﻿—would he have secured it? He would have been in too great haste for such things as securing a boat. Moreover, in fastening it to the wharf, he would have felt as if securing evidence against himself. His natural thought would have been to cast from him, as far as possible, all that had held connection with his crime. He would not only have fled from the wharf, but he would not have permitted *the boat* to remain. Assuredly he would have cast it adrift. Let us pursue our fancies.﻿—In the morning, the wretch is stricken with unutterable horror at finding that the boat has been picked up and detained at a locality which he is in the daily habit of frequenting﻿—at a locality, perhaps, which his duty compels him to frequent. The next night, *without daring to ask for the rudder*, he removes it. Now *where* is that rudderless boat? Let it be one of our first purposes to discover. With the first glimpse we obtain of it, the dawn of our success shall begin. This boat shall guide us, with a rapidity which will surprise even ourselves, to him who employed it in the midnight of the fatal Sabbath. Corroboration will rise upon corroboration, and the murderer will be traced.”

「而我们有什么手段达到真？我们会发现这些手段随着进行而增多、而清晰起来。让我们把第一次私奔那桩事筛到底。让我们弄清『那位军官』的全部历史，连同他此刻的境况，和他恰在凶杀时期的行踪。让我们把投给晚报的各封信细细互相比对——那几封信的目的在给*一伙*栽罪。这既办了，再把这些信——就文体与手迹两方面——同先前投给晨报、那样激昂地坚持梅奈有罪的那些信比对。这一切既办了，再把这些形形色色的信同那军官已知的手迹比对。让我们竭力借对德吕克太太和她孩子们的反复追问，也借对公共马车夫瓦朗斯的反复追问，弄清那『深色脸膛的人』的相貌与举止的更多一点。巧妙地引导的问话，不会不从这些人里的一部分问出关于这一要点（或别的要点）的消息——那消息这些人自己也许还不知道自己握有。而此刻让我们去追那只船——驳船水手在六月二十三日星期一早晨捡起的那只，它在尸体被发现之前的某个时期被从驳船事务所取走，值班官员不知情，*又没有舵*。凭着适当的谨慎与坚韧，我们将必然追到这只船；因为不但捡它的水手能认出它，而且*舵就在手边*。一只帆船的舵，不会被一个心里全然安宁的人丢下不要，也不问一声。这里容我停一停，插进一个问题。这只船的捡得，没有*登过广告*。它被一声不响地送到驳船事务所，又一声不响地被取走。但它的主人或雇它的人——在星期二早晨那样早的时期，他*怎么会*不经广告之助，便得知星期一捡起的船的所在——除非我们设想某种同*海军*的关系——某种个人的、常设的关系，通着它的细小的利害，它那些鸡毛蒜皮的本地消息？

[For reasons which we shall not specify, but which to many readers will appear obvious, we have taken the liberty of here omitting, from the MSS. placed in our hands, such portion as details the *following up* of the apparently slight clue obtained by Dupin. We feel it advisable only to state, in brief, that the result desired was brought to pass; and that the Prefect fulfilled punctually, although with reluctance, the terms of his compact with the Chevalier. Mr. Poe’s article concludes with the following words. —﻿Eds.50]

It will be understood that I speak of coincidences and *no more*. What I have said above upon this topic must suffice. In my own heart there dwells no faith in praeternature. That Nature and its God are two, no man who thinks, will deny. That the latter, creating the former, can, at will, control or modify it, is also unquestionable. I say “at will;” for the question is of will, and not, as the insanity of logic has assumed, of power. It is not that the Deity *cannot* modify his laws, but that we insult him in imagining a possible necessity for modification. In their origin these laws were fashioned to embrace *all* contingencies which *could* lie in the Future. With God all is *Now*.

I repeat, then, that I speak of these things only as of coincidences. And farther: in what I relate it will be seen that between the fate of the unhappy Mary Cecilia Rogers, so far as that fate is known, and the fate of one Marie Rogêt up to a certain epoch in her history, there has existed a parallel in the contemplation of whose wonderful exactitude the reason becomes embarrassed. I say all this will be seen. But let it not for a moment be supposed that, in proceeding with the sad narrative of Marie from the epoch just mentioned, and in tracing to its dénouement the mystery which enshrouded her, it is my covert design to hint at an extension of the parallel, or even to suggest that the measures adopted in Paris for the discovery of the assassin of a grisette, or measures founded in any similar ratiocination, would produce any similar result.

「说到那孤独的凶手把他的重负拖向岸边，我已经提示过他*借一只船*之助的可能。此刻我们要明白：玛丽·罗热*正是*从一只船上被抛下的。这本是自然的事。尸体不能托给岸边的浅水。被害人背上与肩上那些特殊的印记，诉说着一条船的底肋。尸体被发现没有系重物，也佐证这个观念。倘若从岸上抛的，会系上重物。它缺席，我们只能这样解释：假定那凶手在撑离之前，疏忽了备下重物的预防。在把尸体付给水的行动里，他无疑会察觉他的疏忽；但那时解救已不在手。任何风险他都会宁取，而不回到那该诅咒的岸边。既已脱掉他那怕人的重负，那凶手会赶回城里去。在那里，在某个冷僻的码头，他会跳上岸。但那只船——他会把它拴牢吗？他为拴船这类事忙得太急。况且把它拴在码头上，他会觉得仿佛在系住不利于自己的证据。他自然的念头会是把一切同他的罪有过牵连的东西，尽量远远抛开。他不但会逃离那码头，而且不会容许*那只船*留下。无疑他会把它放走随水漂去。让我们追我们的幻想。——早晨，那恶棍发觉那只船被捡起、扣在一个他每日惯常出入的地方——或许在一个他的职务迫使他出入的地方，一阵无可言说的恐怖把他击中。第二夜，*不敢去讨那只舵*，他把船取走了。此刻*那只没舵的船*在哪里？把它找出来，当作我们头一个目标。我们对它得到第一瞥的时光，我们成功的黎明便开始。这只船将以连我们自己都要吃惊的速度，引导我们到那在致命的安息日的午夜雇它的人那里。佐证将在佐证上叠起，凶手将被追到。」

===Original===

For, in respect to the latter branch of the supposition, it should be considered that the most trifling variation in the facts of the two cases might give rise to the most important miscalculations, by diverting thoroughly the two courses of events; very much as, in arithmetic, an error which, in its own individuality, may be inappreciable, produces, at length, by dint of multiplication at all points of the process, a result enormously at variance with truth. And, in regard to the former branch, we must not fail to hold in view that the very Calculus of Probabilities to which I have referred, forbids all idea of the extension of the parallel﻿—forbids it with a positiveness strong and decided just in proportion as this parallel has already been long-drawn and exact. This is one of those anomalous propositions which, seemingly appealing to thought altogether apart from the mathematical, is yet one which only the mathematician can fully entertain. Nothing, for example, is more difficult than to convince the merely general reader that the fact of sixes having been thrown twice in succession by a player at dice, is sufficient cause for betting the largest odds that sixes will not be thrown in the third attempt. A suggestion to this effect is usually rejected by the intellect at once. It does not appear that the two throws which have been completed, and which lie now absolutely in the Past, can have influence upon the throw which exists only in the Future. The chance for throwing sixes seems to be precisely as it was at any ordinary time﻿—that is to say, subject only to the influence of the various other throws which may be made by the dice. And this is a reflection which appears so exceedingly obvious that attempts to controvert it are received more frequently with a derisive smile than with anything like respectful attention. The error here involved﻿—a gross error redolent of mischief﻿—I cannot pretend to expose within the limits assigned me at present; and with the philosophical it needs no exposure. It may be sufficient here to say that it forms one of an infinite series of mistakes which arise in the path of Reason through her propensity for seeking truth *in detail*.

===Chinese===

[出于不便言明的缘由——它对许多读者将显得不言自明——我们擅自从交到我们手里的手稿中，略去了杜宾追索那条表面轻微的线索的经过部分。我们只觉得宜于简短交代：期望的结果已然达成；总监虽然不情愿，却分毫不爽地履行了他同这位骑士立约的条款。坡先生的文章以下面这些话作结。——编者〔50〕]

要明白：我说的是巧合，*仅止于巧合*。我在这题目上说过的话，说尽也够了。我自己心里住着对超自然的信。自然与它的神是两个，没有一个思想着的人会否认。后者既创造了前者，便能随意控制或改变它，这同样无可置疑。我说「随意」；因为问题在意志，不像逻辑的癫狂所假定的，在能力。并非神*不能*改变他的律法，而是我们设想改变之可能有此必要，是在羞辱他。这些律法在起源上被造成，为的是把*能够*躺在未来里的一切偶然包进去。在神，一切都是*现在*。

我于是再说一遍：我说这些事，单把它们当作巧合说。而且：在我叙述的东西里，将可以看到：在不幸的玛丽·塞西拉·罗杰斯的命运——就它被知道的程度而言——与玛丽·罗热到她历史里某一纪元为止的命运之间，存在过一种平行，那平行之精确得可惊，一想之下理性便窘住了。我说，这一切将可以看到。但切莫有一刻设想：我继续写玛丽的伤心叙述、从方才说的那个纪元起，并追那笼罩着她的谜到它的结局，是暗地里示意这平行会延伸下去，甚或暗示：在巴黎为发现一个灰衣女工的凶手而采用的措施，或建立在任何类似推理之上的措施，会产生任何类似的结果。

因为，就这设想的第二支而言，应当考虑：两桩案子的情形里最微末的一点变动，便可能引起最重要的误算，把两条事件的进程整个岔开；正如在算术里，一个就其自身而言无从察觉的错，靠它在全程每一点上的相乘，终于产出同真理相去极远的结果。而就这设想的第一支而言，我们必须不忘：我所援引的那概率演算本身，禁止平行延伸的一切念头——禁止之坚决、之果断，恰同这平行已经拉得又长又准的程度成正比。这是那些反常的命题之一：看似向完全离开数学的思想呼吁，却唯独数学家能完全领会。比如，没有比说服仅仅寻常的读者更难的事：掷骰子的人接连两次掷出六点，这事实已足以叫人押最大的赌注，赌第三回掷不出六点。这一类的提示通常立刻被智力拒绝。似乎已完成的、如今绝对躺在过去里的两掷，不能对只存在于未来里的那一掷有影响。掷出六点的机会，看上去恰恰同任何寻常时候一样——就是说，只受骰子可能掷出的其他各掷的影响。而这是一种显得极其显豁的回想，以致驳斥它的企图，多半只换得一声讥笑，而得不到任何近乎恭敬的注意。这里牵涉的错——一种酝酿着祸害的粗错——我不能假装在此刻划给我的界限里揭破它；在哲人那里，它无须揭破。这里说这么一句尽够：它构成那无限系列的错误之一——那些错误在理性的路上滋生，由于她*在细节里*寻真的癖性。

## The Pit and the Pendulum / 深坑与钟摆
===Original===
