In about a month afterwards he paid us another visit, and found us occupied very nearly as before. He took a pipe and a chair and entered into some ordinary conversation. At length I said:

“Well, but G﻿—﻿—, what of the purloined letter? I presume you have at last made up your mind that there is no such thing as overreaching the Minister?”

“Confound him, say I﻿—yes; I made the reexamination, however, as Dupin suggested﻿—but it was all labor lost, as I knew it would be.”

“How much was the reward offered, did you say?” asked Dupin.

===Chinese===

「当然；包裹邮包我们一件件拆过；书不但每一本都打开，每一卷还一页一页翻过，不肯像我们有些警官的时兴做法那样，只把书抖一抖就算了。我们还用最精确的量法，把每一本书皮的厚薄量过，对每一本又施以显微镜最苛刻的审视。装订若近期动过手，那事实要逃过观察是万万不能的。有五六卷刚从装订匠手里下来的书，我们用针顺着书脊纵向小心探过。」

「地毯底下的地板你查过？」

「毫无疑问。地毯全揭起来，木板用显微镜验过。」

「墙上的纸呢？」

「验了。」

「地窖你看过了？」

「看过了。」

「那么，」我说，「你是一直算错了账，信并不*在*宅子里，不像你设想的那样。」

「这一点我怕你说得对，」总监说。「那么现在，杜宾，你劝我怎么办？」

「把宅子再彻底查一遍。」

「那绝对多余，」G——答。「我呼吸的把握有多大，信不在府里的把握就有多大。」

「我没有更好的主意给你了，」杜宾说。「你自然有一份信的精确描述喽？」

「哦，有的！」——说到这里，总监掏出一本记事簿，把失踪文件的内里、尤其是外表的形貌，照着念了一遍，细到极处。这份描述念完不久，他便告辞走了，那副意气消沉的样子，比这位好先生以往给我的印象还要彻底。

大约一个月之后，他又来拜访我们一趟，见我们照旧干着老营生。他拿了一只烟斗一把椅子，扯了些寻常的话。末了我开口说：

「呃，可是G——，那封失窃的信怎么样了？想必你到底认了命：要占部长的上风，天底下没有这么一回事吧？」

「这坏东西，我说一声——不错；不过我还是照杜宾的话把宅子重查了一遍——可是全然白费力气，正如我早知道会是的那样。」

「你说悬赏多少来着？」杜宾问。

===Original===

“Why, a very great deal﻿—a *very* liberal reward﻿—I don’t like to say how much, precisely; but one thing I *will* say, that I wouldn’t mind giving my individual check for fifty thousand francs to anyone who could obtain me that letter. The fact is, it is becoming of more and more importance every day; and the reward has been lately doubled. If it were trebled, however, I could do no more than I have done.”

“Why, yes,” said Dupin, drawlingly, between the whiffs of his meerschaum, “I really﻿—think, G﻿—﻿—, you have not exerted yourself﻿—to the utmost in this matter. You might﻿—do a little more, I think, eh?”

“How?﻿—in what way?”

“Why﻿—puff, puff﻿—you might﻿—puff, puff﻿—employ counsel in the matter, eh?﻿—puff, puff, puff. Do you remember the story they tell of Abernethy?”

“No; hang Abernethy!”

“To be sure! hang him and welcome. But, once upon a time, a certain rich miser conceived the design of sponging upon this Abernethy for a medical opinion. Getting up, for this purpose, an ordinary conversation in a private company, he insinuated his case to the physician, as that of an imaginary individual.

“ ‘We will suppose,’ said the miser, ‘that his symptoms are such and such; now, doctor, what would *you* have directed him to take?’

“ ‘Take!’ said Abernethy, ‘why, take *advice*, to be sure.’ ”

“But,” said the Prefect, a little discomposed, “*I* am *perfectly* willing to take advice, and to pay for it. I would *really* give fifty thousand francs to anyone who would aid me in the matter.”

“In that case,” replied Dupin, opening a drawer, and producing a checkbook, “you may as well fill me up a check for the amount mentioned. When you have signed it, I will hand you the letter.”

===Chinese===

「呃，大得很——*很*慷慨的赏格——确切多少我不爱说；可有一点我*要*说：谁要能给我弄到那封信，我并不介意亲手开一张五万法郎的支票给他。实情是，它一天比一天要紧起来；赏格近来已加了一倍。纵使再加一倍，我能做到的也不过做到过的这些。」

「呃，是啊，」杜宾拖长了调子说，在几口海泡石的烟之间，「我真——觉得，G——，这件事上你还没有——使出全力来。你本可以——再稍许多做一点，我想，呃？」

「怎么？——从哪儿做起？」

「呃——噗，噗——你本可以——噗，噗——在这件事上请个参谋，呃？——噗，噗，噗。他们讲的阿伯内西（Abernethy）的那个故事你记得吗？」

「不记得；让阿伯内西见鬼去吧！」

「当然！让他见鬼，多多欢迎。可是，从前有个阔气的吝啬鬼，起意要蹭这位阿伯内西白问他一个医学意见。为这个目的，他在一个私人的小聚会上攀起一场寻常的闲谈，把自己的病情拐弯抹角地透露给医生，只说是某个假想中的人。

「『我们假定，』吝啬鬼说，『他症状如此这般；那么大夫，*你*会吩咐他吃点什么？』

「『吃！』阿伯内西说，『呃，自然是去*请教*喽。』」

「可是，」总监说，有点不自在，「*我*可是*顶*愿意请教、也愿意花钱的。谁肯在这件事上帮我，我*真*愿意给他五万法郎。」

「要是那样，」杜宾答，一面拉开一只抽屉，取出一个支票簿来，「你不妨照提过的数目给我填一张支票。等你签了字，我就把信交给你。」

===Original===

I was astounded. The Prefect appeared absolutely thunder-stricken. For some minutes he remained speechless and motionless, looking incredulously at my friend with open mouth, and eyes that seemed starting from their sockets; then, apparently recovering himself in some measure, he seized a pen, and after several pauses and vacant stares, finally filled up and signed a check for fifty thousand francs, and handed it across the table to Dupin. The latter examined it carefully and deposited it in his pocketbook; then, unlocking an escritoire, took thence a letter and gave it to the Prefect. This functionary grasped it in a perfect agony of joy, opened it with a trembling hand, cast a rapid glance at its contents, and then, scrambling and struggling to the door, rushed at length unceremoniously from the room and from the house, without having uttered a syllable since Dupin had requested him to fill up the check.

When he had gone, my friend entered into some explanations.

“The Parisian police,” he said, “are exceedingly able in their way. They are persevering, ingenious, cunning, and thoroughly versed in the knowledge which their duties seem chiefly to demand. Thus, when G﻿—﻿— detailed to us his mode of searching the premises at the Hotel D﻿—﻿—, I felt entire confidence in his having made a satisfactory investigation﻿—so far as his labors extended.”

“So far as his labors extended?” said I.

“Yes,” said Dupin. “The measures adopted were not only the best of their kind, but carried out to absolute perfection. Had the letter been deposited within the range of their search, these fellows would, beyond a question, have found it.”

I merely laughed﻿—but he seemed quite serious in all that he said.

===Chinese===

我惊呆了。总监的模样简直是遭了雷殛。有几分钟他一言不发，一动不动，张着嘴，眼睛像要从眼窝里迸出来，一脸不信地望着我的朋友；随后，看样子多少缓过了神，他抓起一支笔，几番停笔发怔之后，终于填好并签了一张五万法郎的支票，隔着桌子递给杜宾。后者仔细验过，收进皮夹；然后开开一口写字柜，从里面取出一封信，交给总监。这位大人一把攥住它，欢喜得浑身发痛，手抖着把它拆开，对信里的内容只匆匆一瞥，接着便连滚带爬地奔向门口，末了毫无礼数地冲出屋子冲出宅门——自从杜宾请他填支票那一刻起，他没有吐过一个音节。

他走了以后，我的朋友作了解释。

「巴黎警察，」他说，「在他们那一行里是极有本事的。他们坚韧、机灵、狡黠，对职分似乎主要要求的那种知识，烂熟于心。所以，当G——把他搜查D——府邸的路数细细讲给我们的时候，我完全相信他做了一次令人满意的搜查——在他力所能及的范围之内。」

「在他力所能及的范围之内？」我说。

「对，」杜宾说。「采用的手段不但是同类手段里最好的，而且执行得十足完美。信若藏在他们搜查的范围之内，这些家伙毫无疑问会把它找到。」

我只笑了笑——可他说的每一句都像是极认真的。

===Original===

“The measures, then,” he continued, “were good in their kind, and well executed; their defect lay in their being inapplicable to the case, and to the man. A certain set of highly ingenious resources are, with the Prefect, a sort of Procrustean bed, to which he forcibly adapts his designs. But he perpetually errs by being too deep or too shallow for the matter in hand; and many a schoolboy is a better reasoner than he. I knew one about eight years of age, whose success at guessing in the game of ‘even and odd’ attracted universal admiration. This game is simple, and is played with marbles. One player holds in his hand a number of these toys, and demands of another whether that number is even or odd. If the guess is right, the guesser wins one; if wrong, he loses one. The boy to whom I allude won all the marbles of the school. Of course he had some principle of guessing; and this lay in mere observation and admeasurement of the astuteness of his opponents. For example, an arrant simpleton is his opponent, and, holding up his closed hand, asks, ‘are they even or odd?’ Our schoolboy replies, ‘odd,’ and loses; but upon the second trial he wins, for he then says to himself, ‘the simpleton had them even upon the first trial, and his amount of cunning is just sufficient to make him have them odd upon the second; I will therefore guess odd;’﻿—he guesses odd, and wins. Now, with a simpleton a degree above the first, he would have reasoned thus: ‘This fellow finds that in the first instance I guessed odd, and, in the second, he will propose to himself, upon the first impulse, a simple variation from even to odd, as did the first simpleton; but then a second thought will suggest that this is too simple a variation, and finally he will decide upon putting it even as before. I will therefore guess even;’﻿—he guesses even, and wins. Now this mode of reasoning in the schoolboy, whom his fellows termed ‘lucky,’﻿—what, in its last analysis, is it?”

“It is merely,” I said, “an identification of the reasoner’s intellect with that of his opponent.”

===Chinese===

「这么说来，」他接着说，「那些手段在它们那一类里是好的，执行得也好；它们的毛病在于用不上这桩案子，也用不上这个人。有一套极其机巧的手段，在这位总监手里，成了一种普罗克鲁斯特斯之床，他硬把他的盘算往床上安。可他老是出错：对手头的事情，他要么失之太深，要么失之太浅；多少个学童都比他会推理。我认识一个八岁上下的孩子，玩「单双」猜数百猜百中，博得众口一词的叹赏。这游戏简单，用的是石弹。一人把若干颗这种小玩意握在手里，要另一个人猜那数目是单是双。猜对了，猜的人赢一颗；猜错了，他输一颗。我说的这孩子赢遍了全校的石弹。他自然有一套猜的原则；那原则不过在于观察、量度对手的机敏。比方说，对手是个十足的小傻瓜，举起捏紧的手问：「是单还是双？」我们这位学童答「单」，输了；可第二回他赢，因为他这时对自己说：「傻瓜头一回放的是双，他那点狡狯刚好够他第二回改出个单来；所以这回我猜单；」——他猜单，赢了。换了比头一个高一等的傻瓜，他就会这样推：「这家伙看到头一回我猜了单，第二回他凭头一个冲动，会给自己定下一个从双到单的简单变化，跟头一个傻瓜一样；可随后再一想，他就觉得这变化太简单了，末了他会决定照旧放双。所以我猜双；」——他猜双，赢了。如今，这个被同学们唤作「福气」的学童的推理方式，追到根子上，究竟是什么？」

「不过是，」我说，「把推理者的智力同对手的智力合为一体罢了。」

===Original===

“It is,” said Dupin; “and, upon inquiring of the boy by what means he effected the *thorough* identification in which his success consisted, I received answer as follows: ‘When I wish to find out how wise, or how stupid, or how good, or how wicked is anyone, or what are his thoughts at the moment, I fashion the expression of my face, as accurately as possible, in accordance with the expression of his, and then wait to see what thoughts or sentiments arise in my mind or heart, as if to match or correspond with the expression.’ This response of the schoolboy lies at the bottom of all the spurious profundity which has been attributed to Rochefoucault, to La Bougive, to Machiavelli, and to Campanella.”

“And the identification,” I said, “of the reasoner’s intellect with that of his opponent, depends, if I understand you aright, upon the accuracy with which the opponent’s intellect is admeasured.”

===Chinese===

「是这话，」杜宾说；「我问那孩子，他是靠什么做到那种*十足*的同一——他的成功正在这种同一里——得到这样的回答：『我想知道一个人多聪明、多蠢、多好、多坏，或者他此刻想的是什么，我就把我脸上的神情，尽可能准确地做得同他脸上的神情一样，然后等着看我脑子里、心口里会浮起什么念头、什么情绪，仿佛要同那神情相配、相应似的。』这位学童的答话，正是一切冒牌的深刻所从出的根子——那些深刻，被归在罗什富科（Rochefoucault）、拉布吉（La Bougive）、马基雅维利（Machiavelli）和坎帕内拉（Campanella）的名下。」

「而推理者的智力同对手智力的这种同一，」我说，「如果我理解得不错，靠的是量度对手智力时的精确。」

===Original===

“For its practical value it depends upon this,” replied Dupin; “and the Prefect and his cohort fail so frequently, first, by default of this identification, and, secondly, by ill-admeasurement, or rather through non-admeasurement, of the intellect with which they are engaged. They consider only their *own* ideas of ingenuity; and, in searching for anything hidden, advert only to the modes in which *they* would have hidden it. They are right in this much﻿—that their own ingenuity is a faithful representative of that of *the mass*; but when the cunning of the individual felon is diverse in character from their own, the felon foils them, of course. This always happens when it is above their own, and very usually when it is below. They have no variation of principle in their investigations; at best, when urged by some unusual emergency﻿—by some extraordinary reward﻿—they extend or exaggerate their old modes of *practice*, without touching their principles. What, for example, in this case of D﻿—﻿—, has been done to vary the principle of action? What is all this boring, and probing, and sounding, and scrutinizing with the microscope and dividing the surface of the building into registered square inches﻿—what is it all but an exaggeration *of the application* of the one principle or set of principles of search, which are based upon the one set of notions regarding human ingenuity, to which the Prefect, in the long routine of his duty, has been accustomed? Do you not see he has taken it for granted that all men proceed to conceal a letter﻿—not exactly in a gimlet hole bored in a chair-leg﻿—but, at least, in some out-of-the-way hole or corner suggested by the same tenor of thought which would urge a man to secrete a letter in a gimlet-hole bored in a chair-leg?

===Chinese===

「论实际的效用，它正靠这个，」杜宾答；「总监和他那一党所以屡屡失败，第一，缺了这种同一，第二，量度得不好，或者简直说，没有量度——对他们所交手的那种智力。他们只考虑*自己*那套机巧观；搜藏东西的时候，只想到*他们自己*会拿来藏东西的方式。在这一点上他们是对的——他们自己的机巧，确是*大众*机巧的忠实代表；可一旦哪个犯人的狡狯在品性上同他们的不同，那犯人自然就逃过他们。狡狯高出他们的时候一定如此，低过他们的时候也多半如此。他们的侦查在原则上没有变化；至多，被非常的急务——非常的赏格——催逼起来的时候，把老一套的*做法*伸延放大，原则却碰也不碰。比如这桩D——的案子，为了变化行动的原则，做了什么呢？又是钻孔，又是探查，又是敲击，又是用显微镜细察，又是把房子的表面分成登记在册的平方寸——这一切，除了把那一条搜查原则、或那一组搜查原则的*应用*放大之外，还算什么？而那一条或那一组原则，又是建立在那一套关于人类机巧的观念上的——总监在长年的公务循规里，惯熟的正是那一套。你看不见吗：他把这一点当成了想当然——天下人藏一封信，总要走同一条老路——纵不恰恰藏进椅腿上钻出的锥孔，至少也要藏进什么僻远的洞或角里，而这洞角的暗示，正来自那同一条思路：就是那条会叫人把信藏进椅腿锥孔的思路。

===Original===

And do you not see also, that such recherchés nooks for concealment are adapted only for ordinary occasions, and would be adopted only by ordinary intellects; for, in all cases of concealment, a disposal of the article concealed﻿—a disposal of it in this recherché manner﻿—is, in the very first instance, presumable and presumed; and thus its discovery depends, not at all upon the acumen, but altogether upon the mere care, patience, and determination of the seekers; and where the case is of importance﻿—or, what amounts to the same thing in the political eyes, when the reward is of magnitude﻿—the qualities in question have *never* been known to fail. You will now understand what I meant in suggesting that, had the purloined letter been hidden anywhere within the limits of the Prefect’s examination﻿—in other words, had the principle of its concealment been comprehended within the principles of the Prefect﻿—its discovery would have been a matter altogether beyond question. This functionary, however, has been thoroughly mystified; and the remote source of his defeat lies in the supposition that the Minister is a fool, because he has acquired renown as a poet. All fools are poets; this the Prefect *feels*; and he is merely guilty of a *non distributio medii* in thence inferring that all poets are fools.”

“But is this really the poet?” I asked. “There are two brothers, I know; and both have attained reputation in letters. The Minister I believe has written learnedly on the Differential Calculus. He is a mathematician, and no poet.”

“You are mistaken; I know him well; he is both. As poet *and* mathematician, he would reason well; as mere mathematician, he could not have reasoned at all, and thus would have been at the mercy of the Prefect.”

“You surprise me,” I said, “by these opinions, which have been contradicted by the voice of the world. You do not mean to set at naught the well-digested idea of centuries. The mathematical reason has long been regarded as *the* reason *par excellence*.”

===Chinese===

「你也看不见吗：这种别出心裁的藏匿角落，只合寻常的场合用，也只会有寻常的智力去用；因为凡藏匿的事例，把东西处置起来——用这种别出心裁的方式处置——在头一个环节上就是可推想、也被推想到了的；于是它的被发现，根本不靠眼力，全靠搜查者的细心、耐心和决心；而在案情要紧的地方——或者在政治的眼光看来是一回事的地方，赏格巨大的时候——这些品质*从来不曾*失败过。如今你该明白我的意思了：我所以说，失窃的信倘若藏在总监查验的范围以内的任何地方——换句话说，它藏匿的原则倘若包容在总监的原则之内——它的被发现就该是十拿九稳的事。可是这位大人被彻头彻尾地蒙住了；他败因的远源，在于他设想部长是个傻瓜，因为部长以诗人得名。傻瓜都是诗人；这一点总监*觉得*；由此推论诗人都是傻瓜，他就只犯了一个*中项不周延*（non distributio medii）的错。」

「可这位当真是诗人吗？」我问。「我知道他们是两兄弟；两人都在文墨里得了名声。我想部长写过论微分学的学问文章。他是数学家，不是诗人。」

「你错了；我很了解他；他两者都是。既能做诗人*又*能做数学家，他推理便推理得好；单是数学家，他就根本推不动，也就只好听凭总监处置了。」

「你这番议论叫我吃惊，」我说，「世人的公论跟它相反。你未必敢把几个世纪消化成熟的定见一脚踢开。数学推理长久以来一直被看作*卓越*的推理。」

===Original===

“ ‘*Il y a à parièr*,’ ” replied Dupin, quoting from Chamfort, “ ‘*que toute idée publique, toute convention reçue est une sottise, car elle a convenue au plus grand nombre.*’ The mathematicians, I grant you, have done their best to promulgate the popular error to which you allude, and which is none the less an error for its promulgation as truth. With an art worthy a better cause, for example, they have insinuated the term ‘analysis’ into application to algebra. The French are the originators of this particular deception; but if a term is of any importance﻿—if words derive any value from applicability﻿—then ‘analysis’ conveys ‘algebra’ about as much as, in Latin, ‘*ambitus*’ implies ‘ambition,’ ‘*religio*’ ‘religion,’ or ‘*homines honesti*’ a set of *honorable* men.”

“You have a quarrel on hand, I see,” said I, “with some of the algebraists of Paris; but proceed.”

===Chinese===

「*Il y a à parièr*（不妨打赌），」杜宾引尚福尔（Chamfort）的话答道，「*que toute idée publique, toute convention reçue est une sottise, car elle a convenue au plus grand nombre*（一切公众的观念，一切被接受的成规，都是一种愚蠢，因为它投合了最大多数的人）。数学家们，我承认，已经尽力把你指的那种流行的谬见散布开来；谬见尽管被当成真理散布，终究还是谬见。他们使出一种本值得更好的目标的巧艺，比如，把「分析」这个字眼悄悄塞给代数。这一手特别的骗人，法国人是始作俑者；可倘若字眼真有一点要紧——倘若字眼的价值果真得自它的贴切——那么「分析」之于「代数」所传达的，恰如拉丁语里 *ambitus*（贿选）之于「野心」、*religio*（迷信）之于「宗教」、或 *homines honesti*（体面人）之于一群*正直*的人，传达得一样多。」

「我看你手上要同巴黎的某些代数学家结怨了，」我说，「不过请讲下去。」

===Original===

“I dispute the availability, and thus the value, of that reason which is cultivated in any especial form other than the abstractly logical. I dispute, in particular, the reason educed by mathematical study. The mathematics are the science of form and quantity; mathematical reasoning is merely logic applied to observation upon form and quantity. The great error lies in supposing that even the truths of what is called *pure* algebra, are abstract or general truths. And this error is so egregious that I am confounded at the universality with which it has been received. Mathematical axioms are not axioms of general truth. What is true of *relation*﻿—of form and quantity﻿—is often grossly false in regard to morals, for example. In this latter science it is very usually *un*true that the aggregated parts are equal to the whole. In chemistry also the axiom fails. In the consideration of motive it fails; for two motives, each of a given value, have not, necessarily, a value when united, equal to the sum of their values apart. There are numerous other mathematical truths which are only truths within the limits of *relation*. But the mathematician argues, from his *finite truths*, through habit, as if they were of an absolutely general applicability﻿—as the world indeed imagines them to be. Bryant, in his very learned *Mythology*, mentions an analogous source of error, when he says that ‘although the Pagan fables are not believed, yet we forget ourselves continually, and make inferences from them as existing realities.’ With the algebraists, however, who are Pagans themselves, the ‘Pagan fables’ *are* believed, and the inferences are made, not so much through lapse of memory, as through an unaccountable addling of the brains. In short, I never yet encountered the mere mathematician who could be trusted out of equal roots, or one who did not clandestinely hold it as a point of his faith that x² + px was absolutely and unconditionally equal to q. Say to one of these gentlemen, by way of experiment, if you please, that you believe occasions may occur where x² + px is *not* altogether equal to q, and, having made him understand what you mean, get out of his reach as speedily as convenient, for, beyond doubt, he will endeavor to knock you down.

===Chinese===

「凡是在抽象的逻辑之外、用任何特殊形式培养出来的推理，我都争辩它无用，因而无价值。数学研究养出的推理，我尤其争辩。数学是形与量的科学；数学推理不过是逻辑施用于形与量上的观察。大错在于设想：连所谓*纯粹*代数的真理，也是抽象的或普遍的真理。这错大得离谱，它被接受的普遍程度叫我错愕。数学公理并不是普遍真理的公理。*关系*上——形与量上——为真的，比如在道德上，往往就大错特错。在这后一门科学里，「聚合的部分等于全体」通常就*不*成立。化学里这条公理也失效。考量动机时它也失效；因为两个动机，各有一定价值，合起来的时候，其价值未必等于分开时的价值之和。还有许多别的数学真理，只在*关系*的界限之内是真理。可数学家出于习惯，偏从他的*有限真理*立论，仿佛它们有绝对普遍的适用性——世人也的确把它们想象成那样。布莱恩特（Bryant）在他那部极有学问的《神话学》里，提过一个同类的错误来源，他说：「异教的寓言虽已无人相信，我们却还是不断忘乎所以，把它们当作实存之物，从里面作出推论。」可代数学家自己就是异教徒，「异教的寓言」他们是*信*的；推论之所以照做，倒不是记性不好，而是脑子被一种说不清道理的糊涂搅昏了。总而言之，纯粹的数学家，出了「等根」还能信得过的，我一个也不曾遇到过；把「x² + px 绝对无条件地等于 q」偷偷奉作信条的，也一个不曾缺过。你不妨做个试验，对这些先生当中随便哪一位说，你认为可能有这样的场合，那里 x² + px *并不*全然等于 q；等你把意思给他讲明白，就赶紧退到他够不着的地方去，自便；因为毫无疑问，他要想法子把你打倒。

===Original===

“I mean to say,” continued Dupin, while I merely laughed at his last observations, “that if the Minister had been no more than a mathematician, the Prefect would have been under no necessity of giving me this check. I know him, however, as both mathematician and poet, and my measures were adapted to his capacity, with reference to the circumstances by which he was surrounded. I knew him as a courtier, too, and as a bold *intriguant*. Such a man, I considered, could not fail to be aware of the ordinary policial modes of action. He could not have failed to anticipate﻿—and events have proved that he did not fail to anticipate﻿—the waylayings to which he was subjected. He must have foreseen, I reflected, the secret investigations of his premises. His frequent absences from home at night, which were hailed by the Prefect as certain aids to his success, I regarded only as *ruses*, to afford opportunity for thorough search to the police, and thus the sooner to impress them with the conviction to which G﻿—﻿—, in fact, did finally arrive﻿—the conviction that the letter was not upon the premises. I felt, also, that the whole train of thought, which I was at some pains in detailing to you just now, concerning the invariable principle of policial action in searches for articles concealed﻿—I felt that this whole train of thought would necessarily pass through the mind of the Minister. It would imperatively lead him to despise all the ordinary *nooks* of concealment. *He* could not, I reflected, be so weak as not to see that the most intricate and remote recess of his hotel would be as open as his commonest closets to the eyes, to the probes, to the gimlets, and to the microscopes of the Prefect. I saw, in fine, that he would be driven, as a matter of course, to *simplicity*, if not deliberately induced to it as a matter of choice. You will remember, perhaps, how desperately the Prefect laughed when I suggested, upon our first interview, that it was just possible this mystery troubled him so much on account of its being so *very* self-evident.”

“Yes,” said I, “I remember his merriment well. I really thought he would have fallen into convulsions.”

===Chinese===

「我是想说，」杜宾接着说，我对他方才那番话只付之一笑，「部长倘若单是一个数学家，总监就犯不着给我这张支票了。然而我了解他，他既是数学家又是诗人，我的对策便对着他的能量量体裁衣，也参照他身周的情势。我还了解他是朝臣，是个大胆的*阴谋家*（intriguant）。这样的人，我料想，不会不知道警察寻常的行动路数。他不会不预先料到——事实已证明他不曾失于预料——他遭受的那些拦劫。他家的宅子有人暗中查究，我寻思，他必定预见到了。他夜里频频不在家，总监把这当作他成功的一定之助来欢迎；我却只看作*诡计*，好给警察腾出彻底搜查的机会，也从而叫他们更快地信服那个信念——G——事实上终于到达的信念：信不在宅子里。我又感到，方才我费了不少口舌向你细述的那整条思路——关于搜查藏物时警察行动那条一成不变的原则——我感到这整条思路必然也要从部长心里走过。它会断然引他去蔑视一切寻常的*藏匿*角落。他总不至于弱到看不出来，我寻思：他府邸里最曲折最偏僻的密处，在那双眼睛、那些探针、那些锥子、那架显微镜底下，会同他最寻常的壁橱一样敞开。末了我看明白了：事势会逼着他走向*简单*，即使不是他自己有意把它拣作上策。你也许还记得，头一回会面时我提出：这桩谜案所以这么搅扰他，说不定恰恰因为它*太*不言自明了；当时总监那阵笑得多么要死要活。」

「记得，」我说，「他那份开心我记得清清楚楚。我真当他要笑得抽起筋来。」

===Original===

“The material world,” continued Dupin, “abounds with very strict analogies to the immaterial; and thus some color of truth has been given to the rhetorical dogma, that metaphor, or simile, may be made to strengthen an argument, as well as to embellish a description. The principle of the *vis inertiae*, for example, seems to be identical in physics and metaphysics. It is not more true in the former, that a large body is with more difficulty set in motion than a smaller one, and that its subsequent *momentum* is commensurate with this difficulty, than it is, in the latter, that intellects of the vaster capacity, while more forcible, more constant, and more eventful in their movements than those of inferior grade, are yet the less readily moved, and more embarrassed and full of hesitation in the first few steps of their progress. Again: have you ever noticed which of the street signs, over the shop-doors, are the most attractive of attention?”

“I have never given the matter a thought,” I said.

“There is a game of puzzles,” he resumed, “which is played upon a map. One party playing requires another to find a given word﻿—the name of town, river, state or empire﻿—any word, in short, upon the motley and perplexed surface of the chart. A novice in the game generally seeks to embarrass his opponents by giving them the most minutely lettered names; but the adept selects such words as stretch, in large characters, from one end of the chart to the other. These, like the over-largely lettered signs and placards of the street, escape observation by dint of being excessively obvious; and here the physical oversight is precisely analogous with the moral inapprehension by which the intellect suffers to pass unnoticed those considerations which are too obtrusively and too palpably self-evident. But this is a point, it appears, somewhat above or beneath the understanding of the Prefect. He never once thought it probable, or possible, that the Minister had deposited the letter immediately beneath the nose of the whole world, by way of best preventing any portion of that world from perceiving it.

===Chinese===

「物质的世界，」杜宾接着说，「满是同非物质世界极其严格的类似；于是修辞学那句教条——隐喻或明喻可以拿来加固论证，正如可以拿来装点描摹——也染上了几分真理的颜色。比如*惯性力*（vis inertiae）的原理，在物理学与形而上学里似乎是同一的。在前者，大物体比小物体更难推动，它随后的*动量*同这困难相称；在后者，容量更浩大的智力，运动起来虽然比低一等的更有力、更恒久、更多后果，却更不容易发动，在进展的头几步里更窘迫、更踌躇——两边的真确程度并无二致。再说一遍：店铺门上那一类街招，哪种最惹眼，你可曾留意过？」

「这桩事我从未想过，」我说。

「有一种猜谜的游戏，」他接着说，「在地图上玩。玩的一方要另一方找出一个指定的词——城名、河名、国名或帝国的名字——总之，图上斑驳纷乱的表面上的随便哪个词。玩这游戏的新手，一般专挑字母印得最细琐的名字去为难对手；可是行家拣的，却是那些用大字从图的一端横贯到另一端的名字。这些词，像街上字写得过大的街招和告牌，正因其过分显豁，反倒逃过注意；这里，肉眼的失察，同心智的不觉察恰恰相仿——心智任那些思虑从眼前溜过无人注意，只因它们太露骨、太显豁地不言自明。不过这一点，看光景，多少在总监的理解之上，或者之下。他一次也不曾想到这可能、可想象：部长把信恰恰搁在全世界鼻子底下，正是为了叫这世界无论哪一部分都看不见它。

===Original===

“But the more I reflected upon the daring, dashing, and discriminating ingenuity of D﻿—﻿—; upon the fact that the document must always have been *at hand*, if he intended to use it to good purpose; and upon the decisive evidence, obtained by the Prefect, that it was not hidden within the limits of that dignitary’s ordinary search﻿—the more satisfied I became that, to conceal this letter, the Minister had resorted to the comprehensive and sagacious expedient of not attempting to conceal it at all.

“Full of these ideas, I prepared myself with a pair of green spectacles, and called one fine morning, quite by accident, at the Ministerial hotel. I found D﻿—﻿— at home, yawning, lounging, and dawdling, as usual, and pretending to be in the last extremity of ennui. He is, perhaps, the most really energetic human being now alive﻿—but that is only when nobody sees him.

“To be even with him, I complained of my weak eyes, and lamented the necessity of the spectacles, under cover of which I cautiously and thoroughly surveyed the whole apartment, while seemingly intent only upon the conversation of my host.

“I paid especial attention to a large writing-table near which he sat, and upon which lay confusedly, some miscellaneous letters and other papers, with one or two musical instruments and a few books. Here, however, after a long and very deliberate scrutiny, I saw nothing to excite particular suspicion.

“At length my eyes, in going the circuit of the room, fell upon a trumpery filigree card-rack of pasteboard, that hung dangling by a dirty blue ribbon, from a little brass knob just beneath the middle of the mantelpiece. In this rack, which had three or four compartments, were five or six visiting cards and a solitary letter. This last was much soiled and crumpled. It was torn nearly in two, across the middle﻿—as if a design, in the first instance, to tear it entirely up as worthless, had been altered, or stayed, in the second. It had a large black seal, bearing the D﻿—﻿— cipher *very* conspicuously, and was addressed, in a diminutive female hand, to D﻿—﻿—, the minister, himself. It was thrust carelessly, and even, as it seemed, contemptuously, into one of the uppermost divisions of the rack.

===Chinese===

「可是我越把D——那份大胆、闯劲、明辨的机巧细想；越想到那份文件倘若他真想把它派上好用场，就必须永远*在手边*；越想到总监取得的决定性证据：它没藏在那位大人寻常搜查的范围之内——我就越满意于一个结论：为了藏这封信，部长采用了那个包罗一切、睿智非常的权宜之计，索性不打算藏它。

「满怀这些念头，我备了一副绿眼镜，挑一个好天气的上午，装作全然出于偶然，到部长的府邸去拜访。我见D——在家，照他往常的样子打着哈欠，懒懒地歪着，拖拖沓沓，装出一副无聊到极顶的样子。他也许是当今世上精力最真正旺盛的人——不过那只在没人瞧见他的时候。

「为同他扯平，我抱怨眼睛不好，哀叹非戴眼镜不可；借着眼镜的遮掩，我把整间屋子谨慎而周详地巡视了一遍，表面上却只一心听主人谈话。

「我格外留意他坐在旁边的那张大写字桌，桌面上乱放着些杂七杂八的信件和别的纸，还有一两件乐器、几本书。可是这里，经过长久而极从容的审视，我没看见什么足以挑起特别疑心的东西。

「末了，我的眼睛绕屋子巡到一圈，落在一只华而不实的金银丝细工硬纸板名片架上；架子用一条脏兮兮的蓝丝带悬着，挂在壁炉架正中下方的一枚小铜钮上，摇摇晃晃。架上有三四个格子，里面插着五六张名片和孤零零的一封信。这封信脏污揉皱得厉害。它横着中间几乎被撕成两半——仿佛起先本想把它整个撕掉当作废纸，第二步又改了主意，或者缩了手。信上盖着一个大黑印，D——的花押字在上面*十分*触目；信封上的收信人是部长D——本人，笔迹纤小，是女性的手笔。它被漫不经心地、甚至看光景带着轻蔑地，插进了架子最上层的一格里。

===Original===

“No sooner had I glanced at this letter, than I concluded it to be that of which I was in search. To be sure, it was, to all appearance, radically different from the one of which the Prefect had read us so minute a description. Here the seal was large and black, with the D﻿—﻿— cipher; there it was small and red, with the ducal arms of the S﻿—﻿— family. Here, the address, to the Minister, diminutive and feminine; there the superscription, to a certain royal personage, was markedly bold and decided; the size alone formed a point of correspondence. But, then, the *radicalness* of these differences, which was excessive; the dirt; the soiled and torn condition of the paper, so inconsistent with the *true* methodical habits of D﻿—﻿—, and so suggestive of a design to delude the beholder into an idea of the worthlessness of the document;﻿—these things, together with the hyper-obtrusive situation of this document, full in the view of every visitor, and thus exactly in accordance with the conclusions to which I had previously arrived; these things, I say, were strongly corroborative of suspicion, in one who came with the intention to suspect.

“I protracted my visit as long as possible, and, while I maintained a most animated discussion with the Minister upon a topic which I knew well had never failed to interest and excite him, I kept my attention really riveted upon the letter. In this examination, I committed to memory its external appearance and arrangement in the rack; and also fell, at length, upon a discovery which set at rest whatever trivial doubt I might have entertained. In scrutinizing the edges of the paper, I observed them to be more *chafed* than seemed necessary. They presented the *broken* appearance which is manifested when a stiff paper, having been once folded and pressed with a folder, is refolded in a reversed direction, in the same creases or edges which had formed the original fold. This discovery was sufficient. It was clear to me that the letter had been turned, as a glove, inside out, redirected, and resealed. I bade the Minister good morning, and took my departure at once, leaving a gold snuffbox upon the table.

===Chinese===

「这封信我只瞥了一眼，便断定它正是我要搜寻的那封。诚然，看上去它同总监给我们念过细细描述的那封，根本不同。这边：印是大而黑的，带着D——的花押字；那边：印是小而红的，带S——家族的公爵纹章。这边：写给部长的地址，笔迹纤小，是女性手笔；那边：写给某位王室人物的封皮字样，分明大胆而果断；只有大小还成了对得上的一个点。然而，这些差异的*根本性*过了头；脏污；纸的又污又破的境况，同D——*真正*有条不紊的习惯全不相称，倒像存心叫看的人误信这份文件一文不值；——这些，连同这份文件那过分惹眼的安放，一字排开摆给每个访客看，因而同我先前达到的结论恰好一致；这些，我说，在一个存心起疑而来的人眼里，把疑心强有力地证实了。

「我把拜访拖得越久越好，同部长在一个话题上大谈特谈——我深知那话题从来不曾不叫他入迷、叫他兴奋——可我的注意力其实钉死在那封信上。这么察看之下，我把它的外表和它在架子上的位置记进了心里；末了，还撞上了一个发现，把我心里可能存过的一点微末疑团全然安顿下来。细审纸的边缘，我看出它们*磨损*得过了分。它们显出那种*折裂*的样子：一张硬纸折过一次、拿折纸夹压过之后，再照反方向、循着当初折痕所成的同样的折缝或折边重新折过时，就会显出的样子。这个发现尽够了。我明白：那封信给翻了个面，像手套翻出内里，重新写了地址，重新封了印。我向部长道了早安，立刻告辞，在桌上留下一只金鼻烟盒。

===Original===

“The next morning I called for the snuffbox, when we resumed, quite eagerly, the conversation of the preceding day. While thus engaged, however, a loud report, as if of a pistol, was heard immediately beneath the windows of the hotel, and was succeeded by a series of fearful screams, and the shoutings of a terrified mob. D﻿—﻿— rushed to a casement, threw it open, and looked out. In the meantime, I stepped to the card-rack, took the letter, put it in my pocket, and replaced it by a facsimile, (so far as regards externals,) which I had carefully prepared at my lodgings﻿—imitating the D﻿—﻿— cipher, very readily, by means of a seal formed of bread.

“The disturbance in the street had been occasioned by the frantic behavior of a man with a musket. He had fired it among a crowd of women and children. It proved, however, to have been without ball, and the fellow was suffered to go his way as a lunatic or a drunkard. When he had gone, D﻿—﻿— came from the window, whither I had followed him immediately upon securing the object in view. Soon afterwards I bade him farewell. The pretended lunatic was a man in my own pay.”

“But what purpose had you,” I asked, “in replacing the letter by a facsimile? Would it not have been better, at the first visit, to have seized it openly, and departed?”

===Chinese===

「第二天上午我登门取鼻烟盒，两人急切地接着前一天的谈话谈下去。可正当谈着，楼下宅子的窗户底下，轰地响了一声，像放了一枪，接着是一串骇人的尖叫，还有吓坏了的人群的喊嚷。D——奔到一扇窗前，把窗推开，朝外望。趁这工夫，我走到名片架前，取了信，揣进衣袋，又拿一封摹本放回原处——就外表而言——那是我先前在寓所里仔细备下的：D——的花押字，我用一枚面包做的印章，顺手之至地仿了出来。

「街上的骚乱，起因于一个带滑膛枪的男人的疯狂举动。他对着一堆女人和孩子开了枪。可是枪里原来是没装弹丸的，那家伙也就被当作疯子或醉汉，放他自去了。他走后，D——从窗口回来——我一得手，立刻跟着他到了窗前。随后不久我向他告辞。那个假疯子，是我出钱雇用的人。」

「可你拿摹本换下那封信，」我问，「图的是什么？头一回拜访的时候，公开把信抓到手就走，岂不更好？」

===Original===

“D﻿—﻿—,” replied Dupin, “is a desperate man, and a man of nerve. His hotel, too, is not without attendants devoted to his interests. Had I made the wild attempt you suggest, I might never have left the Ministerial presence alive. The good people of Paris might have heard of me no more. But I had an object apart from these considerations. You know my political prepossessions. In this matter, I act as a partisan of the lady concerned. For eighteen months the Minister has had her in his power. She has now him in hers﻿—since, being unaware that the letter is not in his possession, he will proceed with his exactions as if it was. Thus will he inevitably commit himself, at once, to his political destruction. His downfall, too, will not be more precipitate than awkward. It is all very well to talk about the *facilis descensus Averni*; but in all kinds of climbing, as Catalani said of singing, it is far more easy to get up than to come down. In the present instance I have no sympathy﻿—at least no pity﻿—for him who descends. He is that *monstrum horrendum*, an unprincipled man of genius. I confess, however, that I should like very well to know the precise character of his thoughts, when, being defied by her whom the Prefect terms ‘a certain personage’ he is reduced to opening the letter which I left for him in the card-rack.”

“How? did you put anything particular in it?”

“Why﻿—it did not seem altogether right to leave the interior blank﻿—that would have been insulting. D﻿—﻿—, at Vienna once, did me an evil turn, which I told him, quite good-humoredly, that I should remember. So, as I knew he would feel some curiosity in regard to the identity of the person who had outwitted him, I thought it a pity not to give him a clue. He is well acquainted with my MS., and I just copied into the middle of the blank sheet the words﻿—

“ ‘﻿—﻿— Un dessein si funeste,

S’il n’est digne d’Atrée, est digne de Thyeste.’

They are to be found in Crébillon’s *Atrée*.”

===Chinese===

「D——，」杜宾答，「是个铤而走险的人，也是有胆量的人。他的府邸里，也未必没有效忠他利益的家仆。我若照你那野主意行事，也许永远不会有活着离开部长跟前的那一天。巴黎的好人们也许从此再也听不见我的消息。可除开这些考虑，我另有一个目的。你知道我的政治偏向。这件事里，我是那位有关夫人的同党。十八个月来，部长把她捏在掌心。如今她把他捏在掌心了——因为他不知道信已不在他手中，还会当信在手中似的，继续他的需索。这样，他就必然立刻自投于政治上的毁灭。他的倒台，狼狈之甚，也决不下于急遽之速。说什么*facilis descensus Averni*（下坠艾弗尔努，一路容易），说得漂亮；可凡属攀高，正如卡塔拉尼（Catalani）论唱歌所说，上去远比下来容易。在眼下这件事里，对那个下坠的人，我没有同情——至少没有怜悯。他是那个*monstrum horrendum*（可怕的怪物）——一个没有原则的天才。不过我招认，我很想知道得确切：当那位被总监唤作「某位大人物」的她起而抗违他，他落到不得不去拆开我留给他在名片架里的那封信时，他心里的念头究竟是什么个成色。」

「怎么？你在里面放了什么特别的东西？」

「呃——里头全然空白地留下，似乎总不大对——那近乎侮辱。D——有一回在维也纳坑过我一下，我当时相当和气地告诉他，我会记着的。所以，我知道他对那个斗败了他的人究竟是谁，难免要起几分好奇，我想，不给他一点线索，未免可惜。他极熟我的笔迹，我便把这样的话抄进那张空白信纸的正中——

「——*Un dessein si funeste,*
*S'il n'est digne d'Atrée, est digne de Thyeste.*」
（——如此狠毒的图谋，
若不配阿特柔斯（Atrée），便配提厄斯忒斯（Thyeste）。）

两句都见于克雷比永（Crébillon）的《阿特柔斯》。

## The Thousand-and-Second Tale of Scheherazade / 山鲁佐德的第一千零二个故事
===Original===

Truth is stranger than fiction.

> Old saying

Having had occasion, lately, in the course of some Oriental investigations, to consult the *Tellmenow Isitsöornot*, a work which (like the Zohar of Simeon Jochaides) is scarcely known at all, even in Europe; and which has never been quoted, to my knowledge, by any American﻿—if we except, perhaps, the author of the *Curiosities of American Literature*;﻿—having had occasion, I say, to turn over some pages of the first-mentioned very remarkable work, I was not a little astonished to discover that the literary world has hitherto been strangely in error respecting the fate of the vizier’s daughter, Scheherazade, as that fate is depicted in the *Arabian Nights*; and that the denouement there given, if not altogether inaccurate, as far as it goes, is at least to blame in not having gone very much farther.

For full information on this interesting topic, I must refer the inquisitive reader to the *Isitsöornot* itself; but, in the meantime, I shall be pardoned for giving a summary of what I there discovered.

It will be remembered, that, in the usual version of the tales, a certain monarch, having good cause to be jealous of his queen, not only puts her to death, but makes a vow, by his beard and the prophet, to espouse each night the most beautiful maiden in his dominions, and the next morning to deliver her up to the executioner.

Having fulfilled this vow for many years to the letter, and with a religious punctuality and method that conferred great credit upon him as a man of devout feeling and excellent sense, he was interrupted one afternoon (no doubt at his prayers) by a visit from his grand vizier, to whose daughter, it appears, there had occurred an idea.

Her name was Scheherazade, and her idea was, that she would either redeem the land from the depopulating tax upon its beauty, or perish, after the approved fashion of all heroines, in the attempt.

===Chinese===

真理比虚构更离奇。

——古谚

近来，为了几桩东方学上的查考，我不得不去翻检《*Tellmenow Isitsöornot*》——一部（如同西缅·约凯代斯（Simeon Jochaides）的《佐哈尔》（Zohar）一样）纵在欧洲也几乎无人知晓的书；而据我所知，它也从不曾被任何美国人引用过——若除开《美国文学珍闻》（*Curiosities of American Literature*）的作者或许不算。我说，既然有机会把开头提到的这部极不寻常的书翻了几页，我便不免相当吃惊地发现：文学世界至今对于维齐尔的女儿山鲁佐德（Scheherazade）的命运——按《一千零一夜》（*Arabian Nights*）里描画的那个命运——处于一种离奇的错误之中；那里交代的结局，纵算不算全然失准，至少也该怪它没有把故事往远处再讲得多得多。

欲知这个有趣话题的详情，我只好把好打听烦的读者交给《*Isitsöornot*》本书；但在这期间，恕我把我在那里发现的，撮要奉告。

大家记得，在通常的版本里，某位君主怀着充分的理由嫉妒他的王后，不但把她处死，还指着自己的胡子和先知立誓：每夜娶他治下最美的少女，第二天清早把她交给刽子手。

这个誓他一字不差地履行了多年，严谨规矩近乎宗教——作为一个人怀虔诚之感、见识极佳的人物，这给他增光不少——一天下午，正当祈祷（毫无疑问），他的大维齐尔来访，打断了他；看来，大维齐尔的女儿心里生出了一个主意。

她名叫山鲁佐德；她的主意是：要么把这片国土从那令人口凋零的美貌税里赎出来，要么——照一切女主角交口称许的老套——在尝试里丧命。

===Original===

Accordingly, and although we do not find it to be leap-year (which makes the sacrifice more meritorious), she deputes her father, the grand vizier, to make an offer to the king of her hand. This hand the king eagerly accepts﻿—(he had intended to take it at all events, and had put off the matter from day to day, only through fear of the vizier)﻿—but, in accepting it now, he gives all parties very distinctly to understand, that, grand vizier or no grand vizier, he has not the slightest design of giving up one iota of his vow or of his privileges. When, therefore, the fair Scheherazade insisted upon marrying the king, and did actually marry him despite her father’s excellent advice not to do anything of the kind﻿—when she would and did marry him, I say, will I nill I, it was with her beautiful black eyes as thoroughly open as the nature of the case would allow.

It seems, however, that this politic damsel (who had been reading Machiavelli, beyond doubt), had a very ingenious little plot in her mind. On the night of the wedding, she contrived, upon I forget what specious pretence, to have her sister occupy a couch sufficiently near that of the royal pair to admit of easy conversation from bed to bed; and, a little before cock-crowing, she took care to awaken the good monarch, her husband (who bore her none the worse will because he intended to wring her neck on the morrow)﻿—she managed to awaken him, I say, (although on account of a capital conscience and an easy digestion, he slept well) by the profound interest of a story (about a rat and a black cat, I think) which she was narrating (all in an undertone, of course) to her sister. When the day broke, it so happened that this history was not altogether finished, and that Scheherazade, in the nature of things could not finish it just then, since it was high time for her to get up and be bowstrung﻿—a thing very little more pleasant than hanging, only a trifle more genteel!

The king’s curiosity, however, prevailing, I am sorry to say, even over his sound religious principles, induced him for this once to postpone the fulfilment of his vow until next morning, for the purpose and with the hope of hearing that night how it fared in the end with the black cat (a black cat, I think it was) and the rat.

===Chinese===

于是，虽然并没有逢上闰年（这使她的牺牲更添功德），她委派她的父亲、大维齐尔，向国王献上她的手。国王急切地接受了这只手——（他本来就无论如何打算娶它，只因怕维齐尔，才把这件事一天天往后推）——不过如今在应允的时候，他叫方方面面都明明白白知道：管他大维齐尔不大维齐尔，他的誓言、他的特权，他一丝一毫也无意放弃。于是，当美丽的山鲁佐德执意要嫁国王，不顾她父亲那句顶好的忠告——说什么也别做这种事——真的嫁了他；我说，当她愿意、也果真嫁了他——愿也罢，不愿也罢——她那双美丽的黑眼睛，是照事情的性质所容的程度，睁得十足地开的。

然而看来，这位工于心计的少女（她无疑读过马基雅维利），心里有一个很精巧的小计谋。成婚之夜，她设法——借着我忘了什么像样的口实——让她的妹妹占了一张卧榻，离王后和国王的卧榻近到可以床对床地闲谈；鸡叫之前不久，她设法唤醒了那位好君主、她的夫君（他并不因此存下更深的恶意，虽然他打算第二天拧断她的脖子）——我说，她设法唤醒了他（虽然由于一副顶大的良心和一副好消化的肠胃，他睡得很沉），用的是一篇故事（我想是关于一只老鼠和一只黑猫的）的深厚趣味，这故事她正（自然全压着嗓子）讲给她妹妹听。天亮时，凑巧这篇故事还没有讲完，而山鲁佐德按事情的性质也无法当时讲完，因为正到了她起床去受弓弦勒杀的时候——那件事比绞架好不了多少，只是体面那么一点点罢了！

可是国王的好奇心，说来遗憾，竟压过了他健全的宗教原则，使他破例一回，把誓愿的履行推迟到第二天早上，指望当天夜里听到那只黑猫（我想是只黑猫）和那只老鼠的下场如何。

===Original===

The night having arrived, however, the lady Scheherazade not only put the finishing stroke to the black cat and the rat (the rat was blue) but before she well knew what she was about, found herself deep in the intricacies of a narration, having reference (if I am not altogether mistaken) to a pink horse (with green wings) that went, in a violent manner, by clockwork, and was wound up with an indigo key. With this history the king was even more profoundly interested than with the other﻿—and, as the day broke before its conclusion (notwithstanding all the queen’s endeavors to get through with it in time for the bowstringing), there was again no resource but to postpone that ceremony as before, for twenty-four hours. The next night there happened a similar accident with a similar result; and then the next﻿—and then again the next; so that, in the end, the good monarch, having been unavoidably deprived of all opportunity to keep his vow during a period of no less than one thousand and one nights, either forgets it altogether by the expiration of this time, or gets himself absolved of it in the regular way, or (what is more probable) breaks it outright, as well as the head of his father confessor. At all events, Scheherazade, who, being lineally descended from Eve, fell heir, perhaps, to the whole seven baskets of talk, which the latter lady, we all know, picked up from under the trees in the garden of Eden; Scheherazade, I say, finally triumphed, and the tariff upon beauty was repealed.

Now, this conclusion (which is that of the story as we have it upon record) is, no doubt, excessively proper and pleasant﻿—but alas! like a great many pleasant things, is more pleasant than true, and I am indebted altogether to the *Isitsöornot* for the means of correcting the error. “*Le mieux*,” says a French proverb, “*est l’ennemi du bien*,” and, in mentioning that Scheherazade had inherited the seven baskets of talk, I should have added that she put them out at compound interest until they amounted to seventy-seven.

===Chinese===

夜晚到了，山鲁佐德夫人不但给黑猫和老鼠的故事收了尾（那老鼠是蓝色的），而且在她还没弄清自己身在何处之前，发觉自己已经深深卷进一篇叙述的千头万绪里去了；那叙述（如果我没有全然记错）牵涉到一匹粉红的马（长着绿翅膀），它靠发条驱动，行走的姿态极为猛烈，用一把靛蓝色的钥匙上弦。对这篇故事，国王比先前那篇更深深地入迷——天亮时它还没有讲完（尽管王后竭力想赶在上弓弦之前收束），便又只好像前回一样把那仪式推迟二十四个钟头。下一夜出了同样的岔子，落得同样的结果；再下一夜——然后又一夜；于是到头来，这位好君主在足足一千零一个夜晚里无可奈何地被剥夺了履行誓言的一切机会，到这个期限终了的时候，要么把誓言全然忘掉，要么按正规的办法求得赦免，要么（这更可能）干脆毁誓，顺手把他告解神父的脑袋也敲破了。无论如何，山鲁佐德——她既是夏娃的嫡系子孙，也许就承继了那全部七篮子话；那七篮子话，我们都知道，是夏娃女士从伊甸园的树底下拾来的——山鲁佐德，我说，到底胜利了，美貌税也废除了。

如今，这个结局（这是有案可稽的故事里的结局）无疑极其得体、极其可喜——可是唉！同许多可喜的事一样，它可喜多过真实；纠正这个错误的手段，我完全得自《*Isitsöornot*》。法国谚语说：「*Le mieux est l'ennemi du bien*」（更好是好的敌人）；既然提到山鲁佐德继承了七篮子话，我本该补上一句：她把它们放了出去生复利，直到涨成七十七篮子。

===Original===

“My dear sister,” said she, on the thousand-and-second night, (I quote the language of the *Isitsöornot* at this point, verbatim) “my dear sister,” said she, “now that all this little difficulty about the bowstring has blown over, and that this odious tax is so happily repealed, I feel that I have been guilty of great indiscretion in withholding from you and the king (who I am sorry to say, snores﻿—a thing no gentleman would do) the full conclusion of Sinbad the sailor. This person went through numerous other and more interesting adventures than those which I related; but the truth is, I felt sleepy on the particular night of their narration, and so was seduced into cutting them short﻿—a grievous piece of misconduct, for which I only trust that Allah will forgive me. But even yet it is not too late to remedy my great neglect﻿—and as soon as I have given the king a pinch or two in order to wake him up so far that he may stop making that horrible noise, I will forthwith entertain you (and him if he pleases) with the sequel of this very remarkable story.”

Hereupon the sister of Scheherazade, as I have it from the *Isitsöornot*, expressed no very particular intensity of gratification; but the king, having been sufficiently pinched, at length ceased snoring, and finally said, “Hum!” and then “Hoo!” when the queen, understanding these words (which are no doubt Arabic) to signify that he was all attention, and would do his best not to snore any more﻿—the queen, I say, having arranged these matters to her satisfaction, reentered thus, at once, into the history of Sinbad the sailor:

“ ‘At length, in my old age,’ (these are the words of Sinbad himself, as retailed by Scheherazade)﻿—‘at length, in my old age, and after enjoying many years of tranquillity at home, I became once more possessed of a desire of visiting foreign countries; and one day, without acquainting any of my family with my design, I packed up some bundles of such merchandise as was most precious and least bulky, and, engaging a porter to carry them, went with him down to the seashore, to await the arrival of any chance vessel that might convey me out of the kingdom into some region which I had not as yet explored.

===Chinese===

「亲爱的妹妹，」在第一千零二夜，她说（此处我逐字引用《*Isitsöornot*》的话），「亲爱的妹妹，」她说，「如今弓弦这桩小小的难处已经吹过去了，这可憎的税也这样可喜地废除了，我觉得，我把航海家辛伯达（Sinbad）的结局瞒着你们和国王不放（我很遗憾地说，他打鼾——这可不是绅士做的事），实在犯了极不检点的过失。这个人经历的种种奇遇，比我讲过的那些还要多、还有趣得多；可是实情是，讲它们的那一夜我困了，于是受了诱惑，把它们截短了——这是一桩令人痛心的失德，我只求安拉宽恕我。可是即便此刻，补救我这大疏忽也还不算太迟——等我给国王拧上一两把，把他拧醒到肯停下那可怕声响的程度，我就立刻给你们讲（他若乐意，也捎上他）这篇极不寻常的故事的后文。」

于是，据《*Isitsöornot*》，山鲁佐德的妹妹并没有表出什么特别的欣悦；可是国王被拧够了数，终于止了鼾，末了说了一声「哼！」又一声「呼！」王后听懂了这两个词（无疑是阿拉伯话），明白它们的意思是他全神贯注了，会尽力不再打鼾——我说，王后把这些事安排到自己满意之后，立刻重新接上了航海家辛伯达的故事：

「『终于，到我年老的时候，』（这些是辛伯达自己的话，由山鲁佐德转述）——『终于，到我年老的时候，在家中享了多年清福之后，我又一次动了游历外邦的心思。一天，我没让家里任何人知道我的打算，把几捆最值钱又最不占分量的货色捆好，雇了一个脚夫替我挑着，同他一起下到海边，等随便哪条凑巧的船，把我带出这个王国，去到我还不曾探过的一片地域。

===Original===

“ ‘Having deposited the packages upon the sands, we sat down beneath some trees, and looked out into the ocean in the hope of perceiving a ship, but during several hours we saw none whatever. At length I fancied that I could hear a singular buzzing or humming sound; and the porter, after listening awhile, declared that he also could distinguish it. Presently it grew louder, and then still louder, so that we could have no doubt that the object which caused it was approaching us. At length, on the edge of the horizon, we discovered a black speck, which rapidly increased in size until we made it out to be a vast monster, swimming with a great part of its body above the surface of the sea. It came toward us with inconceivable swiftness, throwing up huge waves of foam around its breast, and illuminating all that part of the sea through which it passed, with a long line of fire that extended far off into the distance.

“ ‘As the thing drew near we saw it very distinctly. Its length was equal to that of three of the loftiest trees that grow, and it was as wide as the great hall of audience in your palace, O most sublime and munificent of the caliphs. Its body, which was unlike that of ordinary fishes, was as solid as a rock, and of a jetty blackness throughout all that portion of it which floated above the water, with the exception of a narrow bloodred streak that completely begirdled it. The belly, which floated beneath the surface, and of which we could get only a glimpse now and then as the monster rose and fell with the billows, was entirely covered with metallic scales, of a color like that of the moon in misty weather. The back was flat and nearly white, and from it there extended upwards of six spines, about half the length of the whole body.

“ ‘The horrible creature had no mouth that we could perceive; but, as if to make up for this deficiency, it was provided with at least four score of eyes, that protruded from their sockets like those of the green dragonfly, and were arranged all around the body in two rows, one above the other, and parallel to the bloodred streak, which seemed to answer the purpose of an eyebrow. Two or three of these dreadful eyes were much larger than the others, and had the appearance of solid gold.

===Chinese===

「『把包裹放在沙上之后，我们在几棵树底下坐下来，朝海上张望，指望看见一条船；可是几个钟头里，我们什么也没有看见。末了，我觉得听见一阵奇异嗡营的声音；脚夫听了一会儿，也说他听得出。这声音随即大起来，接着更大，以致我们毫无可疑：弄出它来的那个东西正朝我们过来。终于，在天际的边上，我们看出一个黑点，它飞快地涨大，直到我们认出它是一个庞然巨怪，大半个身子露出海面，向我们游来。它以不可想象的速度逼近，在胸前掀卷起巨大的浪沫，用一道长长的火线，把它经过的那片海照得通明，火线远远伸进天边。

「『这东西近了，我们把它看得分明。它的长度抵得上三棵最高的树的长度；它的宽度，哦，哈里发中最尊崇、最宽宏的陛下，抵得上你王宫里那座大觐见厅。它的身子不像寻常的鱼，硬得像石头；凡露出水面的部分，一概黑得发亮，只有一道窄窄的血红条纹完完全全绕它一圈。它的肚腹浮在水面底下，随着浪头一起一落，我们只能偶尔瞥上一眼：上面密密覆着金属的鳞片，颜色像雾天的月亮。背是平的，近乎白色，从背上竖起六根以上的脊刺，大约有全身的一半长。

「『这可怕的畜生没有我们看得见的嘴；可是仿佛为了补偿这个欠缺，它至少备着八十只眼睛，像绿蜻蜓的眼睛一样从眼窝里凸出来，顺着身子周围排成两行，一行在上，一行在下，同那道仿佛充当眉毛的血红条纹平行。其中两三只可怕的眼睛比别的都大，有实心金子的样子。

===Original===

“ ‘Although this beast approached us, as I have before said, with the greatest rapidity, it must have been moved altogether by necromancy﻿—for it had neither fins like a fish nor web-feet like a duck, nor wings like the seashell which is blown along in the manner of a vessel; nor yet did it writhe itself forward as do the eels. Its head and its tail were shaped precisely alike, only, not far from the latter, were two small holes that served for nostrils, and through which the monster puffed out its thick breath with prodigious violence, and with a shrieking, disagreeable noise.

“ ‘Our terror at beholding this hideous thing was very great, but it was even surpassed by our astonishment, when upon getting a nearer look, we perceived upon the creature’s back a vast number of animals about the size and shape of men, and altogether much resembling them, except that they wore no garments (as men do), being supplied (by nature, no doubt) with an ugly uncomfortable covering, a good deal like cloth, but fitting so tight to the skin, as to render the poor wretches laughably awkward, and put them apparently to severe pain. On the very tips of their heads were certain square-looking boxes, which, at first sight, I thought might have been intended to answer as turbans, but I soon discovered that they were excessively heavy and solid, and I therefore concluded they were contrivances designed, by their great weight, to keep the heads of the animals steady and safe upon their shoulders. Around the necks of the creatures were fastened black collars, (badges of servitude, no doubt,) such as we keep on our dogs, only much wider and infinitely stiffer, so that it was quite impossible for these poor victims to move their heads in any direction without moving the body at the same time; and thus they were doomed to perpetual contemplation of their noses﻿—a view puggish and snubby in a wonderful, if not positively in an awful degree.

===Chinese===

「『这畜生虽然照我先前说的以最大的速度逼近我们，它想必全然是靠妖术驱动的——因为它既没有鱼那样的鳍，也没有鸭那样的蹼，也没有海贝那样的翅——那种海贝像船一样被吹着走；它也不像鳗鱼那样拧着身子往前拱。它的头和尾形状一模一样，只是离尾不远有两个小孔，权充鼻孔，巨怪从那里以骇人的力气喷出浓浊的呼吸，带着一声刺耳难听的啸音。

「『看见这丑恶的东西，我们的恐惧极大；可是等走近一瞧，看见那畜生背上驮着许许多多动物，个头和形状都同人大致相仿，而且同人也十分相像，只是不像人那样穿衣裳（人有衣裳穿），却天生（无疑是大自然供的）披着一种难看难受的罩子，像布，却绷在皮肉上绷得那样紧，弄得这些可怜虫可笑地笨拙，显然疼痛不堪——我们的惊骇更远胜恐惧。在它们头顶的最尖上，顶着几只方方正正像匣子的东西；乍一看，我以为它们是拿当头巾用的，可我很快看出它们又重又实，于是断定它们是一种装置，凭它们的重量，好把畜生的头稳稳当当安在肩膀上。畜生的脖子上都拴着黑项圈（无疑是奴役的徽记），就像我们拴在狗身上的那种，只是宽得多、也硬得多，硬到这些可怜的牺牲者要朝哪个方向动一动头，非连身子一齐动不可；于是他们注定要永远凝视自己的鼻子——那副塌鼻翘鼻的模样，纵说不上吓人，也出奇得可以。

===Original===

“ ‘When the monster had nearly reached the shore where we stood, it suddenly pushed out one of its eyes to a great extent, and emitted from it a terrible flash of fire, accompanied by a dense cloud of smoke, and a noise that I can compare to nothing but thunder. As the smoke cleared away, we saw one of the odd man-animals standing near the head of the large beast with a trumpet in his hand, through which (putting it to his mouth) he presently addressed us in loud, harsh, and disagreeable accents, that, perhaps, we should have mistaken for language, had they not come altogether through the nose.

“ ‘Being thus evidently spoken to, I was at a loss how to reply, as I could in no manner understand what was said; and in this difficulty I turned to the porter, who was near swooning through affright, and demanded of him his opinion as to what species of monster it was, what it wanted, and what kind of creatures those were that so swarmed upon its back. To this the porter replied, as well as he could for trepidation, that he had once before heard of this sea-beast; that it was a cruel demon, with bowels of sulphur and blood of fire, created by evil genii as the means of inflicting misery upon mankind; that the things upon its back were vermin, such as sometimes infest cats and dogs, only a little larger and more savage; and that these vermin had their uses, however evil﻿—for, through the torture they caused the beast by their nibbling and stingings, it was goaded into that degree of wrath which was requisite to make it roar and commit ill, and so fulfil the vengeful and malicious designs of the wicked genii.

“This account determined me to take to my heels, and, without once even looking behind me, I ran at full speed up into the hills, while the porter ran equally fast, although nearly in an opposite direction, so that, by these means, he finally made his escape with my bundles, of which I have no doubt he took excellent care﻿—although this is a point I cannot determine, as I do not remember that I ever beheld him again.

“ ‘For myself, I was so hotly pursued by a swarm of the men-vermin (who had come to the shore in boats) that I was very soon overtaken, bound hand and foot, and conveyed to the beast, which immediately swam out again into the middle of the sea.

===Chinese===

「『巨怪快要到我们站的岸时，突然把一只眼睛大大地顶出去，从眼里射出一道可怕的火光，伴着一团浓烟，还有一声我只能比作雷的响。烟散开时，我们看见一只奇怪的半人畜立在大畜生的头部附近，手里握着一只喇叭；他把喇叭凑上嘴，立刻用响亮、粗糙、难听的声音向我们说话；那声音若不是完全从鼻子里出来，我们或许会当成言语。

「『既然分明是在同我们说话，我却不知怎么回答，因为说的什么我一句也不懂；为难之际，我转向脚夫——他吓得几乎晕过去——问他这是什么种类的怪物，它要什么，那些密密驮在它背上的又是什么畜类。脚夫抖着，尽他的力答道：这海兽他从前听说过；它是一个凶恶的魔鬼，肚肠是硫磺，血是火，由邪恶的神灵造出来，作给人类降祸的器物；它背上那些东西是寄生的小畜，如同有时作践猫狗的那种，只是稍大一些、更凶一些；而这些小畜尽管作恶，却有用处——因为它们又啃又蜇，折磨那畜生，把它激到发怒的分量，那分量恰够叫它吼叫行凶，从而实现那些恶神复仇施毒的图谋。』」

「这篇叙述叫我拿定主意撒腿就跑，头也不回一回，我拼着命往山上跑；脚夫跑得一样快，虽然几乎朝着相反的方向，于是他就靠这个法子，终于带着我的包裹逃了性命，包裹他想必照看得极好——不过这一点我无法断定，因为我不记得往后还见过他。

「『至于我自己，一群人形的小畜（他们乘着船来到岸上）紧迫不舍，追得那么急，我很快就被追上，手也捆了脚也绑了，被送到那畜生跟前；那畜生立刻又游回海心去了。

===Original===

“ ‘I now bitterly repented my folly in quitting a comfortable home to peril my life in such adventures as this; but regret being useless, I made the best of my condition, and exerted myself to secure the goodwill of the man-animal that owned the trumpet, and who appeared to exercise authority over his fellows. I succeeded so well in this endeavor that, in a few days, the creature bestowed upon me various tokens of his favor, and in the end even went to the trouble of teaching me the rudiments of what it was vain enough to denominate its language; so that, at length, I was enabled to converse with it readily, and came to make it comprehend the ardent desire I had of seeing the world.

“ ‘Washish squashish squeak, Sinbad, hey-diddle diddle, grunt unt grumble, hiss, fiss, whiss,’ said he to me, one day after dinner﻿—but I beg a thousand pardons, I had forgotten that your majesty is not conversant with the dialect of the Cock-neighs (so the man-animals were called; I presume because their language formed the connecting link between that of the horse and that of the rooster). With your permission, I will translate. ‘Washish squashish,’ and so forth:﻿—that is to say, ‘I am happy to find, my dear Sinbad, that you are really a very excellent fellow; we are now about doing a thing which is called circumnavigating the globe; and since you are so desirous of seeing the world, I will strain a point and give you a free passage upon back of the beast.’ ”

When the Lady Scheherazade had proceeded thus far, relates the *Isitsöornot*, the king turned over from his left side to his right, and said:

“It is, in fact, *very* surprising, my dear queen, that you omitted, hitherto, these latter adventures of Sinbad. Do you know I think them exceedingly entertaining and strange?”

The king having thus expressed himself, we are told, the fair Scheherazade resumed her history in the following words:

“Sinbad went on in this manner with his narrative﻿—‘I thanked the man-animal for its kindness, and soon found myself very much at home on the beast, which swam at a prodigious rate through the ocean; although the surface of the latter is, in that part of the world, by no means flat, but round like a pomegranate, so that we went﻿—so to say﻿—either up hill or down hill all the time.’

“That I think, was very singular,” interrupted the king.

===Chinese===

「『这时我痛悔自己的愚蠢：撇下舒服的家，把性命拿来冒险，冒成这等奇遇；可是懊悔无用，我便随遇而安，竭力去讨那个握喇叭的半人畜的好，他似乎在他的同伴中间操着权威。这番努力我做得如此之好，以致没几天，那畜生就赏我种种恩宠的表示，到末了甚至肯费神教我一点它妄自称作它的语言的初步；于是我终于能同它谈得上来，也叫它明白了我心里那股要看世界的热望。

「『Washish squashish squeak, Sinbad, hey-diddle diddle, grunt unt grumble, hiss, fiss, whiss，』一天饭后，他对我说——可我求千金宽恕，我忘了陛下不熟鸡嘶人（Cock-neighs）的方言（那些半人畜被这样称呼；我猜想，因为他们的语言凑成了马的话和公鸡的话中间的那一环）。承陛下允准，我来翻译。『Washish squashish』等等，就是说：『亲爱的辛伯达，我很高兴发现你实在是个顶好的人；我们现在正要做一件叫做环球航行的事；你既然那样渴望见世面，我愿意通融一回，给你在那畜生的背上搭一趟免费。』」

山鲁佐德夫人讲到这里，据《*Isitsöornot*》，国王从左边翻到右边，说：

「事实上这实在*很*惊人，亲爱的王后，你到如今竟把这些后期的辛伯达奇遇漏下了。你知道吗，我觉得它们有意思极了、也奇极了。」

国王这样表示过之后，我们被告知，美丽的山鲁佐德用下面的话接上了她的历史：

「辛伯达照这个样子讲下去——『我谢了那半人畜的好意，很快发觉自己在那畜生的背上如鱼得水；那畜生在海里游得奇快；虽然在那一片海域，海面绝说不上平，倒像石榴一样滚圆，于是我们——可以这么说——一路不是上山就是下山。』」

「这个嘛，我想，是很奇特的，」国王插话。

===Original===

“Nevertheless, it is quite true,” replied Scheherazade.

“I have my doubts,” rejoined the king; “but, pray, be so good as to go on with the story.”

“I will,” said the queen. “ ‘The beast,’ continued Sinbad to the caliph, ‘swam, as I have related, up hill and down hill until, at length, we arrived at an island, many hundreds of miles in circumference, but which, nevertheless, had been built in the middle of the sea by a colony of little things like caterpillars.’ ”51

“Hum!” said the king.

“ ‘Leaving this island,’ said Sinbad﻿—(for Scheherazade, it must be understood, took no notice of her husband’s ill-mannered ejaculation) ‘leaving this island, we came to another where the forests were of solid stone, and so hard that they shivered to pieces the finest-tempered axes with which we endeavoured to cut them down.’ ”52

“Hum!” said the king, again; but Scheherazade, paying him no attention, continued in the language of Sinbad.

“ ‘Passing beyond this last island, we reached a country where there was a cave that ran to the distance of thirty or forty miles within the bowels of the earth, and that contained a greater number of far more spacious and more magnificent palaces than are to be found in all Damascus and Bagdad. From the roofs of these palaces there hung myriads of gems, like diamonds, but larger than men; and in among the streets of towers and pyramids and temples, there flowed immense rivers as black as ebony, and swarming with fish that had no eyes.’ ”53

“Hum!” said the king.

“ ‘We then swam into a region of the sea where we found a lofty mountain, down whose sides there streamed torrents of melted metal, some of which were twelve miles wide and sixty miles long;54 while from an abyss on the summit, issued so vast a quantity of ashes that the sun was entirely blotted out from the heavens, and it became darker than the darkest midnight; so that when we were even at the distance of a hundred and fifty miles from the mountain, it was impossible to see the whitest object, however close we held it to our eyes.’ ”55

“Hum!” said the king.

“ ‘After quitting this coast, the beast continued his voyage until we met with a land in which the nature of things seemed reversed﻿—for we here saw a great lake, at the bottom of which, more than a hundred feet beneath the surface of the water, there flourished in full leaf a forest of tall and luxuriant trees.’ ”56

===Chinese===

「尽管如此，这是千真万确的，」山鲁佐德答。

「我有我的疑心，」国王回嘴；「不过，劳驾，还是把故事讲下去吧。」

「我讲，」王后说。「『那畜生，』辛伯达对哈里发接着说，『照我方才讲的，上山下水地游，一直游到末了，我们到了一座岛跟前；岛周长好几百英里，却分明是海中央由一群毛虫似的小东西造起来的。』」〔51〕

「哼！」国王说。

「『离开这座岛，』辛伯达说——（必须说明，山鲁佐德对她丈夫这声失礼的惊叹毫不理会）『离开这座岛，我们来到另一座，那里森林是整块整块的石头，硬到我们想法砍倒它们用的最精淬的斧头全都崩成了碎片。』」〔52〕

「哼！」国王又说一声；可是山鲁佐德对他毫不理会，用辛伯达的话接下去。

「『过了这最后一座岛，我们到达一个国度，那里有一个洞，在地腹里伸进三十到四十英里，里面包容着无数宽敞得多、堂皇得多的宫殿，大马士革和巴格达所有的加在一起也比不上。这些宫殿的顶上，悬着数不清的宝石，像金刚钻，却比人大；在塔、金字塔和庙宇的街道中间，流着浩大的河，黑得像黑檀，河里挤满了没有眼睛的鱼。』」〔53〕

「哼！」国王说。

「『我们于是游进海里一个区域，在那里看见一座高耸的山；山的两坡流下熔化金属的急流，有的宽十二英里、长六十英里〔54〕；山顶上一个深渊里涌出数量极大的灰，把太阳从天上整个抹掉，天黑得比最黑的午夜还黑；以致我们纵然离山一百五十英里之遥，也看不见最白的物件，无论把它举得离眼睛多近。』」〔55〕

「哼！」国王说。

「『离开这带海岸之后，那畜生继续他的航行，直到我们遇见一片国土，那里事物的本性仿佛颠倒了——因为我们在这里看见一个巨湖，湖底在水下一百多英尺深处，一片高树茂叶的森林枝繁叶茂地活着。』」〔56〕

===Original===

“Hoo!” said the king.

“ ‘Some hundred miles farther on brought us to a climate where the atmosphere was so dense as to sustain iron or steel, just as our own does feather.’ ”57

“Fiddle de dee,” said the king.

“ ‘Proceeding still in the same direction, we presently arrived at the most magnificent region in the whole world. Through it there meandered a glorious river for several thousands of miles. This river was of unspeakable depth, and of a transparency richer than that of amber. It was from three to six miles in width; and its banks which arose on either side to twelve hundred feet in perpendicular height, were crowned with ever-blossoming trees and perpetual sweet-scented flowers, that made the whole territory one gorgeous garden; but the name of this luxuriant land was the Kingdom of Horror, and to enter it was inevitable death.’ ”58

“Humph!” said the king.

“ ‘We left this kingdom in great haste, and, after some days, came to another, where we were astonished to perceive myriads of monstrous animals with horns resembling scythes upon their heads. These hideous beasts dig for themselves vast caverns in the soil, of a funnel shape, and line the sides of them with rocks, so disposed one upon the other that they fall instantly, when trodden upon by other animals, thus precipitating them into the monster’s dens, where their blood is immediately sucked, and their carcasses afterwards hurled contemptuously out to an immense distance from “the caverns of death.” ’ ”59

“Pooh!” said the king.

“ ‘Continuing our progress, we perceived a district with vegetables that grew not upon any soil but in the air.60 There were others that sprang from the substance of other vegetables;61 others that derived their substance from the bodies of living animals;62 and then again, there were others that glowed all over with intense fire;63 others that moved from place to place at pleasure,64 and what was still more wonderful, we discovered flowers that lived and breathed and moved their limbs at will and had, moreover, the detestable passion of mankind for enslaving other creatures, and confining them in horrid and solitary prisons until the fulfillment of appointed tasks.’ ”65

“Pshaw!” said the king.

===Chinese===

「呼！」国王说。

「『再往前几百英里，把我们带到一个气候里：那里的空气密到能托住铁和钢，正如我们这里的空气托住羽毛。』」〔57〕

「胡拉乱唱，」国王说。

「『照同一个方向再往前走，我们不久便到了全世界最堂皇的地域。一条辉煌的大河蜿蜒着穿过它，绵延好几千英里。这条河深得无法言说，透明得比琥珀还贵气。宽从三英里到六英里；两岸以一千二百英尺的直立高度耸起，顶上戴着一树树常开的花、永不凋谢的香花，把整个地域变成一座壮丽的花园；可是这片丰饶的土地名叫恐怖之国，踏进去便是必死。』」〔58〕

「哼嗯！」国王说。

「『我们仓仓皇皇离了这座国，过了几天，来到另一座；我们惊见成千上万巨大的兽，头顶着镰刀似的角。这些狰狞的畜生在土里替自己掘出漏斗形状的大洞穴，洞壁用石块砌衬，一块块叠得只消别的兽一踩上去，便立刻塌落，把它们抛进怪物的巢穴；在那里，它们的血立刻被吸干，尸首随后被轻蔑地抛掷到离「死亡之洞」极远极远的地方。』」〔59〕

「呸！」国王说。

「『我们继续前行，看见一个地区，那里的菜蔬不长在任何土里，却长在空气里〔60〕。有的菜蔬从别的菜蔬的实体里长出来〔61〕；有的从活物的身体里取得它们的实体〔62〕；又有一些通体燃着烈火〔63〕；又有一些随意从一处挪到另一处〔64〕；更奇的是，我们发现了会活、会呼吸、会随自己意思动弹肢体的花，而且它们怀着人类那种可憎的热衷：奴役别的造物，把它们关进可怕而孤寂的监牢，直到指定的差事办完为止。』」〔65〕

「啐！」国王说。

===Original===

“ ‘Quitting this land, we soon arrived at another in which the bees and the birds are mathematicians of such genius and erudition, that they give daily instructions in the science of geometry to the wise men of the empire. The king of the place having offered a reward for the solution of two very difficult problems, they were solved upon the spot﻿—the one by the bees, and the other by the birds; but the king keeping their solution a secret, it was only after the most profound researches and labor, and the writing of an infinity of big books, during a long series of years, that the men-mathematicians at length arrived at the identical solutions which had been given upon the spot by the bees and by the birds.’ ”66

“Oh my!” said the king.

“ ‘We had scarcely lost sight of this empire when we found ourselves close upon another, from whose shores there flew over our heads a flock of fowls a mile in breadth, and two hundred and forty miles long; so that, although they flew a mile during every minute, it required no less than four hours for the whole flock to pass over us﻿—in which there were several millions of millions of fowl.’ ”67

“Oh fy!” said the king.

“ ‘No sooner had we got rid of these birds, which occasioned us great annoyance, than we were terrified by the appearance of a fowl of another kind, and infinitely larger than even the rocs which I met in my former voyages; for it was bigger than the biggest of the domes on your seraglio, oh, most Munificent of Caliphs. This terrible fowl had no head that we could perceive, but was fashioned entirely of belly, which was of a prodigious fatness and roundness, of a soft-looking substance, smooth, shining and striped with various colors. In its talons, the monster was bearing away to his eyrie in the heavens, a house from which it had knocked off the roof, and in the interior of which we distinctly saw human beings, who, beyond doubt, were in a state of frightful despair at the horrible fate which awaited them. We shouted with all our might, in the hope of frightening the bird into letting go of its prey, but it merely gave a snort or puff, as if of rage and then let fall upon our heads a heavy sack which proved to be filled with sand!’ ”

“Stuff!” said the king.

===Chinese===

「『辞了这片国土，我们不久到了另一片；那里的蜜蜂和鸟儿是何等天才、何等博学的数学家，天天给帝国里的智者们讲授几何学。该地的国王悬赏求解两道极难的题目，题当场便解出来了——一道由蜜蜂解出，另一道由鸟儿解出；可是国王把解法守成秘密，直到男子数学家们历经最深的研究与劳作、写下无穷卷帙浩繁的大书、一连串年头过去之后，才终于到达了同蜜蜂和鸟儿当场给出的解一模一样的解。』」〔66〕

「哦我的天！」国王说。

「『我们几乎还没有望不见这个帝国，就发现自己紧挨着另一个；从那岸边，一群禽鸟从我们头顶上飞过，群宽一英里，长二百四十英里；所以，虽然它们每一分钟飞一英里，整群飞过我们头顶竟花了足足四个钟头——群里计有数百万个百万只禽鸟。』」〔67〕

「哎呀呀！」国王说。

「『我们刚摆脱这些鸟——它们叫我们大不舒服——就又给另一种鸟的出现吓住了；那鸟比我在前几次航行里遇见的大鹏还要大出无限；因为，哦，最宽宏的哈里发，它比陛下内宫最大的圆顶还要大。这可怕的飞禽没有我们看得见的头，却整个儿是一只肚腹塑成的；那肚腹肥大滚圆得惊人，是一种看着柔软的东西，光滑，发亮，条纹斑斓。它的爪里，怪物正朝它天上的巢带去一座房子——房顶已叫它敲掉了，房里我们分明看见人，那些人毫无疑问，正为等着他们的可怕命运陷于恐怖的绝望。我们放足了嗓子喊，指望吓那鸟丢开捕获物；它只哼哧喷了一口气，像恼了似的，随后把一只沉甸甸的口袋摔在我们头上——那口袋后来证明装满了沙子！』」

「胡说！」国王说。

===Original===

“ ‘It was just after this adventure that we encountered a continent of immense extent and prodigious solidity, but which, nevertheless, was supported entirely upon the back of a sky-blue cow that had no fewer than four hundred horns.’ ”68

“*That*, now, I believe,” said the king, “because I have read something of the kind before, in a book.”

“ ‘We passed immediately beneath this continent (swimming in between the legs of the cow), and, after some hours, found ourselves in a wonderful country indeed, which, I was informed by the man-animal, was his own native land, inhabited by things of his own species. This elevated the man-animal very much in my esteem, and in fact, I now began to feel ashamed of the contemptuous familiarity with which I had treated him; for I found that the man-animals in general were a nation of the most powerful magicians, who lived with worms in their brain,69 which, no doubt, served to stimulate them by their painful writhings and wrigglings to the most miraculous efforts of imagination!’ ”

“Nonsense!” said the king.

“ ‘Among the magicians, were domesticated several animals of very singular kinds; for example, there was a huge horse whose bones were iron and whose blood was boiling water. In place of corn, he had black stones for his usual food; and yet, in spite of so hard a diet, he was so strong and swift that he would drag a load more weighty than the grandest temple in this city, at a rate surpassing that of the flight of most birds.’ ”70

“Twattle!” said the king.

“ ‘I saw, also, among these people a hen without feathers, but bigger than a camel; instead of flesh and bone she had iron and brick; her blood, like that of the horse, (to whom, in fact, she was nearly related,) was boiling water; and like him she ate nothing but wood or black stones. This hen brought forth very frequently, a hundred chickens in the day; and, after birth, they took up their residence for several weeks within the stomach of their mother.’ ”71

“Fal lal!” said the king.

===Chinese===

「『恰恰在这桩奇遇之后，我们遇上了一片大陆，广阔无边，坚实无比，可是分明整个支撑在一头天蓝色的母牛的背上，那牛的角不下四百只。』」〔68〕

「*这个*嘛，如今我信了，」国王说，「因为从前我在一本书里读到过这一类的东西。」

「『我们立刻从这片大陆底下经过（从母牛的腿中间游过去），过了几个钟头，发觉自己到了一个真正奇妙的国度；那半人畜告诉我，那是他的故乡，住着他同种的那些东西。这一来，那半人畜在我眼里的身价大涨；实在说，我开始为待他时那种轻慢的亲昵羞愧起来；因为我发现，半人畜总的来说，是一个最有威力的魔法师的民族，他们的脑子里同虫子住在一起〔69〕，那虫子痛苦的扭动蜷曲，无疑正好刺激他们，叫他们的想象力作出最奇迹的腾跃！』」

「一派胡言！」国王说。

「『在魔法师们中间，养着几种极特别的家畜；比方说，有一匹巨大的马，骨头是铁，血是滚水。代替谷子，他拿黑石头当日常的食料；可是尽管口粮这么硬，他却强壮神速，拉得动比这座城里最宏伟的神殿还重的载，速度赛过大多数鸟的飞行。』」〔70〕

「胡诌！」国王说。

「『这些人里，我还看见一只没有羽毛的母鸡，却比骆驼还大；她没有肉和骨，有的是铁和砖；她的血，同那匹马的一样（实在说，她同马是近亲），是滚水；同马一样，她除了木头和黑石头什么都不吃。这只母鸡下崽极勤，一天产出一百只鸡；而且小鸡出生之后，还在母亲的胃里一住好几个星期。』」〔71〕

「啦啦啦！」国王说。

===Original===

“ ‘One of this nation of mighty conjurors created a man out of brass and wood, and leather, and endowed him with such ingenuity that he would have beaten at chess, all the race of mankind with the exception of the great Caliph, Haroun Alraschid.72 Another of these magi constructed (of like material) a creature that put to shame even the genius of him who made it; for so great were its reasoning powers that, in a second, it performed calculations of so vast an extent that they would have required the united labor of fifty thousand fleshy men for a year.73 But a still more wonderful conjuror fashioned for himself a mighty thing that was neither man nor beast, but which had brains of lead, intermixed with a black matter like pitch, and fingers that it employed with such incredible speed and dexterity that it would have had no trouble in writing out twenty thousand copies of the Koran in an hour, and this with so exquisite a precision, that in all the copies there should not be found one to vary from another by the breadth of the finest hair. This thing was of prodigious strength, so that it erected or overthrew the mightiest empires at a breath; but its powers were exercised equally for evil and for good.’ ”

“Ridiculous!” said the king.

“ ‘Among this nation of necromancers there was also one who had in his veins the blood of the salamanders; for he made no scruple of sitting down to smoke his chibouc in a red-hot oven until his dinner was thoroughly roasted upon its floor.74 Another had the faculty of converting the common metals into gold, without even looking at them during the process.75 Another had such a delicacy of touch that he made a wire so fine as to be invisible.76 Another had such quickness of perception that he counted all the separate motions of an elastic body, while it was springing backward and forward at the rate of nine hundred millions of times in a second.’ ”77

“Absurd!” said the king.

===Chinese===

「『这个大力法师之邦里，有一位用铜、木头和皮革造出一个人来，赋予他那样的智巧，他下起棋来会赢整个人类，只除了伟大的哈里发哈伦·拉希德（Haroun Alraschid）〔72〕。这些法师里另一位，用同样的材料造出一只造物，它叫造它的那位天才本人也自愧不如；因为它的推理力大到这样的地步：一秒钟里它完成的计算，范围之广，要五万个血肉之人合力干一年也干不完〔73〕。可是还有一位更奇妙的法师，给自己造出一件了不起的东西，既不是人也不是兽，可它有铅做的脑子，掺着一种沥青似的黑色物质，手指使唤起来又快又巧到不可思议的程度，一个钟头里抄出两万部《古兰经》也毫无困难，而且精确得妙绝：所有抄本里找不出一部同另一部有最细的头发丝那样宽的出入。这东西力大无穷，一口气便建立起或推翻掉最强大的帝国；它的力量，为恶为善行得一样。』」

「荒唐！」国王说。

「『在这批行妖术的人中间，还有一位血里流着火蜥蜴的血；他毫不犹豫地坐进一只烧得通红的烤炉里抽他的烟管，直到他的晚饭在炉底烤得透熟〔74〕。另一位有一种本事，能把寻常的金属变成金子，变化的当口连看都不看它们一眼〔75〕。另一位触觉精细，能把一根丝拉细到看不见〔76〕。另一位知觉敏锐，能数清一根弹性物件的每一次单独的动弹，而它正以一秒钟九万万次的速率来回弹跳〔77〕。』」

「荒谬！」国王说。

===Original===

“ ‘Another of these magicians, by means of a fluid that nobody ever yet saw, could make the corpses of his friends brandish their arms, kick out their legs, fight, or even get up and dance at his will.78 Another had cultivated his voice to so great an extent that he could have made himself heard from one end of the world to the other.79 Another had so long an arm that he could sit down in Damascus and indite a letter at Bagdad﻿—or indeed at any distance whatsoever.80 Another commanded the lightning to come down to him out of the heavens, and it came at his call; and served him for a plaything when it came. Another took two loud sounds and out of them made a silence. Another constructed a deep darkness out of two brilliant lights.81 Another made ice in a red-hot furnace.82 Another directed the sun to paint his portrait, and the sun did.83 Another took this luminary with the moon and the planets, and having first weighed them with scrupulous accuracy, probed into their depths and found out the solidity of the substance of which they were made. But the whole nation is, indeed, of so surprising a necromantic ability, that not even their infants, nor their commonest cats and dogs have any difficulty in seeing objects that do not exist at all, or that for twenty millions of years before the birth of the nation itself had been blotted out from the face of creation.’ ”84

“Preposterous!” said the king.

“ ‘The wives and daughters of these incomparably great and wise magi,’ ” continued Scheherazade, without being in any manner disturbed by these frequent and most ungentlemanly interruptions on the part of her husband﻿—“ ‘the wives and daughters of these eminent conjurors are everything that is accomplished and refined; and would be everything that is interesting and beautiful, but for an unhappy fatality that besets them, and from which not even the miraculous powers of their husbands and fathers has, hitherto, been adequate to save. Some fatalities come in certain shapes, and some in others﻿—but this of which I speak has come in the shape of a crotchet.’ ”

“A what?” said the king.

===Chinese===

「『这些魔法师里又有一位，借一种谁也不曾见过的流体，能叫他朋友们的尸首挥舞胳膊、踢蹬腿、厮打，甚至照他的意思站起来跳舞〔78〕。另一位把嗓子练到那样程度：他能叫世界这一头听见他，传到那一头〔79〕。另一位手臂长到他能坐在大马士革，在巴格达写一封信——或者实在说，随便多远〔80〕。另一位吩咐闪电从天上下来到他跟前，闪电应召而来；来了还给他当玩物。另一位拿两声巨响，从里面造出一片寂静。另一位拿两道辉煌的亮光，造出一片深沉的黑暗〔81〕。另一位在烧红的炉子里造出冰〔82〕。另一位吩咐太阳给他画像，太阳画了〔83〕。另一位拿了这个天体，连同月亮和行星，先以一丝不苟的精确把它们称过，又探入它们的深处，查明它们的实体由什么质料构成、坚实到何等程度。可是整个这一族，妖术的本领实在惊人到这样的地步：连他们的婴孩，连他们顶寻常的猫和狗，看见全然不存在的物件——或在那一族自身诞生之前二千万年就从创世的脸上被抹掉的物件——也毫无困难。』」〔84〕

「岂有此理！」国王说。

「『这些无与伦比的伟大而智慧的法师们的妻女，』」山鲁佐德接着说——对她丈夫这些频频的、最失绅士体统的打岔毫不动气——「『这些卓越的法师们的妻和女，凡可算有教养、有风雅的一切都在她们身上；若不是一桩不幸的恶运缠着她们——这恶运连她们丈夫和父亲的神通至今也救不了她们——凡可算有趣、美丽的一切本也都在她们身上。有的恶运以某种形状来，有的以别的形状来；可是我说的这一桩，来时形状是一副裙撑（crotchet）。』」

「一副什么？」国王说。

===Original===

“ ‘A crotchet’ ” said Scheherazade. “ ‘One of the evil genii, who are perpetually upon the watch to inflict ill, has put it into the heads of these accomplished ladies that the thing which we describe as personal beauty consists altogether in the protuberance of the region which lies not very far below the small of the back. Perfection of loveliness, they say, is in the direct ratio of the extent of this lump. Having been long possessed of this idea, and bolsters being cheap in that country, the days have long gone by since it was possible to distinguish a woman from a dromedary﻿—’ ”

“Stop!” said the king﻿—“I can’t stand that, and I won’t. You have already given me a dreadful headache with your lies. The day, too, I perceive, is beginning to break. How long have we been married?﻿—my conscience is getting to be troublesome again. And then that dromedary touch﻿—do you take me for a fool? Upon the whole, you might as well get up and be throttled.”

These words, as I learn from the *Isitsöornot*, both grieved and astonished Scheherazade; but, as she knew the king to be a man of scrupulous integrity, and quite unlikely to forfeit his word, she submitted to her fate with a good grace. She derived, however, great consolation, (during the tightening of the bowstring,) from the reflection that much of the history remained still untold, and that the petulance of her brute of a husband had reaped for him a most righteous reward, in depriving him of many inconceivable adventures.

===Chinese===

「『一副裙撑』」山鲁佐德说。「『恶神里有一位，永远蹲着守候降祸，把这桩事放进了这些有教养的太太们的脑袋：我们称作个人美的东西，全部在于腰眼下面不远处那个部位的隆起。可爱的极致，她们说，同这一块隆起的幅度成正比。这念头既已揣了多时，那国里枕头又便宜，日子久了，要从一头单峰驼里分辨出一个女人来，早就不可能了——』」

「住口！」国王说——「这个我受不了，也决不受。你那些谎已经叫我的脑袋疼得厉害。天也，我看，开始亮了。我们结婚多久了？——我的良心又开始找起麻烦来了。还有那单峰驼的形容——你当我是傻子不成？总而言之，你不妨起床受勒去。」

这几句话，据我从《*Isitsöornot*》得知，又叫山鲁佐德伤心，又叫她吃惊；可是她知道国王是个一丝不苟守信的人，决不至于食言，便体体面面地听凭命运摆布了。不过她还是得到很大的安慰（在弓弦收紧的当儿）：想到故事还有许多留着没讲；想到她那畜生丈夫的急脾气，替他自己收下了一笔最公正的报赏——把许多不可思议的奇遇从他那儿夺了去。

## Some Words with a Mummy / 与木乃伊的一席话
===Original===

The symposium of the preceding evening had been a little too much for my nerves. I had a wretched headache, and was desperately drowsy. Instead of going out therefore to spend the evening as I had proposed, it occurred to me that I could not do a wiser thing than just eat a mouthful of supper and go immediately to bed.

A *light* supper of course. I am exceedingly fond of Welsh rabbit. More than a pound at once, however, may not at all times be advisable. Still, there can be no material objection to two. And really between two and three, there is merely a single unit of difference. I ventured, perhaps, upon four. My wife will have it five;﻿—but, clearly, she has confounded two very distinct affairs. The abstract number, five, I am willing to admit; but, concretely, it has reference to bottles of Brown Stout, without which, in the way of condiment, Welsh rabbit is to be eschewed.

Having thus concluded a frugal meal, and donned my nightcap, with the serene hope of enjoying it till noon the next day, I placed my head upon the pillow, and, through the aid of a capital conscience, fell into a profound slumber forthwith.

But when were the hopes of humanity fulfilled? I could not have completed my third snore when there came a furious ringing at the street-door bell, and then an impatient thumping at the knocker, which awakened me at once. In a minute afterward, and while I was still rubbing my eyes, my wife thrust in my face a note, from my old friend, Doctor Ponnonner. It ran thus:

“Come to me, by all means, my dear good friend, as soon as you receive this. Come and help us to rejoice. At last, by long persevering diplomacy, I have gained the assent of the Directors of the City Museum, to my examination of the Mummy﻿—you know the one I mean. I have permission to unswathe it and open it, if desirable. A few friends only will be present﻿—you, of course. The Mummy is now at my house, and we shall begin to unroll it at eleven tonight.

“Yours, ever,

“Ponnonner.”

By the time I had reached the “Ponnonner,” it struck me that I was as wide awake as a man need be. I leaped out of bed in an ecstasy, overthrowing all in my way; dressed myself with a rapidity truly marvellous; and set off, at the top of my speed, for the doctor’s.

===Chinese===

前一晚的那场酒宴，对我的神经稍稍重了些。我头终得厉害，困得要死。因此我没有照原先的打算出门消磨这个晚上，而是想到：再没有比吃一口晚饭、立刻上床更聪明的了。

当然是*一顿清淡的*晚饭。我极其爱吃威尔士干酪烤面包。不过一次吃一磅多，未必样样时候都合适。话虽如此，两磅总没有什么大不了的反对象吧。而两磅与三磅之间，实在只差一个单位。我大胆吃了，兴许，四磅。我太太咬定是五磅；——可她显然把两码事搞混了。抽象的五这个数，我愿意承认；可具体说来，它指的是黑啤酒的瓶数——少了这味作料，威尔士干酪烤面包还是不吃为妙。

这顿清筒的饭既毕，戴上睡帽，怀着安详的希望指望享受到第二天正午，我把头放到枕上，凭着一副上好的良心，立刻随入沉睡。

可人类的希望几时兑现过？我第三声鼾还没打完，街门的铃便发疯似的响起来，接着门环上一阵不耐烦的捶打，一下子把我惊醒了。随后不出一分钟，我还揉着眼睛，我太太已把一张便条塞到我脸上，是我老友蓬农纳医生的。条子上写道：

「收到此条，务必立刻来我这里，我亲爱的好朋友。来同我们一道欢喜。经过长期坚韧的外交，我终于争得市博物馆重事们的同意，准我检查那具木乃伊——您知道我指哪一具。他们准我解开缠布、打开来看，如有必要。只请几位朋友到场——您自然是其中之一。木乃伊现已在我家；今晚十一点我们开始解裹。

「您永远的

「蓬农纳」

读到「蓬农纳」三个字时，我发觉自己已清醒得不能再清醒。我一阵狂喜蹿下床，一路撞翻挡道的一切；以真正惊人的速度穿好衣裳；撒腿狂奔，直奔医生家。

===Original===

There I found a very eager company assembled. They had been awaiting me with much impatience; the Mummy was extended upon the dining-table; and the moment I entered its examination was commenced.

It was one of a pair brought, several years previously, by Captain Arthur Sabretash, a cousin of Ponnonner’s from a tomb near Eleithias, in the Lybian mountains, a considerable distance above Thebes on the Nile.
